Male flowers: stalk with bract subapical; peduncle 4–8 cm long; bract subcircular or reniform, 10–30 by (10–)15–40 mm, apex rounded or ± acute-acuminate, margin entire or crenulate, finely pubescent, inside glabrous, soft-hairy or scabrous; pedicel 3–12 mm long; receptacle-tube saucer-shaped, 2 by 4 mm, green or blackish; sepals (ovate-)oblong, (4–)6–15 by 3–7(–10) mm, subacute, obtuse or notched, blackish, apical portion not out-curved; petals obovate-elliptic, 20–30(–50?) by (10–)15–20 mm, broadly obtuse, three with (always?) dark blotch at base, scales 2, broadly rounded; filaments ca 3 mm long, inserted almost at the base of the receptacle-tube, dark-coloured outside, papillose-pubescent towards base; anthers coherent in a subglobose mass, with apex 5-bullate with coarsely papillose semiglobose extensions corresponding with the thecae; thecae plicate; disc as minute appendages near insertion of stamens. Female flowers: stalk 3–15 cm long; bract minute, at or below the middle; pedicel 15–120 mm long; ovary fusiform, more narrowed at apex, 8–12 by 2–4 mm, (finely) densely pale brown papillose-pubescent or hispid and with 8–10 lengthwise irregular (verrucose) low ridges or rows of ± flattened tubercles; sepals linear, 4–5 mm long; petals obovate-oblong, 20–50 by 10(–15) mm, acute or obtuse; style ca 5 mm long. Fruit ovoid or ellipsoid, narrowed at apex, 3–7 cm long, subglabrous or (densely) pubescent or soft spiny, with 8–10 irregular undulate lengthwise ridges or with irregularly crested ribs or with lengthwise rows of flattened tubercles. Seeds 10–20, somewhat compressed, 6–12 by 5–8 mm, margin shallowly undulate, testa grey-brown or blackish, not sculptured.

description: Evergreen tree, up to 30 m high; bark greyish-brown, longitudinally fissured; twigs lenticellate, first covered by yellowish hirsute, stellate hairs; leaf-scars prominent; stipules linear-lanceolate, 2–4 by 0.5–0.8 cm. description: Annual herbaceous delicate ca 1 m long climber; early glabrescent (few gland-hairs). Male inflorescences broadly paniculate, terminal and axillary, 10–30 cm long, peduncle 1.5–4 cm long, branches (glandular)pubescent or subglabrous, bracts linear, minute 0.5–2 mm long, the basal ones larger and 3(–5)-foliolate, to 1 cm long, flowers up to 5 (sub)fascicled, in condensed terminal racemes. Male flowers: pedicel slender, 5–10 mm long, (glandular)pubescent or subglabrous; bud ovoid; perianth 5–8 mm diam., receptacle shallow, 1.5–2 mm diam., sometimes saccate below sepals; sepals ovate-oblong, ca 2 mm long, acuminate; petals ovate, subobtuse or acute, 2.5–3 by (1.5–)2 mm, glabrous or puberulous; filaments free, ca 0.5 mm long; anthers less than 0.5 mm diam. Female inflorescences paniculate, 2–10 cm long, up to 10 flowered. Female flowers: pedicel ca 10 mm long; ovary subcylindrical, 7–8(–10) mm long, finely pubescent; styles short, stigma lunate, margin not lobulate. Infructescence one- or several-fruited; fruits 4–8 cm long, glabrous or pubescent, base narrowed or rounded, at apex 1.2–2.5(–3) cm wide; fruiting pedicel 1–2 cm long. description: Climber 3–7 m long, glabrous; perennial from woody rootstock. Tendrils often with terminal adhesive pads. description: Tree, up to 40 m high; bark dark grey, smooth or shallowly fissured, lenticellate, producing poisonous sap; wood white or yellowish; twigs tomentose, glabrescent with stiff hairs. description: Liana up to 15 m high; branches sparsely pubescent to glabrescent; tendril-like shoots 10–40 cm long, with strongly reflexed hook-like branches 0.5–2 cm long; foliage evergreen. Inflorescences paniculate thyrses, 10–70 cm long, highly branched; axes sparsely to moderately pubescent, often becoming glabrescent, minor axes pale green or pale brownish when dry; main branches 4–14, to 30 cm long; main axis persistent, often tendrillate, with strongly recurved, hook-like branch bases; cymose units very condensed with flowers appearing fasciculate; bracts to 8 by 1.6(–2.6) cm, petiolate, biglandular, blade obovate or narrowly elliptic, apex acute. Staminate flowers: pedicel 6–14 mm long; sepals (4)5, 1.3–2.3 mm long and wide, apex obtuse or rounded, very sparsely pubescent; disc subannular, indistinct; androecium of 3 free, subsessile anthers fused basally. Pistillate flowers: pedicel 3–12 mm long; sepals 5, broadly to very broadly ovate, 1–1.8 mm long and wide, very sparsely to sparsely pubescent; gynoecium broadly oblong-obovoid, becoming subglobose post anthesis, 1.6–3 by 1.4–2.8 mm, apex broadly truncate and depressed, glabrous; stylar column present as broadly truncate apex, 0.3–0.5 by 0.9–1.5 mm. Fruits schizocarpous capsules, 3-lobed, 1.8–2.6 by 2.9–4.2 cm, separating into 3 loculicidally dehiscent cocci; pericarp 1.5-2 mm thick, smooth, becoming hard (woody) and brittle. Seeds subglobose or broadly ellipsoid, 1.5–2.9 by 1.4–2.5 by 1.2–2.1 cm, pale brown, more or less glossy, mostly smooth; outer seed coat very thin, adherent, persistent.

description: Shrub, creeping when young by means of stolons. Juvenile stems angular, flattened, keeled at nodes, smooth and slightly ridged, bracteate at the base, giving a jointed appearance, older branches terete, bark with shallow longitudinal fissures. Leaves 22–44 (11–28 by 7–12) mm, apex acuminate, tip mucronate, base attenuate, primary vein raised on the upper and lower surfaces, leaves sometimes covered in a powdery bloom. Male inflorescences in leaf axils; peduncles angular, 6–10 by 0.5 mm, flowers crowded at the apex of the peduncle, many caducous, only 4–5 reaching maturity; each flower subtended by a single tortuous, lanceolate bract, bract 1 by 0.2 mm; flowers grouped in triads with 1 central and 2 lateral flowers, the central flower reaching maturity first. Male flowers green; pedicel approximately 1 mm long, tapering towards the base; tepals fleshy, broadly ovate, 1–2 by 1.2–1.5 mm, leaf-like with one central veinlet, apiculate at the tip on the inner surface, margins slightly involute, papillose; filaments slightly dilated at the base, 0.4 by 0.1 mm; anthers 0.2 by 0.3 mm. Female inflorescences with peduncle 3–4 mm long. Female flowers subtended by an involucre of 3 tortuous, lanceolate, valvate bracts, which reach at least halfway up the flower, resembling a calyx; tepals broadly ovate, 1–2 by 1.2–1.5 mm, shortly apiculate on the inner surface, papillose along the inner margin; style 0.5 by 0.3 mm, stigma lobes fleshy, pointed, smooth; nectary flat or slightly concave. Fruit ripening orange or red, 5–6 by 5–5.5 mm.

description: Shrub or treelet, to 5 m high, the branchlets slightly flattened and becoming cylindric, at first minutely stellate-furfuraceous, later glabrous. Inflorescence axes stellate-furfuraceous, later glabrous, 20–34 cm long, flowers in umbellate clusters on the distalmost branchlets, peduncle 4-angled, bracts and bracteoles subulate, 1–4 mm long and covered with stellate hairs, caducous after flowers mature. Flowers 4-merous, pedicels 15–20 mm long, minutely puberulous. Hypanthium cylindrical, 3.5–5 mm long, often with 4 or 8 vertical ridges, minutely puberulous; calyx lobes triangular, less frequently ligular, 1–1, 5 mm long. Petals 7–9 mm long, obovate to elliptic, pink. Stamens 8, dimorphic, the 4 outer ones linear, purple and twice as long (7–9 mm) as the inner 4, short, yellow ones. Capsule obconical, 5–6 mm long, crowned by the persistent calyx rim.

description: Epiphytic or rarely epilithic shrubs, to 1.5 m high, adventitious roots with tuberous, orange to brown swellings, young branchlets flattened, grooved or with two ridges, becoming terete and smooth, covered with a red-brown indumentum or glabrous. Leaves 5.5–24 x 2–8.5 cm, lanceolate to elliptic or obovate, base narrowed, rounded, or cordate, apex obtuse or acuminate, lamina with 1 pair of lateral primary veins, midrib prominent, secondary venation obscure, subcoriaceous, often purplish below, petioles 0.3–1.5 cm long. Inflorescences many-flowered terminal paniculate cymes, often with bright red axes, 2–6 cm long, peduncle 1–3 cm long, bracts and bracteoles minute, triangular and persistent. Flowers 4-merous, 5-10 mm long. Hypanthium urceolate, 3–4 x ca 2 mm, calyx rim truncate with 4 thickened cusps, sparsely furfuraceous, pink, ovary ⅓ as long as the hypanthium, completely adnate to the hypanthium, stamen pockets lacking. Petals oblong or obovate, acuminate and thickened at the tip, clawed at the base, 5–7 mm long, white to pink, often tinged pink, sometimes yellow, glabrous. Stamens 8, isomorphic, 5–6 mm long, anthers cylindrical, curved at the tip, connective with a 0.5–0.75 mm long dorsal spur arising from the lower half. Berry 5–7 mm in diam., capped by the red calyx remnant, urceolate when young, later globose, immature yellowish-green, mature orange to dark red.

Berry 4–6 mm in diam., globose, capped by the calyx neck, turning green to dark red while ripening.

description: Epiphytic shrubs, occasionally terrestrial, scandent or erect, to 4.5 m high, climbing with adventitious roots, roots sometimes swollen and tuberous, branchlets terete, smooth, glabrous, becoming ridged and wrinkled when older, drying reddish. Leaves lanceolate or ovate, 5–10 x 2–5 cm, base narrowed or slightly rounded, apex short to long-acuminate, lamina with 1 pair of lateral primary veins, subcoriaceous to fleshy and coriaceous, above often with a rugose surface and dark green except for the reddish midrib, below reddish, margip sometimes serrulate when dry, petioles 1–1.7 cm long. Inflorescences few-flowered terminal cymes, 2–6 cm long, or rarely solitary flowers, axes terete, often succulent, glabrous, peduncle 1–3 cm long. Flowers 4 merous, 14–22 mm long, bracts and bracteoles lanceolate, 1–3 mm long. Hypanthium 4–8 mm x ca 2 mm, urceolate, constricted above the ovary, calyx rim 1–1.5 mm high, truncate, undulate or with 4 triangular lobes or cusps, rarely ciliate, ovary globose, ¼ as long as the hypanthium, 1–2 mm across and completely adnate to the hypanthium, stamen pockets lacking. Petals ovate, 12–18 mm long, base truncate, apex acuminate, dorsally with thickened cusps, changing from pink to white from the base to the tip. Stamens 8, subequal, with a rostrate tip, connective ventrally bilobed, dorsally with a produced spur, presence and length of the dorsal spur differing within single flowers, episepalous (outer) stamens with 6–10 mm long anthers, anthers either light yellow or purplish, epipetalous (inner) stamens with 5–7 mm long anthers. Berry 6–8 mm in diam, subglobose and with a distinct, 2–3 mm high and 4–5 mm wide neck, pericarp glabrous, rugose when dry, green turning red.

description: Vine, with long, slender, twining stems from woody rootstock; stems 1.5–3.5 mm in diam., often drying dark reddish-brown, sparsely to moderately hirsute. Inflorescences narrow, 1–8 cm long, axes sparsely to densely hirsute and short pubescent; bracts 1.2–2.2 mm long, drying reddish-brown. Staminate flowers pale green, 2–3 mm in diam. when open, greenish; pedicel 1–2.3 mm long; calyx lobes ovate, 0.9–1.3 by 0.5–1 mm, sparsely to moderately pubescent, apex acute; disc 0.8–1.3 mm in diam.; androecium 0.4–0.8 mm wide; anthers 0.3–0.5(–0.6) mm long, the two anther sacs parallel to divergent. Pistillate flowers pale green; pedicel 0.5–1.5 mm long; sepals lanceolate, narrowly elliptic, or sometimes ovate, 1.4–2.4 by (0.4–)0.6–0.9 mm, sparsely pubescent; ovary 0.8–1.8 by 1–2.7 mm; styles 0.6–1.3 mm long, 0.4–1 mm wide, glabrous or sparsely hairy; stigmas 0.3–0.7 mm long, glabrous, with inner surface stigmatic. Fruits: pedicel 3–4.5 mm long, thick, often distinctly bent; sepals persistent, reflexed; capsules 5–6.5 by 9–11.5 mm, drying dark brown, sparsely covered in stinging hairs. description: Tree up to 20 m high, dbh 25 cm; bark smooth, greyish-brown; apical branches distinctly pubescent. Indumentum creamish-brown, consisting of stellate-dendritic hairs, ca 0.2 mm in diam. with ca 8–15 radii. Stipules present as a pair of nearly spherical glands, ca 1 mm in diam. Leaves: petiole 3–16 cm long, pubescent; blade obovate-elliptic, 16–46 by 7–17 cm, length/width ratio 2.3–2.7, chartaceous, base obtuse to slightly acute, margin serrate with teeth 5–15 mm apart, apex acuminate, both sides distinctly pubescent on midrib and side veins, sparsely pubescent otherwise, basal glands above spherical, ca 1 mm in diam., sometimes absent, brighter below although not whitish, complete venation distinct, side veins 17–19, arching directly into the marginal teeth (craspedodromous), lowermost pair different and mostly on the basal leaf margin. Inflorescences 20–40 cm long panicles, side branches 1–2 cm long, distant at base and more crowded apically, distinctly pubescent throughout, with yellowish flowers; bracts of side branches ca 3 mm long, linear, often absent, but a pair of nearly spherical glands 1 mm in diam. usually present; side branches with few triangular, eglandular bracts, ca 2 mm long, each subtending several flowers. Staminate flowers densely pubescent outside; pedicels 2–3 mm long; sepals 3–4 by ca 2.5 mm, often with small dorsal appendices; petals ca 5 by 2.5 mm; disc lobed, pubescent with simple hairs. Pistillate flowers: sepals 3–5 by 2.5–3.5 mm, at least in fruit usually with knob like dorsal appendices; petals ca 4 by 2 mm, glabrous. Fruits: pedicels 10–15 mm long; spherical, 20–21 by 21–22 mm, densely pubescent, brownish, hardly sulcate or carinate. description: Tree up to 35 m high; branchlets faintly puberulous, glabrescent. description: Shrub or small tree, 3–4 m high; young. shoots glabrous, armed with stiff prickles up to 2–3 cm, sometimes reddish. Leaves bipinnate with a short common petiole. ending with a spine and 2–4 pinnae; raehis broad, flattened arid ridged, “phylloclade like”, with numerous, very small, obovate leaflets, subopposite to alternate, 2–5 by 1 mm. Stipules 2, forming short spines. Flowers in axillary, glabrous racemes up to 20 cm. Bracts minute, caducous. Pedicels filiform, up to 15 mm. Buds ovoid, glabbrous. Receptacle flattened, very short. Sepals ovate-oblong, glabrous, reflexed, 5–7 mm long. Petals golden yellow with hairy claw, 12–14 mm long; the median one with 6 mm long claw and suborbicular lamina, the lateral ones with shorter claw and rhomboidal lamina. Stamens nearly equal, filaments hairy below the middle, widened towards base; anthers elliptic, 1.5 mm long, opening lengthwise. Ovary hairy, subsessile; style glabrous; stigma indistinct; ovules 6–15. Pods narrow, cylindric 5–15 by 0.5–0.7 cm, glabrous, yellowish, with 6 or more seeds. Seeds oblong, 10 by 4 mm.

description: Perennial herbs; roots thickened, fusiform; stems stout, erect, 20–80 cm, simple or with many lax branches, terete, subdensely lanate. description: Branches light green, slender, tortuous, slightly flattened and ridged, covered in a dense, villous tomentum, short side shoots arranged spirally, curving upwards. description: Herb, 15–30 cm tall, lower part of the stem fleshy and prostrate. description: Liana to 30 m high, to 11 cm in diam. Bark greyish-brown, shallowly and irregularly longitudinally fissured. Ovary broadly ovoid-globose, faintly 3-grooved, ca 0.8 mm long, densely brown hairy (hairs stellate, but arms long and patent); style glabrous, 1.5–2 mm long; stigma minute, faintly 3-lobed, papillate. description: Vine, monoecious; stem twining, becoming woody. Stipules 1.2–2 by 0.5–0.8 mm. Inflorescences racemes, terminal appearing, leaf-opposed or sometimes on short shoots, or rarely axillary, 1.5–5 cm long, bisexual with a single pistillate flower at the basal node, staminate flowers one or rarely two per node, flowers subtended by a bract and 2 very small bracteoles, staminate bracts narrowly triangular, 0.5–1 mm long. Staminate flowers 1.5–2.3 mm in diam. when open, very sparsely pubescent to glabrescent; pedicel 1.3–2.5 mm long; sepals 4, ovate or elliptic, ca 1 by 0.6 mm, apex acute; disc absent; androecium 0.4–0.6 by 0.6–0.8 mm; stamens 8–14 on small globose or convex receptacle; filaments conical, <0.1 mm long. Pistillate flowers sparsely pubescent to glabrescent; pedicel 1.5–9 mm long, elongating to 2–5 cm in fruit; sepals narrowly triangular or elliptic, 1.2–2.2 by 0.5–1 mm; ovary –2.5 mm in diam., 4-winged, wings rounded, laterally compressed, 0.5–2 mm long, elongating to 13 mm in immature fruit; styles completely connate into a depressed-globose column, 0.5–0.7 by 0.8–1.1 mm, glabrous, with cross-shaped stigmatic surface. description: Erect shrub 1–5 m. Twigs, shortly hairy, glabrescent. Leaves ovate to elliptic to slightly obovate, apex acuminate, base cuneate to rounded, midrib slightly sunken on upper surface, hairy, lamina glabrous to sparsely appressed hairy, especially on veins and towards margin, 5–13 (rarely to 18) by 1.5–8.5 cm; petiole 5–10 mm. Inflorescence terminal or axillary, with 10–60 flowers, unbranched, rather slender and lax, erect to pendulous, but never reflexed at base, shortly hairy, to 20 cm; bracts caducous, ovate-caudate, up to 2.8 mm. Flowers yellow, 14–19 mm, pedicel 4–5 mm. Outer sepals sparsely hairy, ciliate, unequal, the two lower oblong to ovate 3.5–4.5 mm, the upper markedly saccate at the base, 6–8 mm. Alae obovate, cucullate, minutely ciliate, 11–14 mm. Upper petals glabrous or slightly hairy at base, 11–14 mm, free parts oblong 5–6 mm. Keel 12–16 mm, appendage finely divided with more or less connate lobes, 1.7–2.3 mm. Stamens 11–14 mm. Disk annular, 0.7 mm. Ovary oblong to orbicular, winged, glabrous or ciliate, 2.0–2.2 by 1.6–2.2 mm; style 9–11 mm. Capsule green, more or less purple-tinged, oblong, more or less two lobed, glabrous, with prominent concentric ridges, 9–11 by 11–15 mm, wing ribbed, up to 4 mm. Seeds spheroid, glabrous, 4.0–4.5 by 5.0 mm; aril bright orange, helmet-shaped and apically projecting and covering up to half the seed, 2–5 mm.

description: Erect dichotomously or trichotomously branched herb, 10–30 cm. Stem ridged, glabrous. Inflorescence axillary or terminal, unbranched, glabrous, with 20–100 flowers, to 15 cm; bracts linear, soon caducous, 0.7 mm. Flowers yellow, 3.0–3.5 mm; pedicel 0.5 mm. Outer sepals almost equal, broadly ovate, glabrous or sparsely ciliate at apex, 1.0–1.2 mm. Alae obovate, to oblong or elliptic and shortly stalked, 3.0–3.2 mm. Upper petals spathulate, more or less sinuate, 3.0–3.5 mm, free parts 1.5–1.8 mm. Keel 3.0–3.5 mm, appendage 2-lobed, adnate to keel, 1 mm. Stamens equally connate, ca 2.6 mm. Capsule obcordate, with prominent concentric ridges, 2.2–3.3 by 2.6–3.6 mm, wing up to 0.6 mm wide, markedly ribbed. Seeds ellipsoid, 1.2–1.5 mm, dark grey or black, tuberculate, glabrous, with shiny black strophiole, 0.2 mm by 0.6 mm. Aril apically projecting, shortly lobed, to 0.5 mm.

description: Erect sometimes woody herb 15–60 cm. Stems terete, indumentum of short curved and long patent hairs, especially on young parts. Leaves alternate to subopposite, elliptic to narrowly ovate or obovate, apex mucronate, acute to rounded or occasionally retuse, base cuneate to rounded or scarcely cordate, midrib flat or prominent above, margin inrolled, glabrous or ciliate, lamina sparsely to rather densely appressed hairy, glaucous below, 0.9–7.0 by 0.6–2.4 cm, length:width ratio 2–12; petiole with short curved hairs, 1.0-2.0 mm. Inflorescence supra-axillary, with 3–20 flowers, dense, unbranched, glabrescent or with short curved or long patent hairs, 0.5–3.0 cm; bracts very early caducous, broadly ovate or triangular, ciliate, 0.5–0.7 mm. Flowers greenish, white or pink, 3.5–4.5 mm; pedicel 0.5–1.5 mm. Outer sepals unequal, ovate, acuminate, ciliate, the two lower 1.4–2.1 mm, the upper 1.9–2.8 mm. Alae ovate or oblong, oblique, apex acuminate, margin ciliate, shortly hairy, or rarely with long, straight hairs, 4.2–7.0 by 1.1–2.3 mm. Upper petals spathulate or obtriangular, hairy in lower half, 3.2–5.0 mm, free parts 2.7–4.0 mm. Keel more or less auriculate, 4.7–5.5 mm, appendage of two more or less connate brush-like bundles, 2.0–2.5 mm. Stamens irregularly connate to about half-way, 4.4–6.0 mm. Disk absent. Ovary orbicular, densely long ciliate along margin towards apex, 0.7–1.0 by 0.8–1.0 mm; style curved, strongly reflexed apically, 3.5–5.5 mm. Capsule with persistent calyx, wider than long, orbicular or rectangular, emarginate, ciliate, sparsely short hairy and rarely with long straight hairs, 3.2–4.4 by 3.7–4.7 mm. Seeds ovoid to almost globular, black with short, white hairs, 2.1–3.3 by 1.4–2.1 mm; aril irregularly 3-lobed, the lobes 0.5–1.7 mm long.

description: Suffruticose perennial to 20 cm. Stems terete, with indumentum of short, curved and at least occasional long, spreading hairs. description: Herb, tall, erect and little-branched or short and bushy, 10–30 cm; densely hairy throughout, with short curved and longer spreading hairs. Stems terete. description: Tap-rooted shrub to 15 cm, strongly branched from base. Stems with a dense indumentum of short, curled hairs. Leaves elliptic or oblong towards apex, ovate or orbicular at base, apex acute or rounded, mucronate or shortly apiculate, base cuneate or obtuse, margin inrolled, secondary and sometimes tertiary venation prominent on upper surface, sparse indumentum of minute, curved hairs on both surfaces, glaucous below, 0.6–2.5 by 0.3–1.6 mm; petiole densely hairy, ca 0.5 mm in basal leaves, 1.0 mm in upper leaves. Inflorescence terminal or supra-axillary, unbranched, with a dense indumentum, 8–15 flowers, 1–3 cm; bracts soon caducous, ovate, ciliate, hairy, 0.7–0.5 mm. Flowers pink, violet or purple, 4–5.5 mm; pedicel 1–3 mm. Ovary glabrous, oblong or obovate, 0.8–1.2 by 0.6 mm; style almost straight, 2–2.4 mm; the stigmas knob-like, one apical, the other lateral, 0.5–1 mm apart. description: Shrub, 2–4 m tall, sometimes scrambling, with thin sharply 4-angled branchlets, subglabrous, leaf nodes with distinct interpetiolar lines. description: Tree or large shrub to 9 m, Outer bark, smooth light grey-green-brown, soon peeling or flaking, inner bark light-brown, twigs sharply 4-angled, often pubescent, glandular. description:
Usually growing in open areas, up to 2000 m alt., common throughout Thailand, the two varieties sometimes growing side by side; sometimes forming a big thicket at edge of forest, or recent clearing in sunny places. This is one of the acidiphilous plants and common in pine forest but rather rare in limestone areas. The rhizomes run deeply underground, and can produce but after fire. This species as a whole distributed throughout the temperate and tropical regions and is usually known as bracken. The young leaves are edible, and starch is available from rhizome.

Among twelve varieties recognized by Tryon, two are known in Thailand.

description: Rhizome short, creeping or ascending, 7–10 mm diam., bearing close fronds, densely scaly at apex; scales linear, rather stiff, up to 5 mm long, dark brown to nearly black with paler edge, entire. Stipe dark brown and scaly at base, stramineous, castaneous above, puberulous or glabrescent, 50–80 cm long. Lamina oblong, imparipinnate, up to 60 by 30 cm; rachis stramineous or castaneous beneath, winged in upper part, puberulous; lateral pinnae 3–7 pairs, never branching, sessile or shortly stalked in lower ones, adnate or decurrent downwards in upper ones, falcate, gradually narrowing towards cuneate base, caudate with long tail at apex, margin subentire or minutely serrate at apical portion, up to 30 cm or more long, 3 cm broad, terminal pinnae like the lower lateral pinnae but straight, chartaceous, veins close, visible on both surfaces. Sori continuous along the margin of pinnae except at base and towards apex; indusia thin but firm, pale brown.

description: Tree, up to 45 m high, 300 cm girth, always with straight bole; bark grey, smooth, and flaking near base, lenticellate; twigs stout, pubescent, with prominently raised, large leaf scars. Leaves ovate or cordate, 5–17 x 8–12 cm, subcoriaceous, apex acute to acuminate, base cordate, with soft hairs on lower surface 6 nerves at base, nerves and scalariform veins prominent on lower surface. Petiole 6–9 cm., glabrescent. Inflorescences terminal and axillary in upper leaf scars, erect, ca 9 cm long. Buds ellipsoid, 10 x 7 mm, glabrescent except along edge of calyx lobes. Sepals 5, united ⅔ at base, narrowly funnel-shaped, 3-3.5 cm, hairy along margin. Male flowers with (8–)10 stamens. Fruit a large boat-shaped follicle with a hook or spur, membranous, 5–8 x 1.5–2 cm. Seed 1–2, at base of follicle, wingless.

description: Tree, 15–30 m high, usually with straight bole, buttressed; bark greyish, smooth; young twigs slender and terete with prominently raised leaf scars, hairy then glabrescent. Flower buds oblong, ca 2 x 0.7 cm, surrounded by 3 persisting laciniate and hairy, 2–3 x 1–1.5 cm bracts. Sepals 5, lanceolate, 5–6 x 0.5 cm, hairy on both surfaces. description: Tree, up to 30 m high, 200 cm girth; buttressed; usually straight bole; bark grey, shallowly fissured; twigs slender with prominently raised leaf scars, young parts with golden stellate hairs. Leaves broadly ovate, 10–30 x 10–22 cm, apex acute to broady acute, margin entire, base cordate or truncate, coriaceous with green upper surface, paler on lower surface, sparsely hairy then glabrescent; (3–)5(–7) nerves at base, scalariform veins prominent on lower surface. Petiole 4-20 cm long, usually swollen at both ends. Inflorescences in axils of upper leaf scars and the end of twigs, up to 20 cm long. Buds ovate-oblong, 1.5–2 x 0.6–1 cm, hairy. Bracteoles caducous. Sepals 5, linear-lanceolate, ca 20 x 5 mm, hairy on both surfaces. Stamens 20, in 5 groups, on a staminal column around a sterile ovary; anthers sessile. Carpels 5, free, hairy; locule with many ovules; staminodes as many as stamens; style short and curved outwards; stigma rounded. Fruits consisting of 5 follicles borne on a common stalk, each globose-ellipsoid, depressed on both sides, woody, pubescent, 8–9 x 5–6 cm and 4.5–5 cm thick. Seeds many, ovoid, ca 2 x 1.5 cm, with a terminal spathulate wing, 2.5–3 x 1.5 cm.

description: Small to big tree, up to 30 m high, up to 45 cm; bole straight with basally small buttresses. Leaves: petiole 1.9–4.3 cm long, especially apically pulvinate, round, subglabrous to hairy; blade elliptic to oblong, 11.3–24.5 by 3.7–7.8 cm, length/width ratio 3.1–5, chartaceous to coriaceous, base cuneate, margin entire, apex acuminate, sometimes round extrafloral nectaries on both surfaces, mainly in lower half of blade, lower surface often slightly hairy, venation distinct on both sides, nerves in 8–15 pairs, veins scalariform. Inflorescences axillary racemes or narrow panicles, up to 10.5 cm long, golden brownish tomentose; bracts triangular, 1.5–2 by 0.6–1 mm. Flowers greenish to yellow. Staminate flowers only known in bud; upper part pedicel ca 2.7 mm long, tomentose; sepals hairy, especially outside. Pistillate flowers subsessile to pedicel up to 3 mm; sepals 5 or 6, triangular to ovate, ca 2 by 1–1.3 mm, hairy; disc densely hairy; ovary (2)3(4)-locular; stigmas ca 1.5 mm long. Fruits globose or pyriform, dorsiventrally flattened and symmetric, 1.7–3 by 1.6–2.2 by 1.4–1.6 cm, brown tomentellous. Seeds ovoid, dorsiventrally compressed, ca 13 by 8 by 6 mm.

description: Tree, 7–20 m high, 60–100 cm girth. Terminal buds ovoid, ca 3 by 2 mm, pubescent then glabrescent. Leaves obovate, ovate, elliptic or ovate-oblong, 7–22 by 3–10 cm; base slightly cuneate to obtuse, oblique; apex obtuse or broadly acute; margins slightly serrate at apical one third, sometimes undulate; coriaceous, rigid, brittle when dry, sparsely pubescent or glaucous on the upper surface; densely yellow tomentose on the lower; midrib and nerves prominent on the lower surface; depressed on the upper; lateral nerves 9–12 pairs, straight then forking or anastomosing near margins, scalariform veins distinct on the lower surface; subdepressed on the upper. Petiole 1–2.5 cm, with sparse, blackish hairs. Male inflorescence 2–3 simple, tufted or few branched, pendulous catkins, axillary to leaves or upper leaf-scars, 5–10 cm long, tomentose; bracts and bracteoles, triangular, ca 2 by 1 mm, pubescent outside. Male flowers solitary or in 1–3–5-flowered cluster, perianth broadly campanulate, 6-lobed, lobes obovate, divided by ca ⅔, pubescent outside and towards apex inside; stamens 6, glabrous. Female inflorescence spike erect, axillary to leaves and upper leaf-scars, 3–5 cm long, tomentose, each spike with 5–10 free flowers, other characters as in male flowers; styles 3, connate; stigmata capitate. Acorns sessile, broadly ovoid, 1–2.5 by 1–2 cm (including cupule), on erect infructescence, 2–5 cm long, acorns free, 4–8 per infructescence. Cupule saucer-shaped, enclosing ⅓ to ½ of the nut, rim not dilated; wall comprising greyish hairs or scales, set in 5–6 rings or lamellae. Nut 1, conical, 2–2.5 by 1.8–2 cm, sometimes broader than long when mature, sparsely silky hairs, then glabrescent.

description: Tree, 10–40 m high, 100–200 cm girth. Twigs sparsely tomentose then glabrescent. Bark brown to blackish, lenticellate. Stipules linear, ca 0.5 cm long, tomentose on both surfaces. Leaves lanceolate or elliptic-lanceolate, 6–16 by 2–4 cm, always whorled at ends of twigs; base cuneate; apex acuminate to caudate; margins usually serrate in upper half or entire; subcoriaceous to chartaceous, glabrous except sparsely pubescent along midrib on the lower surface, dull green on the upper; pale on the lower surface; midrib and nerves fine, distinct on the lower surface; conspicuous on the upper; lateral nerves 10–14 pairs, scalariform veins hardly distinct. Petiole 0.5–1.5 cm, reddish tomentose near base. Male inflorescence a catkin, simple, tufted, pendulous, terminal or axillary to leaves or upper leaf-scars, 3–5 cm long, tomentose; bracts and bracteoles triangular to ovate, acute, ca 2 by 1 mm, pubescent outside, ciliate. Male flowers free or in 1–3-flowered cluster; perianth campanulate, 6-lobed, 1–1.5 mm long, lobes united by ⅓ to ½, tomentose on both sides; stamens 6, 2–2.5 cm long, hairy near base. Female inflorescence spike erect, terminal and axillary, 2–3 cm long, tomentose, each spike with 3–5 free flowers, other characters as in male flowers; styles 3–5, divergent, hairy; stigmata dilated. Acorns sessile, ovoid or ellipsoid, 2–3.5 by 1.4–1.7 cm (including cupule), on erect infructescence 2–5 cm long, usually 2 per infructescence. Cupule cup or dish-shaped, enclosing to ⅓ of the nut, rim not dilated; wall comprising tomentose scales, set in 7–9 rings or lamellae. Nut 1, ovoid or conical, 1.5–2.5 by 1–1.5 cm; scar basal , ca 0.6 cm in diam.

description: Tree, 4–25 m high, 60–160 cm girth. Twigs reddish-brown hairy, then glabrescent. Bark greyish; inner bark reddish-brown or brown, 1–4 cm thick. Stipules linear, 4–6 by 0.2 mm, densely tomentose. Leaves obovate, oblong or elliptic, 5–18 by 2–6 cm, usually whorled at ends of twigs; base cuneate; apex acute or obtuse, shortly mucronate, rarely acuminate; margins serrate in the upper half or entire; coriaceous or subcoriaceous, densely tomentose then glabrescent on the upper surface; glaucous on the lower; midrib and nerves prominent and sparsely pubescent on the lower surface; subdepressed on the upper; lateral nerves 8–12 pairs, curved but not anastomosing, scalariform veins hardly distinct. Petiole 1.5–2.5 cm, tomentose then glabrescent. Male inflorescence a catkin, simple or in a tuft of 2–3, pendulous, axillary to leaves or upper leaf scars, or terminal, 1–7 cm long, tomentose; bracts and bracteoles narrowly lanceolate, ca 2 by 0.5 mm, pubescent outside. Male flowers free. Perianth 6–8) lobed, campanulate, lobes obovate, ca 2 by 1 mm, divided to or near the base, but linked by cilia; stamens 8, ca 1 mm long, glabrous. Female inflorescence spike erect, axillary, 1–2.5 cm long, tomentose. Female flowers simple, other characters as in male flowers, styles (4)–5 divergent, pubescent; stigmata capitate, decurved. Acorns ovoid, 2.5–3 by 2.5–4 cm (including cupule), fruit-stalk ca 0.5 cm long, on erect infructescence 2–3 cm long, each infructescence usually with one acorn. Cupule cup or dish-shaped, enclosing half of the nut (ca ⅔ when young), rim always dilated when mature; wall comprising silky scales, set in 8–12 rings or lamellae. Nut 1, ovoid, 2–3 by 1.8–3 cm, indumentum rusty then glabrous except around the umbo.

description: Tree, 15–35 m high, 100–300 cm girth, usually with buttresses to 5 m high. Budsovoid, ca 5 by 3 mm; bracts ovate, acute, hairy outside. Twigs tomentose then glabrescent, lenticellate. Bark dark brown, slightly fissured; inner bark orange or reddish with brown stripes. Stipules linear, tomentose outside, ciliate. Leaves obovate, oblong or broadly elliptic, 9–30 by 4–10.5 cm, usually in whorls of 3–4 leaves at ends of twigs; base cuneate, rarely obtuse; apex acuminate, acute to shortly cuspidate; margins serrate in apical half to one third, sometimes entire; chartaceous to subcoriaceous, glabrous and glossy green on the upper surface; pubescent then glabrescent except midrib on the lower; midrib and nerves prominent on the lower surface; subdepressed on the upper; lateral nerves 12–16 pair, arched but not anastomosing, ending at tips of marginal serrations, scalariform veins fine, distinct on the lower surface. Petiole 1–3 cm, pubescent then glabrescent. Male inflorescence a catkin, simple, or in a tuft of 2–3, pendulous, 5–15 cm long, axillary to leaves or upper leaf-scars, tomentose; bracts and bracteoles narrowly lanceolate, ca 3 by 1 mm, tomentose outside, ciliate. Male flowers solitary or in 1–3–5-flowered cluster; perianth broadly campanulate, 3–4 mm long, lobes 6, divided by ca ⅔, pubescent outside; stamens 6–(10–12), 6–8 mm long, pubescent at anthers and base of filaments. Female inflorescence spike erect, axillary, 1–2 cm long, tomentose, each spike with 2–3 free flowers, other characters as in male flowers; styles (3) 4–5, divergent; stigmata capitate. Acorns sessile, ovoid and strongly depressed at both ends, 1.5–2.5 by 3–4 cm (including cupule), on stout infructescence, 1-2 cm long, acorns free, usually one per infructescence. Cupule saucer shaped, enclosing ⅔ to ⅘ of the nut, rim not dilated; wall comprising tomentose or rusty scales, the irregular apex of scales reflexed not fused with wall of cupule, set in 5–7 rings or lamellae. Nut 1, broadly ovoid to more or less flattened, 1.5–2 by 3–3.5 cm, apex slightly convex.

description: Tree, to 12 m high. Budsovoid, ca 2 by 1.5 mm, glabrous. Twigs glabrous, blackish when dry. Bark blackish with grey patches at intervals, longitudinally furrowed; sapwood yellowish-white. Leaves oblong-lanceolate, 8–19 by 3–5 cm; base obtuse or cuneate, minutely oblique; apex caudate or acuminate; margins serrate on apical one third; chartaceous, glabrous, glossy green on the upper surface; pale on the lower; midrib and nerves prominent on the lower surface; subdepressed on the upper; lateral nerves 7–11 pairs, arched but not anastomosing, scalariform veins hardly distinct. Petiole 1.5–2 cm, glabrous, blackish when dry. Male and female inflorescences not seen. Acorns obconical or ovoid, 2–2.5 by 1.5–2 cm (including cupule), on erect and woody infructescence, 3–10 cm long, acorns single and in clusters of 3–4 at intervals, 3–10 in total per infructescence. Cupule obconical, enclosing ½ of the nut (enclosed completely, except the umbo when young), rim not dilated; wall comprising grey scales, set in 5–7 rings or lamellae. Nut 1, conical or ovoid, 1.5–1.8 by 1.2–1.4 cm, glossy reddish-brown, except around umbo; scar basal, ca 1 cm in diam.

description: Tree, 4–8 m high, 30–50 cm girth. Terminal buds ovoid, ca 3 by 2 mm; bracts linear, 3–5 mm long, pubescent outside. Twigs tomentose then glabrescent. Stipules linear, ca 1 cm long, glabrous, not early caducous. Leaves ovate-elliptic, 3–7.5 by 2.2–4.5 cm; base broadly obtuse or cordate; apex obtuse or broadly acute; margins entire; coriaceous, glabrous except along midrib on the upper surface; pubescent then glabrescent on the lower; midrib and nerves raised on the lower surface; depressed on the upper; lateral nerves 8–12 pairs, anastomosing near margins; reticulate veins inconspicuous on the lower surface. Petiole 2–4 mm, pubescent then glabrescent. Male inflorescence a catkin, usually tufted, pendulous, axillary, upper leaf scars, or terminal, 5–10 cm long, tomentose; bracts and bracteoles triangular or ovate, pubescent outside, ciliate. Male flowers free or in 1–3-flowered cluster; perianth 4–6-lobed, lobes united to half, pubescent outside, ciliate; stamens 4–6–7, 1.5–2 mm long, hairy near base. Female inflorescence spike erect, short, axillary. Female flowers 2–4 in each spike; styles 3, connate; stigmata elongate, decurved. Acorns ovoid or elliptic, 1.5–2 by 2–2.5 cm (including cupule), fruit stalk 3–5 mm long, on erect infructescence 1.5–2 cm long, each infructescence with (1) 2 acorns. Cupule cup or saucer-shaped, enclosing ½ of the nut (more or less obovoid and enclosed completely, except the umbo when young); wall comprising alternate, thin, pubescent scales throughout. Nut 1, globose or ovoid, 1.5–2 by 1.5–1.7 cm, glabrous and more or less wrinkled.

description: Tree, 10–40 m high, 85–200 cm girth. Twig tomentose then glabrescent. Leaves oblong, lanceolate or elliptic-oblong, 8–13 by 2–4 cm; base cuneate or obtuse; apex acuminate; margins slightly serrate; subcoriaceous or chartaceous, glabrous and dull green on the upper surface; pubescent then glabrescent on the lower except along midrib; midrib and nerves prominent on the lower surface; depressed on the upper; lateral nerves 9–14 pairs, scalariform veins hardly distinct. Petiole 1–2 cm, densely pubescent then glabrescent. description: The main value is in the oil of the seeds (castor oil, wonder oil), but the plants also have a high horticultural value. The plant is cultivated in plantations and improvement schemes are carried out to increase its oil content. The oil from the seeds is used in the industry for a large variety of products and in medicine. It is a versatile fixed oil, which means that it can be altered chemically. It can be changed into sebacic acid which is used to manufacture plastics and synthetic, durable fibres. The oil can also be changed into a drying oil for varnishes, enamels, and paints (softer, more elastic, and better resistant against yellowing than linseed or tung oil = Vernicia). Other uses are in linoleum, leather, printing ink, lithographic varnishes, a special kind of soap, lubricants, and sticky fly paper. When sulfonated it is used as a red dye (Turkey red oil). Medicinally it is mainly a purgative due to the fact that lipases change triricinolein (main component of castor oil) into glycerin and rininoleic acid; the latter irritates the intestines. The residual oil cake is poisonous and only buffaloes seem able to eat it, however, the cake is an excellent fertiliser. Other uses are also mainly medicinal. The leaves and stem are used by the Dusun Kinabatangan (Borneo, Sabah) as a remedy against stings and bites of insects and animals. Sap from the heated petioles and young branches is used as ear drops (Indonesia). In the Philippines pounded leaves are applied as a poultice to the breast to stimulate milk secretion, boiled pounded leaves may be used to wash ulcers and pounded roasted seeds mixed with oil can be applied over affected skin areas and is also good for haemorrhoids; variations exist in other countries, but especially the leaves seem to act against all kinds of skin diseases. The seeds are eaten cooked in Irian Jaya (New Guinea; n.b. uncooked seeds are toxic due to the phytotoxin ricin) or burned and used to paint hair or head black (Papua New Guinea) (Mainly after Araéez, 1980).

description: Large spreading tree up to ca 20 m high; branchlets puberulous to tomentose. Perianth tube 6–8 cm long; segments 10 in two series, broad-triangular, 6–8 cm long, 4–6 cm wide, obtuse, red with yellow speckles; at their insertion the tube is partly closed by a corona; upper surface of corona covered with numerous filiform processes, in the central part an aperture 1–2 cm wide; below the aperture about 20 longitudinal ridges are found in the blood-coloured throat; from the base of the tube appears a columnar structure much flattened and widened in its top part. Anthers 20, sessile on the column immediately below the widened part, 2-celled, opening with a pore. In the female flower the column is considerably thicker; here 20 small outgrowths are found at the same position as the anthers; they have been interpreted as rudimentary anthers or stigmatoid tissue respectively. Position of stigmatoid tissue not exactly known. Ovary inferior with numerous irregular cavities which on their internal walls carry innumerable ovules.

description: Terrestrial herb, 2–40 cm tall, with a perennial rhizome and annual stems, leaves sometimes spotted white, stem fleshy, occasionally corky, quadrangular to winged, sometimes rooting at the nodes, glabrous. Leaves of a pair sometimes slightly unequal in size, elliptic, larger ones (1.7–)3.5–9(–13.3) x 0.8–6 cm, smaller ones 1.2–6 x 0.6–5 cm, base attenuate to broadly rounded, apex acuminate or acute, margin entire or serrulate, lamina with 1(–2) pair(s) of lateral primary veins, glabrous or with a few hairs and minute sessile glands, petioles 0.4–4(–6) cm long. Inflorescences terminal or axillary few-flowered fascicles, peduncle 1–2(–8) cm long. Flowers 4-merous, bracts leaf-like, pedicels 1–12(–20) mm long. Hypanthium campanulate, usually 4-winged, 1.4–2.5(–4) mm long. Petals broadly obovate, 5–13 mm long, apiculate, glabrous, pink. Stamens 8, isomorphic, anthers 1–2 mm long, yellow, connective with a dorsal spur 0.6–1.2 mm long (Fig. 402C). Ovary 4-locular, fully united with the hypanthium for half its length, apically deeply depressed and with a crown of 4 thick lobes, glabrous or with minute sessile glands. Capsules quadrangular, 4–7 mm long, crowned by a tetrapterous disk; calyx lobes persistent and forming a 2–5 mm broad protruding fringe (Fig. 42D & E).

description: Woody herb, up to 1 m high, glabrous, asperities absent; young branches with 2 ribs, older ones faintly 4. Stipules triangular on young branches, large and falcate on older ones, 0.7–3 by 0.3–2 mm. Leaves: petiole 1–1.2 mm long, pulvinate; blade (elliptic to) obovate, 2—3.2 by 0.4–2 cm, length/width ratio 1.3–2, papery, base slightly oblique to truncate to cuneate, margin flat to revolute, apex round to acute, mucronulate, whitish below, nerves rather distinct, 3–6. Flowers axillary single or few fascicled with both sexes, deep maroon. Staminate flowers 2–3.2 mm in diam.; pedicel 1.7–4 mm long; calyx flat, lobes 0.5–1.1 by 0.6–1.1 mm, deeply divided up to scales, apices acute, scales as broad or slightly broader than lobes, quite high; stamens: androphore ca 0.2 mm high, anthers ca 0.2 by 0.2 mm. Pistillate flowers 3.5–5 mm in diam.; pedicel 1.2–2 mm long; calyx lobes spade-like, smaller ones 1.2–2 by 1.3–2.6 mm, larger ones 1.8–2 by 1.4–3 mm; ovary obpyramidal, 0.7–0.6 by 1.2–1.7 mm; stigmas horizontal, up to 1 mm long, split till halfway. Fruits subglobose, ca 4.5 by 4 mm, with small apical rim around persistent stigmas; column ca 2.8 mm long, tapering towards apex. Seeds triangular in section, ca 3.8 by 2 by 2 mm.

description: Small shrub (to tree), up to 1(–8) m high, glabrous, with woody rootstock; stems without asperities, with 4 shallow ribs. Stipules triangular, often eared basally, 1.2–2.6 by 0.9–1.6 mm. description: Shrublet with ascending habit, up to 0.5 m high, glabrous, smooth; young branches with 4 distinct ribs; bark not corky, nor fissured. description: Shrub to small tree, up to 3 m high, glabrous; young branches with 2 ridges, in between ridges often (faint) asperities. Stipules triangular, 2.5–4.2 by 0.3–1.2 mm. Flowers axillary, single or in small fascicles, seldom on short, up to 5 mm long racemes, greenish to pale yellowish-green. Staminate flowers 4–6.5 mm in diam.; pedicel 6.5–15 mm long; calyx flat, not to slightly lobed, circular, lobes 0.5–0.8 by 1.2–2.5 mm, scales present; stamens: androphore 0.1–0.4 mm long, anthers 0.4–0.7 by ca 0.4 mm. Pistillate flowers 4–8 mm in diam.; pedicel 3.8–13 mm long; calyx lobes almost free, ovate to obovate, often thick, smaller ones 2–3.5 by 1–3.1 mm, larger ones 2.5–5 by 1.3–2.7 mm; ovary bell-shaped, 1–1.5 by 1–1.9 mm; stigmas 1–2 mm long, apically split, slender, horizontal, coiling in more than full circle. Fruits ovoid to globose, 7–8 by 9–11 mm, thin-walled, wall parts remaining stuck to base after dehiscence, spreading star-like, green; column absent. description: Small, deciduous tree to about 15 m tall, young shoots pubescent. Leaves 20-30 cm long, with 5–7 leaflets, leaflets ovate to lanceolate or elliptic-oblong, (7–)8–11(–15) cm long, (2.5–)4–5(–9) cm broad; base narrowed, attenuate onto the petiolule to rounded; apex acute to somewhat acuminate; softly pubescent below, scattered pubescent above or glabrous; margins entire; (6–)7 primary veins on each side of the midrib, raised below, immersed above, venation reticulate; petioles 6–10 cm long, swollen at the base, pubescent, at least when young, lateral petiolules 5–15 mm long, articulated with the rachis, terminal petiolules 15–40 mm long. Inflorescence terminal, cymose-paniculate, corymbose, 6–10(–15) cm long, many-flowered, glabrous or slightly pubescent; bracts linear-lanceolate, early caducous; pedicels 1–5 mm long. Calyx campanulate, puberulent; tube 2–3 mm long, accrescent in fruit; lobes obscure. Corolla salver-shaped; tube 8–11 mm long; lobes 6–7, 4–6 mm long, 4 mm broad, obovate to somewhat obcuneate, rounded to slightly emarginate, upper surface covered with brown, swollen hairs. Anthers 2 mm long; filaments very short; connective not developed into an appendage. Ovary 1 mm tall; style 5 or 10 mm long, slightly bilobed, stigma capitate, 0.75 mm long. Capsule hard, woody, obpyriform, 5–6 cm long, 3–3.5 cm diameter; seeds 3–4 cm long, winged, embryo basal on one side.

description: Widely branched plant, up to 2.5 m high. Sheath 5.3–12.5 cm long; pulvinus 0.4–1.0 cm long, green, glabrous; lamina elliptic to broadly elliptic 5.8–14.0 by 2.8–6.7 cm, glabrous, acute at the apex, broadly cuneate at the base, dark green above, pale below. Flowers white, 4.9–5.0 cm long; sepals 3, one free almost to the base, 10.0–10.2 mm long, the others joined to the staminodal tube, narrow, ca 5.0 by 0.6 mm, white; petal lobes narrowly oblong, rounded to acute at apex, 2.6–3.0 cm long, white; staminodal tube ca 2.6 cm long; outer staminodes 2, their petaloid lobes large, subequal, obovate, 1.6–2.0 by 1.3–1.8 cm, white; cucullate staminode with free part of ca 6.3 by 2.5 mm, pale yellow at the tip, appendage ca 2.5 mm long; callose staminode bilobed, with free part of ca 1.2 by 0.7 cm, white; fertile stamen ca 2.4 mm long, petaloid appendage spathulate, ca 3.2 by 1.8 mm; style with free part of ca 6.8 mm long; ovary ca 1.2 mm long, sparsely hairy. description: Stout perennial herb, 5–10(–15) m long, stem 2–10 mm diam., with tuber-like rootstock; almost glabrous. Leaves: blade usually 5-angular or shallowly lobed, subcircular in outline, 10–20 cm diam., lobes acute, margin finely sparsely dentate, finely scabrous especially on upper surface, distinctly reticulately veined; petiole 5–15 cm long. Male racemes 8–30 cm long, 10–30-flowered, with flowers 2(–6) subfasciculate. Male flowers: pedicel 1–6 mm long; receptacle-tube ca 5 mm wide; sepals oblong-linear, 5–7 mm long; petals subglabrous, 10–17 mm long; staminal column 1–2 mm long, spreading free parts ca 1 mm long; anthers ca 2 mm diam. Female flowers: ovary ca 5 mm long, glabrous or hairy; style 3–4 mm long; stigma ca 3 mm diam., papillose. Fruit 7–15(–20) cm long, often with irregular surface, low-warted or irregularly sulcate, smooth or (soft) spiny, green or whitish; later on the embryo germinating in the seed and emerging at apex of fruit; fruiting pedicel 2–3 cm long. Seed 5–10 cm long.

description: The timber is used for canoes and is supposed to be suitable for indoor work. Leaves have been applied to cure fever and gonorrhoea (Burkill, 1935). Fruits and leaves are boiled together with clothes as black dye, but also yellowish-green colours can be obtained from it (e.g., in lower Thailand: Burkill, 1935). The green fruits are used as a fish poison, e.g., by the Dusun (Borneo). The “juice of the fruits” is applied by Kinomeri (Papua New Guinea) to cure toothache. The seeds contain a drying oil (Burkill, 1935) and can be eaten, whereas the fruit wall as well as other parts of the plant contains toxic latex, also known as fish poison (Dragendorff, 1898). In view of the variety of uses, the species is considered as an interesting crop species for places too wet for other crops (Purwaningsih, 1991).

description: Climber, 2 to 10 m long, with one annual shoot from a subterraneous perennial tuber ca 10 cm diam.; stem 5-angular, 2–3 mm thick. Tendrils finely hairy. description: Large climber; stems 1–8 m long, terete or obtusely angular, internodes 8–25 cm long, 3–12 mm thick, smooth or with sparse divergent to recurved prickles 2–3 mm long; branches 25–50 cm long, straightish, internodes 2–10 cm long, 1–3 mm thick, smooth, or sometimes loosely prickly. Leaves highly variable in form and size; blades basically ovate to ovate-oval, sometimes elliptic or narrowly so, or ovate-elliptic, rarely broadly elliptic, 7–18 cm long, 2.5–13 cm wide, the base subabruptly contracted or rounded, at times subacute, or rarely shallowly emarginate, gradually or subabruptly tapering from below the middle to acute apex, coriaceous, more or less glaucous; costas 5 or 7 including a weak marginal pair, the median 3 connate for 5–13 mm j above base, thick and highly raised on lower surface, shallowly impressed on upper surface, lateral veinlets patent, straightish or incurved, reticulations rather not elongate, prominent on lower surface; petioles 1.5–4(–6) cm long, 3-angular with subacute abaxial angle, sheathing for 0.8–4 cm; wings broadly ovate, 1.5–2.5 cm long, 0.7–1.2 cm wide, gradually tapering above to subacute apex, the cordate base deeply clasping the node; wings of stem leaves much larger, up to 6 cm long and 2.7 cm wide; tendrils 7–20 cm long. Inflorescences borne on lower and middle part of branches, mostly 1- to 3-umbellate, but in staminate ones occasionally up to 15-umbellate with some umbels 2- to 4-nate at 4 to 6 nodes; common axis usually 1–3 cm long, rarely up to 15 cm long in staminate inflorescences; prophylls ovate, acute, 0.8–1 cm long; peduncles 2–5 cm long, rigid. Umbels of both sexes 3–5 cm across, densely 20- to 70-flower-ed: receptacles ellipsoid, 4–5 mm by 3–4 mm; rays 7–15 mm long, slender. Staminate perianth 5.5–6.2 mm long, strongly recurved at anthesis; outer tepals oblong, obtuse, 1–1.2 mm wide, inner ones linear 0.3 mm wide; filaments 6 mm long; anthers elliptic-oblong, 1.2 mm long, white. Pistillate perianth patent at anthesis, 4–5 mm long; tepals lance-ovate, gradually narrowed to subacute apex, outer ones 1.2 mm wide, inner ones 0.5 mm wide; ovary ellipsoid, 2.2–2.5 mm long, 1 mm across, tapering at both ends; stigmas erect, 1–1.25 mm long; staminodes 3, needle-like, 1.8–2.1 mm long. Berries 1–1.2 cm in diameter, maturing red, 1- or 2-seeded; seeds obovate-orbicular, thickly lenticular, ca 5 mm long and as wide, deep red.

description: Presumably a herbaceous climber, the whole plant becoming blackishwhen dry; stems as a rule unbranched, slender, terete, rigid, smooth, glabrous, somewhat shiny, internodes 4–11 cm long, 1.5–2.7 mm thick. Leaves spaced; blades broadly ovate to broadly ovate-elliptic, 8–14 cm long, 6–8 cm wide, rounded to or truncate or shallowly emarginate at base, narowed from ⅓ above the base to the rather suddenly acute or acuminate apex, herbaceous to thinly coriaceous, strongly glaucous and white-powdery beneath; costas 5 or 7 including a weak marginal pair, all separate from the base, equally spaced, the main 3 median costas markedly elevated on lower surface, lateral veinlets distinct, ascending, irregularly divided forming fine and not elongate reticulations, costas and veinlets fine but conspicuous on upper surface; petioles 25–35 mm long, not articulate, somewhat laterally compressed with acute edges; sheath 1–1.3 cm long, the wings 1–1.5 mm wide with membranous pale margins, minutely or hardly auriculate at apex; tendrils up to 10 cm long, slender. Umbels of both sexes 3–6 cm in diameter, densely 40- to 70-flowered; peduncles slender, wiry, 3–6 cm long; receptacles 3–4 mm across; bracteoles ca 1 mm long, ovate-deltoid, pale; umbel-rays filiform, 1–2 cm long. Staminate perianth 4.5–5 mm long and obovate-oblong in mature buds; tepals reflexed from base at anthesis, outer 3 oblanceolate, obtuse, 4.7–5 mm long, 1.5 mm wide, inner 3 oblanceolate-oblong, obtuse, 4–4.5 mm long, 1–1.2 mm wide. Stamens 6, obliquely ascending; filaments 2–3.5 mm long; anthers clavate, white, 1.5–1.7 mm long. Pistillate flowers not seen. Immature berries subglobose.

description: Densely branched shrub; stems 80–150 cm tall, 2–4 mm thick at middle, bearing a few remote scales below; branches patent, straight, internodes 7–15 mm long, ca 1 mm thick, not or very rarely sparsely aculeate with short prickles ca 1 mm long, 4-angled with acute wing-like edges. Leaves 2-ranked, almost sessile with the base decurrent to the angles of branches; blades rhombic-ovate or broadly ovate, (1.2–)2–5 cm long, (0.7–)1.2–3 cm wide, cuneate at base, narrowed from about above the base to briefly acute apex, herbaceous, costas 3, all separate from the base, faint on upper surface, slender but distinct on lower surface, lateral veinlets relatively few, oblique, reticulations not prominent. Umbels borne on upper part of branches, staminate umbels 5- to 10-flowered, on capillary peduncle 7–12 mm long, the rays 5–8 mm long; pistillate umbels few-flowered, on short peduncles less than 1 cm long, the rays 5–8 mm long; receptacles hardly thickened; bracteoles setaceous, 1 mm long. Staminate perianth yellowish-green, campanulate to spreading, 2.5–3 mm across; outer and inner tepals alike, lance-ovate, gradually subacute at apex, 1.5–1.8 mm long, 0.6–0.75 mm wide. Stamens 6; filaments ca 0.5 mm long; anthers nearly globose, 0.2 mm long, white. Pistillate perianth similar to staminate but slightly smaller; ovary globose 2 mm long; staminodes 3, 1–1.5 mm long, needle-like. Berries 1 to 3 to an umbel, 5–7 mm across, 1– or 2-seeded, deep red at maturity.

description: Large climber: stems stout, 2–8 m long, internodes terete, striate,lightly green, 7–20 cm long, 5–10 mm thick, glabrous, rather sparingly beset with short divergent or recurved prickles 1–3 mm long; branches 20–60 cm long, internodes 3–10 cm long, 2–4 mm thick, terete, sparsely prickly, lightly green. Leaves elliptic to narrowly elliptic, rarely ovate-elliptic, 6–20 cm long, 3–12 cm wide, suddenly contracted or rounded at base, rounded or shallowly emarginate at usually mucronate apex, thickly herbaceous to subcoriaceous, light-green on upper surface, pale beneath; costas 5 including a weak marginal pair, the main 3 costas united for 5–10 mm above base, thick, highly convexed on lower surface, impressed on upper surface, lateral veinlets obliquely ascending, straightish, reticulations fine, not elongate, conspicuous on both surfaces; petioles 15–30 mm long, trigonous with subacute abaxial angle, at times tinged with red-brown, sheathing for 0.7–2.5 cm; wings broadly ovate, 0.5–1.2 cm wide, herbaceous and soon withering, brownish or reddish-brown, obtuse at apex, the rounded base hardly clasping the internodes; tendrils 7–20 cm long, often absent on flowering branches. Inflorescences borne on branches and distal part of stem, both sexes with 7 to 25 umbels; common axis prophyllate at base, 8–20 cm long, 3- to 5- nodose, internodes 1–5 cm long: prophyll broadly ovate, 5–7 mm long, acute-tipped. Umbels 2- to 5-nate, 1.5–3 cm across, 18- to 40-flowered; receptacles 2–3 mm across; peduncles 1–4 cm long, spreading. Staminate perianth 4–5 mm long, yellow or yellow-green, strongly recurved at anthesis; outer tepals oblong, 1–1.3 mm wide, obtuse at apex, inner ones linear, obtuse, 0.3–0.5 mm wide; filaments 4–4.5 mm long; anthers oblong, recurved, 1.5 mm long, white. Pistillate perianth 3–4 mm long, recurved at anthesis; tepals lance-oblong, subacute at apex, outer ones 0.8–1.2 mm wide, inner ones 0.5 mm wide. Ovary subglobose, 1 mm long and as wide; stigmas 0.8–1 mm long; staminodes 3, needle-like, only 0.5 mm long. Berries unknown.

description: Suberect shrub to scandent vine 30–200 cm tall, somewhat tufted atbase; stems, simple to rather densely branched, straightish, young ones deeply glaucous, subterete, finely striate, smooth or with sparse fine prickles ca 1 mm long, internodes 2–10 cm long, 1.5–3 mm thick. Leaves highly variable in shape; blades on young stems ovate-oblong to ovate-elliptic, sometimes lance-oblong or elliptic, those on old stems ovate-oval to oval or obovate-oval, cuneate to abruptly contracted to the base, occasionally shallowly emarginate, attenuate to obtuse or acute apex, (5–)10–15(–18) cm long, (2–)4–10 cm wide, herbaceous, fresh green above, glaucous and white-powdery beneath, costas 5 or 7 including a marginal pair, the median 3 united to 5–7 cm above the base, raised with sharp edge on lower surface, fine but distinct on upper surface, lateral veinlets obliquely ascending, distinct on both surfaces, further divided, forming relatively loose, obliquely elongate reticulations; petioles 10–20 mm long, weakly incurved, laterally compressed with sharp dorsal edge, sheathing for 3 to 5 mm; wings narrow (ca 0.5 mm), membranous; tendrils none or short, rarely up to 7 cm long on distal part of branches. Inflorescences with 1 or 2 umbels on upper branches; inflorescence axis short (3–5 mm), mostly enclosed in the leaf sheath; prophylls at base of common axis ovate, acuminate, 5–7 mm long; peduncles 1–2 cm long, rather stout. Staminate umbels densely 15- to 40-flowered; pistillate umbels 10- to 17-flowered; receptacles ellipsoid, 4–5 mm long, 2 mm thick. Staminate perianth recurved on upper half; outer tepals oblong, obtuse, 3–4 mm long, 1–1.5 mm wide; inner tepals linear, obtuse, 2–2.5 mm long, 0.5 mm wide. Stamens exserted; filaments 2.5–3 mm long; anthers oblong, 0.7–1 mm long. Pistillate perianth patent; outer tepals lanceolate, 3–3.5 mm long, 0.5 mm wide, acute. Ovary ovoid, 3 mm long, 1.2–1.5 mm across; stigmas 0.7–1 mm long; staminodes 3, needle-like, 1.2–1.5 mm long. Berries 0.8 mm in diameter, maturing reddish, 1- or 2-seeded.

description: Climber to 4 m long, with relatively slender stems; flowering branches more or less straight, 30–50 cm long, 2–3 mm thick, terete, hardly striate, somewhat shiny, smooth or very sparsely aculeate, the internodes 2–8 cm long. Leaves not highly variable in shape; blades broadly elliptic or ovate-orbicular, 6–13 cm long, 3–10 cm wide, rounded-truncate or suddenly contracted at base, rounded or contracted above to short-acuminate apex, thickly herbaceous to subcoriaceous; costas 5, all divided to base, the median 3 markedly convex on lower surface, lateral veinlets obliquely ascending, line but distinct on both surfaces, the reticulations more or less obliquely elongate; petioles 15–30 mm long, 2–3 mm thick, subterete; sheath 7–10 mm long; wings 1–1.5 mm wide, thinly herbaceous, the apices ending in a narrowly deltoid auricle 2–3 mm long; tendrils on vegetative leaves 10–20 cm long, those on flowering leaves vestigial or wanting. Inflorescences reduced to a single umbel, the common axis very short (0.3–1 cm), bearing 2 bracts at apex; prophyll ovate, acute, 5–6 mm long; peduncle 2.5–4 cm long; bracts ovale, 4–5 mm long. Staminate umbels ca 3 cm across, densely 50- to 70-flowered; receptacle oblong-ellipsoid, 3–6 mm long; rays filiform, ca 1 cm long. Pistillate umbels 2.5–3 cm across, 25- to 40-flowered; receptacle oblong, 5 mm long; rays 8–10 mm long. Staminate perianth 5–5.5 mm long, white; outer tepals oblanceolate-oblong, 1 mm wide, obtuse, inner ones narrowly lanceolate, 0.8 mm wide. Umbels oblong, 0.8 mm long; filaments 6 mm long. Pistillate perianth 4–4.5 mm long, white; outer tepals elliptic, 1.7 mm wide, rounded, inner ones lanceolate 0.7 mm wide. Ovary ovoid, 3 mm long. Staminodes 3, needle-like, 2 mm long. Berries globose, 7–9 mm in diameter, dirty yellow.

description: Plant sparingly pubescent in younger parts, glabrescent, rarely hairy. Probract 1–5 mm long, caducous. Leaves: blade unlobed, ovate or hastate, or 3- or 5-angular, or shallowly or deeply 3- (rarely 5-)lobed, glands several or many, small, scattered, most glands near the insertion of the petiole, margin minutely or conspicuously sparsely 1–2 mm mucronate-dentate, apex acute(-acuminate), 3 or 5 palmately veined, reticulation distinct on both surfaces; petiole 0.5–1(–1.5) cm long. Male inflorescences with a solitary (abortive) flower at the node, co axillary with 1 (or 2) persistent sub-umbellate or brush-like dense raceme(s), sessile or to 4 cm peduncled, flowers numerous, sparsely hairy, leaving persistent pedicels. Male flowers: pedicel 3–6(–10) mm long, articulate at apex; bract lanceolate or linear, 2–5 mm long, inserted on the pedicel (sometimes towards the apex), somewhat fleshy, with or without glands, persistent or caducous; receptacle-tube 3–4(–5) by 2–3 mm; sepals triangular, 0.2–0.5 mm long, wide apart; petals triangular, 1–2 mm long, finely papillose-hairy (without gland-hairs); filaments 2–3 mm long, glabrous, inserted at or slightly above the base of the receptacle-tube, anthers subglobose, 1–2 mm long, connective broad, convex above, papillose-hairy; thecae oblique or horizontal, curved, forming a nearly closed ring; disc lobes papillose-hairy, 1–2 mm long. Female flowers solitary (rarely a few in a short-shoot); pedicel 3–5 mm long; ovary (narrowly-)ellipsoid, ca 10 mm long, short (densely) hairy, with or without scattered or irregular lines of dark-coloured dots; perianth resembling male but slightly larger, ± persistent in young fruit; style ca 2 mm long, stigma, consisting of 3 subglobose long-papillose lobes; staminodes elongate, 0.5–1 mm long, glabrous; disc 1–2 mm long, hairy. Fruit (narrowly-)ellipsoid, 2–5 by 1.5–2.5 cm, velutinous or scabrous, green, paler striped; when ripe yellow or red; pulp yellowish; fruiting pedicel 0.5–1(1.5) cm long. Seeds (5–)10–20, nearly globose or somewhat elongate, (5–)6–7 mm long, ca 5 mm thick, smooth, with a very faint border, grey.</br>Field-notes.— In living specimens the leaves are conspicuously pale, glaucous below. Unripe fruits are green with irregular whitish stripes, ripe fruits red.

description: Slender herb, 20–30 cm tall, the stem subangular, glabrous and tinged purplish tan, the internodes to 6 cm long. Leaves mostly clustered at nodes, those of a pair isomorphic, obovate or broadly rounded, (1.2–)3–5 x 1.5–2(–4) cm, sessile or petiolate, the petiole to 2 cm long, base rounded or attenuate, apex acute, margin denticulate and ciliate, lamina pinnately veined with 2–4 pairs of lateral primary veins departing above the blade base, above sparsely fine pilose, the hairs 1–2 mm long (as also along the leaf margin), often with white stripes along the midrib and veins, below glabrous and reddish-purple or green. Inflorescence a terminal scorpioid cyme with 3–9 flowers, peduncle 3–5.5 cm long, glabrous. Hypanthium campanulate, 4–5 mm long and 2–2.2 mm in diam., glabrous; calyx lobes broadly triangular, about 1 mm long; pedicels 2–3 mm long. Petals elliptic and shortly acuminate, 1–1.3 cm long, purple. Stamens 3, 4.5–5 mm long, cordate or bilobed at the base, yellow. Capsule cylindrical or with six inconspicuous longitudinal ribs, 5–6 mm long, crowned by the persistent calyx lobes, smooth and glabrous.

description: An erect, usually much-branched herb, 5–50 cm tall, branchlets ± quadrangular, glandular-pilose or puberulous. Leaves distributed along the branchlets, those of a pair isomorphic, thinly membranous, elliptic-oblong, lanceolate, or linear, 0.6–3 x 0.4–2 cm, base acute, cuneate, or attenuate, apex acute or rounded, margin finely serrate or remotely coarsly ciliate, with 1(–2) pair(s) of lateral primary veins departing from the blade base, sparsely setose on the upper surface, more densely so below, or glabrous, petioles 0.2–0.4 cm long. description: A slender acaulescent herb or with a short succulent or rhizomatous stem, 4–10(–15) cm tall, the stem sparsely minute-setose, sometimes winged, the wings drying transparently. Inflorescence an axillary unilateral cyme with 16–20 sessile flowers in two rows, the peduncle 1–2 cm long, sparsely pubescent. description: Erect branched or unbranched herb (sometimes drying somewhat woody), 20–60 cm tall, rarely appearing creeping due to vegetative reproduction, stem quadrangular, often ± winged, covered with 2–3 mm long whitish hairs or furfuraceous-puberulous, often reddish. description: Evergreen tree, 6–20 m high; bark greyish brown, smooth, sparsely lenticelate; twigs cylindrical, rusty red tomentose then glabrescent, leaf scars distinct. description: Woody climber; twigs light to dark brown without lenticels, densely tomentose becoming glabrous with age, terete; spines absent; tendrils unknown. Leaves: petiole 1–4 mm, densely tomentose, lamina lanceolate to narrowly elliptic, 5.2–10.3 by 2.6–3.6 mm; base acute to rounded, apex acute to acuminate, chartaceous, tomentose along upper and lower nerves when young, becoming glabrous; 3–5-plinerved, midrib slightly sunken above, rounded below. Stipules a distinct line, densely tomentose when young, glabrous when old. Inflorescence to 30 mm, terminal or axillary in upper leaf axils, fairly dense, tomentose, many-flowered; peduncle distinct, 1.2–1.9 cm; pedicels absent or to 7 mm. Calyx 0.7–0.8 mm; sepals ovate to triangular, outside and inside sparsely tomentose. Corolla 2.2–3.1 mm, colour unknown; tube slightly shorter than lobes; outside sparsely woolly; inside densely woolly on lobes; lobes not thickened. Stamens inserted in mouth of corolla-tube; filaments 0.4–0.5 mm; anthers 0.5–0.7 mm, ovate, glabrous, apiculate. Ovary and style 1.4–1.7 mm, sparsely pubescent in lower half of the style, sometimes hairs extending to very upper part of the ovary, stigma capitate. Fruit 1.7–2.3 cm diam., ellipsoid to globular, thin walled, with 1–4 seeds. Seeds 12.5–15 mm, 3.5 mm thick, ellipsoid, woolly tomentose.

description: Shrub or small tree, rarely a large tree to 45 m high and 80 cm diam; twigsrusty tomentose or velvet, glabrescent, rarely pubescent appressed-pilose, or glabrous; terminal buds hairy. Leaves rusty or brownish pubescent or tomentose beneath, especially on midrib and nerves, rarely glabrous, (ovate) to elliptic to (obovate) with cuneate, rarely rounded base, glandular dentate or crenulate margin and more or less acuminate apex, (6–)12–25 by (2.5–)3–1 cm; nerves (8–)10–14(–16) pairs, very prominent beneath, parallel to each other, mostly quite straight, curved upwards towards the margin and nearly reaching it, whether forming an intramarginal vein or not; reticulation usually rather fine; petiole (2–)5–17 mm. Inflorescence with spicate branches, 3–15 cm, axis densely rusty tomentose or pubescent; bracts and bracteoles persistent, with same indumentum, the former at least 2 mm long and wide, but usually longer, exceptionally up to 10 mm long, with the 2 smaller bracteoles forming a calycle hiding the ovary. Flowers faintly scented to fragrant. Calyx (appressed-pubescent) divided into (1–)2(–3) mm long lobes. Corolla white (according to some collectors with a yellow spot on each lobe) 3–5 mm long. Stamens 30–70. Disk glabrous. Ovary glabrous, 0.5–1 mm high; style glabrous, 3–5 mm. Fruit ampulliform or globose, 5–7 by 4–5 mm, more or less ribbed when dry, often narrowed into a cylindrical neck, crowned by the usually closed, enlarged calyx lobes which form a conical beak on top; mesocarp thin, fleshy. Seed 1, twice curved with similar curved embryo.

description: Shrub or small tree to 18 m; twigs glabrous or pubescent to appressed orspreadingly-long-hairy, sometimes with a mixed indumentum of a short tomentum and long spreading hairs; terminal buds hairy. description: Shrub, or less often a tree to 22 m high and 50 cm diam; twigs sparsely pilose, puberulous, or appressed-pubescent, glabrescent, often zig-zag; terminal buds hairy. Leaves alternately or (on the leaders) spirally arranged, glabrous above, sparsely finely adpressed-hairy beneath, rarely patently hirsute, especially on midrib and nerves and towards the margin, (narrowly) elliptic or sometimes ovate, acuminate to caudate with acute to rounded base, 5–13(–18) by 2–4.5(–6) cm; acumen 5–20 mm; margin entire or glandular, but glands hot closely spaced; nerves (4–)6–8(–11) pairs, meeting in a looped intramarginal vein; reticulation coarse; petiole 2–8 mm. Flowers in a fascicle of reduced, often branched, racemes to 2.5 cm long; bracts and bracteoles persistent, minute (rarely to 3 mm), like the axis pubescent; often several bracts present, indicating origin from a more branched inflorescence; pedicels 1–5 mm, pubescent. Calyx divided into (4–)5(–6) broadly ovoid, rounded, appressed-pubescent or glabrous lobes, ca 1 mm long but sometimes the lobes different in size, often some of the lobes petaloid. Corolla glabrous or more often with minute hairs towards the outer base, rarely some hairs on the back also, 2–4.5 mm. Stamens 12–35. Disk glabrous to more or less pilose, low annular. Ovary appressed-hairy, ca 1 mm high; style hairy, especially towards the thickened base, rarely glabrous, 2–3.5 mm. Fruit broadly or narrowly ampulliform, often curved, the belly globose or ovoid, the neck broadly conical, 5–7 by 3–5 mm; mesocarp thin, rather fleshy, or papyraceous; stone ruminate with ca 10 shallow grooves or not ruminate. Seed 1 much lobed with slightly curved embryo.

Involucral bracts 2 pairs, decussate, sessile; outer pair ovate, 1–3 by 0.5–2 cm; inner pair ovate, 0.5–2.5 by 0.3–1 cm. Bracts filiform 6–20, up to 8 cm long. Pedicels 1.5–3 cm long. Flowers 1–2 by 0.5–1 cm, greenish-white to brownish or dark purple. Perianth 6-lobed; 3 outer lobes ovate or triangular, 5–11 by 2–5 mm; 3 inner lobes broadly ovate, 4–5 by 4–5 mm. Stamens greenish. Ovary 3–6 by 4–7 mm. Fruit dehiscent, triangular, funnel-shaped, ± 1 by 0.7 cm; perianth persisting. Seeds oblong-ovoid, 2–2.5 by 0.6–1 mm, and ± 5 mm thick.

description: Tree up to 20 m high, rarely more; young twigs pubescent later glabrous. Leaves parlpinnate, with 10–18 pairs of small leaflets. Petioles and rhachis 5–12cm long, pubescent to glabrous. Stipules minute, caducous. Petiolules glabrous or pubescent. Leaflets glabrous, oblong-linear, unequal, at base rounded, at apex mucronatc, 8–30 by 3–9 mm. Racemes terminal, 2–6 cm with a ± puberulous axis. Bracts ovate-oblong caducous, 5 by 3 mm. Pedicels puberulous to glabrescent, up to 10 mm; bracteoles similar to the bracts, densely ciliate, pubescent on lower surface, glabrous on upper. Receptacle narrowly turbinate, 4–4.5 mm long. Sepals 4, oblong-elliptic, imbricate, yellowish, glabrous but hairy at base, 12 by 5 mm. Petals 3, unequal, yellowish-orange; upper petal oblong-cordate, 10–12 by 2–3 mm; 2 lateral ones, obovate-oblong, narrowed towards the hairy base, 12–13 mm long, 5–6 mm broad. Perfect stamens 3, connate to an open staminal tube, filaments short; tube plus filaments 12–15 mm long; anthers oblong. Ovary ± pubescent, linear. 7 mm long on an equally long stipe; style rather thick, 7 mm long, pubescent; stigma terminal, truncate, subcapitate. Pods oblong, incurved, thick, light brown, indehiscent, 5–15 by 1–2.5 cm; mesocarp pulpy, acid. Seeds compressed, obovate-orbicular, varying in shape, ca 1 cm long, glossy, dark brown.

Lamina oblong-lanceolate, acute to acuminate at apex, 15–70 by 5–40 cm, variable in size; lower pinnae suddenly reduced to auricles, lowest normal pinna often reduced and deflexed, middle pinnae linear-lanceolate, gradually narrowing towards long-acuminate apex, broadly cuneate at sessile base, deeply lobed to ¾ way to costa; segments narrowly oblong, oblique, acute at apex, entire or crenate; chartaceous, deep green; veins pinnate, veinlets simple, basal ones running to callous-membrane in sinus between segments. Sori round, medial to costular; indusia persistent, glabrous.

description: Small tree, up to 10 m high; crown bushy. Leaves oblong, 17–28 x 7–10 cm, apex acute to broadly acute, base obtuse, sub-coriaceous, glabrescent; 3-nerved at base, midrib and nerves prominently ridged when dry. Inflorescences simple, on main stem and branches, 1–7-flowered; pedicel 1–1.5 cm long. Buds ovate; ca 6 x 4 mm, hairy. Flowers white or yellowish. Sepals linear-lanceolate; 5–7 x 1–1.5 mm, hairy on outer part. Petals in 2 part; the upper obtrullate, ca 8 x 2 mm; the lower part bowl-shaped; these two parts connected by an appendix. Ovary ovoid, hairy, style single up to 1 mm long; stigma with narrow apex. Fruit pear-shaped, ca 25 x 10 cm, fleshy and indehiscent. Seeds ovoid, up to 1 cm long.

description: Herb, stems long, angular, sulcate, side shoots concentrated at shoot apices, spirally inserted. Leaves bract-like. Juvenile shoots bracteate at the apex; bracts crowded, spirally inserted, 1–1.5 by 0.6 mm, elongate-deltoid, outer surface covered in a smooth waxy deposit, older stems sparsely bracteate with occasional side shoots arising from bract axils. Inflorescences terminal, subtended by an involucre of quincuncially arranged bracts; bracts ovate, lanceolate, 1.5–2 by 0.7 mm, apex acuminate, outer surfaces convex, inner surface flat. Flowers with receptacle 1 by 0.8–1 mm; tepals deltoid 0.5–0.6 by 0.5 mm, fleshy, outer surface convex, inner surface flat with a distinctive lip or edge at the margin; filaments slender, tortuous, 0.3 by 0.1 mm; anthers dorsifixed, 0.4 by 0.3 mm; nectary membranous, concave, smooth, 5-lobed; stigma sessile. Fruit nut-like, 4–4.5 by 3–3.5 mm, sessile or shortly pedicellate; pedicel decurrent, exocarp thin, rugulate with 10 longitudinal, raised bands running from the apex to the base of the fruit; mesocarp absent; endocarp 2.5–3 by 3–3.5 mm.

description: Subligneous or herbaceous climber 4–10 m long, putatively from a tuberous root; stem (leafy shoots) 2–3 mm diam., variously grey or yellowish brown soft long-hairy, hairs 1.5–4 mm long. Probract absent or rarely present at base of male peduncle, ca 10 mm long, basal part narrow, apex incised. Tendrils spiraling over almost all their length, but basal part straight for at least 1 cm. Leaves: blade simple, ovate(-oblong), 6–12(–15) by 4–9(–12) cm, upper surface rather densely appressed scabrid, later on leaving cystoliths, lower surface densely softer hairy, especially on veins, base deeply cordate, margin finely (coarsely) dentate, apex acute-acuminate; petiole 2–9 cm long, (sparsely) soft-hairy. Male inflorescences one (or rarely 2) peduncled raceme(s), sometimes with the persistent pedicel of a previously developed flower at base; peduncle 2–10 cm long; flowers few, bracteate, crowded, all pubescent with short or long hairs, hairs up to 2(–4) mm long; bracts elliptic-oblong or ± wedge-shaped, 1–1.5 by 0.4–1 cm, shallowly or up to halfway incised, apices of lobes long-acute. Male flowers: pedicel 5–10 mm long, longer in basal solitary male flower; receptacle-tube cup-shaped, ca 5 by 6 mm, throat minutely papillose; sepals linear, 6–10 mm long, ca 1 mm wide or less, 1-veined; petals (10–)15 by 8–10 mm, obtuse, inside papillose; filaments ca 4 mm long, anthers (2–)2.5 by ca 1.5 mm; petal basal scales papillose, largest ca 3 by 2 mm, and 3 (or 4) much smaller ones; disc subglobose, ca 2 mm diam. Female flower solitary or 2 or 3 in a short bracteate raceme; pedicel 5(–10) mm long; perianth similar to male flowers but somewhat larger; ovary ellipsoid, ca 12 by 7 mm, faintly 10-ribbed, densely (appressedly) hairy, hairs ca 2 mm long; receptacle tube narrow; sepals (10–)15 mm long, linear; petals 20–22 by 15 mm; style-column ca 0.5 mm long, arms 4(–5) mm long; stigmas irregularly broadly reniform, papillose, each 3–4 mm wide; petal basal scales 3, ca 1 mm long; staminodes 3(–5), erect, 1–1.5 mm long, papillose. Fruit solitary (or 2), ellipsoid, 4–5 by 2.5–3 cm, 10-ribbed, hairy, smooth, not fenestrately ornamented between the ribs; fruiting pedicel 1–1.5 cm long. Seeds ovoid, ca 4 by 3 by 2 mm, pale brown, finely rugose.

description: Perennial much-branched climber to 8 m long; subglabrous or hairy; stem of leafy shoots 2(–3) mm diam.; rarely monoecious. Probract usually present. Tendrils spiraling either throughout their length or only in the upper part. Leaves: blade simple, ovate, 6–10 by 4–9 cm, upper surface appressed-hairy, scabrous by cystoliths, lower surface hairy or subglabrous, base deeply cordate, margin coarsely or finely dentate, apex acute-acuminate; petiole 3–6 cm long, finely hairy or subglabrous. Male inflorescences a peduncled bracteate raceme (sometimes with a previously developed solitary flower at base), 5–10 cm, sparsely minutely pubescent; peduncle 2–5 cm long, at or close to the base with a rhombiform or sub-elliptic (5–)10 mm long irregularly incised probract; flowers few or several, bracts close together, or in older inflorescences the scars of the fallen flowers and bracts more spaced, forming an up to 3 cm long spike, with few bracteate flowers and buds at apex; bracts obovate or obtriangular, 10–15 mm long, the margin in the apical half (irregularly) dentate or incised to ca ¼ deep. Male flowers: pedicel ca 10 mm long; receptacle-tube obliquely cup-shaped, tapering, 3–4 mm diam., throat short-hairy; sepals long-triangular, or oblong, 8–12 by 3–5 mm, acute, 3(–5) veined, sometimes reflexed; petals in bud erect and much shorter than sepals, expanded petals obovate-elliptic, 15–20 by ca 15 mm, apex rounded and faintly dentate; filaments short, 3–5 mm long, ± curved, ± dilated towards the base, anthers 3–5 mm long, slightly curved, median(?) petal with conspicuous curved scale, ca 4 mm, concealing the disc in the receptacle-tube; disc inserted slightly laterally, large, ellipsoid, ca 4 mm long. Female flowers solitary; pedicel 10–40 mm long, with probract at or near base; perianth as in male flowers; ovary ovoid-ellipsoid, densely woolly grey-hairy, ca 10 mm long; style-column ca 2 mm long, arms 4–5 mm long; stigmas 2-lobed, lobes broadly reniform, each ca 3 mm diam., staminodes ca 1.5 mm long, erect. Fruit solitary; oblong-cylindrical, (2–)3–6 by 2–2.5 cm, broadly rounded at both ends, sparsely or densely bristly hairy, outer surface fenestrately pitted in ca 15 rows; fruiting pedicel 1.5–4 cm long. Seeds ovoid, 5–6 mm long, somewhat flattened, rugose, margin shallowly 2-grooved.
