description: Herbaceous few-branched climber 1.5–4 m long, from a tuberous root; young parts finely hairy, largely glabrescent; stem 2(–4) mm diam. Probract absent, except in connection with inflorescences, in male small, up to 5 mm long, at or towards base of inflorescences, in female not obvious. Tendrils not spiraling basally. Leaves: blade simple, unlobed or lobed, or 3- or 5-foliolate, (broadly) ovate in outline, 7–20(–25) by 4–15(–20) cm, upper surface with sparse (minute) coarse hairs, later on leaving sparse cystoliths, lower surface glabrous, except for few hairs on veins, base deeply cordate, margin finely (coarsely) dentate, apex acute acuminate; petiole 2–7 cm long, petiolules to 1 cm long. Male inflorescences usually a peduncled raceme (rarely few-branched), 2–12 cm long, including 1.5–5 cm long peduncle, early glabrescent, at base usually with a scar of fallen small probract, and a solitary pedicel 20–30 mm long of previously developed flower; flowers in raceme (few to) numerous; lower portion of pedicels persistent; bracts absent. Male flowers: bud with open calyx, imitating small flowers; pedicels 5–15 mm long; receptacle-tube shallowly cup-shaped, 2–3 by 5–7 mm, slightly oblique at base because of eccentric disc, inside minutely gland-hairy, throat minutely gland-hairy; sepals narrowly elliptic, 4–6 by 2–2.5 mm, 3- or 5-veined, out-curved, apex greenish (often black on drying), (sub)acute; petals ovate-oblong, 10–15 by 8–10 mm, obtuse, 5(–7)-veined, at apex of midvein with a minute gland; filaments short, 3–4 mm long, anthers ca 2.5 mm long; median? petal at base with a large curved scale, ca 2.5 mm long, concealing the disc; disc globose ellipsoid, ca 2.5 mm diam. Female flowers solitary or 2 or 3 in up to 2 cm long raceme; pedicel (10–)20 mm long; sepals and petals similar to those of male flowers, but narrower; ovary subfusiform, ca 15 by 3 mm, at apex long-tapering, brownish short-woolly; style ca 2.5 mm long, stigma-arms 0.5(–1) mm long; stigmas reniform, ca 1.5 mm diam.; staminodes in two pairs and 1 solitary, ca 0.5 mm long, glandular-papillose; basal petal scale not obvious. Fruit (after Hooker and Thomson 1703, Khasia (K), and A.M. Lu & Zhi Y. Zhang, Flora Sinica) narrowly or broadly oblong, 3.5–6 by 2–3 cm, rounded at base, tapering at apex, minutely sparsely hairy, white, green striped; fruiting pedicel slender, ca 3 cm long. Seeds broadly ovoid, 6–7 by 5 mm, base obtuse-rounded, smooth.

description: Climber a few meters long, putatively with a tuberous rootstock; leafy shoot 2–3 mm thick, soft grey-hairy, hairs 1–2 mm long, glandular or not. Probract not obvious. Leaves: blade simple, ovate or ovate-oblong, 9–17 by 5–10 cm, upper surface sparsely hairy, cystoliths not obvious, lower surface more densely hairy, especially on veins, base deeply cordate, margin finely dentate, apex acute-acuminate; petiole 2.5–6 cm long, soft-hairy. description: Climber to 10 m long, possibly with tuberous root; stem of leafy shoots (2–)3(–4) mm thick, rather densely soft-patently hairy, hairs pale brown, (1–)2–3 mm long. Probract usually absent, occasionally present (when male inflorescence with solitary flower at base of peduncle present), ± rhomboid-elliptic, ca 15 mm long, dentate or incised in apical half. Tendrils not spiraling in lower third, hairy. Leaves: blade simple, ovate (or ovate-oblong), 7–17 by 4.5–12 cm, upper surface ± sparsely mixed-hairy, the shorter hairs finally leaving small cystoliths, lower surface more densely hairy especially on veins, base deeply cordate, margin (densely) finely dentate, apex acute-acuminate; petiole 4–12 cm, soft-hairy. Male inflorescences a peduncled raceme, 6–15 cm long, with up to 20 bracteate flowers crowded in a head 2.5–4 cm diam. at apex; peduncle 5–10 cm long, soft-hairy, hairs (1–)2–3 mm long; bracts ± rhomboid-obovate or wedge-shaped, 1.5(–2) by 1.5 cm, the apical part rounded, shallowly or deeply (¼ to ½) incised, the lobes acute to long-acuminate, base narrow, subglabrous to (sparsely) long-hairy, hairs 0.5–2 mm long; bracts persistent after flowering. Male flowers sparsely hairy, frequently up to 3 open flowers in one raceme; pedicel short, 2(–3) mm long, articulate towards base; receptacle-tube broadly cup-shaped, ca 3 by 5 mm, finely papillose in the throat; sepals (oblong-)linear, 8–12 by 1–1.5 mm, 3(–5)-veined, sparsely hairy; petals oblong, obtuse, 15–20 by 7–10 mm, 7-veined, inside finely papillose; basal petal scales one or two large, 2–2.5 mm long, up to 3 smaller ones present or absent; filaments 3–4 mm long (one shorter than the others), glandular-hairy, anthers 3–4 mm long; disc ca 2.5 mm diam. Female flowers solitary or 2; pedicel ca 15 mm long; perianth slightly smaller than in male; ovary broadly ellipoid, densely pale brown-hairy, 8–10 by ca 6 mm. Fruit solitary, subglobose, ca 3 by 2.5 cm, irregularly striate-verrucose, (sparsely) hairy; fruiting pedicel ca 6 cm. Seeds pear-shaped (or ovoid), somewhat narrowed at base, rather flattened, ca 5 by 3.5 by 1.5 mm, finely verrucose, margin ± square.

description: Shrublet, about 1 m high, rusty tomentose; branches zigzag, woody, nodes thickened. Leaves with petiole 5–8 mm, tomentose; lamina obovate-oblong, oblong, elliptic-oblong or lanceolate, 26–33.5 by 8.5–17.5 cm, base rounded or slightly cordate, margin entire, apex acute or acuminate, glabrous above, laxly tomentose below, pinnately 6–7-nerved, veins transverse, venation reticulate, smooth above, strongly prominent below. Inflorescences axillary, racemose, 7–10 cm long, 3–5-flowered, drooping, from the middle or near basal part of the stem; bracts leafy, ovate, 7–9 by 2.5–3 mm, tomentose, many. description: Climber 2–3 m long (stouter in all parts in var. anguina); annual or subperennial; monoecious; with (sparse) minute hairs, partly glabrescent; plant green, not reddish tinged; cystoliths not obvious; stem 1.5–2(–5) mm diam. Fruits green, turning orange-red, paler speckled or longitudinally banded, ovoid or narrowly ellipsoid, narrowed towards apex, 2.5–5 by 1.5–4 cm (up to ca 100 cm long in var. anguina, see note); exocarp thinly leathery, smooth; pulp orange; fruiting pedicel 1–2(–3) cm long. description: Climber 5–20 m long; rarely monoecious; (sub)glabrous, hairs minute; plant green, blackish on drying, petals white; cystoliths usually not obvious; stem 3–5 mm diam. Leaves: blade 3–5-angular or lobed to ca ¼ deep, suborbicular in outline, 8–21 by 7–16 cm, ± scabrous above, glands several or numerous, close to the vein-axils, especially several in the axils of the main veins at very base of the blade, 0.5–1 mm diam.; base deeply cordate, lobes triangular; margin entire; apex acute-acuminate; petiole 2.5–8(–10) cm long. Male inflorescences 10–25(–30) cm long, glabrescent; peduncle 7–14 cm long, 2–3 mm thick; rachis with 5–20 flowers, bracts late-caducous, (ob)ovate-elliptic or ± rhomboid, 15–25 mm long, with glands near mid vein, margin (sub)entire. Male flowers: pedicel (sub)caducous, 2–5(–10) mm long; receptacle-tube 30–50 mm long, at apex ca 7 mm wide; sepals long-triangular, 10–15 mm long, 2–3 mm wide at base, margin with few slender side-lobes in basal part; petals very finely hairy, obovate or broadly cuneate, ca 20 mm long, threads 10–15 mm long; synandrium 6–8 mm long, filaments 1–3 mm long, glabrous. Female flowers: pedicel 5–8(–20) mm long; ovary (ovoid-)ellipsiod, ca 8 by 4 mm, glabrous; receptacle-tube (25–)40–60 mm long; sepals smaller and narrower than in male, ca 10 by 1 mm, entire. Fruits bright red, (depressed) globose, 5–6(–7) cm diam., apex not beaked; pericarp 10–15 mm thick; exocarp leathery, smooth, coarsely wrinkled on drying or not; pulp green-black; fruiting pedicel 1–3 by 0.4–0.5 cm, usually curved. description: Climber, 4–10 m long; glabrous or very minutely hairy, glabrescent; plant green, not reddish tinged, petals white; cystoliths not obvious; stem 2–4 mm diam. Probract absent. description: Climber 8–25 m long; brown or grey-white villose, hairs ca 1 mm long, to 3 mm long in sterile running shoots; plant green, petals white; cystoliths not obvious; stem 3–4 mm diam. description: Trees, up to 30 m high, dbh up to 40 cm; buttresses sometimes present or slightly fluted. description: Tree, 15–30 m high, 100–200 cm girth. Bark brown to dark brown; outer part scaly, inner part with fine long and narrowed ridge, always depressed; sapwood as narrow canals. Interpetiolar stipules narrowly triangular, ca 3 by 1 mm. Leaves elliptic to more or less obovate, 6–12 by 2–5.5 cm; base cuneate; apex acute; subcoriaceous, green and shiny on the upper surface; pale on the lower; midrib prominent on the lower surface, lateral nerves 10–15 pairs, finely ridged on the lower; scalariform veins distinct on the lower surface. Petiole 0.5–1.5 cm long, glabrous, flat at adaxial, petiole and midrib pinkish when dry. Male inflorescences suberect, 3–10 cm long, puberulous throughout. Male flowers sessile, perianth campanulate, 6 lobed, free or minutely connate near base; stamens 6; anthers ovoid, basifixed; rudimentary ovary a cluster of hairs. Female inflorescences catkin erect, perianth as male, adnate to ovary at base; staminodes 6; styles 3, decurved or connate near base; stigmata capitate. Cupule sessile, broadly saucer-shaped, ca 1 cm in diam., with 7 or more irregular lobes, all covered with brown hairs, glabrescent, normally bearing 1–3 nuts. Nut prominently longitudinally triangular ridged, 5–10 by 6 mm (young), densely, brown hairs then glabrous and shiny.

description: Shrub or tree, up to 20 m high; monoecious, deciduous with flowers appearing before the leaves. Stipules 4–12 by 2–4 mm. Leaves: petiole (5.5–)20(–26) cm long, glands at apex sessile, tuberculiform or cushion-shaped; blades not to shallowly 3-lobed, (4.5–)10–25 by (3.5–)10–22 cm, length/width ratio 1-1.2(–1.4), apex subacute to obtusely acuminate to slightly cuspidate, ending in a small gland. Inflorescences usually bisexual, (3–)8–16 by 7-21 cm, few flowered. Flowers 25–30 by 25–35 mm in diam., reddish-white to purple, suffused and veined with pink, yellow in the centre; calyx lobes 8–10 by 5–8 mm; petals orbicular-ovate to broadly spathulate, 20–35 by 8–20 mm, claw 3–6 by 1.5–2 mm. Staminate flowers: pedicel 8–18 mm long; disc glands subulate to triangular-elliptic, 3–4.5 by 0.5–1 mm, acute, somewhat fleshy; stamens (7)8(–14), the (4)5(–8) outer ones 7–10 mm long, the 3(–6) inner ones 11–15 mm long; anthers 1.5–2 by 0.5–1 mm. Pistillate flowers: pedicel 5–14 mm long; disc glands as staminate flowers, 2–4 by 0.8–1.0 mm; ovary 4(5)-locular, ovoid-subglobose, 4–5 by 3–4 mm; styles 4–5 mm long, shortly bifid. Fruits spherical to subglobose or slightly compressed, apically sharply pointed, basally stiped, abruptly narrowed into the base, surface smooth or faintly lineate, but without any grooves or ridges: 4–6 by 3–5 cm in diam., dull brown when ripe, glabrescent. Seeds 20–25(–30) by 18–22 by 14–15 mm, conspicuously warty and ridged dorsally and ventrally.

description: The seeds are pressed for oil; two varieties are won: White t’ung oil, drawn cold, is yellow, translucent, moderately thick and used in Central China for varnishing furniture and umbrellas, for oiling paper, and for lighting purposes. Black t’ung oil is extracted by heat and pressure, it is thick, blackish, opaque and cheaper than the other variety; in China it is used in putty for caulking boats and for varnishing them. In Europe and America it is also used in varnishes, paint, linoleum, etc.; it is of better quality than linseed oil. The seeds have drastic purgative properties and can cause severe poisoning if eaten raw. The seed remnants are used as manure in China.

Inflorescence with up to 6 branches; densely patently hairy, without nodal glands. Flowers yellow, drying orange red; pedicel 1–2 mm, outer sepals 1.7–2 mm, inner sepals 2.3–3 mm; upper petals ca 8 mm, glabrous except outside at apex and occasionally sparsely at base; lateral petals ca 7.5 mm, glabrous outside except at apex, inside glabrous; keel 6.5 mm, hairy outside along middle, glabrous inside; keel shorter than the other petals. Stamens swollen above base and hairy there, ca 6 mm; anthers ca 0.5 mm. Gynoecium 6 mm, stipe 0.3 mm, ovules 4; ovary densely patently hairy, style sparsely hairy in basal half only. Fruit globular, up to 1.5 cm diameter, glabrous and densely tuberculate; seeds 1 or 2.

Leaves: blade (broadly) ovate-elliptic, 8–15 by 5–10 cm, membranous or subcoriaceous, both surfaces glabrous or hairy; base broadly rounded or cordate or sometimes somewhat hastate; apex (sub)obtuse, minutely mucronate; 2–5-pinnately veined and one pair of basal veins, reticulation distinct on lower surface; petiole 1.5–3 cm long. Male inflorescences glabrous or hairy, (10–)15–60 cm long, little or much branched (sometimes also branched from the base), lateral branches to 15 cm long, flowers often in bundles of up to 5, the bundles ± spaced, the larger inflorescences often from the older wood. Female inflorescences 5–40 cm long, raceme-like or branched panicles, few-or many-flowered, flowers solitary (or 2). Male flowers: pedicels rather thick, 1–3(–5) mm long, articulate at ± halfway; buds 2 mm diam.; sepals membranous, almost free, subtriangular, ca 2 mm long; petals ovate narrowly elliptic, 2.5–3.5 mm long, apex narrowed, subacute, adaxially papillose; stamens inserted on a fleshy disc, leaving the centre free; filaments 0.5–1 mm long, fleshy; anthers transversely ellipsoid, (0.5–)1 mm long. Female flowers: sepals triangular, 2–4 mm long; petals ovate-narrowly elliptic, 3–8 mm long, subacute, finely papillose-hairy; ovary subcylindrical-obconical, 5–12 by 2–3 mm, glabrous or hairy; styles very short; stigmas with 2 incurved horizontal horns, papillose. Fruits pendulous, few to many per infructescence, very variable in size, (4–)5–10 by 1.5–4.5(–5) cm, glabrous, glabrescent or hairy. Seeds pale, elliptic, flat, not ornamented, 15(–20) by 8(–10) mm, winged all around, the wing leathery, much elongated and rounded at both ends; seed with wing 40–60(–80) by 13–15(–20) mm.

description: Subherbaceous 2–6 m long climber; monoecious; plant subglabrous, generally drying (dark) brownish. Leaves: blade ovate-triangular, 4–12 by 3–10 cm, rarely shallowly lobed, base subtruncate or broadly shallowly cordate, margin denticulate, apex acute-acuminate; petiole 2–5 cm long. Inflorescences: in male a peduncled 3–10-flowered short or sometimes ± spike like proliferous raceme, peduncle 1–5 cm long, usually co-axillary with a previously developed single female flower; female flowers solitary or rarely few, sub-umbellate, peduncled. Male flowers: pedicel 1–4 mm long; receptacle-tube ca 3 by 2 mm, inside with long hairs, especially at the throat; sepals 0.5 mm long; petals ovate, ca 2 mm long, subacute, inner surface and apex hairy; stamens inserted halfway along receptacle-tube or rather lower (but not at the base of tube); filaments 1–2 mm long, subglabrous or long-haired about middle; anthers circular in outline, 1 mm diam., thecae curved, the two nearly forming a ring, connective ± hairy, not produced, disc depressed globose, 1 mm diam. Female flowers: pedicel slender, 2–5 mm long; ovary ovoid-globose, ca 3 by 2.5 mm, glabrous (except minute raised gland-dots), neck 1 mm long; perianth as in male flower but petals 2.5–3 mm long; style ca 3 mm long, glabrous, stigma 3-lobed, 1.5–2 mm diam., papillose; disc 0.5 mm high; staminodes slender, ca 2 mm long, the basal portion adnate with the receptacle-tube. Fruit solitary (rarely 2 or 3), globose, 0.8–1.2 mm diam., glabrous, green, at last red, finely netted or pitted when dry; fruiting pedicel 0.3–1 cm long. Seeds rather many, (narrowly) elliptic, ca 5 by 3–3.5 mm, narrowly margined, smooth, pale brownish when dry.

description: Annual delicate climber 50–100 cm long; monoecious; subglabrous; green on drying. Leaves: blade subovate in outline, 3–9 by 2.5–8 cm, (3–)5-angular or shallowly lobed, scabrid with minute cystoliths above, base shallowly or deeply cordate, margin sparsely shallowly dentate, apex acute or (long-)acuminate; petiole 1.5–3.5 cm long. Male inflorescence a solitary slender peduncled spike-like raceme; peduncle 1.5–4 cm long, flower-bearing portion 2–4.5 cm long, with 5–15 patently short-pedicelled, spaced flowers, the basal ones usually paired. Male flowers: pedicel 2.5–4 mm long, glabrous; perianth 2.5–3 mm diam.; receptacle tube (broad) cup-shaped, 1.5–2 by 2–3 mm, glabrous except few slender hairs inside; sepals 0.2 mm long; petals ovate-elliptic, 0.8–1 by 0.8–1 mm, subobtuse, minutely papillose towards apex; stamens inserted near the base of the receptacle-tube; filaments 1.5–1.8 mm long, glabrous; anthers 0.3 mm diam., thecae vertical, somewhat curved, 0.2–0.3 mm long, connective slightly swollen, with few stiff hairs; disc depressed globose, 0.5 by 1 mm. Female flowers solitary on the node or co-axillary with male raceme; pedicel filiform, 12–15 mm long; ovary fusiform-ellipsoid, ca 1.5 by 1.2 mm, glabrous, neck nearly 1 mm long; perianth as in male flower; style 1–1.2 mm long, stigma 0.7 mm diam., consisting of 3 sessile subglobose papillose free lobes; staminodes not seen; disc conspicuous, a ± 3-lobed ring, 0.5 mm high, at base partly connate with receptacle. Fruit globose, ca 0.6 cm diam., few-seeded; pericarp thin, leaving the seeds shining through; fruiting pedicel 1.5–2.5 cm long. Seeds flat, pyriform in outline, ca 5 by 3 mm, narrowly margined, smooth, pale.

description: Evergreen or rarely deciduous trees or shrubs, with spiral primary branching; bark longitudinally striate or cracked into plates, rarely loose and longitudinally fissured. Indument of simple hairs. Leaves coriaceous to chartaceous, mostly elliptic to lanceolate or rarely oblong to ovate, base symmetrical or rarely asymmetrical, cuneate, rounded, cordate or rarely attenuate, midrib plane or sunken above, prominent below, secondary venation indistinct, usually not prominent, tertiary venation reticulate, forming a loose or close network. Inflorescences leaf-opposed or internodal, 1–20-flowered. Flowers hermaphroditic, conical in bud. Sepals 3, valvate, connate at base or free, much shorter than petals. Petals in two whorls of 3, valvate, free, mostly triangular-ovate to ovate, subequal or inner petals slightly shorter and narrower than outer petals, base expanded, saccate, apex reflexed at anthesis, outer petals spreading to strongly revolute and inner petals erect. Stamens 12–65, anthers aseptate, anther connective apex miliusoid (not covering anther thecae), apiculate. Carpels 1–15, stigmas U-shaped to globose; ovules few to many per ovary, biseriate. Receptacle conical, hairy. Fruits apocarpous, monocarps indehiscent, up to 8 per fruit, yellow, dull green or pale orange when mature, cylindrical, ellipsoid, ovoid or globose, glabrous or pubescent, smooth or verrucose, stipitate or subsessile; pericarp thick, leathery or woody when dried. Seeds attached laterally in 2 rows, up to 16 per monocarp, not separating from endocarp, smooth or wrinkled, glabrous, pale brown to dark brown, perichalazal ring raised, aril absent, endosperm ruminations lamellate.</br></br>A tropical Asian genus of about 38 species, bearing small flowers with saccate petals, reflexed at the tips, and miliusoid stamens; 17 species are represented in Thailand.

description: Tree ca 15 m tall; bark greyish brown, longitudinally striate. Twigs densely covered with brown appressed hairs when young, later moderately to sparsely hairy. Inflorescences 1–3-flowered, peduncle 2–10 mm long, pedicels 10–15 mm long, each bearing a single bract near base; buds conical. Sepals connate at base to near midpoint, ovate, 1.5–2 mm long, obtuse. Outer petals brownish yellow, triangular-ovate to ovate, 12–16 by 6–8.5 mm, apex obtuse, hairy on both sides. Inner petals creamy white to whitish yellow, triangular-ovate, 12–17 by 7.5–9.5 mm, apex acute, hairy outside, glabrous, sometimes sparsely hairy at apex, inside. Stamens 42–52, oblong-elliptic to oblong, 0.8–1.2 mm long. Carpels 11–13, ovaries oblong, 2–3 mm long. Fruit of 2–6 monocarps borne on a pedicel 15–20 mm long. Monocarps yellow, ellipsoid, ovoid, ovoid-ellipsoid or globose, 1.5–3.5 by 1.5–2.3 cm, smooth, densely brown-hairy, with a longitudinal groove on one side, with 2–7 raised rings of transverse ridges on monocarp when dried, apex rounded, base contracted into a stipe 8–25 mm long. Seeds 2–8 per monocarp, ellipsoid-ovoid or reniform-ovoid, 8–15 by 5–8 mm.

description: Evergreen shrubs or small trees, with distichous primary branching. Indument of simple hairs. Sepals (2–)3, valvate, minutely connate at base, much shorter than petals, hairy outside, glabrous inside. Petals in two whorls of 3, or inner petals absent, valvate, free, outer petals erect to slightly spreading at anthesis, thickened, upper part on inner side flattened, bifacial to keeled, inner petals erect at anthesis, subequal or slightly shorter, narrower and sometimes with a clawed base, inner side bifacial to keeled in upper part. Stamens 15–88, innermost sometimes staminodial, anthers aseptate, anther connective apex apiculate or obtuse. Carpels few to many, stigmas U-shaped; ovules 2 per ovary, sub-basal, collateral. Receptacle convex. Fruit apocarpous, monocarps adaxially dehiscent, clavate, pubescent to glabrescent in age, smooth, often with an persistent apical beak, long-stipitate; pericarp thick, woody or leathery when dried. Seeds sub-basal or attached at base, 1–2 per monocarp, obovoid, asymmetrical, outer side convex, inner side flattened, pointed at base, smooth, shiny, black, perichalazal ring not evident, aril absent, endosperm ruminations oblique, irregularly ribbon-shaped.</br></br>A tropical genus unique in the family for the explosive dehiscence of its monocarps. description: Shrub to tree 2–8 m tall. Twigs greyish brown to brown, markedly to slightly angled in cross-section, sparsely hairy or glabrous. Leaves subcoriaceous to chartaceous, oblong, elliptic-oblong, elliptic, obovate or obovate-oblong, 8–20 cm by 3–8 cm, base slightly acute or rounded, apex obtuse to acuminate, the acumen 3–20 mm long, glabrous on both surfaces, midrib plane to slightly sunken above, secondary veins 6–12 per side; petioles 5–12 mm long, glabrous. Inflorescences terminal or leaf-opposed, 1–5-flowered, or plants cauliflorous, peduncles 3–10 mm long, pedicels 5–20 mm long; buds ovoid or globose. Sepals ovate or triangular-ovate, 4–6 mm long, obtuse to acute. Outer petals pale green to white, ovate-triangular or ovate, 12–25 mm by 8–14 mm, inner side varying from bifacial just below apex to bifacial or broadly keeled in upper third to upper half, slightly to strongly thickened toward apex, apex obtuse or acute, sparsely hairy to glabrous outside, glabrous inside. Inner petals present or absent (in var. tripetala), white, elliptic-rhomboid, 7–22 mm by 4–10 mm, inner side bifacial to broadly keeled in upper third, concave at middle part of inner side, apex acute to acuminate, glabrous on both surfaces. Stamens 37–88, spatulate, 2.5–4 mm long, plus 10–25 staminodes. Carpels 3–16, ovaries oblong or linear-oblong, 1.7–2 mm long. Fruit of 1–16 monocarps borne on a pedicel 10–20 mm long. Monocarps brown to blackish brown at maturity, 2.5–3.5 cm by 0.7–1 cm, persistent apical beak straight, 0.1–0.8 mm long, sometimes absent in var. tripetala, stipe 12–25 mm long, hairy. Seeds 1–2 per monocarp, obovoid, 10–13 mm by 6–8 mm.

description: Evergreen, semi-deciduous, or deciduous trees or shrubs, with distichous primary branching. Indument of simple hairs (in species occurring in Thailand). Leaves chartaceous to subcoriaceous, base symmetrical, cuneate to rounded, midrib plane or slightly sunken above, secondary venation eucamptodromous or brochidodromous, conspicuous or not, tertiary venation reticulate. Inflorescences terminal, leaf-opposed, or extra-axillary, 1–5-flowered, plants sometimes cauliflorous, pedicellar bract one, attached near pedicel base, caducous, minute, triangular. Flowers hermaphroditic, narrowly ovoid to ovoid or subglobose, rarely deltoid or subcordiform, in bud. Sepals 3, valvate, free, broadly ovate to ovate-triangular with acute apex, much shorter than outer petals. Petals in two whorls of 3, inner whorl of petals sometimes reduced or absent, valvate or imbricate, free or connate in a ring at base, ovate, narrowly ovate, or narrowly oblong, sometimes with a laterally flattened wing, basally concave. Stamens numerous, anthers aseptate, anther connective apex capitate, truncate, or apiculate. Carpels many, partially connate at base, stigmas clavate, tuberculate; ovule 1(–2) per ovary, basal. Receptacle conical or hemispherical. Fruits pseudosyncarpous, composed of fleshy receptacle and fleshy separate carpels secondarily grown together, pseudosyncarp ovoid to nearly globose, usually glabrescent and sometimes glaucous, surface divided into areoles representing the monocarp apices, these ornamented with knobs, bulges, or prickles, or less often smooth, monocarp bases sessile; pericarp juicy, white to orange and aromatic when fresh, thick, leathery or woody when dried. Seeds numerous per pseudosyncarp, one per monocarp, smooth, glabrous, perichalazal ring indistinct on surface, not raised or sunken, arillate ring encircling the micropyle usually present, endosperm ruminations lamellate, peg-shaped, or spiniform.</br></br>About 100 species with distinctive pseudosyncarpous fruits, most Neotropical with a few native to tropical Africa; 5 species have been introduced to Thailand, where they are cultivated for their edible fruits and have become naturalised in some areas.

description: Shrub or tree to 15 m tall, sometimes with buttresses; bark greyish brown to light brown, slightly rugose. Twigs light brown, reddish brown or grey, glabrous, lenticellate, shoot tip densely covered with golden brown hairs. Leaves chartaceous to subcoriaceous, elliptic or ovate, 7–18 by 5–8.5 cm, base broadly cuneate to rounded, apex acute, obtuse, or short-acuminate, the acumen 10–15 mm long, glossy green and glabrous above, light green and glabrous below, secondary veins brochidodromous, 7–12 per side, conspicuous above; petioles 10–25 mm long, glabrous. Inflorescences leaf-opposed or extra-axillary, 1-flowered, peduncle up to 20 mm long, pedicels 15–20 mm long, glabrous; buds ovoid or subglobose. Sepals light green, broadly ovate to ovate-triangular, 3–5 mm long, acute, both sides glabrous. Petals in two whorls of 3, free, cream to yellowish cream, red or purple toward the base inside. Outer petals fleshy, valvate, broadly ovate, 15–30 by 13–25 mm, base cordate, apex acute to acuminate, glabrous outside, minutely puberulent inside. Inner petals slightly thinner than outer petals, valvate, ovate or ovate-elliptic, 15–25 by 7–15 mm, base incurved-cuneate, apex acute to slightly obtuse, glabrous on both surfaces. Stamens numerous, oblong, 3–4 mm long, anther locules unequal, anther connective apex truncate. Carpels numerous, linear or oblong, ca 3 mm long, glabrous. Receptacle conical or hemispherical. Pseudosyncarp borne on a pedicel up to 30 mm long, yellow when mature, ovoid, 5–12 by 5–8 cm, smooth, glossy and glabrous, with faint reticulate pattern formed by monocarp boundaries. Seeds ovoid, obovoid or ellipsoid, 11–15 by ca 10 mm, pale brown to brown, shiny.

description: Tree up to 15 m tall; bark (dark) greyish brown, rugose. Twigs (dark) brown, glabrous, lenticellate, shoot tip densely covered with golden brown hairs. description: Evergreen woody climbers, sometimes bearing thorns arising on axillary shoots, with spiral primary branching. Indument of simple hairs. Leaves membranous to coriaceous, base symmetrical or asymmetrical, cuneate, rounded or decurrent on petiole, midrib raised or plane above, secondary venation brochidodromous to weakly brochidodromous, tertiary venation reticulate, rarely subpercurrent. Inflorescences leaf-opposed, 1–many-flowered, floral buds sometimes remaining dormant for a prolonged period, peduncles often recurved and laterally compressed to form hooks (sometimes reduced), with distal branches bearing the flowers arising from them. Flowers hermaphroditic, ovoid in bud. Sepals 3, valvate, free, usually much shorter than the petals. Petals in two whorls of 3, valvate, free, subequal, divided into a laminar, triquetrous, or terete blade and a concave claw, the latter connivent over the stamens and carpels, blades (if laminar) elliptic, obovate, ovate, lanceolate, deltate, rhombic or linear, outer petal claw densely puberulent outside but glabrous inside, inner petals coherent and abscising as a single unit. Stamens numerous, anthers aseptate, anther connective apex apiculate or truncate. Carpels 2 to many, stigmas cylindrical, rarely clavate or fan-shaped; ovules 2 per ovary, basal, collateral. Receptacle flattened or slightly hemispherical. Fruits apocarpous, monocarps indehiscent, few to many, ellipsoid, obovoid, or ovoid, glabrous or pubescent, smooth or wrinkled, stipitate or sessile; pericarp thick, leathery when dried, or thin, membranous when dried. Seeds basal and collateral, 1–2 per monocarp, ellipsoid (if 1 per monocarp) or plano-convex (if 2 per monocarp), smooth or wrinkled, glabrous, black to brown, perichalazal ring raised or sunken, aril rudimentary, endosperm ruminations lamellate.</br></br>A Palaeotropical genus of climbers with peduncular hooks, comprising about 110 species from Africa to Australia, represented in Thailand by 20 species, one, Artabotrys hexapetalus (L. f.) Bhandari, is a widely cultivated introduction.

description: Evergreen or deciduous trees or shrubs, with spiral primary branching. Indument of simple hairs. Leaves chartaceous, elliptic, ovate to sub-rotund, often asymmetrical at base, midrib raised on both sides, more prominent below, secondary veins somewhat parallel, brochidodromus, tertiary venation more or less percurrent. Inflorescences axillary, leaf-opposed, or internodal, 1–6-flowered, fascicled or short-pedunculate. Flowers hermaphroditic, petals separating early in development. Sepals 3(–4), valvate, connate at very base or free, much shorter than petals. Petals in two whorls of 3, rarely up to 24, valvate, free, oblong, lanceolate to linear, subequal or inner petals slightly smaller, veins prominent. Stamens numerous, anthers aseptate, anther connective apex conical. Carpels many; ovules up to 4 per ovary, biseriate. Receptacle slightly convex, sometimes with slightly concave apex. Fruits apocarpous, monocarps indehiscent, ellipsoid, ovoid or subglobose, glabrous, smooth, stipe articulated at the apex; pericarp thin, membranous when dried. Seeds attached laterally in 2 rows, several per monocarp, ellipsoid, flattened, smooth, glabrous, brown, perichalazal ring raised or not visible, arillate, endosperm ruminations lamellate.</br></br>A genus of 2 species known for its fragrant flowers, distributed across tropical Asia to NE Australia; both species are present in Thailand, and Cananga odorata is widely cultivated.

description: Evergreen trees, with spiral primary branching. Indument of simple hairs. description: Evergreen small trees or rarely climbers, with distichous primary branching. Indument of simple hairs. Leaves chartaceous to coriaceous, often glaucous below, base (slightly) attenuate, cordate or rounded, symmetrical, midrib plane or slightly sunken above, secondary venation brochidodromous, tertiary venation percurrent. Inflorescences axillary, 1-flowered. Flowers hermaphroditic, conical in bud. Sepals 3, much shorter than outer petals, valvate, free. Petals in one (outer) whorl of (2–)3, valvate, free, triangular, ovate, elliptic or lanceolate, apically connivent forming a mitriform dome over reproductive organs, creating a pyramidal floral chamber, often with very small basal apertures between petals, inner petals absent. Stamens numerous, anthers aseptate, anther connective truncate, rounded or apiculate. Carpels numerous, stigmas discoid or bilobed, ovaries densely hairy; ovules 1 to many per ovary, lateral. Receptacle shallowly conical with flat apex. Fruits apocarpous, monocarps indehiscent, moniliform (≥ 2-seeded) or ellipsoid (1-seeded), glabrous to densely hairy, smooth, stipitate; pericarp thin, membranous when dried. Seeds attached laterally, up to 8 per monocarp, globose or ellipsoid, glabrous, yellow, red or brown, perichalazal ring plane to slightly raised, aril absent, endosperm ruminations lamellate.</br></br>About 30 species, throughout tropical and subtropical Asia, the flower petals remaining appressed at maturity; 12 species in Thailand.

description: Evergreen trees, with spiral primary branching. Indument of simple hairs, rarely stellate. Leaves chartaceous-subcoriaceous to subcoriaceous, narrowly elliptic, elliptic or elliptic-oblong, base wedge-shaped, obtuse, rounded or subcordate, symmetrical, midrib sunken above, secondary venation rather conspicuous, tertiary venation percurrent. Inflorescences axillary or from axils of fallen leaves, 1–many-flowered. Flowers hermaphroditic, globose to ellipsoid in bud, petals separating late in development. Sepals 3, valvate or imbricate, free, slightly overlapping at the base, or connate, much shorter than petals, persistent in fruit. Petals in two whorls of 3, valvate, free, heart-shaped, ovate or oblong, the inner petals slightly smaller than the outer petals. Stamens 9–11, 14 or 50–56, anthers aseptate, anther connective apex truncate. Carpels 1–2, stigmas enlarged and more or less peltate; ovules 3–10, lateral, uniseriate or biseriate. Receptacle flat to elevated. Seeds 2 to 9 per monocarp, in one or two rows, flattened-ellipsoid or ellipsoid, flattened-D-shaped or D-shaped, more or less brown when dried, surface transversely striate, perichalazal ring nearly plane to raised, aril absent, endosperm ruminations lamellate.</br></br>A tropical Asian genus of 3 species in the Malay Peninsula and Sumatra; represented in Thailand by 1 species.

description: Evergreen woody climbers or scandent shrubs, with distichous primary branching. Indument of simple hairs. Leaves membranous to subcoriaceous, often glaucous below, usually oblong, lanceolate, or elliptic, symmetrical with a pair of linear marginal glands at base, midrib sunken or plane, secondary veins somewhat parallel, curving toward the margin but not clearly brochidodromous, tertiary venation percurrent or reticulate. Inflorescences supra-axillary, leaf-opposed, or extra-axillary, rarely axillary or terminal, 1-flowered (in Thai species). Flowers hermaphroditic, petals separating early in development. Sepals 3, much shorter than petals, valvate, free. Petals in two whorls of 3, valvate, free, lanceolate, elliptic, or oblong, occasionally oblanceolate to obovate, often undulate along the margins, outer petals slightly longer and wider than inner petals, venation raised or impressed, base of inner petals tightly compressed and enclosing reproductive organs. Stamens numerous, anthers aseptate, anther connective apex truncate or rounded. Carpels numerous, stigmas globose or clavate; ovules up to 8, attached laterally in a single row. Receptacle cushion-shaped. Fruits apocarpous, monocarps indehiscent, cylindrical, moniliform (≥ 2 seeds) or ellipsoid (1 seed), glabrous or pubescent, smooth, stipitate; pericarp thin, membranous when dried. Seeds attached laterally in a single row, up to 8 per monocarp, smooth, glabrous, brown, perichalazal ring plane, indistinct, aril absent, endosperm ruminations lamellate.</br></br>About 30 species of woody climbers, distinguished by basal leaf glands and moniliform monocarps, distributed throughout tropical Asia to N Australia. description: Evergreen small trees or shrubs, primary branching pattern unknown. Indument of simple hairs. Leaves chartaceous to subcoriaceous, oblanceolate to elliptic, cuneate, short-decurrent, and symmetrical at base, venation indistinct, midrib plane above, secondary veins indistinct, arcuate or diverging at irregular angles, tertiary venation reticulate. Inflorescences terminal, 1–3-flowered. Flowers hermaphroditic, petals separating early in development. Sepals 3 (in Thai species), valvate or somewhat imbricate, free, shorter than petals. Petals in two whorls of 3, valvate or slightly imbricate, free (in Thai species), oblanceolate to panduriform, the outer petals slightly longer and wider than the inner petals. Stamens numerous, anthers aseptate, anther connective apex depressed-globose. Carpels up to 200, stigmas narrowly oblong, obtuse at the apex; ovules 1–3, uniseriate. Receptacle cushion-shaped. Fruits apocarpous, monocarps indehiscent, ellipsoid, stipe articulated at the apex; pericarp thin, membranous when dried. Seeds attached laterally in 1 row, up to 3 per monocarp, ellipsoid or flattened-ellipsoid, smooth, glabrous, brown and shiny, perichalazal ring slightly raised, aril absent, endosperm ruminations lamellate.</br></br>Nine species in tropical and subtropical Asia, represented in Thailand by a single species. description: Evergreen trees, with spiral primary branching. Indument of stellate hairs (rarely simple). Leaves papyraceous to coriaceous, elliptic or oblong, base cuneate, rounded or cordate, symmetrical or asymmetrical, midrib plane or sunken above, secondary venation brochidodromous, tertiary venation percurrent. Inflorescences supra-axillary, 1–8-flowered. Flowers hermaphroditic, ovoid or conical in bud. Sepals 3, valvate, free, (slightly) shorter than petals. Petals in two whorls of 3, valvate, free, oblong, linear, ovate, elliptic or lanceolate, (sub-)equal in length, similar in shape, broad at base but constricted above and enclosing reproductive organs. Stamens numerous, anthers aseptate, anther connective apex truncate, dilated. Carpels (1–)2–32, glabrous or pubescent; stigmas ellipsoid or obconical; ovules many per ovary, 1–2-seriate. Receptacle flat or elongated. Fruits apocarpous, monocarps indehiscent, ovoid, ellipsoid, or cylindrical, sometimes constricted between seeds, glabrous or pubescent, smooth or verrucose; pericarp of variable thickness, leathery or woody; stipes present or absent. Seeds attached laterally in 1–2 rows, few to numerous per monocarp, ovoid, flattened-ovoid, or lenticular, smooth, pitted, or wrinkled, glossy or matt, light to deep brown, perichalazal ring plane or sunken, rarely raised, aril absent (except in D. pruniferus), endosperm ruminations peg-like (sometimes spiniform).</br></br>Twenty-six species, distributed throughout tropical Asia and in the W Pacific; 1 species in Thailand. The Thai species has a monopodial habit with lateral branches resembling compound leaves, the “phyllomorphic ramuli” of Corner (Ann. Bot., n. s., 13: 392, 1949).

description: Evergreen woody climbers, branches often flexuous and wrapping around adjacent supports, with distichous primary branching. Indument of simple hairs. Leaves chartaceous to coriaceous, occasionally glaucous below, elliptic, oblong, or oblanceolate, occasionally ovate or obovate, base symmetrical, cuneate, rounded, or subcordate, midrib plane or sunken above, secondary veins usually conspicuous, parallel and barely joining near leaf margin, tertiary venation weakly to strongly percurrent. Inflorescences terminal, usually leaf-opposed, rarely axillary, 1–20-flowered, pedicels arising from a short common peduncle (fasciculate) or an extended rachis (racemose). Flowers hermaphroditic, ovoid to conical in bud. Sepals 3, valvate, slightly connate at base or free, much shorter than petals. Petals in two whorls of 3, valvate, free, lanceolate to ovate, the inner petals slightly shorter, narrower, and more acute than the outer petals, at anthesis the outer petals spreading or reflexed and the inner petals erect with the tips slightly spreading to form a narrow aperture. Stamens numerous, anthers aseptate, anther connective apex acute to rounded, sometimes tongue-shaped. Carpels 10–20, stigmas narrowly oblong to clavate, truncate, bilobed, or bifurcate at the apex; ovules 2 to many per ovary, biseriate. Receptacle elevated, truncate. Fruits apocarpous, monocarps indehiscent, globose, ellipsoid, obovoid, or oblongoid, glabrous or pubescent, often marked by bumps and ridges, stipitate; pericarp thick, leathery or woody when dried. Seeds attached laterally in 1–2 rows, up to 13 per monocarp, semicircular, wedge-shaped in cross-section, smooth, glabrous, shiny, brown, reddish brown, or black, perichalazal ring not evident, aril absent but a light-coloured ring encircling the micropyle often present, endosperm ruminations lamellate.</br></br>A genus of over 60 species, distributed across tropical and subtropical Asia. Twelve species are confirmed for Thailand, but the genus remains poorly known, as the plants are woody climbers flowering in the canopy. Collectors often comment on the sweet fragrance of the flowers.

description: Woody climber to 15 m high. Twigs brown-pubescent, eventually glabrate. Leaves chartaceous, oblong to elliptic, occasionally oblong-ovate or oblanceolate-elliptic, 7.7–22 by 3.3–7.5 cm, base cuneate to rounded, apex acute to obtuse or rounded, occasionally retuse or short-acuminate, glabrous or with a few hairs on the midrib above, erect-pubescent below, secondary veins 11–20 per side, tertiary venation prominent below, irregularly percurrent; petioles 5–16 mm long, of even thickness from midpoint to leaf blade. Inflorescences terminal on young shoots, eventually leaf-opposed, 1–6-flowered, peduncle ca 1 mm long, pedicels 2–7.5 mm long, bearing 2 bracts up to 5.5 mm long; buds broadly conic-ovoid. Sepals broadly ovate to triangular, coriaceous, 2.8–4 mm long, obtuse, pubescent. description: Evergreen woody climbers or scandent shrubs, rarely shrubs or treelets, often with twigs forming loops around supports, with distichous primary branching. Indument of simple hairs. Leaves chartaceous to coriaceous, frequently glaucous below, base symmetrical with a pair of linear marginal glands near petiole, midrib sunken above, secondary venation conspicuous, tertiary venation percurrent. Inflorescences internodal to leaf-opposed, occasionally supra-axillary, 1(–2)-flowered. Flowers hermaphroditic, conical in bud. Sepals 3, valvate or rarely imbricate at base, free or sometimes basally connate, much shorter than outer petals, often persistent in fruit. Petals in two whorls of 3, valvate, free, outer petals long and narrow, spreading at anthesis, inner petals much shorter than outer petals, connivent to form a pyramidal cone over the stamens and carpels, each petal with a short broad claw. Stamens numerous, anthers aseptate, anther connective apex truncate to ovoid. Carpels 9–20, stigmas globose or clavate; ovules 1(–2), basal(–lateral). Receptacle conical. Fruits apocarpous, monocarps indehiscent, ellipsoid, oblongoid, or ovoid, smooth or finely verrucose, glabrous or pubescent, stipitate; pericarp thin, membranous when dried. Seed(s) attached basally, 1(–2) per monocarp, often difficult to separate from pericarp, ellipsoid, smooth, glabrous, light brown, perichalazal ring evident as a thin line, aril absent, endosperm ruminations lamellate.</br></br>About 45 tropical Asian species of climbers with basal leaf glands and strong smelling flowers. There are 16 species in the Thai flora.

description: Evergreen trees, with distichous primary branching. Indument of simple hairs. Leaves papyraceous to coriaceous, attenuate, cuneate or rounded and symmetrical at base, midrib plane or sunken above, secondary venation brochidodromous, tertiary venation reticulate to percurrent. Inflorescences axillary or very slightly internodal on young growth, or from woody tubercles on trunk or main branches, 1(2–4)-flowered. Flowers hermaphroditic, generally pendent, ovoid to ellipsoid in bud with outer petals often separating before maturity. Sepals 3, valvate, free or sometimes basally connate, shorter than outer petals. Petals in two whorls of 3, valvate, free, ovate, elliptic or lanceolate, outer petals longer than inner petals (rarely subequal), sometimes slightly clawed, inner petals basally clawed with blade much longer than claw, apically connivent over reproductive organs, forming a mitriform dome with 3 lateral apertures. Stamens numerous, anthers septate, connective apex truncate to apiculate. Carpels 4–ca 100, stigmas subulate, fusiform or funnel-shaped, sometimes enlarged; ovules 1–several, basal or lateral. Receptacle triangular at base. Fruits often with sepals persistent, apocarpous, monocarps indehiscent, subglobose to ellipsoid, sometimes moniliform, glabrous or pubescent, smooth or bumpy, generally stipitate; pericarp thin, membranous when dried, or thick, leathery or woody when dried. Seeds attached basally, or laterally in one row, 1–3(–10) per monocarp, often surrounded by mucilage, generally round to ellipsoid, smooth or slightly striate, glabrous to densely hairy, perichalazal ring raised, plane, or sunken, aril absent, endosperm ruminations lamellate.</br></br>About 130 species, throughout tropical and subtropical SE Asia and east to the W Pacific; 27 species in Thailand. The voucher specimen for the report of Goniothalamus saigonensis Pierre ex Finet & Gagnep. from Thailand by Craib (1925), Collins 914 from Prachin Buri, could not be located and its identity is unknown. The generic name refers to the angular base of the receptacle.

description: Evergreen or rarely deciduous shrubs, treelets or trees, with spiral primary branching. Indument of simple hairs. Leaves chartaceous to subcoriaceous, elliptic to obovate, base attenuate, cuneate, obtuse, or rarely (sub)cordate, symmetrical or seldom slightly asymmetrical, midrib sightly raised, flat, or sunken above, secondary veins inconspicuous to conspicuous, with hairy domatia often present at vein axils below, tertiary venation reticulate. Inflorescences axillary, sometimes from axils of fallen leaves, 1(–2)-flowered, rarely plants cauliflorous and then inflorescences > 3-flowered. Flowers hermaphroditic, petals separating early in development. Sepals 3, valvate, free or rarely basally connate, usually shorter than petals. Petals in two whorls of 3, valvate, free, whorls equal or subequal, ovate, elliptic to linguiform. Stamens generally more than 40, ± elongated wedge-shaped, anthers aseptate, anther connective apex truncate, covering tops of thecae. Carpels generally more than 10, stigmas ± globose, ellipsoid, obovoid, ellipsoid-ovoid or ellipsoid-cylindrical; ovule 1 per ovary, sub-basal. Receptacle flat to raised with flat-topped or rarely rounded apex. Fruits apocarpous, monocarps red, indehiscent, globose, ellipsoid, obovoid, or cylindrical, glabrous, smooth, stipitate or rarely (sub)sessile); pericarp thin. Seed sub-basally attached, 1 per monocarp, globose, ellipsoid, obovoid to cylindrical, smooth, glabrous, ± brown when dried, perichalazal ring plane or slightly raised, aril absent, endosperm ruminations spiniform.</br></br>A Palaeotropical genus of about 35 species segregated from Polyalthia, distributed from E Africa and Madagascar across tropical Asia and east to islands of the W Pacific; 2 species in Thailand.

description: Evergreen trees. Indument of simple hairs. Leaves coriaceous, elliptic-oblong to obovate, base cuneate to obtuse, symmetrical, midrib sunken above, secondary veins brochidodromous, forming a conspicuous intramarginal vein, tertiary venation percurrent. Inflorescences leaf-opposed or internodal, usually on leafless branches, 1–3-flowered. Flowers hermaphroditic, ellipsoid or ovoid in bud. Sepals 3, valvate, connate at base, shorter than petals. Petals in two whorls of 3, valvate, free, elliptic, ovate, obovate or oblong, subequal, spreading at anthesis, short-clawed at the base. Stamens numerous, anthers aseptate, anther connective apex truncate. Carpels 1–5, stigmas peltate or disc-shaped, lobed and slightly concave; ovules ca 10 per ovary, lateral, biseriate. Receptacle concave beneath the carpels. Fruits apocarpous, monocarps indehiscent, cylindrical, broadly ellipsoid, or globose, minutely pubescent, verrucose, sessile; pericarp thick, leathery, stony, or fleshy. Seeds attached laterally in 2 rows, ca 10 per monocarp, oblong, compressed, wrinkled, glabrous, dark brown, perichalazal ring raised into a distinct rib, aril absent, endosperm ruminations spiniform.</br></br>Four species, occurring in Peninsular Malaysia, Singapore, Sumatra, and Borneo; 1 species in Thailand.

description: Tree 15–30 m tall, crown conical with dense branching; bark blackish brown, smooth or shallowly cracked. Twigs pubescent to glabrescent. Leaves coriaceous, elliptic-oblong to obovate, 12–25 by 4–10 cm, base cuneate to obtuse, apex attenuate to acuminate, secondary veins 10–15 pairs, prominent below, tertiary venation percurrent; petioles ca 6 mm long. Inflorescences 1–3-flowered, pedicels ca 10 mm long. Sepals 1/2-connate, often spreading to slightly reflexed, ovate, ca 10 mm long, apex acute, puberulous on both surfaces. Petals greenish yellow, turning golden yellow to orange with age, erect to spreading, elliptic to obovate, sparsely pubescent on both surfaces except the base, which is densely pubescent outside and nearly glabrous inside; outer petals 40–60 by 20–40 mm; inner petals 38–58 by 18–38 mm. Stamens oblong, 1–2 mm long. Carpels 3–5, commonly 3, oblongoid-ellipsoid, appressed-pubescent. Fruit of up to 3 (–5) monocarps borne on a stout woody pedicel ca 10 mm long. Monocarps rusty brown, broadly ellipsoid to globose, 4–8 by 3–6 cm, verrucose, covered with velvety rusty brown hairs; pericarp ca 5 mm thick. Seeds ca 10 per monocarp, in 2 rows, oblong, compressed, 30–40 by 10–20 mm, dark brown, rough.

description: Evergreen or sometimes deciduous trees, with spiral primary branching. Indument of simple hairs. Leaves thinly chartaceous to coriaceous, pellucid dots present, oblong to elliptic, lanceolate, or oblanceolate, symmetrical at base, midrib slightly raised, plane, or sunken above, secondary veins more or less parallel, eucamptodromous or rarely brochidodromous, tertiary venation weakly to strongly percurrent or rarely reticulate. Inflorescences axillary or rarely supra-axillary, 1–many-flowered plants sometimes cauliflorous. Flowers hermaphroditic, ovoid to subglobose in bud. Sepals 3, valvate or imbricate, free, shorter than petals. Petals in two whorls of 3, valvate, free (in Thai species), linear, oblong, elliptic, lanceolate or ovate, erect or spreading, bases of inner petals in several species incurved over the stamens and sometimes with a short claw. Stamens numerous, anthers aseptate, anther connective apex truncate or slightly convex. Carpels 4–numerous, stigmas subglobose, obovoid, clavate or oblongoid, lower to higher than the anther connective apices; ovule 1, basal. Receptacle cushion-shaped, conical or convex, with a truncate or shallowly concave apex. Fruits apocarpous, monocarps indehiscent, fusiform, asymmetrically ellipsoid, ellipsoid, subglobose, sub-ovoid or oblongoid, glabrous, sparsely hairy, or tomentose, glaucous in some species, smooth or rugose, stipitate or rarely sessile; pericarp thin to thick, membranous or leathery when dried. Seed attached basally, 1 per monocarp, oblongoid, or ellipsoid, smooth, glabrous, brown and often shiny, perichalazal ring deeply sunken, aril absent, endosperm ruminations lamellate.</br></br>Comprising about 70 species, the genus is distributed across tropical and subtropical Asia to N Australia; 21 are recorded for Thailand. Two species groups occur, one with thin petals spreading at anthesis and red to purple monocarps, and the other, which includes the former genus Enicosanthum, with thick erect petals and green to yellow monocarps; the adnate bract on the pedicel is shared by both groups.

description: Tree up to 15 m tall, bark slightly rough, brown. Twigs glabrous with slightly conspicuous lenticels. description: Evergreen trees, with spiral primary branching. Indument of simple hairs. Leaves chartaceous to coriaceous, densely covered with minute papillae below, giving a whitened appearance, base cuneate to rounded, symmetrical, midrib sunken above, secondary veins indistinct, tertiary venation reticulate. Inflorescences axillary, 1–10-flowered, often forming tubercles, plants sometimes cauliflorous or ramiflorous. Flowers hermaphroditic, ovoid to narrowly ovoid in bud. Sepals 3, valvate, free, shorter than petals. Petals in two whorls of 3, valvate, free, subequal in size, (narrowly) oblong to strap-like, or oblong-ovate, flat, occasionally with a slight constriction toward base. Stamens numerous, anthers aseptate, anther connective apex truncate to slightly convex. Carpels many, oblong, glabrous to tomentose or densely puberulent, stigmas globose or slightly elongate; ovule 1 (rarely 2) per ovary, basal or sub-basal. Receptacle terete, hemispherical. Fruits apocarpous, monocarps indehiscent, ellipsoid or globose, glabrous, smooth, stipitate; pericarp thin. Seeds attached basally or sub-basally, 1(–2) per monocarp, ellipsoid or globose, smooth, glabrous, brown, perichalazal ring raised or slightly sunken, aril absent, endosperm ruminations spiniform or sometimes formed into narrow triangular plates.</br></br>A tropical Asian genus of about 6 species, distinct from other Polyalthia segregates in the fine indistinct secondary veins and whitened lower surface of the leaves; 2 species are reported for Thailand.

description: Tree up to 35 m tall; bark whitish or pale greyish brown, smooth, often encircled by raised, transverse rings, knee roots present on plants growing in swamp forest. Twigs whitish or pale greyish brown, smooth; shoot tip glabrous. Leaves subcoriaceous to coriaceous, elliptic, oblong-elliptic or (narrowly) obovate, 9–20 by 3–7 cm, base cuneate to rounded, apex acute to acuminate, the acumen up to 10 mm long, glossy green and glabrous above, whitened from dense papillae below, secondary veins indistinct, 15–30 per side; petioles 6–15 mm long, glabrous. Inflorescences axillary, 2–10-flowered, or plants cauliflorous or ramiflorous, pedicels 12–30 mm long, reddish green to maroon, glabrous, each bearing a single, minute, triangular, caducous bract below the pedicel midpoint; buds ovoid. Sepals light green or reddish, ovate-triangular, 2–2.5 mm long, acute, outside pubescent, inside glabrous. Petals greenish yellow to yellow, apex obtuse, both sides finely pubescent; outer petals (narrowly) oblong to strap-like, 10–20 by 3–5 mm; inner petals (narrowly) oblong to oblong-ovate, 10–17 by 2.5–4 mm. Stamens numerous, (broadly) obovate, oblong or obconical, ca 1 mm long, anther connective apex truncate to slightly convex. Carpels 8–10, ca 15 mm long, oblong, glabrous to slightly pubescent, ovule 1 per carpel. Fruit with pedicel 15–25 mm long. Monocarps 2–12 per fruit, reddish, purplish or blackish when mature, globose, ca 15 mm in diam., glossy, glabrous, stipe up to 15 mm long; pericarp fleshy, not adhering to seed when dried. Seeds globose, 11–15 mm in diam., slightly striate, brown, ring encircling seed visible but slightly sunken, endosperm ruminations spiniform, sometimes formed into narrow triangular plates.

description: Tree up to 30 m tall; bark whitish or pale yellowish, smooth. Twigs whitish or pale yellow, smooth; shoot tip glabrous. Leaves chartaceous to subcoriaceous, elliptic to narrowly elliptic, 6–11 by 2–3.5 cm, base cuneate, sometimes asymmetrical, apex acuminate, the acumen up to 12 mm long, glossy green and glabrous above, whitened from dense papillae below, secondary veins indistinct, 15–30 per side; petioles 6–10 mm long, glabrous. Inflorescences axillary or also borne on branches below leaves, tubercles absent or poorly developed, 1-flowered, peduncle much reduced, up to 1.8 mm long, pedicels 1–7.5 mm long, bract caducous, minute, triangular, attached below pedicel midpoint; buds ovoid. Sepals light green, triangular, 0.7–1.2 mm long, acute, outside densely tomentose, inside glabrous. Petals greenish yellow to yellow, apex obtuse, both sides finely pubescent; outer petals (narrowly) oblong to strap-like, 4–11 by 1–2.4 mm; inner petals (narrowly) oblong to strap-like, 4–12 by 0.8–1.9 mm. Stamens numerous, (broadly) obovate, oblong or obconical, 0.7–1.1 mm long, anther connective apex truncate to slightly convex. Carpels 3–9, 0.5–1.2 mm long, oblong, glabrous or slightly pubescent to densely pubescent, ovule 1 per carpel. Fruit with pedicel 10–15 mm long. Monocarps 1–5 per fruit, green and becoming reddish, purplish or blackish when mature, ellipsoid, ca 11–20 by 9–14 mm, glossy, glabrous, stipe 2–5 mm long; pericarp thin. Seed ellipsoid, 12–16 by 9–11 mm, slightly striate, pale brown, ring encircling seed visible and raised, endosperm ruminations needle-like, very fine.

description: Evergreen trees, with spiral primary branching. Indument of simple hairs. Leaves thinly coriaceous, linear or narrowly oblong, cuneate and symmetrical at base, apex acute or acuminate, midrib impressed above, secondary veins brochidodromous, tertiary venation reticulate. Inflorescences internodal, supra-axillary or leaf-opposed, sometimes arising from leafless twigs, 1–3-flowered. Flowers hermaphroditic, discoid in bud. Sepals 3, valvate, connate at base, shorter than petals. Petals in two whorls of 3, valvate, free, curved inward over the stamens and carpels, fleshy, broadly elliptic or oblong, apex acute or blunt, outer petals slightly smaller than inner petals. Stamens numerous, anthers aseptate, filament conspicuous, anther connective apex truncate or slightly convex. Carpels numerous, stigmas capitate, higher than anther connective apex, ovule 1 per ovary, basal. Receptacle cushion-shaped. Fruits apocarpous, monocarps indehiscent, oblongoid to oblongoid-ellipsoid, smooth, glabrous, stipitate; pericarp thin, membranous when dried. Seed attached basally, 1 per monocarp, oblongoid, smooth, glabrous, brown, shiny, perichalazal ring sunken, aril absent, endosperm ruminations spiniform.</br></br>A tropical Asian genus of 5 species, all with short thick concave petals; 1 species is reported for Thailand.

description: Treelet to 4 m tall, bark smooth. Twigs glabrous. Leaves chartaceous, narrowly elliptic to oblong, 11.5–18(–25) by 2.2–4(–5.5) cm, base cuneate, apex acute to acuminate, the acumen 6–10 mm long, glabrous on both surfaces, secondary veins 10–13 per side, indistinct below; petioles 3‒5 mm long, 1.8‒2 mm thick. Inflorescences 1–3-flowered, pedicels (3–)5‒7 mm long, each bearing 1 triangular bract at the base. Sepals triangular, 2–3 mm long, acute. Petals inwardly curved, green at anthesis, ovate, apex acute; outer petals 5–7 by 4‒5 mm; inner petals 6–8 by 5‒6 mm. Stamens numerous, oblong, 2.8–3 mm long, anther connective apex truncate or slightly convex. Carpels numerous, 0.8‒1.2 mm long, ovaries appressed-villous, stigmas more or less capitate, more expanded toward the apex. Fruit of up to 36 monocarps borne on a pedicel 8‒15 mm long. Monocarps red, oblongoid to oblongoid-ellipsoid, 15–20 by 8–10 mm, slightly wrinkled when dried, apex obtuse, apiculate, base contracted into a stipe 15–19 mm long. Seed oblong, 11–13 by 6–7 mm, slightly rugose when dried.

description: Evergreen trees or occasionally shrubs, with spiral primary branching. Indument of simple hairs. Leaves chartaceous, rarely subcoriaceous, elliptic to oblong, occasionally ovate or lanceolate, cuneate to rounded and symmetrical at the base, midrib plane or sunken above, secondary veins weakly brochidodromous, tertiary venation frequently percurrent. Inflorescences axillary or from axils of fallen leaves, 1–3-flowered, plants sometimes cauliflorous. Flowers hermaphroditic, conical to ovoid in bud but petals usually separating early in the bud stage. Sepals 3, imbricate or valvate at base, free or connate at base, much shorter than petals. Petals in two whorls of 3, valvate, free, often with the inner petals remaining loosely pressed together at anthesis, linear to ovate, occasionally elliptic or oblong, the inner petals slightly shorter and narrower than the outer, with a conspicuous glabrous patch of warty or corrugated tissue toward the base on the inner surface. Stamens numerous, anthers aseptate, anther connective apex truncate, sometimes sunken in the centre, obliquely elongated on stamens bordering the carpels. Carpels 1–17, stigmas globose to obovoid; ovules 3–16, attached laterally in 1–2 rows. Receptacle flat or slightly convex. Fruits apocarpous, monocarps indehiscent, oblongoid, ovoid, or cylindrical, occasionally ellipsoid or pyriform, slightly to strongly torulose, smooth or verrucose, usually pubescent, sessile or stipitate; pericarp thick or thin, membranous, woody or leathery when dried. Seeds attached laterally in 1–2 rows, up to 12 per monocarp, semicircular or elliptic in lateral view, usually flattened, smooth or slightly pitted, glabrous, perichalazal ring slightly sunken or raised, aril absent, endosperm ruminations lamellate or spiniform.</br></br>A genus of about 35 species distributed across tropical Asia, N Australia and the W Pacific, characterised by a warty to corrugated base on the inner petals; 8 species occur in Thailand.

description: Tree up to 20 m tall; bark dark brown, greyish brown or reddish brown, smooth to slightly rough. Twigs puberulent, soon glabrate. Leaves chartaceous, elliptic, oblong-elliptic, ovate, or oblanceolate, 7.5–20.3 by 2.5–6.3 cm, base cuneate to rounded, apex acuminate to caudate, the acumen 9–26 mm long, glabrous or with a few hairs on the secondary veins below, secondary veins arcuate, 7–11 per side, tertiary venation weakly percurrent; petioles 2.5–3 mm long. Inflorescences from axils of fallen leaves, 1(–2)-flowered, rarely plants cauliflorous, extended rachis absent, pedicels 5–7 mm long, 1–1.2 mm thick, pubescent, with 2–4 bracts on proximal half of pedicel; buds ovoid, slightly 3-angled in cross-section, apex acute. Sepals connate or slightly imbricate at base, reflexed, triangular, 3–4 mm long, acute. Petals pale tan-coloured to orange-brown, ovate to lanceolate, apex acute to obtuse; outer petals spreading at anthesis, 7–17 by 4.5–6.5 mm, finely pubescent on outer surface; inner petals erect to slightly spreading at anthesis, 6–11 by 4.5–5.3 mm, with a pale pink corrugated patch present on lower 1/2 of inner surface. Stamens cuneate to clavate, ca 0.7 mm long, anther connective apex truncate. Carpels 5–14, stigmas obconical, ca 0.8 mm long. Fruit of up to 14 monocarps borne on a pedicel ca 8 mm long. Monocarps green to brown, oblongoid, ovoid, or pyriform, not torulose or rarely weakly torulose, 2.4–4.4 by 1.9–2.5 cm, verrucose, velvety black to orange-brown-tomentose (hairs matted), apex obtuse, sometimes apiculate, base contracted into a stipe 9–18 by 4–6 mm, sometimes with a distal abscission ring along which the seed-containing portion breaks irregularly; pericarp ca 2 mm thick. Seeds in two rows, up to 10 per monocarp, flattened-ellipsoid, 13–15 by 10–13 mm, ring encircling seed slightly sunken.

description: Tree to 10 m tall; bark brown. Twigs with a mixture of long appressed hairs and short erect hairs, eventually glabrate. Leaves chartaceous, narrowly to broadly elliptic, 5.9–11 by 1.6–4 cm, base cuneate, apex narrowly acuminate, the acumen 9–11 mm long, glabrous except for short erect hairs on the midrib above, sparsely appressed-hirsute below, secondary veins arcuate, brochidodromous, 6–9 per side, tertiary venation indistinctly percurrent; petioles 2–6 mm long. Inflorescences axillary, 1-flowered, extended rachis absent, pedicels 2–4 mm long, with 1–2 small bracts near the base; buds ovoid, petals separating early. Sepals valvate, free, broadly ovate, 2.5–5 mm long, obtuse to acute. Petals yellowish orange; outer petals linear-lanceolate to lanceolate, 15–20 by 4–6 mm, subacute, pubescent on outer surface; inner petals lanceolate, ca 18 by 5 mm, with a light pink corrugated patch on the proximal 1/3 of inner surface, obtuse. Stamens cuneate, 1.5–2.5 mm long, anther connective apex truncate. Carpels 5–9, stigmas globose. Fruit of up to 4 monocarps borne on a pedicel ca 4 mm long. Monocarps green, cylindrical, slightly torulose, 1–2.7 by 0.7–0.9 cm, densely appressed-hirsute, apex often with a beak 4–8 mm long, base contracted into a stipe 3–5 mm long; pericarp thin. Seeds in a single row, up to 5 per monocarp, subglobose, ca 7 mm in diam., ring encircling seed raised.

description: Shrub or tree to 6 m tall. Twigs densely pubescent with persistent erect brown hairs. Leaves chartaceous, elliptic to oblong, 14.2–27.5 by 4.2–11.2 cm, base rounded, apex acuminate, the acumen 8–17 mm long, glabrous above, densely pubescent with erect hairs below, secondary veins more or less parallel, 11–16 per side, tertiary venation distinctly percurrent; petioles 4–7 mm long. Inflorescences borne on rachides 7.8–15 cm long emerging from the trunk, often near the base, branched, only a single flower maturing at a time at the end of each branch; pedicels 15–30 mm long, 1.2–1.3 mm thick, pubescent with erect hairs, with 2–5 lanceolate bracts up to 4.5 mm long attached along the proximal half of the axis; buds long-conical, apex obtuse. Sepals free or connate at base, lanceolate, 8–12 by 3.5–4 mm, caudate. Petals pale green, becoming red in vivo, linear-lanceolate, long-attenuate; outer petals slightly spreading at anthesis, at least 15–21 by 3.5–4.5 mm, ca 1 mm wide at midpoint, crisped-pubescent on outer surface; inner petals erect at anthesis, with small gaps between the bases, ca 17 by 4.5 mm, with a corrugated patch on proximal 1/8 of inner surface. Stamens many, narrowly cuneate, 1.5–2.5 mm long, anther connective apex truncate, slightly sunken in the middle, papillate. Carpels 5–6, stigmas globose, sparsely pubescent. Fruit of up to 6 monocarps borne on a pedicel ca 30 mm long. Monocarps irregularly oblong, weakly to strongly torulose, 3.4–3.9 by 1.3–1.7 cm, densely pubescent with erect brown hairs, apex rostrate, the beak 3–7 mm long, base rounded, sessile or contracted into a stipe 1–3 by 3 mm; pericarp thin. Seeds in a single row, up to 6 per monocarp, elliptic or semicircular in lateral view, flattened, 9–14 by 7–10 mm, ring encircling seed raised.

description: Tree up to 10 tall; trunk with stilt roots and aerial roots at the base to a height of 1 m, bark medium grey-brown, smooth. Twigs glabrate. Leaves chartaceous, elliptic to oblong-elliptic, 18–22.8 by 6–8.9 cm, base rounded to broadly cuneate, apex acuminate to caudate, the acumen 13–15 mm long, glabrous above, soon glabrate or with a few hairs below, secondary veins more or less parallel, 12–14 per side, tertiary venation weakly percurrent; petioles 6–8 mm long. Inflorescences borne on rachides emerging from the lower part of the trunk and plunging downward into the soil, the flowers arising from the inflorescence axis up to 3 m from the trunk, branching, with only a single flower maturing at a time at each shoot tip, pedicels 8.5–18 mm long, 0.8–1 mm thick, initially appressed-pubescent but soon glabrate, with 2–4 ovate bracts 2–4.5 mm long scattered along the axis; buds ovoid, apex acute, petals separating well before maturity. Sepals free, ovate, 3.5–4 by ca 3 mm, acute to slightly acuminate. Petals pink to red, lanceolate; outer petals spreading at anthesis, 12–20 by 4.5–7 mm, acute to attenuate-acute, crisped-pubescent on outer surface; inner petals erect at anthesis, 8.5–15 by 5–6 mm, acute to obtuse, with a corrugated patch on proximal 1/3 of inner surface. Stamens cuneate, 1.4–1.7 mm long, anther connective apex truncate, pubescent. Carpels ca 2, stigmas ovoid to globose, ca 1 mm long. Fruit and seeds unknown.

description: Tree up to 8 m tall. Twigs sparsely pubescent, soon glabrate. Leaves chartaceous, elliptic to oblong-elliptic, 13.5–24 by 4.8–9.8 cm, base rounded to broadly cuneate, apex narrowly acuminate, acumen 6–10 mm long, glabrous above, with a few hairs on the midrib and secondary veins below, secondary veins slightly arcuate, 8–11 per side, tertiary venation weakly percurrent; petioles 5–8 mm long. Inflorescences axillary or from axils of fallen leaves, 1-flowered, or rarely plants cauliflorous, extended rachis absent, pedicels 5–9 mm long, bearing 2 small bracts on proximal half of pedicel; buds not seen. Sepals connate at base, broadly ovate, 2.5–4 mm long, apex obtuse, recurved. Petals cream-coloured, obtuse; outer petals obovate, elliptic, or broadly lanceolate, 19–22 by 12–15 mm, sericeous on outer surface, inner petals broadly lanceolate, 17–18 by 7–9 mm, with a corrugated patch on proximal 1/4 of inner surface. Stamens ca 80, obconical to broadly clavate, 1–1.5 mm long, anther connective apex truncate, papillate. Carpels 3–4, stigmas obovoid, ca 1.3 mm long, densely pubescent. Fruit a single monocarp borne on a pedicel 8–10 mm long. Monocarps oblongoid, not torulose, 2.7–5.5 by 2.3–3.2 cm, wrinkled or smooth, pubescent with fine matted brown hairs, apex rounded, sessile; pericarp leathery. Seeds in two rows, ca 12 per monocarp, 12–17 mm long.

description: Tree up to 15 m tall; bark brownish white, brown-grey, or grey, smooth. Twigs densely pubescent with erect short brown hairs, eventually glabrate. Leaves chartaceous, elliptic, elliptic-oblong, or lanceolate-oblong, 25.6–34.5 by 5.7–9.8 cm, base cuneate to nearly rounded, apex acuminate, the acumen 12–26 mm long, glabrous above, sparsely pubescent with erect acicular hairs below, secondary veins ascending and parallel, 16–19 per side, tertiary venation distinctly percurrent; petioles 8–10 mm long. Inflorescences from axils of fallen leaves, 2–3-flowered, or plants sometimes cauliflorous, extended rachis absent, pedicels 4–7 mm long, pubescent, with 2 ovate bracts 2–4 mm long on proximal half of pedicel; buds lanceolate, but petals separating early. Sepals free or connate at base, ovate, 4–7 mm long, acute. Petals cream-coloured to light yellow, somewhat spreading at anthesis, linear, attenuate, acute, sericeous on outer surface; outer petals 29–35 by 5–6 mm; inner petals 26–27 by 4.5–5 mm, with a pink to purple corrugated patch on proximal 1/8 of inner surface. Stamens cuneate, ca 1 mm long, anther connective apex truncate. Carpels 4–6, stigmas clavate, pubescent. Fruit of up to 6 monocarps borne on a pedicel 11–15 mm long. Monocarps ovoid to oblongoid, 2–4.9 by 1.8–3.1 cm, slightly torulose or not torulose, rugose, densely covered with short erect brown hairs, apex rounded, sessile; pericarp ca 2.7 mm thick. Seeds in two rows, up to 11 per monocarp, semicircular in lateral view, slightly flattened, ca 22 mm by 11 mm, ring encircling seed slightly sunken.

description: Tree up to 20 m tall; bark pale grey, smooth. Twigs glabrous. Leaves chartaceous to subcoriaceous, elliptic-oblong, 7.5–17 by 4–5.5(–6.2) cm, base cuneate to broadly cuneate, apex broadly blunt-acuminate, the acumen 6–9 mm long, glabrous on both surfaces, secondary veins arcuate, 11–13 per side, tertiary venation reticulate; petioles 4–6 mm long. Inflorescences axillary, 1-flowered, extended rachis absent, pedicels (2–)5–10 mm long, with 3 small bracts proximal to the midpoint; buds ovoid, apex obtuse, petals separating early in bud. Stamens cuneate, 1–2 mm long, anther connective apex truncate, sometimes sunken in the centre. Carpels 3–12, stigmas clavate, ca 1.5 mm long. Fruit of up to 15 monocarps borne on a pedicel 7.5–10 mm long. Monocarps green to whitish green, cylindrical, slightly torulose, 2–2.8 by 0.8–0.9 cm, glabrous, apex obtuse to rounded, base contracted into a thick stipe 1.5–3 mm long; pericarp orange when fresh, thin, membranous. Seeds in two interdigitated rows, up to 8 per monocarp, broadly elliptic in lateral view, flattened, ca 9 by 7–8 mm, ring encircling seed sunken into a groove.

description: Shrub or tree up to 12.5(–15 m) tall; bark grey to brown-grey, smooth. Twigs puberulent, soon glabrate. Leaves chartaceous, elliptic, ovate, or sometimes oblong-elliptic, 9.8–22 by 4.5–9 cm, base broadly cuneate to rounded, apex acuminate, the acumen 7–15 mm long, pubescent along midrib on both surfaces but otherwise glabrate, secondary veins slightly arcuate, 7–15 per side, tertiary venation distinctly percurrent; petioles 5–9 mm long. Inflorescences axillary, 1-flowered, extended rachis absent, pedicels ca 3 mm long, with 2 small bracts; petals separating early in bud. Sepals free to minutely connate, broadly ovate, ca 5 mm long, acute to attenuate. Petals cream-coloured to pale brownish yellow, acute to obtuse; outer petals linear to linear-lanceolate, 13–17 by 2.5–3.5 mm, finely pubescent on outer surface; inner petals lanceolate, 9–10 by 3–3.5 mm, with a pink-red, purple, or brown corrugated patch on proximal 1/2 of inner surface. Stamens clavate, ca 1 mm long, anther connective apex truncate. Carpels 3–5, stigmas globose, ca 0.5 mm long. Fruit of up to 4 monocarps borne on a pedicel 3–5 mm long. Monocarps green, purplish, brown, or blackish yellow, oblongoid to ellipsoid, not torulose, 2.2–5.4 by 2.2–2.8 cm, grey- or brown-tomentose (hairs matted), apex rounded, sessile or rarely base contracted into a stipe up to 3 mm long; pericarp ca 3.5 mm thick, woody when dried. Seeds in two rows, 11–15 per monocarp, semicircular in lateral view, flattened, 15–20 by 10–11 mm, ring encircling seed raised as a ridge.

description: Evergreen trees, with distichous primary branching; buttresses small or absent. Indument of simple hairs. Leaves coriaceous to subcoriaceous, usually oblong or elliptic-lanceolate, base attenuate, obtuse, or cuneate and symmetrical, midrib sunken to slightly raised above, secondary veins prominent on both surfaces, brochidodromous, tertiary venation reticulate. Inflorescences axillary, 2–9-flowered, plants often ramiflorous. Flowers hermaphroditic, ovoid in bud. Sepals 3, valvate, free to short-connate at base, much shorter than petals. Petals in two whorls of 3(–4), valvate, free, (narrowly) elliptic, (narrowly) ovate to (narrowly) oblong, inner petals shorter than outer petals, elliptic to ovate. Stamens 9–18, arranged in 2 or 3 whorls, sometimes staminodial, anthers aseptate, anther connective apex truncate. Carpel 1, with a groove running from stigma to base, stigma flat to capitate or horseshoe-shaped; ovules 2 per ovary, lateral, uniseriate. Receptacle slightly concave or elevated, hairy. Fruit a single indehiscent monocarp, globose, ellipsoid, or obovoid, glaucous, smooth when young and becoming verrucose when mature, stipitate or sessile; pericarp thick, woody when dried. Seed(s) attached laterally in 1 row, (1–)2, ellipsoid, flattened on one side, smooth, glabrous, brown to black, seed coat thick and woody, perichalazal ring slightly raised, aril absent, endosperm ruminations lamellate.</br></br>About 5 tropical Asian species; 2 species are known from Thailand. The hard seeds, up to 50 mm long, are among the largest in the family.

description: Tree ca 18 m tall. Twigs nearly glabrous. Leaves coriaceous, elliptic, 5.5–8.1 by 2.3–3.6 cm, base cuneate, apex acute, acuminate, or obtuse-rounded, rarely retuse, glabrous on both surfaces, secondary veins ca 12 per side; petioles 5–8 mm long. Inflorescences axillary from the axils of fallen leaves, in fascicles of up to 6 flowers, peduncle inconspicuous, bracts few, ovate-elliptic; pedicels ca 6.5 mm long, lacking bracts. Sepals ca 1/5-connate at base, erect to slightly spreading, broadly triangular-ovate, ca 1.1 mm long, broadly acute, densely and minutely pubescent outside. Petals in two whorls of 3, bright green, coriaceous; outer petals elliptic, ca 4.2 by 2.8 mm, obtuse; inner petals obovate, ca 4 by 2.2 mm, acute to obtuse. Stamens 14–18 per flower, broadly clavate, ca 0.6 mm long. Carpel ca 1 mm long, ovaries glabrous, stigma flat. Receptacle slightly elevated, tomentose-villous with appressed and erect hairs between stamens. Fruit [ex Sinclair 1955] subglobose, 3.7–5 cm in diam., with waxy bloom, sessile. Seeds [ex Sinclair 1955] 2, oblong, sub-compressed, 20–50 mm long.

description: Tree 12–40 m tall. Twigs brown to dark brown, glabrous, lenticellate. Leaves coriaceous, oblong to elliptic-lanceolate, 6–17 by 2.5–3.5 cm, base attenuate to obtuse, apex attenuate to acuminate, margin often wavy, secondary veins 8–10 per side; petioles 5–10 mm long. Inflorescences axillary or from axils of fallen leaves, fascicled, (1–)2–4(–9) flowered, peduncle inconspicuous, pedicels 5–15 mm long with a minute bract at base. Sepals free, often reflexed, ovate, ca 3 by 2 mm, mucronate. Petals in two whorls of 3(–4), greenish yellow; outer petals lanceolate to linear-lanceolate, sometimes linear, 12–15 by 2–3 mm; inner petals ovate to oblong, 5–6 by 2–3 mm. Stamens (9–)12(–16), broadly clavate, ca 0.8 mm long. Carpel ca 0.2 mm long. Fruit a single monocarp borne on a thickened pedicel 10–20 mm long. Monocarp yellowish green or brownish cream when mature, ovoid to ellipsoid or rarely subglobose, 4–8 cm long, glaucous when immature, sessile; pericarp thick and hard when dried. Seeds 2, flattened-ellipsoid, 30–40 by ca 20 mm, smooth, black.
