description:
Evergreen or deciduous shrubs or trees, with spiral primary branching. Indument of simple hairs. Leaves usually petiolate, sessile in a few species, chartaceous to subcoriaceous, base narrowly to broadly cuneate, obtuse, rounded, subcordate or cordate, symmetrical or asymmetrical, sometimes clasping twigs, midrib flat or slightly sunken, seldom raised, secondary veins inconspicuous to conspicuous, tertiary venation reticulate or reticulate-percurrent. Inflorescences axillary, from axils of fallen leaves or terminal developing to internodal, 1–9-flowered, occasionally a pair of 1-flowered inflorescences arising from the same leaf axil, peduncle present or absent, sometime extending into a short rachis up to 19 mm long. Flowers hermaphroditic or rarely unisexual (staminate in M. thorelii), subglobose, ovoid, ellipsoid or triangular pyramidal in bud, sometimes depressed at the apex, inner petals separating at a late developmental stage. Sepals 3, valvate, free or basally connate, much shorter than inner petals. Petals in two whorls of 3, valvate, free, triangular, ovate, elliptic or linguiform; outer petals similar in size to sepals, inner petals much larger than outer petals, erect, spreading or reflexed, sometimes with conspicuous glandular structures inside, base sometimes ± saccate and occasionally with translucent areas. Stamens 3–232, sometimes staminodial, ± clavate, anthers aseptate, anther connective apex miliusoid (not covering anther thecae), acute to obtuse or rounded, sometimes nearly absent. Carpels 3–80; ovule(s) 1 to 12 per ovary, basal to lateral, uniseriate or biseriate. Receptacle nearly flat to elevated, variable in shape. Fruits apocarpous, monocarps indehiscent, globose, subglobose, ellipsoid, cylindrical or irregular-shaped, glabrous or seldom hairy, smooth to verruculose, apex rounded or apiculate, sessile or stipitate and the stipe often obliquely attached to seed-containing portion; pericarp thin and membranous when dried, in a few species moderately thick and ± woody when dried. Seeds attached basally or laterally in 1–2 rows, up to 9 per monocarp, globose, subglobose, ellipsoid or cylindrical, sometimes flattened, smooth, glabrous, ± brown when dried, perichalazal ring sunken, aril absent, endosperm ruminations lamellate.

An Asian genus of about 60 species, witgh 23 species, 11 of them endemic, Thailand is probably the centre of diversity for the genus. [Coordinator Note: The four species groups delineated by Chaowasku & Kessler (2013) are all illustrated: Fig. 36, Plates XIX: D, Plates XX: B, XXI: F‒G (Miliusa mollis group); Plate XX: A (M. horsfieldii group); Plates XX: C‒D, XXI: C‒D (M. velutina group); Fig. 37, Plates XIX: E‒F, XX: E‒G, XXI: A‒B, E (M. campanulata group)].

description: Shrub or treelet to 8 m tall, evergreen. Twigs puberulous-tomentose. Leaves chartaceous-subcoriaceous, obovate to elliptic, 9.3–26 by 4–11 cm, base cordate, moderately asymmetrical, often ± clasping twigs, apex acuminate to slightly caudate-acuminate, glabrous on upper surface, almost glabrous to puberulous on lower surface, secondary veins 12–18 per side, tertiary venation reticulate. Inflorescences axillary, 1–2-flowered, peduncles 1–3 mm long or absent, rachis absent, pedicels 7–18 mm long, each bearing 1–2 bract(s). Flowers hermaphroditic. Sepals connate at base, triangular, 1.3–1.5 mm long, apex ± acute. Outer petals triangular, 1.8–2 by 1.5–1.8 mm, apex ± acute. Inner petals greenish cream, chartaceous-subcoriaceous, completely separate, broadly ovate, 5–7.3 by 5–7.5 mm, apex ± acute, both sides of margin somewhat recurved at anthesis, base not saccate but with ± blackish brown glandular structures inside, thickened, between crescent-shaped and semicircular. Stamens 23–35, 0.8–1 mm long, anther connective apex acute-obtuse. Carpels 17–22, ovaries glabrous, stigmas capitate to clavate; ovule 1, basi-lateral. Receptacle hemispherical. Fruit of up to 15 monocarps borne on a pedicel up to 18 mm long. Monocarps purplish black, subglobose-ellipsoid, 0.7–0.8 by 0.6–0.7 cm, ± smooth, glabrous, apex rounded, base contracted into a stipe 3–5 mm long. Seed 1, subglobose-ellipsoid, 6.5–7.5 by 5.5–6 mm.

description: Shrub or treelet to 8 m tall, evergreen. Twigs glabrous. Leaves rather chartaceous, elliptic to slightly obovate, 7–23 by 2.3–6.3 cm, base cuneate to narrowly cuneate, symmetrical, apex acute, acuminate or caudate-acuminate, glabrous to almost glabrous on upper surface, glabrous on lower surface, secondary veins 8–18 per side, tertiary venation reticulate. Inflorescences axillary or in axils of fallen leaves, sometimes two inflorescences present in the same axil, 1–4-flowered, peduncles 1–3 mm long or absent, rachis ca 2 mm long or absent, pedicels 14–60 mm long, each bearing 1–3 bract(s). Flowers hermaphroditic. Sepals free, triangular to ovate-triangular, 1.5–2 mm long, apex ± acute. Outer petals ovate-triangular to narrowly ovate-triangular, 2–3 by 0.8–1 mm, apex ± acute. Inner petals with discolouration on basal half of inner petals (both sides) remarkably reticulate (much more clearly observed in living plants), chartaceous, usually tightly pressed together along margins from base to ± midpoint, ovate, 9.5–11.5 by 5–7.5 mm, apex acute, base slightly saccate, presence or absence of glandular structures undetermined, translucent window-like structures at base conspicuous (in living plants). Stamens 39–40, 1–1.3 mm long, anther connective apex obtuse to acute. Carpels ca 26, ovaries appressed-puberulous to appressed-villous, stigmas subglobose, ovoid, ovoid-ellipsoid to ellipsoid; ovule(s) 1(–2), basi-lateral, uniseriate when 2 ovules. Receptacle ± hemispherical to ellipsoid cylindrical. Fruit of up to 30 monocarps borne on a pedicel up to 60 mm long. Monocarps purplish black, ± subglobose, 0.7–0.9 by 0.6–0.8 cm, ± slightly verruculose, glabrous, apex rounded, base contracted into a stipe 10–20 mm long, sometimes attached obliquely to seed-containing portion. Seed(s) 1(–2), ± subglobose, sometimes slightly flattened, 6.5–7.5 by 5.5–7 mm.

description: Treelet to 1.5 m tall, evergreen. Twigs appressed-tomentose. Leaves rather chartaceous, elliptic to obovate-elliptic, 12.2–18 by 3.3–6 cm, base cuneate, symmetrical, apex caudate-acuminate, glabrous on both sides, secondary veins 9–12 per side, tertiary venation reticulate. Inflorescences axillary, sometimes two inflorescences present in the same axil, 1-flowered, peduncle and rachis absent, pedicels (11–)14–22(–30) mm long, each bearing 3–4 bracts. Flowers hermaphroditic. Sepals free, ovate, 1.5–2 mm long, apex acute. Outer petals triangular-ovate, 1.5–2 by 1 mm, apex acute. Inner petals light green, with red-purple reticulation toward base, chartaceous, usually tightly pressed together along margins from base to ± midpoint, base slightly saccate, presence or absence of glandular structures undetermined, with translucent window-like structures, elliptic, 15–18 by 7–8.5 mm, apex broadly acute, obtuse, or rounded, with apical half strongly recurved. Stamens 48–50, 1–1.5 mm long, anther connective apex nearly absent. Carpels 49–71, ovaries appressed-puberulous, stigmas horseshoe-shaped; ovule 1, sub-basal. Receptacle ovoid. Fruit of up to 6 monocarps borne on a pedicel up to 30 mm long. Monocarps green (immature), subglobose, 0.95–1.1 by 0.9–0.95 cm, smooth, glabrous, apex rounded, base contracted into a stipe 11–18 mm long. Seed 1, subglobose, ca 8.5 by 7.5 mm.

description: Shrub or treelet to 4 m tall, evergreen. Twigs ± tomentose. Leaves chartaceous, elliptic to narrowly elliptic, 7.5–17.5 by 2.3–5.5 cm, base cuneate to narrowly cuneate, symmetrical, apex acuminate to caudate-acuminate, glabrous on upper surface, almost glabrous to villous on lower surface, secondary veins 11–18 per side, tertiary venation reticulate. Inflorescences axillary or in axils of fallen leaves, 1–2-flowered, peduncles ca 2 mm long or absent, rachis absent, pedicels 15–60 mm long, each bearing 1–3 bract(s). Flowers hermaphroditic. Sepals free, ovate-triangular to narrowly ovate-triangular, 1.5–3 mm long, apex ± acute. Outer petals narrowly triangular, 4–6 by 0.8–1 mm, apex acute-acuminate. Inner petals yellowish green, with reticulate discolouration on basal half, chartaceous, usually tightly pressed together along margins from base to ± midpoint, ovate, 10–21 by 6–12 mm, apex acute to sub-acute, base moderately saccate, presence or absence of glandular structures undetermined, with translucent window-like structures. Stamens 34–52, 0.8–1.2 mm long, anther connective apex obtuse to rounded. Carpels 32–50, ovaries puberulous-tomentose, sometimes hairs also appressed, stigmas ± ellipsoid to terete; ovule(s) 1(–2), lateral to basi-lateral, uniseriate when 2 ovules. Receptacle short-cylindrical, apex sub-acute to rounded. Fruit of up to 50 monocarps borne on a pedicel up to 60 mm long. Monocarps dark purple, subglobose to ellipsoid, 0.7–1.1 by 0.6–0.7 cm, ± slightly verruculose, glabrous, apex sometimes apiculate, base contracted into a stipe 6–12 mm long, often obliquely attached to seed-containing portion. Seed(s) 1(–2), subglobose to ellipsoid, sometimes slightly flattened, 6.5–10 by 5.5–6 mm.

description: Shrub or treelet to 10 m tall, evergreen. Twigs glabrous to almost glabrous. Leaves rather chartaceous, obovate, elliptic or narrowly elliptic, 5–22.5 by 2–8 cm, base broadly to narrowly cuneate, symmetrical, apex acuminate to caudate-acuminate, sometimes ± caudate-acute, glabrous on both surfaces, secondary veins 8–13 per side, tertiary venation reticulate. Inflorescences axillary, 1-flowered, peduncle and rachis absent, pedicels 19–52 mm long, each bearing 2–3 bracts. Flowers hermaphroditic. Sepals free, ovate-triangular to broadly ovate-triangular, 1–2 mm long, apex acute. Outer petals ovate-triangular, 1.5–2.5 by 0.7–1.5 mm, apex acute. Inner petals ± yellow, ± pink-red discolouration on basal half of inner petals (more clearly visible inside) not (or very slightly) reticulate (much more clearly visible in living plants), chartaceous, usually tightly pressed together along margins from base to ± midpoint, ovate-elliptic to narrowly ovate-elliptic, 12–16 by 5–8 mm, apex acute-obtuse, base moderately saccate, presence or absence of glandular structures undetermined, window-like structures at base indistinct (in living plants, sometimes absent). Stamens ca 39, ca 1 mm long, anther connective apex obtuse. Carpels ca 19, ovaries appressed-pilose, stigmas ± ellipsoid; ovules 2, lateral, uniseriate. Receptacle hemispherical-subglobose. Fruit of up to 26 monocarps borne on a pedicel up to 52 mm long. Monocarps bright red, subglobose to ellipsoid, sometimes irregularly shaped, 0.7–1.3 by 0.6–0.8 cm, ± smooth, glabrous, apex rounded or slightly apiculate, base contracted into a stipe 17–30 mm long. Seed(s) 1(–2), subglobose to ellipsoid, sometimes slightly flattened, 6–9 by 5–7 mm.

description: Shrub or tree to 15 m, semi-deciduous to deciduous. Twigs velvety, hairs sometimes appressed, bud scales present, obvious, covering vegetative buds. Leaves chartaceous, ± subsessile, elliptic, sometimes slightly ovate or slightly obovate, 2.7–9 by 1.7–3.2 cm, base cuneate to rounded, usually slightly asymmetrical, apex acute to slightly acuminate, glabrous on upper surface, glabrous to almost glabrous on lower surface, secondary veins 12–15 per side, tertiary venation reticulate. Inflorescences axillary on new sprouting shoots, 1-flowered, peduncle and rachis absent, pedicels 4–15 mm long, each bearing 2 bracts. Flowers hermaphroditic. Sepals slightly connate at base, triangular, ca 1.2 by 1 mm, apex ± acute. Outer petals ovate-triangular, ca 1.9 by 1.1 mm, apex ± acute. Inner petals greenish yellow, chartaceous-subcoriaceous, completely separate, ovate-triangular, 3–3.4 by 2.5–3.1 mm, densely hairy inside (mostly near margin and on apical half), apex ± acute-obtuse, base not saccate but with greenish yellow glandular structures inside, slightly thickened, ± semicircular. Stamens ca 16, ca 0.8 mm long, anther connective apex nearly absent. Carpels 2–5, ovaries glabrous, stigmas ellipsoid; ovule 1, subbasal. Receptacle ovoid-ellipsoid. Fruit of up to 3 monocarps borne on a pedicel up to 15 mm long. description: Shrub or treelet to 6 m tall, evergreen. Twigs puberulous-velvety to velvety. description: Shrub or treelet to 6 m tall, evergreen. Twigs glabrous to almost glabrous. description: Tree to 20 m tall, deciduous. Twigs tomentose-villous. description: Evergreen woody climbers, with distichous primary branching. Indument of simple hairs. Leaves chartaceous to subcoriaceous, base cuneate to rounded, midrib slightly sunken above, secondary venation indistinct, brochidodromous, tertiary venation reticulate. Inflorescences axillary, sometimes with a vegetative shoot growing out from the same axil, 1–2-flowered. Flowers hermaphroditic, obovoid to ellipsoid and strongly three-angled in bud. Sepals 3, valvate, connate at the base, much smaller than outer petals. Petals in two whorls of 3, valvate, free, fleshy, ovate, ovate-lanceolate, or elliptic, spreading at anthesis, concave at the base, inner petals shorter than the outer petals, forming a dome over the centre of the flower. Stamens numerous, anthers aseptate, anther connective apex capitate. Carpels numerous, stigmas filiform, lanceolate, or oblong; ovules up to 8 per ovary, lateral, biseriate. Receptacle cushion-shaped, truncate at apex. Fruits apocarpous, monocarps indehiscent, globose to ovoid, glabrous, smooth, stipitate; pericarp thin, membranous when dried. Seeds attached laterally, interdigitated to form a single row, up to 5 per monocarp, circular, flattened, pitted, black, shiny, perichalazal ring slightly raised, aril absent, endosperm ruminations spiniform, slightly flattened.</br></br>About 8 tropical Asian species of climbers with strongly three-angled buds; 1 species in Thailand.

description: Woody climber to ca 10 m. Twigs glabrous, or sparsely fine-puberulent and soon glabrate. description: Evergreen trees, with spiral primary branching. Indument of simple hairs. Leaves coriaceous (rarely papyraceous), ovate, elliptic or lanceolate, base symmetrical, midrib slightly sunken or plane above, secondary venation brochidodromous, tertiary venation reticulate. Inflorescences terminal or leaf-opposed (later becoming extra-axillary), 1–3-flowered, sometimes elongated and forming a rachis. Flowers hermaphroditic; buds broadly depressed-ovoid. Sepals 3, valvate, ± basally connate, shorter than petals. Petals in two whorls of 3, valvate, free, outer petals generally larger than inner, not clawed; inner petals 3, basally clawed, apically connivent over reproductive organs, forming a mitriform dome with 3 lateral apertures, petal glands absent. Stamens numerous, anthers aseptate, anther connective apex truncate, dilated. Carpels few to numerous, stigmas narrowly obconical; ovules lateral, biseriate, 2–18 per ovary. Receptacle cushion-shaped. Fruits apocarpous, monocarps indehiscent, 2–22 per fruit, subglobose, obovoid or oblongoid, pubescent, smooth or rarely warty, sometimes with a longitudinal ridge, sessile or stipitate; pericarp of variable thickness. Seeds attached laterally in 2 rows, 1–14 per monocarp, semi-lenticular (lowermost and uppermost within monocarp) or discoid (others), transversely striate and pitted, glabrous, light brown to dark brown, perichalazal ring shallowly sunken, aril absent, endosperm ruminations spiniform.</br></br>About 50 species of trees with showy, often multi coloured, flowers, distributed throughout tropical and subtropical S & SE Asia and Australia (Queensland); 11 species in Thailand.

description: Evergreen trees, with spiral primary branching. Indument of intermixed stellate and simple hairs. Leaves chartaceous to subcoriaceous, base obtuse, cuneate, or broadly cuneate, symmetrical, midrib slightly sunken above, secondary veins rather conspicuous, tertiary venation percurrent. Inflorescences axillary or from axils of fallen leaves, 1–few-flowered. Flowers hermaphroditic, subglobose to ovoid in bud, petals separating at a late developmental stage. Sepals 3, valvate, free, shorter than petals. Petals in two whorls of 3, valvate, free, ± carnose; outer petals elliptic to elliptic-ovate; inner petals ovate to (broadly) ovate-elliptic, slightly smaller than the outer whorl, often apically thickened. Stamens 12–40, anthers aseptate, anther connective apex truncate. Carpels 4–12, stigmas subglobose-ellipsoid to ellipsoid-cylindrical; ovule 1(–2) per ovary, basal. Receptacle more or less flat. Fruits apocarpous, monocarps indehiscent, ellipsoid to ellipsoid-ovoid, hairy, nearly smooth, sessile; pericarp rather thick. Seed basally attached, 1 per monocarp, ellipsoid to ellipsoid-ovoid, rather smooth, glabrous or hairy, ± brown when dried, perichalazal ring sunken, aril absent, endosperm ruminations lamellate.</br></br>A tropical Asian genus of about 8 species. Two species are known from Thailand; the stellate indument and tree habit are shared only with Drepananthus in the Thai flora.

description: Evergreen shrubs, treelets, or trees, with spiral primary branching. Indument of simple hairs. Leaves chartaceous to subcoriaceous, base cuneate, broadly cuneate, obtuse, or rounded, seldom cordate or subcordate, symmetrical to slightly asymmetrical, midrib ± sunken, secondary veins inconspicuous to conspicuous, tertiary venation reticulate, reticulate-percurrent or percurrent. Inflorescences axillary, sometimes from axils of fallen leaves, or terminal developing to supra-axillary or internodal, 1–5-flowered, pedunculate, pedicels sometimes borne on an elongated rachis. Flowers hermaphroditic, subglobose, ovoid, or ± triangular-pyramidal, sometimes depressed at the apex, in bud. Sepals 3, valvate, free or basally connate, shorter than petals. Petals in two whorls of 3, valvate, free, outer petals ca twice as large as sepals, usually more or less ovate, separating at a middle developmental stage, inner petals divided into blade and claw, blade ± rhombic, ± trullate, or ± subcircular, nectary glands usually present adaxially, blades generally connivent at anthesis, sometimes tips ± separated at anthesis, claw short to long. Stamens 3, 6, 9, or 12, ± clavate, outermost sometimes staminodial, anthers aseptate, anther connective apex miliusoid (not covering anther thecae), nearly lacking. Carpels 3, 6, 9, or 12, rarely 11 or 14, stigmas ± curved-terete, ellipsoid, subglobose, or globose; ovule(s) 1–10 per ovary, basi-lateral or lateral, uniseriate when multiple ovules. Receptacle slightly elevated, hairy, apex rounded to flat-topped. Fruits apocarpous, monocarps indehiscent, ellipsoid, ellipsoid-cylindrical, cylindrical, or globose, rarely short-oblongoid, sometimes moniliform, glabrous or hairy, smooth, subsessile or stipitate; pericarp thin. Seeds attached sub-basally or laterally in 1 row, up to 6 per monocarp, ellipsoid, cylindrical or globose, sometimes flattened on one side when globose, smooth or shallowly pitted, often transversely wrinkled when dried, glabrous, ± brown when dried, perichalazal ring nearly plane to sunken, aril absent, endosperm ruminations spiniform.</br></br>An Asian genus of about 60 species; 2 subgenera, Orophea and Sphaerocarpon Kessler, are recognised, both represented among the 8 species occurring in Thailand. The name Orophea refers to the “roof” formed by the inner petals. Leonardía & Kessler (2001) reported O. malayana Kessler to occur in Peninsular Thailand, but our re-investigations do not support this.

description: Tree to 10 m tall. Twigs tomentose with erect and appressed hairs. Leaves chartaceous, elliptic to slightly obovate, 9.3–24 by 3.3–9.5 cm, base obtuse, rounded or slightly subcordate, symmetrical, apex caudate-acuminate, the acumen 11–32 mm long, puberulous with erect and appressed hairs on both surfaces, secondary veins 8–13 per side, rather distinct below, tertiary venation percurrent. Inflorescences terminal, developing to supra-axillary or internodal, 1–4-flowered, peduncle 4.5–13 mm long when present, rachis up to 10 mm long when present, pedicels 11–23 mm long, each bearing a single bract near midpoint. Flowers ovoid in bud. Sepals free, ovate-triangular, 5–7 mm long, apex ± acuminate. Outer petals yellowish green, ± chartaceous, ovate, elliptic, broadly ovate or broadly elliptic, 10–16 by 8–10 mm, apex acute to acuminate. Inner petals yellowish green, ± red-pink toward apex, coriaceous, ± rhombic to ± broadly elliptic, 12–15 by 4–4.5 mm, blades connivent at anthesis, apex acute-acuminate, claw 8.5–11.5 mm long, nectary gland one, covering ± 80 percent of blade, ± red-pink, ± subcircular, raised and sunken in the middle. Stamens ca 1.8 mm long, fertile stamens 6, staminodes 6, anther connective apex obtuse. Carpels 6, ovaries villous with appressed hairs, stigmas ± curved-terete; ovule 1, basi-lateral. Fruit of up to 2 monocarps borne on a pedicel up to 23 mm long. Monocarps orange, ellipsoid-cylindrical, ca 2.2 by 0.7 cm, puberulous with erect and appressed hairs, apex apiculate, base contracted into a stout stipe ca 3 mm long. Seed 1, ellipsoid-cylindrical, ca 20 by 6.5 mm, surface not observed.

description: Tree to 12 m tall. Inner petals ± pink, yellowish green toward apex, chartaceous, ± trullate and clawed toward base, 5–7.5 by 2–4 mm, blades connivent at anthesis, apex acute to obtuse, claw 2.5–3.5 mm long, nectary glands two, side-by-side, colour unknown, each ± semicircular to ± subcircular, slightly sunken. Stamens ca 1 mm long, fertile stamens 6, staminodes 6, anther connective apex acute. description: Shrub or tree to 10 m tall. description: Tree to 9 m tall. Twigs almost glabrous. Leaves subcoriaceous, elliptic, 8.6–20.6 by 3.5–7.7 cm, base cuneate to obtuse, symmetrical, apex ± caudate-acuminate, seldom acute, glabrous on upper surface, puberulous with appressed hairs on lower surface, secondary veins 6–10 per side, rather distinct below, tertiary venation reticulate or sometimes reticulate-percurrent. description: Evergreen trees or shrubs, with spiral primary branching. Indument of simple hairs. Leaves chartaceous to subcoriaceous, often turning black when dried, oblanceolate, oblong-oblanceolate or elliptic, base symmetrical, cuneate, midrib sunken above, secondary veins straight, brochidodromous, tertiary venation percurrent. Inflorescences internodal or rarely terminal, 1–4-flowered, peduncle short with 1–2 persistent triangular bracts; pedicels slender with 1 bract or bract absent. Flowers hermaphroditic, conical in bud. Sepals 3, valvate, connate at base or free, much shorter than inner petals. Petals in two whorls of 3, valvate, free, outer petals sepal-like, much shorter than inner petals, inner petals triangular to triangular-ovate, base broad, saccate. Stamens numerous, anthers aseptate, anther connective apex truncate. Carpels 15–60, stigmas ellipsoid to clavate; ovules 1(–2) per ovary, lateral. Receptacle subglobose, small. Fruits apocarpous, monocarps indehiscent, 1–several, ellipsoid to globose, pubescent, smooth, stipitate; pericarp thin, membranous when dried. Seeds attached laterally, 1(–2) per monocarp, ellipsoid, smooth or wrinkled, glabrous, brown to dark brown, perichalazal ring sunken, aril absent, endosperm ruminations lamellate.</br></br>A tropical Asian genus of about 8 species, with outer petals of the flowers much smaller than the inner; 2 species are known from Thailand.

description: Shrub or tree 4–15 m tall; bark greyish black, moderately smooth. Twigs lenticellate, densely reddish brown-villous when young, later sparsely hairy to subglabrous. Leaves membranous, oblanceolate, oblong-oblanceolate or elliptic, 7–24 by 3–8 cm, base cuneate, apex acuminate or cuspidate, the acumen 8–30 mm long, glabrous to sparsely hairy except with denser hairs on midrib and secondary veins above, pilose below, the hairs densest on midrib and secondary veins, secondary veins 11–15 per side; petioles 5–10 mm long. Inflorescences 1–3-flowered, peduncle 8–20 mm long, bract 1(–2), pedicels 40–60 mm long, each bearing a single bract near midpoint. Sepals brownish green to green, linear-lanceolate to lanceolate, 1.5–4 by 0.5–1.5 mm, acute, hairy on both surfaces. Outer petals brown, linear-lanceolate, 3–7 by 1–2 mm, apex acute, hairy on both surfaces. Inner petals green to yellowish green, ovate, 16–27 by 8–16 mm, with 5–7 prominent veins, apex acute, densely hairy outside, sparsely hairy inside except for glabrous base. description: Evergreen trees, with spiral primary branching. Indument of simple hairs. Leaves thinly coriaceous, oblong-lanceolate, base cuneate to rounded, symmetrical, midrib plane or slightly sunken, secondary veins brochidodromous, tertiary venation reticulate. Inflorescences axillary from axils of fallen leaves, few–many-flowered, fasciculate. Flowers hermaphroditic, globose in bud. Sepals 3, valvate, connate into a 3-lobed cup, shorter than petals. Petals in two whorls of 3, valvate, free, ovate, outer petals spreading at anthesis, inner petals subequal to or slightly shorter than outer petals, narrowed toward the base but not clawed, cohering into a mitriform cap over the reproductive organs. Stamens 20–35, anthers aseptate, anther connective apex miliusoid, minute and not exceeding the anther thecae. Carpels 1–3, stigmas sessile, capitate, slightly bilobed; ovules 6–10, lateral, biseriate. Receptacle flat or slightly raised, provided with a ring of stiff hairs around the carpels, otherwise glabrous. Fruits apocarpous, monocarps indehiscent, 1–3 per fruit, globose, ovoid, or cylindrical, pubescent to glabrate, finely verrucose, sessile; pericarp up to 5 mm thick, woody when dried. Seeds laterally attached, biseriate.</br></br>A genus of 2 species, one in the Philippines and the other in SE & Peninsular Thailand, Peninsular Malaysia, Sumatra, and Java.

description: Tree up to 40 m tall, sometimes with small buttresses. Twigs glabrous. description: Evergreen shrubs, treelets or trees, with spiral or distichous primary branching. Indument of simple hairs. Leaves chartaceous to thinly coriaceous, oblong, elliptic, lanceolate, oblanceolate or obovate, base asymmetrical and/or cordate, sometimes minutely so, rarely symmetrical, auriculate, rounded, obtuse or cuneate, midrib plane or sunken above, secondary venation simple- or festooned-brochidodromous, or rarely mixed eucamptodromous, slightly conspicuous to conspicuous, tertiary venation reticulate or weakly percurrent. Inflorescences terminal, leaf-opposed, supra-axillary, internodal, or axillary, or on woody tubercles of leafless twigs or trunk, 1‒many-flowered, plants sometimes ramiflorous or cauliflorous; peduncle and rachis absent or rarely present, pedicels with 1(–2) bracts attached between base and midpoint. Flowers hermaphroditic, lanceolate, ovoid, or broadly ovoid in bud. Sepals 3, ovate or lanceolate, valvate or imbricate, base free or connate, shorter than the petals. Petals in two whorls of 3(‒4), separate at base and valvate at apex, erect, incurved, or spreading at anthesis, ovate, lanceolate, oblong-elliptic or linear. Stamens numerous, cuneate to oblong, anthers aseptate, anther connective apex truncate or slightly convex, overhanging the anther thecae. Carpels 1‒40, cylindrical, stigmas globose, subglobose, obovoid, clavate or oblongoid, higher than or equal to anther connective apices; ovules 1‒6, attached laterally, sub-basally, or occasionally basally, uniseriate. Receptacle convex or cushion-shaped, simple, slightly concave or flat at the top, glabrous or hairy. Fruits apocarpous, monocarps indehiscent, globose to oblongoid or ellipsoid, sometimes slightly torulose, surface smooth or slightly puckered and verrucose, glabrous or pubescent, apex rounded, obtuse, apiculate or mucronate, usually stipitate; pericarp thin, membranous when dried or sometimes leathery. Seeds subglobose, plano-convex, subdiscoid or disk-shaped, surface smooth, slightly to deeply wrinkled or pitted, perichalazal ring sunken, aril absent, endosperm ruminations spiniform.</br></br>The genus is distributed throughout tropical Asia to N Australia. Despite the removal of many species to the segregate genera Huberantha, Maasia, Marsypopetalum, and Monoon, about 90 species of shrubs and understorey trees remain; 21 occur in Thailand. The monocarps in the segregate genera have a single basally attached seed; in Polyalthia, the seeds are usually attached laterally, less often basally or sub-basally, and there are often more than one per monocarp.

description: Evergreen small trees or shrubs with spiral primary branching. Indument of simple hairs. Leaves chartaceous, elliptic, oblong, or obovate, base broadly cuneate to rounded and asymmetrical, midrib plane or sunken, secondary veins arcuate, tertiary venation usually percurrent. Inflorescences leaf-opposed, 2–7-flowered, pedicels arising from a short perennial axis. Flowers hermaphroditic, globose to ovoid in bud. Sepals 3, valvate, free, shorter than the petals. Petals in two whorls of 3, valvate, free or connate in a ring at base, ovate, the inner petals slightly longer than the outer, cucullate and forming a tooth at the apex. Stamens ca 20, anthers aseptate, anther connective apex truncate. Carpels 6–7, stigmas clavate; ovules basal to lateral, uniseriate, 2–4 per ovary [ex Ganesan]. Receptacle flat, 1.3–1.5 mm in diam., often bristly-pubescent. Fruits apocarpous, monocarps indehiscent, globose, smooth or slightly wrinkled, sessile or stipitate; pericarp thin, membranous when dried, often tightly adherent to the seed. Seeds attached laterally, up to 4 per monocarp, globose to ellipsoid, somewhat flattened, pitted, wrinkled, or tuberculate, glabrous, light brown, perichalazal ring raised, aril absent, endosperm ruminations spiniform.</br></br>About 26 tropical Asian species; with petals often 2–3 mm long, the flowers are among the smallest in the Annonaceae; 2 species are reported for Thailand.

description: Evergreen trees, with spiral primary branching. Indument of simple hairs. Leaves papyraceous to coriaceous, elliptic, ovate or obovate (occasionally linear or needle-shaped), base symmetrical, midrib raised, secondary venation brochidodromous, tertiary venation percurrent. Inflorescences axillary, solitary to clustered (up to 30), each with up to ca 18 flowers, sometimes plants ramiflorous or cauliflorous. Flowers staminate, pistillate, or hermaphroditic; buds globose. Sepals 3, valvate, free or ± basally connate, shorter than petals. Petals in two whorls of 3, valvate, free, outer petals generally shorter than inner petals, generally not clawed, inner petals basally clawed, apically connivent over reproductive organs, forming a mitriform dome with 3 lateral apertures (rarely with additional apical aperture), with 1–2 adaxial glands (sometimes absent). Stamens 1–45(–90) in bisexual flowers, 18–153 in staminate flowers, anthers aseptate, anther connective apex generally truncate. Carpels 1–30 in hermaphroditic flowers, 1–9 in pistillate flowers, stigmas variable in shape; ovules 1–20, lateral, uniseriate or biseriate. Receptacle shallowly conical, ± flat or narrowly cylindrical (staminate flowers) and depressed-ovoid or ± flat (pistillate flowers). Fruits apocarpous, monocarps indehiscent, globose or ellipsoid, rarely (ob-)ovoid, glabrous to densely pubescent, smooth or rarely warty, sometimes with a longitudinal ridge, sessile or stipitate; pericarp mostly < 2 mm thick, rarely up to 4 mm thick. Seeds attached laterally in 1–2 rows, 1–20 per monocarp, smooth to rugose, hairy or glabrous, colour variable, perichalazal ring sunken, aril absent, endosperm ruminations spiniform (rarely peg-shaped).</br></br>About 60 species, throughout tropical and subtropical SE Asia to N Australia; 12 occur in Thailand. The connivent inner petals are similar to those of Orophea, but the truncate anther connectives distinguish Pseuduvaria.

description: Tree to 4 m tall. Young branches subglabrous. description: Evergreen woody climber with lateral branches wrapping around adjacent supports, with distichous primary branching. Indument of simple hairs. Leaves subcoriaceous, base rounded, truncate, or cordate, symmetrical, midrib slightly sunken, secondary veins indistinct, brochidodromous, tertiary venation reticulate. Inflorescences axillary, 1–3-flowered. Flowers hermaphroditic, conical and somewhat three-angled in bud. Sepals 3, valvate, connate to form a flat circular to triangular disc, much smaller than outer petals. Petals in two whorls of 3, valvate, free, fleshy; outer petals linear to lanceolate; inner petals forming a dome over the centre of the flower, much shorter than outer petals. Stamens numerous, anthers aseptate, anther connective apex truncate to capitate. Carpels 5–13, stigmas capitate, multi-lobed; ovules ca 20, lateral, biseriate. Receptacle convex, slightly elevated. Fruits apocarpous, monocarps indehiscent, oblongoid, ellipsoid, or cylindrical, pubescent to glabrate, smooth or verrucose, sometimes tuberculate, short-stipitate; pericarp thick, leathery when dried. Seeds attached laterally in 2 rows, up to 20 per monocarp, flattened-ellipsoid or ellipsoid-oblongoid, smooth, shiny, dark brown, perichalazal ring not evident, arillate ring encircling the micropyle, endosperm ruminations spiniform or flattened pegs.</br></br>A monotypic genus distributed from the Malay Peninsula to Sumatra and Borneo. Pyramidanthe may be confused with Fissistigma, but the axillary inflorescence and small inner petals forming a dome distinguish it.

description: Evergreen trees, with spiral primary branching. Indument of simple hairs. Leaves (sub)coriaceous, base cuneate or obtuse-rounded, sometimes slightly subcordate, rarely obtuse or broadly cuneate, symmetrical or sometimes slightly asymmetrical, midrib sunken, secondary venation inconspicuous, tertiary venation reticulate. Inflorescences axillary or from axils of fallen leaves, 1–many-flowered, plants sometimes cauliflorous (in Sageraea elliptica). Flowers hermaphroditic or unisexual (staminate and pistillate separate on the same individual), ovoid to very broadly ovoid, subglobose, or transversely ellipsoid in bud, petals separating at a late developmental stage. Sepals 3, slightly imbricate in bud, free or connate, shorter than petals. Petals in two whorls of 3, imbricate, free, outer petals ovate, elliptic, oblong, or obovate, inner petals orbicular, elliptic, obovate or ovate, slightly smaller than the outer petals. Stamens 7–21, ± wedge-shaped, thickened and somewhat fleshy, anthers aseptate, anther connective apex truncate. Carpels one to several, ovaries glabrous, stigmas capitate to cylindrical, sometimes lobed (more or less horseshoe-shaped); ovules 5–12 per ovary, lateral, biseriate. Receptacle flat to hemispheric-obconical. Fruits apocarpous, monocarps indehiscent, subglobose, ellipsoid or obovoid-oblongoid, glabrous, smooth or finely verruculose, usually wrinkled when dried, apex rounded, sessile or short-stipitate; pericarp rather thick, hard when dried. description: Evergreen woody climbers or small trees, with distichous primary branching. Indument of simple hairs. Leaves chartaceous to subcoriaceous, elliptic to oblong or lanceolate, rarely oblanceolate, base symmetrical, cuneate to rounded, midrib plane or slightly sunken above, secondary veins brochidodromous, tertiary venation loosely reticulate. Inflorescences axillary or occasionally pseudoterminal, 1-flowered. Flowers hermaphroditic, globose to depressed-globose in bud. Sepals 3, valvate, free or slightly connate, much shorter than petals, persistent in fruit. Petals in two whorls of 3, valvate, free, ovate to broadly ovate, outer petals spreading, inner petals incurved over centre of flower and triquetrous at apex. Stamens numerous, anthers aseptate, anther connective apex truncate or convex. Carpels numerous, ovaries oblong, stigmas narrowly oblong; ovules 1(–2) per ovary, sub-basal or lateral in a single row. Receptacle elevated, truncate beneath carpels. Fruits apocarpous, monocarps indehiscent, ovoid, ellipsoid, or oblongoid, glabrous or pubescent, smooth or verrucose, stipitate; pericarp thin, membranous when dried. Seeds attached sub-basally or laterally, 1–2 per monocarp, ellipsoid, smooth, glabrous, shiny or dull, light brown, perichalazal ring plane to slightly raised, aril absent, endosperm ruminations lamellate.</br></br>A Palaeotropical genus of 8 or more species, in Africa, Madagascar, and SE Asia; 3 species are known from Thailand, including the familiar lam duan tree.

description: Woody climber. Twigs flexuous, glabrous. Petals rich yellow, fleshy; outer petals ovate, 8–12.5 by 6.7–7.5 mm, obtuse; inner petals ovate, ca 6 mm long, concave, broadly acute. Stamens 1.5–2 mm long, anther connective apex truncate. description: Woody climber to 20 m high. Twigs flexuous, sparsely pubescent, soon glabrate. Leaves subcoriaceous, occasionally chartaceous, concolourous, elliptic to oblong, rarely lanceolate-oblong or oblanceolate, (11.2–)14.5–17.3 by 3.9–7.8 cm, base broadly cuneate to rounded, apex acute, obtuse, or short-acuminate, the acumen 4–6 mm long, glabrous on both surfaces, secondary veins 11–17 per side; petioles 3–10 mm long. description: Evergreen shrubs or small trees, with spiral primary branching. Indument of simple hairs. Leaves chartaceous to subcoriaceous, often bright yellow-green when dried, elliptic to oblanceolate, cuneate to rounded and symmetrical at base, midrib plane or sunken above, secondary venation conspicuous, brochidodromous or eucamptodromous, tertiary venation percurrent and with a fine raised reticulum of smaller veins between them conspicuous below. Inflorescences supra-axillary, internodal, or leaf-opposed, 1–4-flowered, peduncle rudimentary. Flowers staminate or hermaphroditic on the same plant, rarely hermaphroditic only, globose to ovoid in bud. Sepals 3, imbricate, free, shorter than the petals. Petals in two whorls of 3, valvate, free, linear to ovate, oblong, elliptic, or obovate, outer petals sometimes shorter than the inner petals, spreading at anthesis, inner petals connivent at apices or free, erect or spreading at anthesis. Stamens numerous, anthers aseptate, anther connective apex truncate to convex. Carpels 6–30, stigmas capitate to clavate; ovule basal, 1 per ovary. Receptacle cushion-shaped to columnar. Fruits apocarpous, monocarps indehiscent, glabrous or pubescent, smooth or verrucose, stipitate; pericarp thin, membranous and adhering to seed when dried. Seed basally attached, 1 per monocarp, ellipsoid, smooth, glabrous, light brown, perichalazal ring sunken, aril absent, endosperm ruminations flattened, peglike or lamellate.</br></br>About 10 species of small shrubs or less frequently trees, often andromonoecious with bright red monocarps. Asian tropics and subtropics; 7 species known from Thailand.

description: Shrub or treelet up to 5 m tall. Twigs short grey-pubescent, eventually glabrate. Leaves chartaceous, narrowly oblong or oblanceolate, occasionally elliptic, 14–28.8 by 2.8–7.2 cm, base cuneate to rounded, apex acuminate, the acumen 7–26 mm long, glabrous on both surfaces, secondary veins 9–15 per side, eucamptodromous to weakly brochidodromous, arcuate; petioles 5–9 mm long. Inflorescences supra-axillary, 1-flowered, pedicels 4–5.5 mm long, each bearing 1 bract ca 3 mm long; buds with petals separating well before anthesis. Flowers staminate or hermaphroditic. Sepals triangular, 3.5–5 mm long, acute to acuminate, sericeous. Petals creamy white, yellow, or pale orange, coriaceous, glabrous on inner surface, sericeous on outer surface; outer petals spreading at anthesis, lanceolate to linear, 7–12.8 by 1.8–3.7 mm, acute; inner petals spreading at anthesis, linear to linear-lanceolate, 8–15.5 by 1.6–3.2 mm, acute. Stamens ca 150, oblong, 1–1.9 mm long, anther connective apex truncate, glabrous. Carpels 9–18, ovaries ca 1 mm long, pubescent, stigmas flat or globose. Fruit of up to 7 monocarps borne on a pedicel 5–8 mm long. Monocarps oblongoid, 1.8–2.2 by 0.7–0.9 cm, verrucose and faintly ridged, glabrate, apex rounded to a beak 0.8–1.5 mm long, stipe 0.8–2.5 mm long, 2–2.2 mm thick, pubescent; pericarp ca 0.2 mm thick. Seed narrowly ellipsoid, ca 18 mm by 7–7.5 mm, pale orange-brown, smooth.

description: Evergreen woody climbers or sarmentose shrubs, with distichous primary branching. Indument of stellate hairs, rarely with additional simple hairs on leaf venation. Leaves membranous to coriaceous, obovate, elliptic or ovate, base cordate to cuneate, midrib sunken above, secondary veins sub-parallel or convergent, tertiary venation reticulate; petioles sometimes marked by transverse foliations. Inflorescences terminal, leaf-opposed or rarely axillary or supra-axillary, 1–5-flowered, plants cauliflorous in a few species. Flowers hermaphroditic; buds globose to conical. Sepals (2–)3(–4), free and valvate, basally connate or fully connate into a calyptrate calyx, shorter than petals. Petals in two whorls of (2–)3, imbricate, free or connate in a ring at base, ovate, oblong or obovate, whorls subequal, or inner petals smaller and distinct from the outer petals in shape, petals erect, spreading, reflexed or partially reflexed at maturity. Stamens numerous, outermost sometimes staminodial, anthers aseptate, anther connective apex globose, umbonate, truncate, or concave, or elongate and flattened, filament short or absent. Carpels 1–ca 50, stigmas elongate or flattened, lobes conical or U-shaped; ovules 2–36 in two rows, or rarely solitary. Receptacle flat or shallowly convex. Fruits apocarpous, monocarps indehiscent, globose, oblong, or cylindrical, pubescent or rarely glabrous, surface smooth, verrucose, or bearded, often with longitudinal ridges, stipitate or rarely sessile; pericarp thin, membranous when dried. Seeds attached laterally in 2 rows, rarely 1 attached apically or sub-apically, 1–36 per monocarp, ellipsoid, smooth, brown, perichalazal ring flat, aril circular or rectangular, endosperm ruminations lamellate.</br></br>A Palaeotropical genus of about 210 species of climbers with stellate hairs. In Thailand the genus is represented by 23 species, 2 with 2 varieties present in the flora. Uvaria is probably the most ubiquitous Annonaceae genus in Thailand and among the most diverse. Uvaria grandiflora and U. siamensis are grown as ornamentals, and Uvaria rufa is sought for its edible fruits.

description: Woody climber. Young shoots sparsely stellate to subglabrous, eventually glabrous. Leaves subcoriaceous, waxy, drying dark brown above and below, oblanceolate, elliptic-oblanceolate or narrowly obovate, 7.5–24 by 4–9.5 cm, base rounded, broadly cuneate or slightly oblique-rounded, apex acuminate or acute, the acumen 3–15 mm long; glabrous above, and below except for sparse stellate hairs on midrib, secondary veins 9–12 per side; petioles 5–10 mm long, smooth with sparse brown indument, becoming glabrous. Inflorescences supra-axillary or leaf-opposed, 1–3-flowered, often only the primary bud opened, the others enclosed by bracts, peduncle 1.5–3.5 mm long, pedicels 8–11 mm long, peduncle and pedicel terete, indument sparse, persistent; basal bract ovate, 1–2.5 by 0.5–1.5 mm; medial bract ovate 1.5–2 by 1–1.5 mm, obtuse. Sepals 3, valvate, free, green, broadly ovate, 2–2.5 by 2.5–3 mm, concave, apex obtuse to bluntly acute, outer surface indument sparse, prominent at margins outside, inner surface basally glabrous, hairs sparse at margins. Petals in two whorls of 3, green or yellow, with fine vertical furrows on outer surface, indument persistent on outer surface, sparse medially, somewhat prominent at margins, inner surfaces glabrous; outer petals coriaceous, ovate, 4–4.5 by 4–4.5 mm, concave, slightly spreading at maturity to clearly expose carpels, apex bluntly acute; inner petals subcoriaceous, ovate 4–4.5 by 4–4.2 mm, base distinctly contricted, apex bluntly acute. Stamens numerous, cuneate, 1.2–1.5 mm long, anther connective apex flat, cap-like, papillate, filament rudimentary. Carpels 10–18, ovaries 1–1.6 mm long, glabrous except for prominent ring of hairs on ovary neck just beneath stigma, stigmas glabrous, U-shaped, not elongate, 0.5 mm long; ovules 4–12. Monocarps 4–6+, oblongoid, ellipsoid or ovoid-ellipsoid, 2.8–5.5 by 1.8–2.6 cm, glabrous, granular or minutely tuberculate, stipe 30–60 by 2–3 mm, glabrous; pericarp fleshy at maturity, thin when dried. Seeds 4–8(–12), closely packed in 2 rows, 15–18 by 8–10 mm, compressed-ellipsoid, smooth, aril present.

description: Woody climber to 30 m tall. Young shoots tomentose, indument becoming sparse very quickly. Leaves coriaceous, shiny above, elliptic-oblong to narrowly obovate, ca 13–15 by 4–5 cm, base narrowly cordate, apex acute or less often acuminate, glabrous above, sparsely covered with blunt, many-branched hairs below, secondary veins ca 10–12 per side; petioles 7–10 by 1.25 mm, deeply grooved above, often overtopped by margins, transverse foliations distinct, warty. Inflorescences terminal or leaf-opposed by apposition, flowers solitary or with dormant secondary bud, peduncle sometimes evident to 5 mm; pedicels 15–20(–50) by ca 2.5 mm, indument dense and appearing tubercled with many-branched thickly-set hairs; buds globose to conical with prominent acuminate apiculum. Calyx calyptrate in bud, sepals wholly connate, splitting unevenly, (2–)3(–4), basally connate at maturity, ca 11 by 10 mm, ovate-acute, concave, outer surface with same indument as pedicel. Petals 6 (or rarely 4) divided evenly in two whorls, dark pink or red, spreading to reflexed at anthesis, basally connate in a single whorl, very broadly obovate, ca 20 by 15 mm, apex obtuse, detaching from receptacle as connate ring. Stamens numerous, cuneate, ca 3.5 mm long, anther locules equal or subequal in length, extending the length of the stamen, anther connective apex flattened or shallowly truncate, filament absent. Carpels numerous, ca 3.5 mm long, ovaries with flattened, many-branched spreading hairs, stigmas short, U-shaped, not distinctly lobed; ovules 8–10 in two lateral rows. Monocarps ca 5 to many, orange-yellow at maturity, smooth or somewhat tubercled, globose-oblongoid, 1.5–3 by 1–1.7 cm, occasionally constricted between seeds, with 1 or more longitudinal ridges, small apiculum often present, stipe ca 50–100(–120) by 2–4 mm, typically flattened, striate. Seeds 2–10 in two closely-packed rows, ovoid to compressed-ovoid, 8–11 by 6–9 by 3–5 mm, smooth, aril and perichalazal ring not prominent.

description: Shrub or climber to 20 m tall, distinctively persistent-hirsute over all vegetative organs. Young shoots with ferrugineous hairs that become sparser with age. Leaves subcoriaceous, elliptic to narrowly obovate, ca 21–25 by 6–7 cm, base narrowly cordate, apex acute or short-acuminate, hirsute, hairs ferrugineous on both leaf surfaces, ca 0.5–1 mm long, producing a distinctive ferrugineous tint along leaf margins, secondary veins 10–12+ per side; petioles ca 8 by 3 m. Inflorescences leaf-opposed, 2-flowered, peduncle 1.5–12 mm, pedicels ca 20–30 by 1 mm, basal bract narrowly elliptic, ca 8 by 2 mm, often clasping, medial bract ovate to broadly elliptic, 4–5 by 2.5–3 mm; buds globose. Calyx calyptrate in bud, sepals 3, ca 10 by 6 mm, ovate, acute to narrowly acute. Petals in two subequal whorls of 3, white or greenish yellow, elliptic-acute, ca 13 by 6.5 mm, membranous, spreading, inner surface bearing prominent indentations from stamens. Stamens numerous, cuneate to laminar, 3 mm long, anther connective apex truncate on inner whorls or somewhat flat and elongate in marginal stamens, ridge sometimes present on outer surface, papillate, filament absent. Carpels numerous, ca 3 mm long, ovaries with dense combed-tomentose indument, stigmas U-shaped, lobes not broadened; ovules ca 20 in 2 lateral rows. Monocarps 10–30, colour unknown, cylindrical to oblongoid, ca 6.5 by 2.5 cm, ferrugineous-tomentose, stipe 10–40 by 2–3 mm. Seeds ca 16, flattened-ellipsoid, ca 10 by 6 by 4 mm.

description: Climber or sarmentose shrub. Young shoots ferrugineous-tomentose, hairs quickly becoming blunt and sparse, bark striate. Leaves coriaceous, narrowly elliptic-obovate, ca 18–19 by 6–8 cm, base narrowly cordate, acute to distinctly acuminate or cuspidate, indument of 1–4-branched hairs above, of 10-branched hairs below, secondary veins 11–13 per side; petioles 5–7 by ca 2 mm, tomentose, indument becoming sparse. Inflorescences leaf-opposed, flowers solitary or rarely 2–3, pedicels 8–15(–25) mm, often flattened to ca 2 mm broad, otherwise ca 1.25 mm, bracts ovate-acute, ca 4–7(–10) by 1.25–2 mm, often absent; buds 8–15 mm in diam. Calyx calyptrate in bud, splitting into 2–4 often unevenly sized ovate-acute sepals, each (7–)10 by (8–)10 mm, at length spreading. Petals in 2 subequal whorls of 3, yellow or rarely red, spreading, elliptic, 15–20 by 8–10 mm, apex obtuse-acute. Stamens numerous, cuneate, ca 4.5 mm long, anther connective apex truncate, adaxial ridge often present, smooth, filament absent. Carpels 10–15, ca 3.5 mm long, ovaries densely ferrugineous-tomentose, stout in appearance, apex narrowed into neck, stigmas glabrous with conspicuously broad U-shaped lobes, partially occluded by extension of ovary wall above neck; ovules ca 16 in 2 lateral rows. Monocarps 1–8(–10), obliquely attached to stipe, green with brown tint, ca 4.5 by 2.5 cm in diam., oblongoid, epidermis entirely uneven and warted, finely tomentose, stipe 5–10 by 2.5–3 mm, thickly striate, tomentose, pericarp thickened. Seeds 6–12 in 2 rows, ca 10 by 6 by 4 mm, hemi-ellipsoid.

description: Scrambling shrub or climber. Young shoots sparsely tomentose. Leaves subcoriaceous, elliptic-oblong, to 12.5 by 6 cm, base narrowly cordate or rarely cuneate in younger leaves, apex acute to short-acuminate, sparsely pubescent except for midrib sub-tomentose with erect hairs above, becoming more glabrous to sparsely pubescent, with sparse hairs along midrib and veins but otherwise sparsely pubescent to glabrous below, secondary veins 6–13 per side; petioles 5–8 mm long, sparsely tomentose. Inflorescences leaf-opposed, 1-flowered, pedicels to 60 mm long, 1–3 mm in diam., widest at base of receptacle. Sepals 3, free, valvate, ovate-acute, to 5 by 6 mm, outer surface tomentose, inner surface basally glabrous. Petals in two whorls of 3, white-green; outer petals 25–30 mm long, 8–10 mm wide, free; inner petals 23–28 mm long, 5–8 mm wide, lower margins often connivent. Stamens numerous, cuneate, ca 2.5 mm long, locules raised on short filament, anther connective apex convex or flattened, smooth. Carpel 1, stigma disc-shaped, 3 mm in diam., glabrous; ovules laterally inserted in 2 rows, 6–12. Monocarp 1, ovoid to oblongoid, 1.5–3.5 by 1–1.5 cm, subsessile, the stipe 3–4 by 3–4 mm, tomentose. Seeds 6–12.

description: Sarmentose shrub or climber up to 30 m long or more. Young shoots tomentose, becoming glabrous with distinctive pale lenticels. Leaves membranous, elliptic to broadly elliptic to shortly obovate, ca 10–14 by 4.5–6 cm, base sub-cordate to shortly cordate, apex acute, blade sparsely covered with 1–4-branched spreading hairs or becoming subglabrous, tomentose with erect hairs along the sunken midrib above, blade sub-tomentose except with spreading 5+-branched hairs, tomentose near petiole, on veins and midrib the hairs ca 10-branched, ferrugineous, and stocky below, secondary veins 15–18 per side; petioles 3.5–5 by ca 1 mm, tomentose. Inflorescences terminal, pendulous, 1–many-flowered, usually 2–3-flowered, peduncle ca 5–10 mm, pedicels ca 12–25 mm; buds globose. Sepals 3, valvate, connate at base, ovate-acute, ca 3.25 by 4.5 mm. Petals in two whorls of 3, white or yellow-pink, broadly elliptic-acute at first, expanding to obovate-acute at maturity, coriaceous to membranous; outer petals ca 21.5 by 11.5 mm; inner petals ca 20.5 by 10.5 mm, inner surface basally glabrous with two lateral orange-coloured glands inserted above the base. Stamens numerous, cuneate, ca 1.5 mm long, anther connective apex broad and flattened, often forming lip on inner side, papillate, glabrous, locules often uneven in length, filament short. Carpels ca 25, forming a distinct dome above stamens, ca 2.5 mm long, usually hairy below stigma neck and along lateral ridges, stigmas long and hairy with distinct neck, U-shaped; ovules ca 14–16. Monocarps ca 10+, green turning orange and then red, oblongoid to short-cylindrical, ca 1 by 0.65 cm, glabrous, stipe ca 5–10 mm. Seeds 1–8, compressed-ovoid, ca 5 by 4 by 4 mm, perichalazal ring raised, aril transversely compressed.

description: Scrambling shrub to 3 m or large woody climber to 30 m high. Young shoots densely tomentose, becoming striate and subglabrous. Leaves subcoriaceous to coriaceous, elliptic-obovate, 13–19(–25 by 5–7.5(–10) cm, base subcordate to narrowly cordate, apex obtuse-acute, surface sparsely hairy to subglabrous, hairs 1–many-branched above, tomentose to rarely sparsely hairy, hairs all stellate, ca 10-branched, 0.3–0.5 mm in diam., below, secondary veins 11–14(–16) per side; petioles 5–6 by ca 2 mm, warted and transversely foliated, black. Inflorescences leaf-opposed or sub-opposed, solitary or rarely with second dormant bud, or plants cauliflorous with elongate, often many-branched cymes with 3 to many pedicels, pedicels 10–15 by 2 mm, or up to 60 by 2 mm, ferrugineous, bracts leaflike, ovate-elliptic, 10–33 by 5–20 mm; bud 15–25 mm in diam. Calyx calyptrate in bud, later dividing into (2–)3(–4) ovate-acute, 15–25 by 9–18 mm sepals, reflexing at maturity. Petals in 2 subequal whorls of 3, white or deep red to purple, spreading, often reflexed, broadly ovate or elliptic-oblong to rarely very narrowly obovate, 20–50 by 8–25 mm Stamens numerous, linear, 6–8 by ca 1.25 mm, anther connective apex flattened, dorsal ridge often prominent, with stellate indument running length of connective, apex papillate, filament absent. Carpels numerous, 8–8.5 by 1.5 mm, ovaries densely tomentose, stigmas U shaped, glabrous, somewhat lobed, 2 by 1–2 mm; ovules 24–36. Monocarps 6–12(–20), yellow, cylindrical, 5–7.5 by 1–2 cm, smooth or with longitudinal or lateral ridges and constrictions between seeds, ferrugineous-tomentose, becoming smooth to subglabrous at maturity, stipe to ca 30 by 4 mm. Seeds 16–30, hemi-ellipsoid to ovoid, often dorsiventrally flattened, ca 7 by 5 by 2 mm, smooth, ruminations visible.

description: Climber to 25 m high. Young shoots sparsely tomentose, quickly becoming subglabrous, bark black and striate. Leaves membranous or coriaceous, narrowly obovate, 10–15 by 4–6 cm, base narrowly cordate to cordate, apex acute to short-acuminate, hairs erect, sub-tomentose over upper midrib but otherwise glabrous above, midrib quickly becoming sparsely pubescent to glabrous, sparsely pubescent to subglabrous on midrib but otherwise subglabrous to glabrous below, secondary veins 9–15 per side; petioles 5–7 by 1.2–2.5 mm, warted below. Inflorescences leaf-opposed, 1–4-flowered, plants sometimes cauliflorous, peduncle elongate, ca 20–50 mm long by 1.5 mm in diam., pedicels 20–30 mm long. Sepals 3, valvate, free, broadly ovate, 5 mm wide by 3 mm long, often reflexed at maturity. Petals in two whorls of 3, green or yellow, concave, thickened basally and with prominent transverse foliations on outer surface; outer petals broadly ovate, ca 5 by 5 mm; inner petals ovate, 5 by 4 mm, base constricted. Stamens numerous, cuneate, 2–2.5 mm long, anther connective apex ca 0.5–0.7 mm long, incurved, papillate, papillae often hair-like, filament absent. Carpels numerous, ca 3–4 mm long, ovaries tomentose, stigmas glabrous, elongate, conical, ca 1–1.25 mm long, U-shaped in section; ovules 5–6 in 2 rows. Monocarps 2–10+, green-yellow, ovoid to oblongoid but irregular in shape due to compression of pericarp around seeds, 2.5–4 by 1–2 cm, glabrous, stipe ca 20 mm long, 2.5 mm in diam.; pericarp thickened. Seeds 4–6, in two rows but becoming irregularly arranged in mature fruit.

description: Large climber to 30 m, or a scrambling, rarely upright, shrub. Young shoots ferrugineous-hirsute, becoming subglabrous and distinctly striate. Leaves membranous, (elliptic-)obovate, 11.5–17.5(–20.5) by 6–8.5 cm, base subcordate to narrowly cordate, apex acute or very short-acuminate, sub-tomentose with simple and stellate hairs above, sub-tomentose with stellate hairs only, scattered thickly-set rufous hairs on midrib and veins but rare or absent on blade below, secondary veins often distinctively numerous, 11–25 per side, sometimes branching basally or medially; petioles ca 4 by 2 mm, warty. Inflorescences leaf-opposed or sub-opposed, 1–2(–3)-flowered, peduncle ca 5 mm long, pedicels ca 35 by 2 mm, bracts broadly obovate to circular-ovate, often wrapping around pedicel, ca 10 by 10 mm; buds globose, indument rufous with occasional thickly set hairs giving a tubercled appearance. Calyx calyptrate in bud, sepals 3–4, spreading, partially recurved, connate at base, triangular to very broadly ovate, 7 by 10 mm, bluntly acute, indument as for pedicel. Petals in 2 subequal whorls of 3, petals red or white to yellow, spreading, often reflexed, elliptic to oblong to distinctly obovate, 10–22 by 10–14 mm, apex broadly concave-rounded to obtuse. Stamens numerous, linear, 2.5–3 mm long, anther connective apex compact, not extended, papillae often prominent, filament absent. Carpels numerous, ca 2 mm long, ovaries densely tomentose, stigmas glabrous, U-shaped; ovules 10–12. Monocarps 10–14, green, turning red, globose to oblongoid, ca 2 by 1.5 cm, ferrugineous-tomentose, often verrucose, stipe ca 25–35 by 1.25–2.25 mm, striate, especially when thick, tomentose, monocarp attachment basal or sub-basal; pericarp fleshy or thin. description: Climber to 30 m high. Young shoots densely ferrugineous-tomentose, becoming striate and glabrous. Sepals 3, connate in early bud, then splitting to form a basally connate three-pointed ring around the unexpanded petals, ring later splitting into ovate-acute sepals 4–6 by 6–8 mm wide. Stamens numerous, linear to narrowly cuneate, 5–6 mm long, anther locules extending the full length of stamens in central whorls, decreasing in size towards the outermost whorl of narrowly obovate staminodes, anther connective apex elongate, 5–sided in central whorls, flat in outer whorls, minutely papillate, filament absent. Carpels 20–25, 4–4.25 mm long, indument stellate, short and somewhat combed, stigmas short, glabrous, U-shaped, base narrowed and sub-tomentose; ovules 12–14. description: Climber or scrambling shrub with narrow tangling branches forming dense thickets. Young shoots sub-tomentose, striations appearing early. description: Shrub or woody climber up to 25 m high. Young shoots ferrugineous-tomentose, the hairs becoming sparse, striate with prominent lenticels. description: Scandent or erect shrub or tree to 2 m, or climber to 20 m. Young shoots tomentose with large many-branched ferrugineous hairs scattered over smaller, finer, hairs. description: Evergreen trees, with spiral primary branching. Indument of simple hairs. Leaves coriaceous, base cuneate, broadly cuneate, cuneate-obtuse or obtuse, symmetrical, midrib raised above, secondary veins conspicuous, tertiary venation usually reticulate, sometimes intermediate between reticulate and percurrent. Inflorescences clustered on trunks, swollen/unswollen trunk base, and/or large roots. Flowers unisexual (staminate and pistillate separate but intermixed in the same individual, except only staminate observed for W. thailandana), subglobose in bud. Sepals 3, slightly imbricate in bud, basally connate, shorter than petals. Petals in two whorls of 3, imbricate, free, carnose, outer petals elliptic to ovate, inner petals slightly smaller than outer petals, elliptic, ovate, or obovate. Stamens > 30, thickened and somewhat fleshy, anthers aseptate, anther connective apex more or less truncate. Carpels > 25, stigmas with multiple columnar lobes; ovules lateral, biseriate 5–9(–11) per ovary. Receptacle more or less hemispherical in both staminate and pistillate flowers. Fruits apocarpous, monocarps indehiscent, subglobose to ellipsoid, glabrous, shallowly verruculose (finely scaly), apex rounded, subsessile; pericarp thick, rather woody when dried. Seeds attached laterally in 2 rows, ca 6 per monocarp, ± D-shaped, sometimes slightly flattened, smooth, glabrous, ± brown when dried, perichalazal ring ± forming a ridge, aril absent, endosperm ruminations lamellate.</br></br>A tropical Asian genus of 4 species, represented in Thailand by 3 endemic species.

Leaves elliptic, 14–25 by 5–9 cm, base cuneate, broadly cuneate or cuneate-obtuse, apex acute-acuminate to acuminate, glabrous on both surfaces, secondary veins 13–15 per side. Inflorescences clustered on trunks, peduncles inconspicuous, pedicels 27–40 mm long, bracts not seen. Flowers unisexual, staminate and pistillate flowers intermixed on the same individual. Sepals slightly connate at base, ± semicircular, ca 4 mm long, apex rounded. Petals pale rose-coloured, more yellow on outer whorl, non-glaucous and not pitted on inner side; outer petals spreading at maturity, elliptic to slightly ovate, 12.5 by 8.5–10 mm, apex rounded-obtuse; inner petals remaining tightly coherent at maturity, elliptic to slightly ovate, 8.5–9 by 8–8.5 mm, inner side non-glaucous in vivo and not pitted, apex ± obtuse. Stamens ca 36, ± vertical rectangle to ± wedge-shaped, ca 1.9 mm long, rather loosely packed, each slightly bending inward (best observable in outermost whorl). Carpels ca 33, ovaries tomentose, stigmas with 5–7 columnar lobes; ovules 7–9. Receptacle ± hemispherical in both staminate and pistillate flowers. Fruit of up to 7 monocarps borne on a pedicel up to 40 mm long. Monocarps blackish brown, subglobose to slightly ellipsoid, 4–4.5 by 3.8–4 cm. Seeds ca 6, ± D-shaped, ca 40 by 20 mm.

description: Deciduous trees, with spiral primary branching. Indument of simple hairs. Leaves chartaceous, elliptic to slightly ovate, base broadly cuneate to cuneate, symmetrical, midrib sunken above, secondary venation rather conspicuous, eucamptodromous, tertiary venation more or less percurrent-reticulate; petiole enlarged and covering the axillary bud. Inflorescences from axils of fallen leaves, often alongside new vegetative shoot from same axil, 1-flowered. Flowers hermaphroditic, petals separating early in development. Sepals 3, valvate, free, much shorter than petals. Petals in two whorls of 3, valvate, free, (elliptic-)oblong, both whorls similar in shape and size. Stamens ca 150, anthers aseptate, anther connective apex truncate. Carpels 6–9, stigmas globose-capitate; ovules lateral, uniseriate or biseriate, 3–4 per ovary. Receptacle more or less depressed hemispherical. Fruits apocarpous, indehiscent, subglobose to ellipsoid, glabrous, smooth, stipitate; pericarp moderately thick when dried. Seeds attached laterally in 1 row, up to 4 per monocarp, ellipsoid-ovoid, transversely slightly striate, otherwise smooth, glabrous, more or less brown when dried, perichalazal ring sunken, aril absent, endosperm ruminations lamellate.</br></br>A monotypic genus, occurring in E India, Myanmar, S China, and Vietnam.

description: Deciduous tree to 35 m tall. Twigs appressed-pilose. description: Evergreen or rarely deciduous trees or shrubs, with spiral primary branching. Indument of simple hairs. Leaves chartaceous to subcoriaceous, base symmetrical, cuneate, rounded, or subcordate, rarely truncate, midrib slightly raised, plane, or sunken above, secondary veins usually inconspicuous, brochidodromous, tertiary venation reticulate. Inflorescences axillary or from axils of fallen leaves, 1–6-flowered. Flowers hermaphroditic, long-conical to ovoid in bud, petals only separating as anthesis begins. Sepals 3, valvate, minutely to 1/2-connate, much shorter than petals. Petals in two whorls of 3, valvate, free, linear to ovate, the inner whorl slightly shorter, narrower, and with a concave base. Stamens numerous, outermost and innermost usually staminodial, cuneate, oblong, or rarely linear, anthers septate, anther connective apex tongue-shaped, truncate, bluntly conical, or dome-shaped. Carpels one to many, stigmas filiform to clavate; ovules up to 13 per ovary, uniseriate or biseriate. Receptacle with an inconspicuous ring or hollow cone surrounding the ovaries, less often flat. Fruits apocarpous, monocarps one to many, abaxially dehiscent, oblongoid, obovoid, or narrowly cylindrical, sometimes torulose, pubescent or glabrate, smooth, verrucose, or wrinkled, short-stipitate to nearly sessile; pericarp slightly thickened, leathery when dried. Seeds attached laterally in 1–2 rows, up to 13 per monocarp, ellipsoid or oblongoid, smooth or wrinkled, with a pale bluish or greenish grey sarcotesta in vivo (not visible when dried), perichalazal ring raised or not visible, aril a fleshy or corky ring around the micropyle or aril absent, endosperm ruminations lamellate to spiniform.</br></br>A pantropical genus of nearly 200 species, represented in Thailand by 8 species, only 2 occurring north of the Kra Isthmus. The monocarps dehisce to reveal a bright scarlet to pink endocarp contrasting with the colours of the seeds.

description: Tree to 35 m tall; base of trunk with buttresses and stilt roots, bark rough, bright orange-brown. Twigs dark rusty-pubescent, at length glabrate. Leaves chartaceous, elliptic, oblong-elliptic, or oblong-oblanceolate, 9.2–20.7 by 2.3–6.6 cm, base broadly cuneate, rounded, or truncate, apex acute or acuminate, the acumen 1.5–15 mm long, glabrous above, erect-pubescent below, secondary veins 11–17 per side; petioles 3–7 mm long. Inflorescences 1–6-flowered, dark rusty-pubescent, peduncle 2–7.5 mm long, pedicels 6–19 mm long, bract 1, attached just proximal to pedicel midpoint; buds linear-lanceolate, often falciform. Sepals connate at base, narrowly triangular, 3–5.5 mm long, acuminate to caudate, apex often recurved, dark rusty-pubescent outside. Petals greenish yellow, pale yellow, or occasionally orange, sometimes marked with dark purple on the inside of the inner petal base; outer petals linear, 31–60 by 3–4.5 mm at base, apex obtuse, densely pubescent inside, sericeous outside; inner petals linear, 27–34 by 1–2.5 mm at base, apex acute, densely pubescent on both surfaces. Stamens 1.5–2.5 mm long, anther connective apex tongue-shaped. Carpels 18–20. Receptacle flat, with an inconspicous ring surrounding the ovaries. Fruit of up to 22 monocarps borne on a pedicel up to 23 mm long. Monocarps with red exocarp and red endocarp, narrowly cylindrical, torulose, terete in cross-section, 6–11.5 by 0.4–0.6 cm, slightly wrinkled, glabrate, apex rostrate, beak 1–8 mm long, base contracted into a stipe 7–14 mm long. Seeds in a single row, up to 13 per monocarp, oblongoid to ellipsoid, 5–7 by 3–4.6 mm, wrinkled, sarcotesta light bluish to grey, aril absent.

description: Shrub to tree to 17 m tall; bark scaly in irregular bands, mottled with white and pale orange-brown. Twigs pubescent, with hairs of two lengths, eventually glabrate. Leaves chartaceous, oblong, ovate, or elliptic, 5.7–10.5 by 3.7–4.9 cm, base cuneate, rounded, or subcordate-truncate, apex acute to obtuse, occasionally rounded or emarginate, sparsely erect-pubescent on both surfaces, secondary veins 7–8 per side; petioles 6–9 mm long. Inflorescences 1–4-flowered, pubescent, peduncle ca 5 mm long or lacking, pedicels 2.5–3.5 mm long, each with 2 bracts; buds lanceolate. Sepals 1/2-connate, semicircular, 2–2.6 mm long, obtuse, pubescent outside. Petals creamy yellow to orange-yellow, dark purple to purplish red at the base; outer petals lanceolate, 11–14 by 2.5–4.3 mm at base, apex obtuse, pubescent but becoming glabrous toward base on both surfaces; inner petals linear, 11–12.5 by ca 2.5 mm at base, apex acute, pubescent but becoming glabrous toward base on both surfaces. Stamens 2–2.3 mm long, anther connective apex bluntly conical. Carpels 4–7+. Receptacle with a hollow cone 2.2–2.3 mm in diameter surrounding the ovaries. Fruit of up to 12 monocarps borne on a pedicel ca 6 mm long. Monocarps with green exocarp and red endocarp, oblongoid, weakly to strongly torulose, elliptic in cross-section, 3.2–5.5 by ca 0.9 cm, obliquely wrinkled, sparsely pubescent, contracted into a stipe 6–12 mm long. Seeds in a single row, up to 6 per monocarp, ellipsoid, 7.5–8.5 by 5–5.5 mm, smooth, sarcotesta pale greyish green, aril a raised corky ring encircling the micropyle.

description: Terrestrial herbs with pseudobulbous stems, evergreen, glabrous, mostly 30–60 cm tall. Pseudobulbs conical to cylindric, covered by the bases of the foliage leaves, close together. Foliage leaves 3–4, on the apex of the pseudobulb, plicate, lanceolate-ovate, cuneate at the base, petiolate, present during flowering. Inflorescences racemose, suberect and much shorter than the foliage leaves, arising from the basal portion of the new developing shoot; peduncles partly hidden by sheathing sterile bracts; rachis few-flowered; floral bracts persistent. Flowers large, resupinate; in Thai species usually white, cream-coloured, pink or yellowish with darker markings. Sepals united in their lower part into an urceolate body, adnate to the column foot and thereby forming a distinct spur-like or globose mentum. Petals free, smaller than the sepals. Labellum 3-lobed, spurless, mobile on the apex of the column foot, clawed at the base, with erect side lobes and a triangular or oblong mid-lobe; ornamented by one to few longitudinal keels. Column with a long, U-shaped column foot, glabrous; anther incumbent, versatile, with 8 clavate waxy pollinia. Capsule erect, held on an elongate pedicel.</br></br>A genus of 11 species distributed in a broad band ranging from Sri Lanka, southern India and the Himalayas through the whole of SE Asia eastwards to New Guinea, New Caledonia and the islands of the south-western Pacific Ocean, and also ranging northwards to southern and central China and southern Japan; 3 species in Thailand.

description: Flowering shoots to 50 cm tall. Pseudobulbs ovoid-cylindric, usually with 4 nodes, c. 7 by 1–1.5 cm. Foliage leaves (1–)2–3, elliptic to oblong-elliptic, acute, 19–32 by 7–8 cm; petioles 2–16 cm long. Inflorescences: peduncles c. 10 cm long; rachis short, 3- to 6-flowered; floral bracts ovate-lanceolate, to 30 by 18 mm. Flowers white, cream-coloured or yellow with red-brown veins, labellum white and its side lobes with purple markings and a yellow mid-lobe. Sepals obtuse; dorsal sepal oblong, 18–22 by 7–11 mm; lateral sepals obliquely oblong, 24–28 by 13–17 mm, recurved at the apices, basally adnate to the column foot to form a globose mentum. Petals oblong to oblong-lanceolate, obtuse, 18–22 by 6–10 mm. Labellum 3-lobed above the claw; mid-lobe triangular, reflexed at the middle, 4–5 by 2–5 mm; side lobes hatchet-shaped, suberect, 5–8 by 5–9 mm; disk ornamented by 3 rounded and smooth keels, laterals pronounced and median one insignificant. Column 10–12 mm long, column foot 22–26 mm long. Ovary (including pedicel) 20–32 mm long. Capsule not seen.

description: Flowering shoots 35–60 cm tall. Pseudobulbs conical to cylindric, with several nodes, 8–15(–19) by 0.7–2 cm. description: The rhizomes are used to treat neurasthenia, chronic bronchitis, diarrhoea, abdominal distention, chills, colds, externally for abscesses, liver disturbance, and stomach and gut disease. The rhizome of Acorus calamus is most often used because the content of the essential oil is highest in the rhizome; the leaves are sometimes used, although the roots and leaves have a low oil content and are of no wide or practical use. Other uses are reported as aromatizer for wine and tobacco, as perfume and insecticide, and as medicine for ulcers, kidney disease, and other diseases, though basarone is said to be carcinogenic. Both species are grown as ornamentals.

description: Epiphytic, sympodial herbs with very short rhizomes; in addition to normal roots also sometimes producing erect, debris-catching roots (“catch-roots”). Pseudobulbs usually densely clustered, ovoid, relatively short and thick, each consisting of more than one internode and bearing 2–4 leaves. Foliage leaves narrow, much longer than the pseudobulbs, sheathing at base, duplicate, glabrous, deciduous. Inflorescences erect, racemous or paniculate, arising from the base of pseudobulbs, usually with many small flowers, relatively lax. Flowers opening widely. Sepals: dorsal sepal free, lateral sepals connate for their entire length to form a synsepal behind the labellum. Petals free, spreading. Labellum adnate to the basal half of the column, forming a short, narrow tube; labellum lamina bent at right angle to the column. Column straight, hooded at the apex, with 2 slender stelids that are translucent distally; column foot absent; pollinarium composed of 4 elongate solid pollinia arranged in 2 equal pairs and attached to a linear-spathulate stipe (tegule) and a tiny viscidium; rostellum beak-like. Ovary glabrous. Fruit a capsule.</br></br>A genus of c. 6 species distributed in NE India, Myanmar, Yunnan, Indo-China, Malaysia, Indonesia, Philippines, Papua New Guinea, Australia and the SW Pacific islands; 3 species in Thailand.

description: Small to medium sized, moderately robust, helophytic colony-forming herbs, to 55 cm tall. Stem rhizomatous, spongy, much-branched, ca 2 cm diam. Leaves several to many together, erect; petioles terete, spongy, 15–25 by 1–1.5 cm; sheath very short; leaf blade oblanceolate to oblong, thick, 25–40 by 9–11 cm; midrib very thick; primary lateral veins pinnate, weakly differentiated; higher order venation parallel-pinnate. Inflorescence solitary; peduncle terete, 10–22 by ca 1 cm, subequal to petiole, erect during anthesis, declinate in fruit; spathe oblong, cuspidate, convolute, erect, not differentiated into a lower tube and upper limb, 5–7 by ca 2 cm (furled), green at anthesis, then yellow and later marcescent; spadix stipitate, ± cylindrical, a little shorter than spathe, ca 4.5–6 cm; pistillate flower zone with a single whorl of flowers; comprising an oblong-cylindrical pistil, ca 3 mm diam., surrounded by a whorl of 1–3 shorter prismatic staminodes; stigma pale yellow; staminate flower zone subcylindrical, fertile to apex, a mass of undifferentiated flowers; staminate flowers ca 2–3 mm across, white. Infructescence ultimately declinate, few-fruited. Fruit an obovoid to ellipsoid dorso-ventrally compressed berry, ca 3 by 1 cm, pericarp very thick, longitudinally 2-carinate on one or both narrow sides, green, floating. Seed large, ellipsoid, testa thin, smooth, germinating within the pericarp then rupturing the attachment end to emerge as several falcate cataphylls.</br></br>A single species of colonial helophyte with distinctive spongy rhizome-like stems and petioles, and fruits functioning as floating dispersal units.

description: Diminutive to large, slender to robust creeping to suffruticose herbs. Stem epigeal, erect to decumbent and ± unbranched or sub-hypogeal, creeping and often branched. Leaves several together, forming an apical crown in erect stemmed species; petiole terete to weakly channelled; sheath usually long, occasionally very short and then the protective role taken over by cataphylls; leaf blade ovate-elliptic, narrowly elliptic, rarely broadly ovate or sublinear, base often unequal, attenuate to rounded, rarely cordate, often with striking, silvery and pale green patterns of leaf variegation; primary lateral veins pinnate; interprimary veins often weakly differentiated, running into marginal vein; higher order venation parallel-pinnate. Inflorescence 1–9 in each floral sympodium; peduncle shorter or longer than petiole, often deflexing in fruit; spathe ovate to ± globose, erect, boat-shaped to convolute, not differentiated into a lower tube and upper limb, often apiculate, green to white, slightly to strongly decurrent, caducous, marcescent or persistent and then marcescent; spadix cylindrical to clavate, shorter or longer than spathe, usually stipitate; stipe long to almost absent; pistillate flower zonerather few-flowered, contiguous with and much shorter than staminate zone; staminate flower zone fertile to apex, rarely with associated staminodes basally; staminate flowers with free stamens not forming clear floral groups; filaments usually distinct, connective thickened; thecae opposite, obovoid, short, dehiscing by apical pores or reniform transverse slits; ovary subglobose, 1-locular; ovule 1, anatropous, shortly ovoid, funicle very short, placenta basal; stylar region short, thick; stigma broad, discoid, concave centrally. Infructescence globose, few fruited. Fruit an ellipsoid berry, outer layer fleshy, at first green, later turning yellow, white or pink, and finally ripening red. Seed ellipsoid, almost as large as berry, testa very thin, ± smooth.</br></br>Twenty three species distributed from the subtropical eastern Himalaya throughout tropical and subtropical Asia as far east as New Guinea. Nine species in Thailand, one (A. chermsiriwattanae) endemic. Greatest abundance occurs in the wetter south and north, although species with rhizome-like rather than erect stems tend to be associated with seasonally dry mixed deciduous/evergreen forest</br></br>The suffruticose habit and distinctive infructescences readily identify Aglaonema. Species of Aglaonema sect. Chamaecaulon (A. brevispathum, A. costatum, & A. chermsiriwattanae) have a creeping rhizome-like stem and are superficially similar to some Homalomena species, but lack aromatic vegetative tissues, pistils with an associated staminode, and produce exposed red berries.</br></br>For discussion of typfications see Nicolson, A revision of the genus Aglaonema (Araceae), Smithsonian Contr. Bot. 1. 1969.
