description: Evergreen, medium-sized, somewhat robust, hemiepiphytic lianes to 10 m. Stem (adult) root-climbing, producing long flagelliform shoots with reduced cataphylls and scattered foliage leaves. Leaves remote from one another, the nodes between foliage leaves bearing papery cataphylls, although foliage leaves a few together at the tips of stems; petiole 15–35 cm, pulvinate apically and basally; petiolar sheath very short, barely exceeding the basal pulvinus; leaf blade (adult) ovate-cordate or pandurate-trilobed, 12–45 by 9–25 cm, largest leaves with several to many round to oval perforations near midrib, (juvenile) entire to once or twice perforated, rarely pinnatisect; deep glossy green to markedly greyish or strkingly bluish; primary lateral veins pinnate, running into marginal vein; higher order venation wholly reticulate. Inflorescence 1–several in each floral sympodium; peduncle erect, much shorter than petiole, 4–10 cm, subtended by several membranous, later papery cataphylls; spathe conchiform to ovate, apiculate, reflexed at anthesis and then caducous, very occasionally marcescent, ca 9 by 7 cm, white; spadix stipitate, ca 4–6 by 1 cm, white to cream, stipe obliquely inserted onto spadix, 0.5 cm, green; gynoecium obpyramidal or obconoid, tetragonal; stylar region broader than ovary, ca 3.5 by 2 mm, slightly prominent centrally below stigma, otherwise ± truncate; stigma small, hemispherical to transverse-linear. Infructescence comprising individual subglobose berries, these ca 1 cm diam., domed at apex, ripening white.

description: Slender to moderate evergreen lianescent to hemiepiphytic herbs lacking trichosclereids. Leaves distichous, frequently forming a terminal fan on the active shoot; petiole pulvinate apically, with petiolar sheath extending part way or fully to the base of the pulvinus; petiolar sheath persistent or marcescent; leaf blade obliquely ovate-oblong to oblong-lanceolate or oblong, entire; primary lateral veins pinnate, running into marginal vein; higher order venation reticulate. Inflorescence 1–10 or more in each floral sympodium; peduncle relatively long, erect at first, later spreading with the spadix remaining erect; spathe oblong-ovate, boat-shaped to reflexed, white, greenish white, rarely deep green or basally blotched purple, conspicuously rostrate apically, the rostrum much overtopping the spadix, caducous during anthesis, rarely persistent, or marcescent during early fruiting; spadix long-stipitate, cylindrical; flowers bisexual, perigoniate; perigone membranaceous, tepals adnate into a cup-like structure, truncate, equalling or just shorter than gynoecium; stamens 4, free; filaments relatively short, broad, spathulate, connective slender; thecae linear-elliptic, dehiscing by longitudinal slits; gynoecium with ovary obconical or obpyramidal, subquadrangular,1-locular; ovule 1, anatropous, funicle short, placenta basal; stylar region as broad as ovary, truncate; stigma transversely slender oblong. Fruit a berry, distinctly truncate apically, subglobose, ripening orange red with a distinctive transverse stigmatic remnant. Seed rounded, subglobose, testa smooth, glossy, embryo large, endosperm absent.</br></br>At least 30 species (the majority undescribed) distributed from Thailand northwards to southern China and southwards through Malesia as far as Borneo and the Philippines. At least four species in Thailand, three endemic.

description: Evergreen, medium-sized, very slender lianescent secondary hemiepiphyte to 3 m. Stem (adult) root-climbing. description: Terrestrial, rhizomatous herbs; the creeping stem-like rhizome rooting from its nodes. Flowering shoots terminal, erect from a decumbent base. 7–34 cm tall. Foliage leaves (2–)3–7, crowded on the lower part of the stem, petiolate, sheathing at base. Inflorescence racemose (to spicate); bracts acuminate, (glandular-)pubescent on the dorsal side. Flowers 1–15, resupinate. Sepals free, obtuse to acuminate, 1-veined; dorsal sepal porrect over the column, 5.1–13.4 mm long; lateral sepals more or less spreading. Petals adherent (rarely adnate) to the dorsal sepal, acuminate to obtuse. Labellum basally adnate to the column, straight (i.e. not twisted), 6–12 mm long along the mid-line, differentiated into hypochile, mesochile, and epichile; hypochile spurred (protruding below the bases of the lateral sepals when the flower is viewed from the side), spur inside with 1 subsessile appendage on either side; mesochile with one pair of entire to pectinate lateral flanges: epichile deeply bilobed. Column straight (i.e., not twisted), with two parallel wings on the front; stigma bipartite, flat; rostellum triangular, bifid: viscidium 1, naked; anther versatile, (sub)acuminate in front; pollinia 2, basitonous. Ovary (glandular-)pubescent. Fruit a capsule dehiscing by 6 longitudinal slits.</br></br>A genus of ca. 30 species distributed from tropical Southeast Asia to northeastern Queensland and the western Pacific islands; 6 species in Thailand.

description: Flowering shoots 7–32.5 cm tall. Foliage leaves very dark green to brown with pink to whitish reticulation above, uniformly pink below; lamina obliquely (ovate-helliptic, acute to subacuminate, mucronate, (1.8–)3.1–7 by (1.3–)2–5.5 cm. Inflorescence glandular-pubescent; rachis 1.5–7.6 cm long, 3- to 13-flowered; bracts lanceolate-oblong to ovate-lanceolate, 1-veined, pubescent on the dorsal side, 10.1–12 by 3.9–5.9 mm. description: Terrestrial or sometimes lithophytic herbs with corms borne shallowly underground, glabrous. Foliage leaves mostly 2 or 3, plicate, narrowly lanceolate, deciduous. Labellum basally united with the column, spurless, narrow in the lower part, apical part expanded and 3-lobed, without prominent ornaments. description: Terrestrial, mycoheterotrophic herbs with underground, sparsely to densely rooted, often flexuous rhizomes and erect flowering shoots. Stem slender to robust, (purplish-)brown to pale yellowish. Leaves alternate, reduced to brownish scales that are sheathing (below) to non-sheathing (above). Rhizome condensed, producing fibrous roots. Inflorescence terminal, racemose, bearing 3 to many resupinate flowers. Sepals and petals free, subsimilar or sepals distinctly larger than petals. Labellum differentiated into hypochile and epichile; hypochile firmly attached to column, flat to concave (but never saccate or spurred), with or without distinct side lobes; epichile elastically attached, devoid of longitudinal keels, often more or less papillose on the ventral surface. Column slender, (sub)clavate, more or less incurved, glabrous, without stelids and foot; pollinia 2, soft and mealy, devoid of caudicles; rostellum slightly protruding, stipe absent, viscidium absent or obscure; receptive part of stigma concave. Ovary distinctly pedicelled; pedicel not elongating during fruit ripening. Fruit a pedicelled capsule dehiscing by longitudinal slits.</br></br>A genus of c. 25 species distributed throughout Indo-Malesia to Japan and northern Queensland; 4 species in Thailand.

Rachis 1.4–9 cm long, 3- to many-flowered, sparsely glandular-pubescent; floral bracts ovate-lanceolate to elliptic, obtuse to acuminate, mucronate, 2.9–5.4 by 1.6–2.3 mm. Flowers not opening widely, mainly (brownish-)white to cream (sepals often with purple markings; labellum usually white, sometimes with purple margins). Sepals subglabrous; dorsal sepal boat-shaped, lanceolate-oblong, obtuse, 4.2–4.7 by 1.8–2 mm; lateral sepals weakly boat-shaped, obliquely lanceolate-oblong, obtuse to rounded, keeled at apex, 3.5–4.3 by 1.7–1.8 mm. Petals slightly spreading, falcately lanceolate-oblong, subacuminate, 3.2–4.4 by 1.2–1.7 mm. Labellum 2.8–3.2 mm long; hypochile with well-developed, erect, obliquely linear-triangular, rounded to obtuse side lobes, 0.8–1.1 by 2.6–2.8 mm when flattened; epichile 2.6–2.9 mm wide when flattened, porrect (continuing the line of the hypochile), cordate with raised sides and rounded, often slightly hooded apex, entire ventral surface glabrous and smooth. Column slightly incurved, 2.3–2.4 mm long (to apex of anther); anther cordate in upper view, 0.8–1 mm long, apex rounded; rostellum broadly triangular; receptive part of stigma crescent-shaped. Ovary (including pedicel) 5.8–8 mm long, somewhat scurfy-pubescent. Capsule nodding to pendent, fusiform-terete, 0.9–1.1 cm long (excluding perianth remnants and pedicel), c. 0.2 cm in diameter; fruit pedicel 2–3 mm long.

description: Small to moderate herbs. Stem pleionanthic, epigeal, erect to decumbent. Leaves few to many, often clustering terminally on the shoot, innovations generally pink; petiole usually glabrous, sometimes minutely puberulent, leaf sheath fully attached, tapering, persistent to slowly degrading in the marginal distal part; leaf blade oblanceolate to ovate-sagittate, sometimes variegated, glabrous adaxially and abaxially, basally cuneate to sagittate, apex acute to long acuminate; primary and secondary venation bipinnate, tertiary venation obscure. Inflorescence solitary or to 5 in a synflorescence; spathe long, to 20 cm; lower spathe, ovoid, differentiated from the spathe limb with a gradual or abrupt constriction; spathe limb oblong-lanceolate, upper spathe persistent until well after anthesis, then deliquescing, opening only slightly, the distal portion remaining convolute, with only the ventral part of the staminate flower zone exposed; spadix equalling or shorter than spathe; pistillate flower zone more or less cylindrical, obliquely inserted to adnate for up to ½ of its length; pistils globose, sessile; interpistillar staminodes present or absent; interstice prominent, mostly naked with a few groups of small, more or less sessile staminodes; staminate flower zone cylindrical to slightly tapering, the lower part corresponding with the spathe constriction; stamens crowded, dumbbell-shaped to irregular; appendix present; fruiting spathe urceolate, declinate; fruits and seeds not seen.</br></br>About 13 species from S Myanmar to S Thailand, Sumatra (the majority), and Peninsular Malaysia. Two species in Thailand.</br></br>Apoballis is defined by the deciduous leaf sheath, pistillate and staminate flower zones separated by a prominent naked interstice interspersed sparsely with staminodes, and a spathe that hardly opens, and is semipersistent into fruiting. Further, all species so far investigated have spiny pollen (smooth in Schismatoglottis and all other Schismatoglottideae). Apoballis produces a floral odour reminiscent of benzaldehyde (almond oil), contrasting to Schismatoglottis (methyl esterase). This, together with the differences in spadix arrangement and spathe mechanics, suggests pollinator differences.

description: Stem epigeal, pleionanthic, to ca 30 cm long by ca 8 mm diam., decumbent, creeping to decumbent-trailing. Leaves 1–6 per module; petiole ca 15 cm long by ca 3 mm diam., the margins minutely alate and sometimes crisped, slightly asperous, minutely hairy/spinulous (hand-lens required), pale green to purplish, sheathing in the lower ½–¾; petiolar sheath fully attached, tending to degrade at least in the upper half, becoming dark brown and flaking shortly after the emergence of the enclosed leaf; leaf blade (elliptic to) ovate, ca 9–12 by 4–6 cm, widest about the mid-point, pale to mid-green, slightly glossy to dull, tinged bronze when young, the base obtuse to rather weakly cordate with posterior lobes (0–) ca 8 mm long, apex acute to weakly acuminate, margin smooth to weakly undulate; midrib abaxially prominent; primary lateral veins 6–9 on each side, ca 1 cm apart; interprimary veins irregularly present; secondary venation flush adaxially and abaxially, arising from the midrib and the bases of the primary veins; tertiary venation faintly visible adaxially, forming a tessellate reticulum. Inflorescences 1–5 together; peduncle thin, to ca 5 cm by 2.5 mm, erect at anthesis, then dangling; spathe 5.5–7.5 cm long; lower spathe narrow ovoid, to 3.5 by ca 1.5 cm, green; spathe limb persistent until well after anthesis, then deliquescing, lanceolate, acuminate tipped, opening only slightly, the distal portion remaining convolute, with only the ventral part of the staminate zone exposed; spadix 5–6 cm long; pistillate flower zone 2–2.5 cm long, more or less cylindrical, slightly curved towards dorsal side of spathe, obliquely inserted to adnate for ca ⅓ its length; pistils ca 0.75 mm diam., globose-polyhedral, pale green, somewhat distant and sometimes patchily distributed; style absent; stigma globose; interpistillar staminodes numerous, irregularly distributed, ca 1 mm long, larger than the pistils, globular, very shortly stalked, white; sterile interstice 1–1.3 cm long, cylindrical to slightly tapering, 5–8 mm thick, partly naked, consisting proximally of rather crowded structures resembling interpistillar staminodes, distally of scattered groups of much smaller staminodes resembling the stamens; staminate flower zone ca 1.5 by 0.5 cm, cylindrical to slightly spindle-shaped, the lower part corresponding with the spathe constriction; stamens dumbbell-shaped, ca 1 mm across, with the connective rather slender, slightly shorter than the thecae; appendix very short, 3–5 mm long, conical; appendix staminodes columnar, ivory white, ca 1 mm diam. Fruiting spathe declinate, urceolate.

description: Slender to moderately robust, erect herbs, ca 0.35–1.1 m tall; stem epigeal, pleionanthic, ca 2–4 cm thick, often clothed with the remains of old leaf bases in the upper part, the lower part naked as these rot; internodes ca 1–4 cm diam., often with conspicuous, rather thick roots. Leaves ca 5 per module, very variable in size; petiole ca 20–45 cm long, smooth to very faintly asperous to minutely velvety-hairy, adaxially flattened to slightly channelled with the angles rounded to distally inconspicuously alate, pale green to bright dark red, sometimes somewhat glaucous (by minute hairs, not wax), sheathing in the lower ⅓–3∕5; petiolar sheath membranous, fully attached and tapering, deliquescent/marcescent more or less immediately after emergence of leaf within; leaf blade broadly to narrowly ovate-sagittate, ca 12–40 by 6–30 cm, widest from the base to about ⅓ along midrib, the base more or less cordate with posterior lobes prominent, ca 3–12 cm long, triangular to rounded, sometimes almost overlapping across the sinus and posterior costae sometimes clearly differentiated for a few millimetres before dividing into primary venation of posterior lobes, occasionally naked in the sinus for 2–3 mm, more usually with leaf blade to the sinus and occasionally sub-peltate, apex acute to shortly acuminate, somewhat glossy bright mid-green to dull mid-green, usually bronze-tinged to pink when newly emerged; midrib abaxially prominent; primary lateral veins 9–15 per side, sometimes branched, impressed adaxially, prominent abaxially; interprimary veins rather conspicuous and raised abaxially, impressed adaxially; secondary venation flush with leaf blade and mostly inconspicuous; tertiary venation inconspicuous. Inflorescences 2–several together; peduncle rather short, slender; spathe ca 7–15 cm long; lower spathe ca ⅓ the length of the whole, ovoid to subglobose at pistillate anthesis, green to red (correlated with petiole colour); spathe limb narrowly lanceolate, clasping the spadix, barely opening at anthesis, then closing again and temporarily persistent, eventually marcescent or breaking away after senescing, yellowish ivory to pale orange; spadix more or less cylindrical-tapering, subequalling the spathe, sessile, obliquely inserted; pistillate flower zone ca ⅓ the length of the spadix, cylindrical, ca 8–10 mm diam. at base, slightly tapering distally; interpistillar staminodes very sparsely to irregularly densely distributed amongst the ovaries, but usually concentrated at the very base of pistillate zone, stalked and clavate-headed, taller than and conspicuously larger than the pistils; sterile interstice 1–2 by 0.4–0.7 cm, composed of basal sessile interpistillar staminodes, then a concentration of smaller sessile staminodes, these becoming distant distally in small groups of commonly 2–4 surrounded by naked spadix tissue, these then usually concentrated again in an incomplete ring adjoining the staminate zone; staminate flower zone more or less cylindrical, ca 1.3–3.3 cm long, slightly thicker than top of sterile interstice, 5–8 mm diam.; stamens small, rectangular-dumbbell-shaped from above, 0.5 by 1 mm, with the thecae impressed; appendix exceeding to shorter than the staminate zone, ca 1.5–3 cm long, tapering and pointed to cylindrical and round-tipped, basally the same diameter as the staminate zone, rarely narrowly ovoid, composed of columnar flat-topped staminodes. Fruiting spathe declinate, narrowly ovoid.

description:
Moderate sized, solitary or clustering, monoecious palms. Stem often with green internodes, distinct leaf scars distally, and a cone of adventitious roots basally. Leaves 5–10 in crown, spirally arranged; sheath tubular forming a yellowish to brownish tinged green crownshaft; petiole very short or less than 50 cm long, unarmed, smooth; blade splitting in usually regularly distributed, one to several folded, narrowly sigmoid pinnae, distributed in one plane, leaf apex often composed of several irregularly splitting, closely inserted pinnae. Inflorescence infrafoliar, branched from first to third order, sheathed in bud only by the prophyll, this thinly coriaceous and early deciduous, peduncle short, inflorescence branches spreading to stiffly erect. Unisexual flowers in cymose flower cluster of two to three, or solitary towards the rachillae apices, female flowers much larger than male flowers, only fully developed at the very base of the rachillae, male flowering part of rachillae wilting and often present as tails in the infructescence. Fruit one seeded, epicarp smooth usually red at maturity, mesocarp usually thin, fleshy to fibrous, endocarp composed of longitudinal fibres, more or less free at the base, endosperm deeply ruminate.

Fifty species found in tropical and subtropical Asia; four species native in Thailand, one (A. catechu) is only known from cultivation and not included here since it has not been recorded from the wild (Plate XCVIII: A).

description: Low shrubs to robust tree palms, solitary or clustered, monoecious usually with unisexual inflorescences, male and female flowering separated in time, pleonanthic or hapaxanthic. Leaves imparipinnate, induplicate; leaf sheath usually disintegrating into a fibrous mesh; petiole slender to very robust; leafl ets regularly arranged in one plane or unevenly arranged in several planes, strongly asymmetrical at the base, sometimes with one or two auricles. Flowering acropetal in pleonanthic species, basipetal in hapaxanthic species. Inflorescence enclosed in numerous bracts, branched to first or second order, drooping, unisexual, in hapaxanthic species the female ones produced distally before the male ones. Flowers dimorphic. Male flowers usually with more than 15 functional stamens, and without a pistillode. Female flowers with globose ovary, sessile stigmas and 2–3 locules. Fruit globose to ellipsoidal, often somewhat angled, 1–3 seeded; epicarp smooth, dull to brightly coloured, mesocarp fleshy, with high density of raphide-containing ideoblasts causing skin irritation, endocarp not differentiated. Seed with homogeneous endosperm.</br></br>Twenty four species with three varieties in tropical and subtropical Asia to N Australia. Five species in Thailand.

description: Solitary palm tree to 20 m tall, hapaxanthic. Stem 40–60 cm diam., usually covered to the base by persistent leaf sheaths, basally with a cone of adventitious roots. Inflorescences 4–6, interfoliar, flowering sequence on stem basipetal; peduncle 30–60 cm long, upright, and curved; rachis 0.8–1.2 m long, drooping; rachillae 40–70, to 0.6–1.6 m long, drooping. Fruit globose or slightly longer than wide, 5–7 cm diam., bluish-green or dark green at maturity. Seed elongate to elliptic, with a sharp keel, scar from funicle inconspicuous.

description: Very small, slender, seasonally dormant, lithophytic herbs with milky latex, to 12 cm tall. Stem a ± subglobose tuber, ca 2 cm diam., mostly clustered, covered with fibrous cataphyll remains. Leaves solitary; petiole very slender, 6–14 cm, sheath very short; leaf blade peltate, cordate-ovate, 5–10 by 4–10 cm, membranaceous, pale green above, glaucous below, posterior lobes short, fully fused; primary lateral veins pinnate, radiating from petiole insertion, forming submarginal collective vein; higher order venation reticulate. Inflorescences 1–3 in each floral sympodium, appearing before the leaves; peduncle very slender, 4–5 cm, much longer than spathe, erect to spreading; spathe ovate, boat-shaped, 2–2.5 by 1 cm, not constricted, hooded, gaping widely at anthesis, not convolute at base, marcescent, dull yellow; spadix shorter than spathe, ca 1.5 by 0.4 cm; pistillate flower zone adnate to spathe, ca 4 mm long, few-flowered; ovaries rhombic-ovoid to rhombic-ovoid-oblong, ca 3 by 4 mm, pale green speckled purple, stylar region very short; stigma stellate with 4–6 lobes, lobes initially erect, later spreading and reflexed, whitish green; sterile interstice free, naked, ca 3 mm long; staminate flower zone fertile to apex, cylindrical-conoid, ca 10 by 4 mm, many-flowered, dirty very pale yellow; synandria peltate, the connate filaments forming a stipe longer and narrower than dilated common connective, synandria all connate apically, forming continuous surface punctured by cavities with somewhat prominent margins into which pollen is shed from the 6(–8) surrounding thecae of which each pair of thecae belongs to a different synandrium. Fruit a 4–6-angled berry, ca 5 by 5 mm, pale green, stigma persistent.

description: Seasonally dormant geophytic, or evergreen herbs. Stem a subglobose tuber producing tubercles or stolons in deciduous species, or a branching rhizome in evergreen species; petiole(s) either slightly sheathed basally, or forming a pseudostem. Foliage leaves 1–2, rarely 3; leaf blade usually compound, with bilateral or radial symmetry; lobes variable in shape, petiolulate or sessile. Inflorescence emerging with or after the leaves, solitary, monoecious or dioecious; peduncle either independent from petiole(s) or almost completely sheathed by them; spathe with the lower part tubular, variously expanded above into a limb; spadix ending in a sterile appendix, stipitate or sessile, slightly to long-exserted from lower spathe, often with some awn-like or filamentous projections on the basal part, sometimes with these structures covering up to the apex; pistillate flowers usually densely arranged; ovary 1-locular, containing several basal ovules; stigma sessile or on a short style; staminate flowers 2–6-androus; filaments connate, forming a stalk; thecae dehiscing by rounded pores or slits. Infructescence globose, conical or subcylindrical, peduncle erect or nodding; fruits a berry, subglobose, red or orange when ripe, usually few-seeded. Seeds ovoid to globose, testa hard, cream or brown coloured.</br></br>Arisaema differs from all other Araceae by sex changes which may occur, year by year, reversibly; this character is so peculiar that Nakai created the term paradioecious to describe it.</br></br>One of the larger genera of Araceae, with ca 200 species, primarily in warm temperate or subtropical regions. Thailand has 18 species and subspecies, of which 9 are endemic.

description: Deciduous herb to 0.5 m tall. Subterranean stem a subglobose tuber, to 5 cm across by 2.5 cm high, brownish. Pseudostem 10–25 by ca 1.2 cm at the base, olive-green with light pink mottling and faint dark green longitudinal stripes. Leaf solitary; cataphylls to 16 cm long, dark pink with olive-green mottling and slightly prominent pale pink dots; petiole ca 25 by ca 1 cm at the base; leaf blade trifoliolate; leaflets ovate, shiny green; margin entire, apex acuminate often ending in a short arista; central leaflet ca 20 cm by 8 cm, base cuneate with a petiolule ca 1 cm long; lateral leaflets asymmetrical, slightly shorter than the central, base convex with a petiolule ca 0.5 cm long. Inflorescence emerging after the leaf, and held at leaf level; peduncle shorter than the petiole, to 12 cm long by 5 mm across, white-green with faint darker stripes; spathe tube cylindrical, ca 5 by ca 1.5 cm; white-green with dotted purple stripes; spathe mouth margins widely recurved, ca 5–6 mm wide; spathe limb suberect, ovate-oblong, 4–7(–10) by 4–4.5 cm, yellow-green, paler at the base, translucent, with numerous, thin darker longitudinal veins, these prominent outside, limb acuminate, ending in a short thread; spadix appendix exserted from the spathe tube, but shorter than the spathe, 4–6 cm long, tip subulate, covered with many, bristle-like, filiform, flexuous projections, these 1–3 cm long, appendix naked in the middle part, at the base 2 mm wide, sessile and with a few neuter flowers, these 2–5 mm long and inserted just above the fertile part; fertile zone staminate or pistillate, ca 2 cm long; staminate flowers loosely arranged, 2–3-androus; anthers cream, subsessile; thecae dehiscent by a carmine, elongate pore; pistillate flowers: ovary bottle-shaped, green; stigma penicillate, with a short style. Infructescence on an erect peduncle, cylindrical, to 7 by ca 2.5 cm; fruits 10 by 8 mm, prismatic, apically flattened with black stigmatic remains, red-orange when ripe, to 4 seeds per berry. Seeds globose, 3 mm diam.

description: Terrestrial, sometimes rheophytic herbs. Rhizome stout, producing many, densely aggregated flowering shoots. Stem erect, wiry to reed-like, covered by leaf sheaths, often swollen at base. Foliage leaves 6 to many, (sub)distichous, decreasing in size towards the proximal and distal part of the shoot, persistent, green, conduplicate, narrowly linear to linear lanceolate, herbaceous. Inflorescence terminal, racemose or paniculate, elongating gradually during flowering; floral bracts persistent, amplexicaul, much shorter than ovaries. Flowers opening in succession, resupinate, usually pinkish-white with the labellum being violet to magenta (especially towards apex) with a yellow blotch in its central part (but pale as well as very strongly coloured forms occur). Sepals free; lateral sepals more or less connivent behind labellum. Petals spreading, wider than sepals. Labellum trumpet-shaped, 3-lobed, not spurred or saccate; side lobes semi-obovate, rounded, enfolding column; mid-lobe emarginate to deeply cleft; disk ornamented by a few papillose-pubescent longitudinal keels. Column slender, erect, straight to somewhat incurved, dilated and narrowly winged towards apex, devoid of stelids and foot; anther terminal, incumbent; pollinia 8 in 2 groups, more or less waxy, with short caudicles and a common viscidium. Ovary (including pedicel) terete, slender. Fruit a distinctly pedicelled capsule dehiscing by longitudinal slits.</br></br>A probably monospecific genus; distribution as for A. graminifolia subsp. graminifolia (see below).

description: Perennial herbs; root somewhat carrot-shaped. Leaves alternate. description: Stem single, simple, erect, 30–100 cm tall, usually unbranched, rarely branched in response to damage, usually glabrous, sometimes sparsely hairy towards the base. description: Terrestrial, rhizomatous herbs; rhizome irregularly shaped, rooting at nodes with many long fibrous roots. Flowering shoots terminal, erect. Foliage leaves 2–5, often erect, glabrous, plicate, narrowly oblong to narrowly lanceolate, sheathing at the base. Inflorescence racemose, terminal, erect; peduncle terete, with a few sterile bracts; rachis short, terete, simple or occasionally branched; floral bracts lanceolate, caducous. Flowers 2–3, resupinate, often showy, white, pink, purple, or yellow, glabrous; pedicel and ovary slender. Sepals free. Petals free, similar to sepals but slightly larger. Labellum firmly attached, not fused with column, often 3-lobed, porrect, without spur, often ornamented by longitudinal keels, lateral lobes erect and clasping the column. Column arcuate, clavate, winged, glabrous, without column foot; anther incumbent, 2-locular; pollinia 8 in 2 groups of 4, granular, oblong and laterally compressed, caudicles inconspicuous; stigma suborbicular to transversely elliptic; rostellum truncate, projecting forward over the stigma, not producing a viscidium. Ovary terete, glabrous. Fruit a capsule, oblong-fusiform, erect.</br></br>A genus of c. 5 species distributed from northern Myanmar, Indo-China and China to Japan; 1 species in Thailand.

description: Solitary, dioecious, pleonanthic palm trees. Leaves induplicate, costapalmate; leaf sheath splitting to the base, fibrous along margins, with additional triangular cleft below the petiole; petiole robust, deeply channelled above, margins smooth and very sharp; adaxial hastula well developed, abaxial hastula reduced or absent, blade deeply divided into several folded segments, these further parted into single-folded segments, transverse veinlets conspicuous. Inflorescences interfoliar, dimorphic, enclosed at the base in the prophyll and one to few peduncular bracts, more or less drooping at anthesis. Male inflorescences branched to second order, male rachillae with tight spiral of imbricate bracts, subtending and covering sympodial flower clusters of 2–6 flowers, male flowers exserted one at a time as they pass into anthesis, stamens 6–15, pistillode minute to absent. Female inflorescence spicate or with few branches, with tight spiral of overlapping bracts, each subtending a single female flower, this much larger than male flower and only partly covered by the bracts, staminodes much reduced, gynoecium globose, 3-loculate with sessile stigmas. Fruit large, rounded, usually 3-seeded, rarely with fewer seeds, epicarp smooth, mesocarp fibrous, endocarp around individual pyrenes very thick and grooved. Seed with homogeneous endosperm.</br></br>Two species, Peninsular Thailand, Peninsular Malaysia, Borneo. One species in Thailand.

description: Terrestrial, ephiphytic or lithophytic, more or less woody plants. Rhizome creeping, short to somewhat elongated. Stems simple, flexible to stiff, terete to laterally compressed, not swollen. Foliage leaves distichous, articulate, glabrous, herbaceous to hard-coriaceous, duplicate or bilaterally flattened. Inflorescence terminal, racemose, accrescent, usually simple, few- to many-flowered; rachis pubescent or mealy-hairy; bracts persistent, imbricate or very nearly so. Flowers resupinate, opening in succession or very few open at the same time, very short-lived. Sepals free, elliptic or oblong to linear-lanceolate, glabrous; lateral sepals slightly falcate. Petals free, elliptic or oblong to lanceolate, usually thinner than the sepals, glabrous. Labellum concave, 3-lobed; disk glabrous or with scattered hairs; side lobes often densely hairy or papillose; mid-lobe suborbicular to lingulate, more or less recurved, usually ornamented by a papillose or hairy elongate callus. Ovary slender. Fruit a cylindrical capsule, dehiscing by 6 longitudinal slits.</br></br>A genus of c. 27 species, distributed in Sri Lanka, Myanmar, Indo-China, Thailand,  Peninsular Malaysia, Borneo, Sumatra, Java, the Philippines, Maluku, New Guinea and Queensland; 5 species in Thailand.

description: Solitary or clustering, stemless to high-climbing or erect pleonanthic dioecious rattans; sheaths usually heavily armed with spines, the spines frequently highly organized; flagellum (sterile inflorescence) often present, borne on the leaf sheath, sometimes absent and replaced by a cirrus at the end of the leaf, very rarely both present or both absent; knee often present; ocrea sometimes well developed, usually inconspicuous. Male and female inflorescences superficially similar, often ending in a long flagellum, sometimes with gradual succession of branches, often with discrete distant branches (partial inflorescences); bracts always tubular at the base, rarely with broad limbs splitting down one side but, if so, then the base always tubular and unsplit, bracts variously armed; partial inflorescences usually much longer than the subtending bract, very rarely shorter, floral bracteoles inconspicuous. Male flower solitary in each rachilla bract, with cup-shaped calyx, usually with 3 well defined lobes; corolla split almost to the base into 3 petals; stamens 6 (very rarely 12), very shortly epipetalous; pistillode minute. Female flower borne together with a sterile male flower as a pair; sterile male flower like the fertile male, but with empty anthers; female flower usually larger than the male, with calyx shallowly 3-lobed; corolla with 3 petals; staminodes 6, joined basally to form a ring; ovary tipped with 3 stigmas and covered with reflexed scales; locules 3 with one ovule in each. Fruit variously shaped, covered in reflexed scales. Seed usually one only, rarely 3 developing, very variable in shape, covered in a thin to thick sarcotesta; endosperm homogeneous or ruminate; embryo basal or lateral. Seedling leaf bifid or pinnate.</br></br>About 388 species: Africa, Sri Lanka, India and South China, southwards through Malesia to Australia and Fiji. Reaches its greatest diversity in Peninsular Malaysia and Borneo with a secondary centre of diversity in New Guinea. Fifty four species with two subspecies and four varieties in Thailand.</br></br>Calamus can only be identified to genus by a combination of characters. Together with Ceratolobus, Daemonorops and Pogonotium it forms a group of closely related genera in which the female inflorescence bears dyads – pairs of flowers, each consisting of a female flower together with a sterile male flower – while the male inflorescence bears male flowers singly. The differences between these genera are based mostly on the overall structure of the inflorescence, in particular the nature of the bracts. The most reliable character separating Calamus is the persistent tubular nature of the bracts. Some generalisations can be made – rattans with flagella must belong to Calamus, though not all species of Calamus bear flagella. Rattans with subcirrate leaves are usually species of Calamus. If the endosperm is homogeneous, then the rattan cannot belong to Daemonorops, but ruminate endosperms are found in both genera. The differences are summarized in the key to genera. With practice the genera are eventually easily distinguished.

description: Slender clustering rattan. Stem climbing to 20 m, without sheaths 0.6–0.8 cm diam., with sheaths 1–1.2 cm diam., internodes 5–12 cm long. Leaves ecirrate; leaf sheath rather densely covered with solitary spines 0.1–1.3 cm long, with slightly swollen bases, thin scattered pale brown tomentum present between the spines; knee prominent, c. 0.3 cm high, unarmed or more sparsely armed than the sheath; flagellum to 125 cm long; petiole 7–12.5 cm long, c. 0.4 cm wide, armed abaxially and laterally with recurved spines to 0.4 cm, adaxially ± unarmed; rachis 22–47 cm long, armed abaxially with recurved spines; leaflets rhomboid, 5–6 on each side of the rachis, regularly arranged but rather distant, apical pair divergent, basal leaflets 6–10 by 2.8–4.6 cm, middle leaflets 9–17.5 by 3.5–6.5 cm, with numerous radiating veins, transverse veinlets conspicuous, margins undulate and bearing sparse black bristles. Inflorescence (only female known) to 90 cm long including terminal flagellum to 60 cm long, branching to 2 orders, with 1–3 partial inflorescences; prophyll strictly tubular, entire, 8–19 cm long, armed with scattered reflexed spines, rachis bracts similar; partial inflorescences inserted on the rachis at the mouth of the subtending bract; rachillae 5–7, distichously arranged, 1–4 cm long, c. 0.15–0.2 cm diam., ± straight, appearing zig-zag from flower insertions; rachilla bracts striate. Female flower c. 0.3 by 0.2 cm. Fruit broadly ovoid, abruptly beaked, beak to 1.8 by 1.4 cm; scales straw yellow with dark margins, arranged in 18 vertical rows. Seed c. 1 by 0.7–0.8 cm, coarsely pitted; endosperm ruminate. Seedling leaf with two divergent rhomboid leaflets.

description: Clustering moderate-sized rattan forming thickets. Stems climbing to 20 m or more, without sheaths 1.5 cm diam., with sheaths to 3.5 cm diam., internodes to c. 20 cm long. description: Clustering, moderate-sized rattan. Stems potentially climbing to great heights, to 100 m or more, usually much less due to over-exploitation, the clump tending to be very close and dense, without sheaths 0.7–1.8 cm diam., with sheaths to 2.5 cm diam., internodes to 50 cm long, sometimes even longer in juveniles, bare stem highly polished, covered with a shiny silica layer, breaking off in flakes when stem bent. Seed ovoid, c. 1.2 by 0.7 cm; endosperm deeply ruminate. Seedling leaf forked, the two lobes parallel, ¼ the length of the whole lamina, adaxially dark green, abaxially greyish-white.

description: Clustering acaulescent non-climbing palm of the forest undergrowth. Mature fruit ellipsoid, to 2.5 by 1.8 cm, strongly beaked, covered in 18–27 vertical rows of chestnut brown scales. Seed c. 1.8 by 1.2 cm; endosperm homogeneous. description: Clustering massive erect non-climbing rattan. Stems to 6 m tall, without sheaths 3–5 cm diam., with sheaths to 7 cm diam., internodes short, not usually exceeding 8 cm long. description: Slender solitary or clustering rattan. Stems climbing to 15 m long, usually less, without sheaths 0.4–0.6 cm diam., with sheaths 1.5 cm (rarely to 2.5 cm) diam.; internodes to 15 cm long. Leaves ecirrate; sheaths dull greyish-brown, vary variable in armature, always very densely covered with minute spines giving a scabrid feel to the whole sheath, triangular spines to 1.2 cm long with hairy margins sometimes also present on the sheaths, particularly in montane populations; knee conspicuous, armed as the sheath; ocrea inconspicuous; flagellum to 1.75 m long; petiole to 15 cm long; rachis 20–40 cm long, scabrid as the leaf sheaths, bearing conspicuous pale chestnut-brown hairs adaxially among the bases of the leaflets; leaflets 20–25 on each side of the rachis, regularly arranged, linear-lanceolate to lanceolate, to 15 by 0.8 cm, rather thin in texture, densely covered with fine pale bristles on both surfaces and margins, rarely these bristles almost absent. Inflorescences flagellate, to 75 cm long, with 2–7 partial inflorescences, the male inflorescence branched to 3 orders, the female to 2 orders; rachillae of both sexes strongly reflexed, the male to 1 by 0.1 cm, the female to 4 by 0.3 cm, the flower groups with conspicuous circular cup-like attachment. Mature fruit ovoid to oblong, to 1.3 by 0.8 cm, borne on a large disk, shortly beaked, covered in 15–18 vertical rows of straw-coloured scales. Seed ovoid to oblong, c. 1 by 0.6 cm, flattened on one side, very deeply and sinuously grooved, the whole with a thin, green, intensely bitter and foetid sarcotesta; endosperm homogeneous. Seedling leaf pinnate with up to 10 ciliate hairy leafl ets on each side and conspicuous rusty hairs adaxially along the rachis.

description: Slender clustering rattan. All parts drying pale green. Stem without sheaths c. 0.9 cm diam., with sheaths c. 1.5 cm diam., internodes 15–17 cm long. Leaves ecirrate; sheaths bearing scattered triangular, somewhat flattened black spines to 1.1 by 0.6 cm, with paler bases, the spine bases sometimes rather oblique and downswept, these often interspersed with much smaller black spines to 0.2 cm long, also with swollen bases, scattered caducous indumentum present between spines; ocrea very short, sometimes with a group of spines opposite the petiole; knee present; flagellum to c. 50 cm long; petiole absent in mature climbing stems, present in juveniles, up to 3 cm long; rachis 50–60 cm long, armed with scattered black tipped reflexed spines with swollen bases; leaflets narrow lanceolate, 15–17 on each side of the rachis, regularly arranged, the longest to 27 by 2 cm, the tips long acuminate, adaxially bright shiny green, abaxially paler with some very thin grey caducous indumentum, bristly along mid vein both adaxially and abaxially and along margins. Mature fruit rounded, c. 1.3 cm diam., with a short beak to 0.1 by 0.1 cm, and covered in 17 vertical rows of pale straw-coloured channelled scales with darker margins. Seed c. 1 by 1 by 0.7 cm, flattened laterally with a hollow at the chalaza, deeply grooved and almost brain-like; endosperm homogeneous. Seedling leaf not recorded.

description: Slender clustering rattan. Stem without sheaths c. 0.5 cm diam., with sheaths 0.8 cm diam., internodes c. 15 cm long. Leaves ecirrate; sheaths bearing scattered solitary reflexed narrow triangular spines 0.2–0.6 by 0.1–0.15 cm with swollen bases, and thin caducous brown tomentum; knee well developed, unarmed; flagellum to 60 cm; petiole absent; rachis 20–30 cm long, bearing scattered, reflexed curved spines to 2 by 1.5 cm with black tips and swollen bases; leaflets broadly lanceolate, rather thin, 5–6 on each side of the rachis, the proximal 2–3 reflexed across the sheathed stem, the apical two joined for about one half their length, and forming a group of four with two more leaflets, the other leaflets very distant and somewhat irregularly arranged, basal leaflets 4–16 by 0.7–30 cm; middle leaflets 10.5–26 by 3–4.5 cm; apical leaflets 12–21 by 3–4.5 cm; upper surface of leaflets with conspicuous distant transverse veinlets, undersurface of leaflets covered in thin grey tomentum. Inflorescence flagelliform, only female known, to at least 112 cm long, with at least 2 partial inflorescences; bracts strictly tubular, tightly sheathing, with triangular tips and bearing scattered and rather sparse reflexed spines to 0.2 by 0.1 cm, with scattered brown indumentum between; partial inflorescences to at least 45 cm long, and 2–3 distant rachillae on each side; rachillae held ± at right angles, to 0.45 by 0.2 cm. Immature fruit ovoid to broadly ellipsoid, 0.7 by 0.4 cm with a beak 0.2 by 0.1 cm and covered in 20 vertical rows of pale brown scales with mid-brown margins and central marking and pale tips.

description: Solitary, massive high-climbing rattan. Stems ultimately reaching over 100 m long, but rarely attaining this due to overharvesting, without sheaths to 8 cm diam., sometimes very much more slender near the stem base (c. 2.5 cm diam.), with sheaths to 11 cm diam., internodes to 40 cm long, less in exposed stems from above the forest canopy. Leaf cirrate; sheaths dull grey green, densely armed with black, flattened, hairy-margined, patent or slightly reflexed, triangular spines, the largest to 3 by 1 cm, scattered or arranged in lateral groups, much smaller spines to 0.5 cm long abundant between the larger spines, thin white wax abundant between spines, particularly on newly emerged sheaths; knee conspicuous, armed as the rest of the sheath; ocrea ill-defined; flagellum absent; petiole to 12 by 5 cm, much longer in juveniles, armed as the rachis with short triangular grapnel spines and with scattered indumentum; rachis to 5 m long; cirrus to 3 m long; leaflets pale greyish-green, 45–60 on each side of the rachis, ± regularly arranged, limply pendulous and versatile in adult leaves, somewhat irregular and grouped, not obviously pendulous in juvenile leaves, margins with conspicuous black bristles. Inflorescences very robust, to c. 2.5 m long with numerous (up to 18) rather close partial inflorescences to 70 cm long, subtending bracts densely armed with spines to 0.3 cm long, the male inflorescence branched to 3 orders, the female to 2 orders; male rachillae to 3 by 0.3 cm, the female to 15 by 0.5 cm. Mature fruit ovoid, to 2.8 by 2 cm, with a wide short beak to 0.3 by 0.3 cm, and covered with 15 vertical rows of yellowish scales with blackish-brown margins. Seed ovoid, to 1.8 by 1.2 cm, with finely pitted surface; endosperm densely and deeply ruminate. Seedling leaf with 2 divergent cucullate leaflets with a grey-blue bloom on a dull green surface.

description: Robust clustering rattan. Stem climbing to great heights, to 50 m or more long, without sheaths to 4 cm diam., with rather prominent nodes and frequently slightly angular in cross section, with sheaths to 7 cm diam., internodes to 30 cm long. Leaves subcirrate; sheaths dark green, armed with large triangular, flattened, yellowish-based black spines to 4 by 1 cm, and scattered dull brown scales; knee conspicuous; ocrea short, quickly tattering; flagellum massive, to 10 m or more long, dark green, armed with short black, yellowish-based spines; petiole to 1 m (usually less); rachis to 3 m long; leaflets 20–30 on each side of the rachis, usually pale green, regularly arranged, the proximal to 50 by 5 cm increasing to 80 by 8 cm in the middle, decreasing to minute at the tip, c. 4 by 0.5 cm, the rachis tip forming a subcirrus, the leaflets drying pale green, not blackish, prickly on the upper surface of the veins near the tip and along the margins. Inflorescences to 8 m long including the long terminal flagellum, male and female superficially similar, the male branched to 3 orders, the female to 2 orders, bearing 4–6 partial inflorescences to 80 cm long; male rachillae slender 5–8 by 3 cm, female rachillae robust, reflexed, 10–18 by 0.4 cm. Male flower with 12 stamens. Ripe fruit ellipsoid, to 3 by 2 cm, tipped with a short beak and covered in 15 vertical rows of matt brown to black scales with paler bases. Seed to 2 by 0.8 cm, rather angular and grooved with one flattened lateral face; sarcotesta sour; endosperm homogeneous. Seedling leaf bifid, shiny green.

description: Moderate to robust clustering rattan. Stems climbing to 30 m long, without sheaths 0.3–3 cm diam., with sheaths 0.7–5 cm diam., internodes 15–30 cm long. Leaf cirrate; sheaths bright green, variably armed sparsely to densely with scattered, patent or slightly reflexed red-brown, yellow-based spines to 3 cm long, sometimes interspersed with much smaller broad-triangular dark spines, pale to reddish-brown caducous indumentum usually abundant on newly emerged sheaths, sometimes distinctly striped; knee conspicuous, usually more sparsely armed than the rest of the sheath; ocrea very inconspicuous, unarmed, soon disintegrating; flagellum absent; petiole 5–30 cm long, semi-circular in cross section, the adaxial surface often armed with short erect spines; rachis to 2.5 m or more; cirrus 0.4–1 m; leaflets 10–25 on each side of the rachis arranged in evenly spaced divergent pairs, a few leaflets near the base and the cirrus borne singly, the largest leaflets to 35 by 5.5 cm, rarely larger, tips somewhat cucullate, margins bristly, veins both adaxially and abaxially unarmed. Inflorescences male to 1.4 m long, the female usually much shorter, to 50 cm long, lacking a terminal flagellum, the male branched to 3 orders, the female to 2 orders, partial inflorescences 8–12, close and not very well differentiated; male rachillae 2.5–5 by 0.3 cm long, female rachillae to 10 by 0.4 cm. Fruit rounded, the calyx explanate at fruit maturity so fruit appearing sessile, 0.7–1.2 by 0.7–1 cm, with a short rather triangular reddish beak to 0.15 by 0.15 cm, and covered in 17 vertical rows of white unchannelled scales. Seed c. 0.5–0.9 by 0.5–0.7 cm, ± rounded; endosperm homogeneous.

description: Solitary moderate to robust rattan. Stem climbing to 20 m tall or more, without sheaths c. 2 cm diam., with sheaths 3.5–7 cm diam., internodes 6–20 cm long. Leaf ecirrate; sheaths mid green with broad yellow streaks when fresh, pale brown when dry, armed with scattered large pale yellow green black-tipped flattened spines with conspicuous swollen yellowish bases and black hairy margins, the largest spines to 4 by 0.8 cm, much smaller spines often present between the large ones, sparse caducous brown indumentum present between spines; knee well developed, armed as the sheath, or sometimes unarmed; ocrea poorly developed; flagellum to 3.5 m long; all cut surfaces oozing yellow creamy gum; petiole 0.6–1.75 m long, armed with pale yellowish-green spines with black tips similar to those on sheath; rachis conspicuously arcuate, to 3.5 m long, armed with reflexed grapnel spines to 0.5 cm long; leaflets 30–50 on each side of the rachis, regularly arranged, rather stiff, the longest to 50 by 2–4 cm, main veins bristly on both surfaces, margins bristly near the leaflet tip. Inflorescences 3–6 m long, male and female superficially similar, the male branched to 3 orders, the female to 2 orders with 2–3 partial inflorescences only, to 25 cm long, borne near the inflorescence base, and a long terminal flagellum; primary bracts conspicuous, splitting along part of their length and becoming flattened, tattering near their tips, armed with short triangular spines; male rachillae c. 3 by 0.2 cm, the female to 5 by 0.2 cm, flowers relatively large (to 0.75 cm long). Mature fruit globose to very slightly obovoid, borne on a stalked disc, to 2 by 1.6 cm, with a short beak to 0.2 by 0.1 cm, and covered in 15–16 vertical rows of bright reddish-brown, unchannelled scales. Seed globose, c. 1.5 cm diam., pitted; endosperm deeply ruminate. Seedling leaf with 4–6 very slender leaflets.

description: Short acaulescent or erect solitary non-climbing palm. Stems rarely exceeding 2 m long, without sheaths c. 4.5 cm diam., with sheaths to 6 cm diam., internodes 2–3 cm long. Leaf ecirrate; sheaths dull green, densely covered in paler green spines of varying length, to 4 cm long, but to 20 cm long and upward pointing around the leaf sheath mouth, dense brownish indumentum abundant between the spines, spines generally very sparse or absent below the petiole; knee absent; ocrea poorly defined; flagellum absent; petiole 0.6–1 m long, armed along the margins with robust lateral spines to 4 cm long and scattered smaller spines on adaxial and abaxial surfaces; rachis to 2 m long; leaflets 20–30 on each side of the rachis, rather distant, broad and conspicuously plicate, the longest to 50 by 5 cm, the distalmost pair c. 15 by 2 cm and markedly divergent. Inflorescence lacking a flagellum, confusingly variable but the male and female nevertheless superficially similar, the male branched to 3 orders, the female to 2 orders; peduncle often to 60 cm long; primary bracts very conspicuous, longitudinally splitting, but remaining tubular near the base, enclosing the whole inflorescence or partial inflorescence, the bracts bright mid-brown, armed with short spines near the base only and densely covered in bright brown indumentum, adaxially shining brown; inflorescences occasionally very short, not exceeding 20 cm including the peduncle; male rachillae very congested, c. 0.6 by 0.1 cm, female rachillae usually less crowded, to 4 by 0.4 cm. Mature fruit rounded, c. 0.8–1 cm diam., with a prominent beak to 0.15 by 0.15 cm, and covered in 15–18 vertical rows of bright red-brown scales. Seed rounded, c. 0.8 cm diam., flattened on one side, with a hollow next to the attachment; endosperm homogeneous. Seedling leaf bifid with strongly divergent leaflets.

description: Moderately robust erect rattan to 5 m tall. Stem dimensions not known but probably at least 5 cm diam. Leaves ecirrate; sheath ± open, armed with partial whorls of flattened black spines to 3 cm long, with pale bases thickened and coalescing laterally to form low ridges, abundant groups of much smaller black spines interspersed with large spines; flagellum apparently lacking; petiole probably exceeding 50 cm long, c. 1–1.2 cm diam., rounded abaxially, deeply channelled adaxially, armed on both surfaces with whorls of large and small spines as the body of the sheath; rachis to 1.5 m long, armed as the petiole; leaflets numerous, arranged irregularly in groups of 2–6 held in the same plane, terminal leaflets not joined, the longest leaflets in the middle, to 40 by 2 cm, dark green adaxially with 3 bristly prominent veins, paler abaxially but lacking indumentum and bristles. Inflorescence male unknown; female inflorescences ± erect, at least 80 cm long, branched to 2 orders, partial inflorescences to 40 cm long; bracts on main axis and first order branches tattering to the base; rachillae 1–23 cm long, densely covered with crowded flower groups. description: Terrestrial, lithophytic or rarely epiphytic herbs with pseudobulbous stems, deciduous or evergreen. Flowering shoots 12‒80(‒150) cm tall. Pseudobulbs ovoid, conical or cylindric, either insignificant and hidden by the bases of the foliage leaves or large and swollen, close together or rarely spaced on a creeping rhizome. Foliage leaves few, plicate, present or rarely absent during flowering, almost always uniformly green, petiolate, glabrous or hairy; lamina lanceolate, cuneate at base. Inflorescences unbranched, arising from a basal leaf axil, glabrous or pubescent, few- to many-flowered; floral bracts glabrous or hairy, persistent or caducous. Flowers medium-sized or large, resupinate; mostly with white, pink and yellow colours, often turning dark blue through damage or with age. Sepals free, often hairy (particularly on the outside). Petals similar but almost always glabrous. Labellum entire, 2- or 3-lobed, mid-lobe often bilobulate, labellum base most commonly extensively fused with the sides of the column, disk variously ornamented, sometimes clawed, almost always with saccate or elongate, glabrous or pubescent spur. Column glabrous or rarely hairy; anther versatile and incumbent, with 8 waxy clavate pollinia; rostellum beaked or bifid, with one viscidium; stigma in a cavity below the rostellum. Ovary often hairy, mostly indistinguishable from the pedicel.</br></br>Calanthe is a large genus of 207 species which are mainly found in Asia, northern  Australia and the Pacific Ocean Islands, with several occurring in Africa and Madagascar and  one in central America; 23 species in Thailand.

description: Flowering shoots glabrous, to 75 cm tall. Pseudobulbs insignificant, hidden by the bases of the foliage leaves. Foliage leaves 3‒4, lanceolate, acute, perennial, to 90 by 4‒9 cm; petioles to 18 cm long. Inflorescences semi-dense or lax; peduncles to 20 cm long; sterile bracts few, lanceolate-oblong, acute; rachis 13‒20 cm long, several- to many-flowered; floral bracts caducous, not seen. Flowers white or creamy white, labellum partly yellow. Sepals ovate-elliptic, shortly aristate-acuminate, 5-veined, to 15 by 4‒5 mm. Petals elliptic-ovate, acute, to 12 by 4‒5.5 mm. Labellum 3-lobed, spurred, free portion to 11 mm long, base extensively fused with the sides of the column; mid-lobe elliptic-reniform, apically retuse or slightly cleft, 5–7 mm wide; side lobes oval or rounded-square, to 2 by 3 mm; ornaments of broadly laminate semi-ovate ridges; spur clavate, straight or slightly curved, shorter than the pedicel plus the ovary, 9–10 mm long. Column 4–5 mm long; rostellum with a slender beak. Ovary 4‒7 mm long, weakly differentiated from the 7–11 mm long pedicel. Capsule not seen. description: Flowering shoots 40–70 cm tall. Pseudobulbs insignificant, hidden by the bases of the foliage leaves, cylindric, 4–12 cm long. Inflorescences lax, shortly pubescent; peduncle 20–35(–48) cm long; sterile bracts 3–4, lanceolate, acuminate, to 3.5 cm long; rachis 11–22 cm long, few- to many-flowered; floral bracts lanceolate, acuminate, persistent, to 20 by 1–3 mm. Flowers 20–35 mm in diameter; red to brown with yellow or violet spots, labellum pale violet, spur pink. Sepals oblong-elliptic, acuminate, pubescent on the outside, glabrous or sometimes puberulous on the inside, 15–18 by 5–9 mm. Petals oblong-lanceolate, clawed, acuminate, 15–16 by 3–6 mm. Labellum ovate to reniform, apically emarginate and therefore somewhat bilobed, base fused with the column foot, clawed, 19–25 by 20–26 mm; ornaments of 2 prominent or obscure keels in the centre of the labellum blade; spur conical, 2–4 mm long. Column 5–7 mm long, glabrous, with a prominent foot. Ovary (including pedicel) pubescent, 20–25 mm long. Capsule ellipsoid, c. 30 by 15 mm.

description: Flowering shoots (19–)30–68 cm tall. Pseudobulbs prominent, ovoid, 2.5–8.5 by 1.5–3 cm. description: Flowering shoots glabrous, 28–80 cm tall. Pseudobulbs insignificant, hidden by the bases of the foliage leaves, spaced on an elongate rhizome. Foliage leaves 2–3, lanceolate-oblong, acute, perennial, 23–90 by 3.4–9.5 cm; petioles 13–20 cm long. Inflorescences arising directly from the rhizome next to the leafy shoot, raceme dense or semi-dense, cylindric; peduncles 21–30 cm long; sterile bracts 4–8, lanceolate-oblong, acute, tubular and inflated, 2.8–6 cm long; rachis 10.5–14 cm long, many-flowered; floral bracts lanceolate, acuminate, caducous, 30–50 by 3–8 mm. Flowers to 20 mm in diameter; yellow. Sepals ovate-elliptic, acuminate; dorsal sepal 9–14 by 4–6.7 mm; lateral sepals 10–15 by 4–6 mm. Petals obovate-elliptic, slightly spathulate, acute, 9–14 by 4–6.5 mm. Labellum 3-lobed, base fused with lower half or two thirds of the column, 8–13.5 mm long; mid-lobe rectangular, emarginate, 3–5 by 3.5–5 mm; side lobes semi circular, 2–3 by 2–3 mm; ornaments of 2 short lamellate keels between the side lobes; spur clavate, apically slightly bifid or entire, 8–10 mm long. Column 6–7 mm long, with a short rostellum beak which hardly or not at all projects. Ovary 7–9 mm long, distinct from the 8–12 mm long pedicel. Capsule ellipsoid, 10–13 by 5–6 mm.

description: Flowering shoots to 100 cm tall. Pseudobulbs insignificant, hidden by the bases of the foliage leaves. Sepals elliptic-lanceolate, acute, pubescent on the outside; dorsal sepal 16–18 by 6–8.2 mm; lateral sepals 17–17.5 by 6.4–8.6 mm. description: Flowering shoots 25–60 cm tall. Pseudobulbs insignificant, hidden by the bases of the foliage leaves, ovoid, 2–4 by c. 2 cm. Foliage leaves 5–7, elliptic-oblong, acuminate, perennial, 6–25 by 3–7 cm; petioles 7–10 cm long. Inflorescences lax, puberulous, greenish-purple; peduncles 19–48 cm long; sterile bracts lanceolate, acuminate, glabrous, 1.8–3.2 cm long; rachis 6–12 cm long, few- to many-flowered; floral bracts lanceolate, acuminate, persistent, 15–25 by 3–5 mm. description: Perennial (or annual, not in Thailand) herbs, with woody rootstock. Leaves alternate. description: Moderate-sized to robust tree palms, solitary or clustered, monoecious with bisexual inflorescences, male and female flowering separated in time, hapaxanthic. Leaves bipinnately divided, induplicate; sheath closed at first, later disintegrating into a fibrous network opposite the petiole, often densely covered by rusty scaly hairs; pinnae regularly arranged, straight and more less orientated in one plane, each divided into a number of pinnules (second order pinnae), these evenly distributed in one plane to drooping and untidy looking, triangular in outline with two straight sides and one irregularly lobed, praemorse side. Female flowers with ± three-angled ovary, sessile stigmas and 3 locules. Fruit globose, 1–2 seeded; epicarp smooth, brightly coloured to dark at maturity, mesocarp fleshy, with high density of raphide containing ideoblasts causing skin irritation, endocarp not differentiated. Seed with homogeneous or ruminate endosperm. </br></br>Thirteen species in India, throughout SE Asia, N Australia and W Pacifi c to Vanuatu. Four species in Thailand.

description: Terrestrial herbs with condensed underground rhizomes and fibrous roots; sometimes mycoheterotrophic (including all species found in tropical Asia south and south-east of the Himalayas and Himalayan foothills). Foliage leaves alternate, well-developed to vestigial. Inflorescence racemose, 1- to many-flowered. Flowers erect to spreading, resupinate, not always opening fully. Sepals and petals free. Labellum firmly attached, differentiated into hypochile and epichile, both usually ornamented by longitudinal ridges or keels; hypochile more or less  saccate; epichile more or less recurved. Column elongate, glabrous, without a column foot; anther dorsal, elongated, versatile; pollinia 2, soft and mealy, partly cleft, devoid of caudicles; rostellum well-developed to strongly reduced, neither producing stipe nor viscidia; receptive part of stigma concave with protruding margins. Ovary sessile, twisted through 180°. Fruit an erect capsule, dehiscing by 6 longitudinal slits.</br></br>A genus of c. 15 species distributed from Europe and Mediterranean North Africa to southern and eastern Asia, with a single species in western North America; 1 species in Thailand.

description:
Terrestrial or lithophytic herbs with several-noded cane-like stems, subglabrous or hirsute. Foliage leaves in the upper stem part, few, perennial, plicate, elliptic-lanceolate, acuminate, their petioles forming a pseudostem. Inflorescences lax, racemose, few- to many-flowered, arising laterally on the cane-like stem, hairy; peduncles with a few tubular sterile bracts; floral bracts caducous. Flowers medium-sized, resupinate, in Thai species usually yellow or orange-yellow, often turning dark blue when old or through damage. Sepals and petals similar, spreading, free, pubescent or not. Labellum 3-lobed, almost entirely free from the column and only fused with it at the very base, spurless, with erect side lobes that are partly wrapped around the column, ornaments (if present) as two basal ridges. Column more or less hairy, anther incumbent and versatile, pollinia 8, waxy, clavate. Ovary distinct from the pedicel or not.

Five species from NE India to Maluku and northwards as far as China, Taiwan, the Philippines and S Japan; 2 species in Thailand.

description: Terrestrial or lithophytic, rhizomatous herbs; the creeping, clearly segmented rhizome with internodal rhizoids (roots absent or hair-like). Flowering shoots terminal, erect from a decumbent base, 2.5–30(–37) cm tall. Foliage leaves 3–10, scattered along the stem or placed in a basal rosette, petiolate, sheathing at base. Inflorescence racemose to spicate; bracts glabrous or (glandular-)pubescent on the dorsal side. Flowers 1–10(–15), resupinate. Sepals connate to form a 3.5–19 mm long tubular synsepal. Labellum adnate to the lower half of the column, straight (i.e., not twisted), 3.5–18.5 mm long along the mid-line, differentiated into hypochile, mesochile (sometimes obscure), and epichile; hypochile concave to slightly saccate (sac hidden by the synsepal), inside with 1 to many, sometimes branched appendages on either side; mesochile (if recognizable) devoid of lateral flanges; epichile simple and entire to deeply bilobed, or coarsely dentate (rarely vestigial). Column straight (i.e., not twisted); stigma bipartite, flat (fertile parts) but extended in 2 sterile stylids parallel to the rostellum; rostellum triangular, bifid; viscidium 1, naked; anther versatile; pollinia 2, basitonous. Ovary glabrous or glandular-pubescent. description: Terrestrial, rarely epiphytic herbs with a creeping rhizome; vegetative parts (except floral bracts) consistently glabrous. Pseudobulbs ascending, each bearing either a single leaf or an inflorescence. Foliage leaves convolute, plicate, petiolate, long-lived; petiole channelled. Inflorescence erect, racemose, (fairly) lax, both peduncle and rachis elongating during flowering; floral bracts persistent, entire. Flowers resupinate, bilaterally symmetrical, wide-open or nearly so. Sepals and petals free, subsimilar, obtuse to acute, entire, glabrous. Labellum elastically attached, clawed, 3-lobed, spurless; claw with distinctly undulate margins; side lobes and mid-lobe entire, obtuse to retuse. Column stout to fairly slender, strongly incurved to nearly straight, the ventral side basally ornamented by 2 fleshy keels that are extended onto a spurred column foot (spur with a narrow entrance); anther subterminal, incumbent, versatile; pollinia 2, solid, devoid of caudicles; rostellum slightly protruding, neither producing stipe nor viscidia; receptive part of stigma concave. Ovary (including pedicel) fusiform-terete, curved, twisted, glabrous. Fruit a distinctly pedicelled capsule dehiscing by longitudinal slits.</br></br>A genus of 4 species distributed in most of Indo-Malesia and the south-western Pacific islands (to Fiji); 1 species in Thailand.

description: Pseudobulbs 4.8–5.8 cm long, 0.6–0.9 cm in diameter. Leaves: petiole 7–12.4 cm long; lamina (elliptic-)lanceolate, acuminate, 12.8–29.6 by 4.4–8.8 cm. Sepals: dorsal sepal linear-lanceolate, 10.9–17.6 by 3.3–4.8 mm; lateral sepals falcately (linear-)lanceolate, 9.3–15.2 by 3–5 mm. Petals falcately (ovate-)lanceolate, 9.7–15.4 by 4.8–6 mm. Column 6–6.7 mm long, with the front margins forming lateral wings, each of which has an obliquely triangular to oblong or hook-like process; column foot 1.5–2.3 mm long, with a broadly conical, rounded, 0.5–1.6 mm long spur; anther ovate in upper view, acuminate in front; stigma with entire margins. Ovary (including pedicel) 6.5–12 mm long. Capsule pendent, fusiform-terete, furrowed, 21–26 mm long, 4–6 mm in diameter.

description: Herbs, perennial, rhizomatous, often forming large colonies. Leaves petiolate, opposite, becoming alternate and bract-like in inflorescence. Inflorescences racemes, sometimes branched at base, terminal on main stem and at apex of short axillary branches. Flowers 2-merous, with a floral tube; sepals and petals alternate; petals obcordate or obtrullate, apex notched, white or pink; stamens opposite sepals, anthers white or pink, pollen in monads, white; nectary wholly within floral tube or elongated and projecting above opening of floral tube as a fleshy cylindrical or ring-like disk; ovary locules 1 or 2, ovules 1 per locule, style equalling or longer than stamens, stigma 2-lobed. Fruit an indehiscent capsule, with stiff uncinate hairs, with or without conspicuous rows of corky tissue. Seeds fusiform or broadly clavoid to narrowly ovoid, smooth, adhering ± firmly to inner ovary. 2n = 22.</br></br>Eight species: temperate and boreal forests of the N hemisphere, from near sea level to 5000 m altitude and from 10°–70° N; one species in Thailand.

description: Sympodial herbs, initially terrestrial, but becoming scandent or epiphytic. Rhizome up to several m long, sturdy, covered with pale brown papery sheaths, rooting from the nodes, producing leafy shoots at intervals. Foliage leaves long-lived, distichous, plicate, many-veined, proximally tapering into a petiole-like sheathing base. Inflorescence terminal on a leafy shoot, racemose or paniculate with few branches, pubescent; floral bracts stiff, persistent. Flowers opening 1 or 2 in succession, fleshy, pale green and whitish, often with more or less conspicuous dark green veins in all perianth parts. Sepals free, pubescent on the dorsal side. Petals free, narrower than sepals. Labellum firmly attached, 3-lobed (to subentire). description: Epiphytes or sometimes lithophytes or terrestrials. Pseudobulbs consisting of 1 internode, close together to wide apart on a creeping rhizome, much shorter than the leaves, 1- to 2-leaved, when young covered by scale leaves. Leaves 1 or 2, convolute, plicate or duplicate; petiole channelled; nerves 3–15, prominent below. Inflorescence a raceme, erect to pendulous; usually glabrous, in sect. Verrucosae with scattered minute scale-like hairs, in sect. Tomentosae subglabrous to densely tomentose; peduncle in some sections with persistent imbricate scale leaves at the base; rachis straight or zig-zag, in some sections with persistent imbricate scale leaves at its base and sometimes also at its top; floral bracts caducous or persistent. Flowers resupinate, (1–)3 to many, 0.6–13 cm across, open simultaneously or in succession. Sepals more or less concave, ovate-oblong to ovate-lanceolate, the lateral ones oblique. Petals linear to ovate lanceolate. Labellum 3-lobed; side lobes erect, usually projecting in front; epichile (mid-lobe) usually shorter than the hypochile; ornaments of longitudinal keels, median on the labellum, incised and/or undulate, broken up, papillous, warty or provided with hair-like structures; mid lobe often with additional keels. Column somewhat curved, often as long as the hypochile, footless, winged (but without stelids); wing widest in upper half. Anther subterminal, incumbent; pollinia 4, solid, each provided with a caudicle, median with a depression; rostellum prominent, not producing a stipe.</br></br>A genus of c. 200 species, distributed throughout SE Asia, Malesia and the western Pacific islands to Samoa; 35 species in Thailand.

description: Terrestrial, rarely epiphytic herbs; rhizome creeping. Pseudobulbs alternating, 1–6 with a leaf and 1 with an inflorescence, articulate at junction with petiole or peduncle, scales 1 per pseudobulb, tubular, early caducous. Foliage leaves 1 per pseudobulb, convolute, plicate, petiolate. Inflorescence racemose, erect, unbranched, both peduncle and rachis elongating during anthesis; floral bracts persistent during anthesis. Flowers few to many, more or less resupinate, turned to all sides, yellow, green, white, pink, or purple, widely opening, often somewhat asymmetrical. Lateral sepals inserted on column foot. Petals free. Labellum not movable, narrowly attached to column foot, entire or 3-lobed; hypochile basal portion claw-like with straight parallel margins, front part with lateral lobes, ornamented by 2 lateral keels, from the base elevating into an entire lobe or into an oblique structure hollow in front, from there continuing to the front, median keel absent or present; epichile recurved. Column semiterete; with a seam in front laterally on either side; column foot with a spur; anther subterminal, incumbent, 2-locular; pollinia 2, hard, waxy, obliquely conical with an obtuse top and a hollow base. Ovary longitudinally grooved, glabrous. Fruit a capsule, fusiform.</br></br>A genus of c. 14 species distributed from NE India, S China, northern Indo-China, Taiwan, Japan and the Malesian region to the SW Pacific; 2 species in Thailand.

description: Small, medium-sized or gigantic, evergreen or seasonally dormant herbs with somewhat milky latex. Stem either a hypogeal, subglobose or subcylindrical tuber, or an epigeal and slender to massive aerial, later decumbent, stem; most species stolon-producing although extent of stolon spread very variable between species. Leaves several, loosely rosulate in acaulescent plants, forming a terminal crown in arborescent species; petiole stout to very slender; petiolar sheath rather long, persistent; leaf blade peltate, ovate-cordate to sagittato– or oblong-cordate, posterior lobes rounded, shortly to almost entirely connate; basal ribs well developed; primary lateral veins pinnate, forming submarginal collective vein, 1–2 marginal veins also present, secondary and tertiary laterals arising from the primaries at a wide angle, arching strongly towards leaf margin and forming varyingly conspicuous interprimary collective veins (‘colocasioid venation’); higher order venation reticulate. Inflorescences 1–many in each floral sympodium; peduncle much shorter than to sub-equalling petiole, erect at first, declinate during fruiting in some species; spathe constricted between lower part and spathe limb, sometimes with a second constriction above staminate zone of spadix; lower part with convolute margins, usually much shorter than limb, ovoid or oblong, persistent, enlarging in fruit and then splitting open irregularly; spathe limb oblong and boat-shaped to narrowly lanceolate, erect to reflexing at anthesis, later caducous, greenish, white or deep yellow or dirty pale brown; spadix sessile to briefly stipitate, shorter than spathe; flowers unisexual, perigone absent; pistillate flower zone short, separated from staminate by narrower zone of sterile staminate flowers; sterile interstice with synandrodes, these depressed-obpyramidal, truncate, laterally compressed; interpistillar staminodes clavate; pistillate flowers an ovary ovoid or oblong, 1-locular, ovules many, hemiorthotropous, funicles relatively long, placentae 2–5, parietal, stylar region short, narrowed or not, sometimes ± absent; stigma discoid-capitate or weakly lobed; staminate flower zone cylindrical to fusiform; staminate flowers 3–6-androus, stamens connate into ± truncate synandrium overtopped by a conspicuous synconnective, thecae lateral, oblong-linear, dehiscing by apical pore; appendix erect, ± smooth, elongate-conoid to fusiform or subulate, sometimes reduced to small, mucronate stub, rarely absent. Fruitsa greenish, whitish or yellowish brown berry, obconoid or oblong, stigma remnants persistent, many-seeded, fruity-smelling at maturity. Seed ovoid to ellipsoid, testa thickish, costate, embryo axile, cylindrical, endosperm copious.</br></br>About 15 species distributed from the subtropical eastern Himalayas throughout subtropical and tropical Asia into the tropical western pacific and eastern Australia.</br></br>Four species in Thailand, none endemic. Colocasia affinis and C. fontanesii have been included in the key below (italic, non bold) since both are widespread and abundant from Assam and Bangladesh to SW China, Myanmar, and N Laos and are to be expected in N Thailand.

description: Medium to large, occasionally very large, moderate to robust, solitary to colony-forming, evergreen herb to 1 m. Inflorescences 1–3 together; peduncle 16–26 cm; spathe 13–24 cm long, constricted between the lower part and the limb; lower part ellipsoid, 3.5–5 by 1.2–1.5 cm, green; spathe limb lanceolate or lanceolate-elliptic, 10–19 by 2–5 cm, acuminate, opening slightly at the base, the rest remaining furled during anthesis, cream to golden yellow; spadix shorter than the spathe; pistillate flower zone conical 3–3.5 by 1.2 cm; ovaries globose, ca 1–3 mm diam., green; stigma subsessile, narrower than apex of ovary, barely lobed; interpistillar staminodes clavate, white, mostly exceeding the ovaries; sterile interstice slender cylindrical, 3–3.3 cm; staminate flower zone cylindrical, 4–6.5 cm by 7 mm; synandria 2–3-merous, ca 0.8 mm diam., mid-yellow; appendix narrow conical, 1.5–4.5 cm, ca ⅕–⅛ entire spadix length. description: Plant terrestrial, often producing several reed-like stems from the same short rhizome. Roots fasciculate and wiry. Leaves several per stem, more or less distichous, (sub)sessile, plicate, sheathing at base, fairly tough, more or less furfuraceous. Inflorescences 1–4 per flowering shoot, lateral, paniculate, much shorter than the leaves; floral bracts boat-shaped, ovate to (triangular-)lanceolate, veins often prominent on the dorsal side. Flowers distichous on each panicle branch (but pedicels twisted to make the flowers appear secundly arranged). Sepals and and petals of subequal length; dorsal sepal very shortly adnate to petals and column; petals usually broader than sepals. Labellum spathulate; claw embracing the column. Column at least 3 times as long as anther, slender and straight, slightly shorter than the labellum, with a pair of subterminal auricles; anther dorsal, versatile, elongated; pollinia 2, sectile, slender; rostellum erect, bifid, producing a long, more or less semiterete hamule and an elliptic-oblong to ovate viscidium; stigma transverse, with 2 recurved triangular lobules in front. description: Solitary, hermaphrodite, hapaxanthic tree palms. Leaves induplicate, costapalmate; leaf sheath splitting to the base, shallowly disintegrating into fibres along the margins, later with conspicuous /\-shaped cleft below the petiole; petiole massive, deeply channelled above, margins with distinct teeth; adaxial hastula well developed, abaxial hastula somewhat irregular, blade regularly divided to half its radius into single fold segments, these further indented along the abaxial folds, adaxial folds of young leaves often terminated by filaments, transverse veinlets conspicuous. Inflorescences each subtended by bract-like leaves, gathered in a massive, terminal, composite flowering structure, individual inflorescences branched to the third order, prophyll bicarinate, rachis bracts tubular, rachillae with spirally arranged cincinni of up to 10 flowers. Flowers on short pseudopedicels formed by a fusion of the base of the calyx and the receptacle, stamens 6, the antesepalous ones free, the antepetalous ones shortly adnate to the petals, gynoecium 3-loculate, distinctly 3-grooved, with elongate style and inconspicuous stigmatic branches. Fruit globose, single-seeded, epicarp smooth, mesocarp fleshy, endocarp poorly differentiated, usually partly attached to seed coat. Seed with homogeneous endosperm.</br></br>Five species in tropical Asia to Australia. Two species are indigenous in Thailand. A third species, C. umbraculifera L., which is native to Sri Lanka and South India has been introduced and is often seen associated with temple compounds and as a grand street tree. It can be distinguished from C. lecomtei by the absence of black bands on the petioles, and from C. utan by the absence of indumentum on the petioles and the presence of ear-like auricles at the base of the petiole.</br></br>Species of Corypha remain very poorly understood.

description: Solitary tree palm, leaf-bearing part of stem usually more than 15 m long at flowering. Stem usually naked in adult trees, 0.8–1 m diam., slightly ventricose, the leaf scars usually describing distinct spirals on the trunk. Leaves 20–30 in crown; petiole 2.5–4 m long, green, armed with regularly arranged, up to 2 cm long black spines; blade c. 2.4–3 m across, slightly wider than long, undulate, costa curved, greyish-green on both sides, divided into 80–100 segments, all rather stiff. Composite flowering structure overall 2.5–5 m tall, rounded to elliptic in outline, individual inflorescences 20–25, the middle ones largest, up to 2.5 m long, rachis straight to slightly curved upwards. Fruit 2–3 cm diam., yellowish-brown at maturity, rounded to slightly elliptic.

description: Terrestrial herbs with corms connected by a rhizome. Foliage leaves 1–2 per corm (leaves absent in one mycoheterotrophic species endemic to Japan), convolute, plicate, petiolate, deciduous, present at the time of flowering; lamina lanceolate to elliptic. Inflorescence arising laterally from the corm, racemose. Flowers nodding to pendent, resupinate, slenderly campanulate (i.e. with sepals, petals and labellum elongate, subequal in length and only slightly spreading). Sepals and petals free. Labellum firmly attached, spathulate with 3-lobed distal part, spurless (but concave to saccate at base). Column straight, elongate, nearly as long as labellum, without column foot; anther subterminal, incumbent, versatile; pollinia 4, closely appressed in 2 pairs, solid, without distinct caudicles; rostellum producing a hamule and a viscidium; receptive part of stigma concave. Fruit not seen.</br></br>A genus of c. 5 species distributed from the southern Himalayas to Sakhalin and the Kuril Islands; 1 species in Thailand.
