description: Corms clustered, ovoid to terete, 1.5–3.7 cm long, 1–2.3 cm in diameter, producing fibrous roots. Leaves 1(–2) per corm, long-petiolate; petiole(s) covered by 2 cataphylls to form a pseudostem; lamina lanceolate, acute to acuminate, 11.7–15 by 2.5–5.4 cm, with 3–5 distinct (and many indistinct) veins. Inflorescence 26–42 cm tall, lax, 15- to 20-flowered; peduncle bearing 2–3 sheathing, scale-like leaves; rachis 11–18 cm long; floral bracts suberect, linear-triangular to lanceolate, acuminate, 6–11 by 1–2 mm. Flowers fragrant, pale purple to orange brown. Sepals glabrous; dorsal sepal linear-oblanceolate, obtuse to acuminate, 28–34 by 3–5 mm; lateral sepals obliquely linear-oblanceolate, acuminate, 25–33 by 2.5–4 mm. Petals obliquely linear-oblanceolate, (sub)acuminate, 27–33 by 2.5–3.5 mm, glabrous. Labellum deeply 3-lobed  at apex, 24–31 mm long, 3–7 mm wide across side lobes when flattened, glabrous; side lobes porrect, obliquely linear to linear-triangular, acute to acuminate, 3–4 mm long; mid-lobe porrect, lanceolate to elliptic, subacute, 5–10 mm long, ornamented by a small, oblongoid, smooth callus at base. Column 22–27 mm long, semiterete with the front margins extended to form 2 narrow subdistal wings on the ventral side; anther cordate in upper view, c. 1.5 mm long; rostellum producing a broadly ovate hamule and a sagittate viscidium; receptive part of stigma broadly elliptic. Ovary (including pedicel) slenderly terete, flaccid, 8–12 mm long, glabrous.

description:
Small to medium, evergreen or less often seasonally dormant herbs with procumbent to erect rhizomes and short to long stolons; plants that grow slowly have short, rugged rhizomes, while quick-growing plants have more slender rhizomes with 0.5–1(–2) cm long internodes. Cataphylls often present in flowering plants, in some species also in non-flowering plants, sub-2-keeled; petiole elongate, basally sheathing; leaf blade elliptic-ovate to strap-shaped, vernationconvolute, base attenuate-truncate to cordate. Inflorescence usually shortly pedunculate; spathe with a basal tube, (the kettle), with united margins, an upper tube (sometimes twisted) with fused margins, and a terminal limb which opens into a flat, ovate surface, or may be more or less spirally coiled; a distinctive “collar” or “collar zone” is often found at the transition between the upper tube and the spathe limb; the inside kettle wall sometimes with depressions (alveoli), in the upper part; spadix small, included in the kettle with a basal pistillate part, a part with olfactory bodies, a thin, naked interstice, a staminate part, and a small naked appendix that at the first day of anthesis is adnate to the base of the flap at the top of the kettle; pistillate flowers 4–8, naked, upright, in a single connate whorl; styles outwards-curved; stigma ovate-elliptic to emarginate, occasionally trilobed; ovules 3–20 per pistil, erect, on the adaxial wall; staminate flowers 25–80(–130); thecae 2 per stamen, with a small horn, through which pollen is extruded. Infructescence a sub-ovoid to globular syncarp-like, multiple fruit, each part ultimately splitting at the adaxial side and becoming star-shaped, follicle-like, a few species splitting in a septicidal/septifragal-ceratium manner. Infructescence at maturity raised above the ground by a quickly-extending peduncle. Seeds ellipsoid, rough, mostly with endosperm (but see C. ciliata).</br></br>About 60 aquatic to amphibious species in Asia from India to New Guinea. Eight species have been included for Thailand. None endemic.</br></br>E c o l o g y.— In and along streams and rivers, in fresh and brackish tidal zones, sometimes also in forest pools, in lowland rainforests, often forming large submerged or emergent stands. The rhizomes and stolons are usually deeply buried, sometimes only with the spathe limb and the upper part of the spathe protruding above the ground. In more quickly running water the plants are mostly rooted in sand or between stones and rocks while, in more slowly running water, they are found deep in mud.</br></br>Species of Cryptocoryne fall into a number of natural groups, correlated with morphology, distribution and chromosome numbers (e.g., Arends et al. op.cit.). The chromosome numbers form dysploid (“aneuploid”) as well as euploid series, where the different numbers are characteristic of the species/groups in question (see under each species). A number of tri-, penta- and hexaploids are known, of which most reproduce only vegetatively.</br></br>In some species, plants growing in deeper water tend to have larger leaves, a longer spathe tube and a longer peduncle than those growing in shallow water or as emergents.</br></br>Several exotic species are cultivated in nurseries in Thailand for use as aquarium plants. Their identity may be checked in: Jacobsen, N., 1987. Cryptocoryne in Dassanayake, M.D. and F.R. Fosberg eds. A Revised Handbook to the Flora of Ceylon, Vol. VI: 85–99, and species 
occurring in neighbouring Peninsular Malaysia may be consulted in Othman, Jacobsen, & Mashhor. 2009.Cryptocoryne of Peninsular Malaysia 1–102, Penerbit Universiti Sains Malaysia.

description: Rhizome short and rugged, sometimes slender with long internodes. Runners long, slender. Leaves green to brownish purple, upper surface purplish green to green, lower surface red to greenish with reddish veins; leaf blade narrowly ovate, with a truncate to narrowly cordate base, 5–15 by 1–4 cm, surface between the veins smooth to bullate (largest specimens in deep, not quite so fast-running water, small compact specimens in faster-running water; emerged specimens with greenish, crumpled leaves); petiole 5–15 cm long; spathe 10–22 cm long; peduncle 1–3 cm long; kettle 1–2 cm long, white, inside purplish in the upper half; tube 2–12 cm long, white, the upper part dark purplish on the outside; limb 3–7 cm long, spirally twisted, black purple, upper part sometimes greenish, somewhat rough; collar elongate, present but more or less concealed in the spirally twisted limb; pistillate flowers 5–8, purplish to purple or greenish and purple spotted, more or less papillose; stigmas ovate to emarginate; olfactory bodies irregularly rounded, upper surface more or less rough, yellow to purplish spotted; staminate flowers 40–60, smooth. Infructescence ovoid. Seeds brownish, surface somewhat rough; endosperm present, embryo cone-shaped, with an undifferentiated plumula. Chromosome number: 2n = 34.

In such places with a strong water current in the flood season, it can be found sheltered between rocks and big stones or on leeward places in the winding riverbed, and, in sheltered places, it can also be found growing in sand and gravel and more or less mud-covered. It has been found growing together with different varieties of C. crispatula.

description: Rhizome creeping with distinctly thickened yearly growths. Leaves linear, to 40 by 1.5 cm, gradually tapering to a fine point, base narrowly attenuate, margin somewhat undulate, smooth to irregularly denticulate, green and, under exposed light conditions, with a brownish tinge and with brownish markings; spathe ca 5–7 cm long; kettle ca 1–2 by 0.5–1 cm, with a thickened wall inside just about the middle, lower inside wall white, upper part with alveoli, red to reddish with small white blotches continuing upwards through the tube which is ca 1–2 cm in length, a 1–3 times spirally twisted limb (before anthesis), with purple, irregular, very pronounced transverse ridges on the surface (most pronounced on the lower part), and a pronounced purple collar structure; pistillate flowers ca 6; stigma round, almost vertical; olfactory bodies distinctly irregular (rounded) with protruding cells, purplish; staminate flowers about 80–120, yellow, surface of the thecae rough from protruding cells. Infructescence splitting in a septicidal/septifragal-ceratium-like manner, greenish to purplish, globose to ovate, 1–1.5 cm long, smooth. Seeds brownish, 5–8 mm, rugose; endosperm present; embryo conical with an undifferentiated plumula. Chromosome number: 2n = 36.

description: Terrestrial herbs producing fasciculate fleshy roots from the basis of an erect, glabrous stem. Foliage leaves basal, long-petiolate. Inflorescence racemose, lax. Flowers non-resupinate, predominantly green to brownish-red, dominated by a large labellum. Sepals free, with inrolled margins. Labellum straight (i.e., not twisted), partly enveloping the column at base, 13.9–20 mm long, simple, entire, minutely papillose on the ventral side, strongly concave at base, devoid of ornaments. Column straight (i.e., not twisted), short, slightly winged; stignia entire to bilobed, convex; viscidium 1, naked; anther versatile, thecae not extending from the column; pollinia 4, acrotonous. Ovary glabrous. Fruit a capsule, dehiscing by 6 longitudinal slits.</br></br>This genus of ca. 25 species has scattered occurrences from Sri Lanka, northeastern India and Taiwan in the northwest to Tasmania, northernmost New Zealand and Samoa in the southeast; 1 species in Thailand.

description: Flowering shoots 24–52.5 cm tall; stem 1–4 mm in diameter. Foliage leaves 1–3; petiole channelled, 3.3–12.5 cm long, spotted with purple; lamina ovate to elliptic or broadly lanceolate, often oblique, acuminate, (6.8–18.4–16 by (2.6–)4–6.7 cm. Inflorescence cylindric, 9- to many flowered; rachis (5.5–)12–30 cm long; bracts ovate-lanceolate, long-acuminate, shorter than or subequal to the ovary, 7–18 by 2–6.2 mm. Flowers short-pedicelled, predominantly dull brownish-red (sepals and petals light green, labellum with dark crimson spots). Sepals subsimilar, linear-triangular, acuminate, glabrous, 3-veined, 14–16.7 by 2.3–2.9 mm. Petals spreading, linear-triangular, acuminate, 1-veined, 8–11.1 by 1.5–1.6 mm, with entire, inrolled margins. Labellum ovate-oblong, 13.9–20 by 5–8.3 mm; distal part flat with an acute to acuminate, distinctly incurved apex. Column semiterete, 2–3 mm long; anther 2.5–2.6 mm long, 1.4–1.5 mm wide, with a recurved, subacuminate apex. Ovary 7.5–17 mm long. Capsule short-pedicelled, ellipsoid, 10–15 mm long, 5–7 mm in diameter.

description: Herbs or subshrubs, annual or perennial, glabrous or (glandular) hairy; branches terete or (sub)angular. Leaves decussate (or whorled), rarely alternate. Inflorescences racemose with single flowers decussate or alternate, beside the leaves (bracts) because of concaulescence; bracteoles 2 or absent. Flowers zygomorphous, 6-merous; calyx tube elongate, at base with (shallow) spur at one side; calyx appendages present or absent; calyx lobes (sepals) short; petals small or large, equal or unequal, persistent or caducous; stamens (4–)11, inserted in upper part of the calyx tube, included or exserted; ovary sessile, incompletely 2-locular, with disc-appendage at base; ovules few or numerous. Fruit a dehiscent capsule enclosed in the calyx tube. Seeds lentiform, sometimes with winged margin.</br></br>About 260 species in Tropical America; 1 species in Thailand, commonly cultivated, locally escaped and possibly naturalised.

description: Epiphytic, lithophytic or terrestrial herbs, rarely mycoheterotrophic. Pseudobulbs ovoid to spindle-shaped, occasionally absent, often concealed within the leaf bases. Roots thick, velamen-covered. Cataphylls several, surrounding the young growth. Leaves up to 13, distichous, duplicate, linear-elliptic or narrowly ligulate to elliptic, acuminate to strongly bilobed, articulated. Inflorescences racemose, usually arising from within the cataphylls but occasionally from within the axils of the leaves. Flowers 1 to many, long-lasting (all open at the same time), often large, showy and sometimes fragrant, each subtended by a small bract. Sepals and petals free, subsimilar, spreading or with the petals porrect. Labellum 3-lobed (to subentire), free or proximally fused to the base of the column; side lobes erect and weakly clasping the column; mid-lobe often recurved; ornaments usually of 2 parallel ridges from near the base of the labellum to the base of the mid-lobe, rarely replaced by a shallow depression or a single ridge. Column arcuate, weakly or strongly winged, glabrous, foot short or absent; pollinia usually 2, partly cleft, or completely cleft to form 4 very tightly coupled pollinia, hard and bony, attached by short caudicles to a usually triangular viscidium (stipe absent). Capsule fusiform to ellipsoidal or oblong-ellipsoidal, narrowing at the base to a short pedicel and at the apex to a short beak formed by the persistent column.</br></br>Some 52 species distributed from the NW Himalayas to Japan, and south through Indo China and Malesia to the Philippines, New Guinea and Australia; 20 species in Thailand.

description: Medium-sized, epiphytic herb. Pseudobulbs 6–9 by 3–4 cm, ovoid, bilaterally flattened. Leaves 4–5 per pseudobulb, 40–100 by 1.5–4.5 cm, ligulate, obtuse to emarginate and unequally bilobed at the apex, coriaceous, rigid, arching. Inflorescence 30–70 cm long, pendulous except at the base, with 20–45 flowers; rachis 24–76 cm long; bracts 2–5 mm long. Flowers 3.5–4.2 cm across; lightly scented; sepals and petals pale yellow to cream with a broad, central, maroon-brown stripe, often with darker streaks; labellum white or cream, side lobes and mid-lobe veined maroon, mid-lobe yellow at the base; ridges and disk yellow. Dorsal sepal 19–24 by 5–8.5 mm, narrowly oblong to narrowly ligulate-elliptic, obtuse, mucronate, erect; lateral sepals similar, oblique, spreading. Petals 18–20 by 5–8.5 mm, narrowly elliptic, obtuse to acute, sometimes mucronate, porrect and almost parallel above the column. Labellum 15–23 by 10–14 mm when flattened, saccate at the base, minutely papillose to minutely pubescent; side lobes acute to acuminate, exceeding the column and the anther; mid-lobe 8.4–12 by 6.5–9 mm, ovate, acute to obtuse, often mucronate, usually recurved, margin entire; ornaments usually of 2 sigmoid ridges often broken in the middle and inflated only towards the base and the apex. Column 10–12 mm long; pollinia 2. Capsule 4–7 by 2–3 cm, oblong-ellipsoidal.

description: Large, epiphytic or rarely lithophytic herb. Pseudobulbs up to 10 by 6 cm, ovoid, bilaterally flattened. Leaves usually 7–9 per pseudobulb, up to 50–90 by 1.5–4 cm, ligulate, obtuse and unequally bilobed at the apex, coriaceous, rigid, arching. Inflorescence 28–75 cm long, arching to pendulous, with 10–33 flowers; rachis 20–55 cm long; bracts 1–4 mm long. Flowers 3.5–4.5 cm across; usually coconut-scented; sepals deep maroon to dull yellow-green with strong maroon staining; labellum white, becoming yellow with age, side-lobes stained maroon-purple, mid-lobe yellow in front of the ridges and blotched with maroon; ridges bright yellow in front, stained maroon behind. Dorsal sepal 28–33 by 7–10 mm, narrowly ligulate elliptic, obtuse, suberect, margins revolute; lateral sepals similar, falcate and oblique, pendulous and porrect. Petals 25–30 by 7.5–11 mm, narrowly elliptic, subacute, weakly porrect, margins sometimes revolute. Labellum 21–25 by 13–15 mm when flattened, usually broadest across the mid-lobe, minutely papillose to minutely pubescent, the longest hairs on the side-lobe tips; side lobes erect, much shorter than the column, apices obtuse and appearing truncated; mid-lobe 11–13 by 13–14 mm, broadly ovate to rhomboid, obtuse to emarginate, weakly recurved, margin entire; ornaments of 2 sigmoid, raised ridges that are rounded and confluent at the apices and merge gradually with the base of the mid-lobe. Column 16–18 mm long; pollinia 2.

description: Medium-sized, epiphytic herb. Pseudobulbs 5–7 by 1.6–2.9 cm, slenderly ovoid, slightly bilaterally flattened. description: Medium-sized, epiphytic herb. Pseudobulbs up to 5 by 2.5 cm, elongate-ovoid, bilaterally flattened. Leaves 5–7 per pseudobulb, sessile, up to 30–68 by 1.2–2.9 cm, narrowly ligulate, obtuse, unequally bilobed to oblique at the apex, cartilaginous, stiff, arching. Inflorescence 10–50 cm long, arching to pendulous, with 5–26 flowers; rachis 8–33 cm long; bracts 1.5–4.5 mm long. Flowers 2.5–4.5 cm across; lightly fruit-scented; sepals and petals pale yellow to cream, with a broad, weakly defined central stripe of maroon-brown; labellum cream, the side lobes finely mottled with maroon, the mid-lobe white to yellow at the base, variously spotted or blotched with maroon; ridges cream to yellow, often finely mottled behind with red-brown. Labellum 12.5–18 by 9.5–15.5 mm when flattened, saccate at the base, minutely papillose to pubescent; side lobes shorter than or as long as the column but not exceeding the anther, obtuse (to subacute); mid-lobe 5.2–8.7 by 6–9.6 mm, broadly elliptic, rounded, usually recurved, minutely papillose to shortly glandular-pubescent, sometimes with an undulating margin; ornaments of 2 ridges that are entire and almost parallel to sigmoid, minutely papillose to minutely pubescent. description: Terrestrial herb. Pseudobulbs subterranean, inconspicuous. Leaves usually 5–8 per pseudobulb, up 32–51 by 0.9–1.5 cm, linear-elliptic, acute, erect, margin entire, conduplicate at the base but not petiolate, the lowest leaves making a gradual transition between the cataphylls and the true leaves. Inflorescence 23–43 cm tall, erect, with 4–7 flowers produced in the apical third; bracts 3–22(–25) mm long, often exceeding the pedicel and ovary in length. Flowers about 4–5 cm across; lemon-scented; sepals and petals pale yellow with 5–7 longitudinal red-brown lines; labellum pale green or whitish, sometimes pale yellow, with red-purple streaks on the side lobes that become confluent at the margin, and red-purple spots and blotches on the mid-lobe. Dorsal sepal 25–35 by 5–8 mm, narrowly oblong-elliptic, acute, erect; lateral sepals similar, spreading. Petals 19–29 by 6–9 mm, ovate to elliptic, acute, usually equal to or narrower than the sepals, porrect, usually closely shading the column. Labellum 17–22 mm long when flattened; side lobes rounded, usually angled at the apex, sparsely pubescent or papillose (at least apically); mid-lobe 9–13 by 8–11 mm, oblong to broadly ovate, obtuse or subacute, often as broad as the side lobes when the labellum is flattened, recurved, with some small papillae that are occasionally sparse and almost confined to the apical region, margin entire; disk ornamented by ridges converging in the apical half to form a short tube at the base of the mid-lobe. Column 10–15 mm long; pollinia 4. Capsule 5–7 cm long, fusiform, erect.

description: Epiphytic herb. Pseudobulbs c. 4 by 2.5 cm, fusiform, slightly bilaterally compressed. Leaves 5–8, sessile, 40–95 by 0.7–1.6(–2.4) cm, linear-elliptic, slightly obliquely acute to acuminate, thickened and coriaceous, dark green, the mid-vein prominent below. Flowers 4–5 cm across; not usually scented; sepals and petals white or cream with a central maroon stripe that does not reach the apex, rarely suffused wine-red; labellum white, with an orange or yellow spot at the base; side lobes white, veined maroon, with a maroon margin; mid-lobe deep maroon with a basal, triangular, pale yellow stripe that does not reach the apex; ridges white or cream. Labellum 15–22 by 10–15 mm when flattened; side lobes as long as the column, with porrect, triangular tips subacute at the apex and minutely papillose; mid-lobe 8–12 by 7–9 mm, recurved, ovate, entire, subacute, mucronate to acuminate, minutely papillose, often with minute hairs towards the base and with 2 lines of longer, often glandular, hairs extending from the ridge apices to the centre of the mid-lobe; ornaments of 2 parallel ridges extending from the base of the labellum to the base of the mid-lobe, covered in glandular hairs. description: Lithophytic or epiphytic herb. Dorsal sepal 20–29 by 7–10 mm, elliptic, obtuse, erect, with recurved margins; lateral sepals similar, oblique, spreading, pendulous. Labellum broad, 14–16(–20) by 10–15 mm, rhombic, papillose, attached to the column foot; side lobes obscure; mid-lobe c. 8 by 8 mm, triangular-ovate, decurved to weakly recurved, obtuse to mucronate; ornaments reduced to 2 swellings at the base of the mid-lobe. description: Terrestrial herb. Pseudobulbs to 3 by 1.5 cm, ovoid, often inconspicuous, occasionally subterranean. description: Epiphytic or lithophytic herb. Pseudobulbs up to 8 by 5 cm, ovoid, bilaterally flattened. description: Epiphytic or lithophytic herb. Pseudobulbs 3–6 cm long, 1.5–3.5 cm in diameter, elongate-ovoid, bilaterally flattened. description: Terrestrial holomycotroph, without leaves or pseudobulbs. Roots often absent, occasionally produced towards the apex of the rhizome. Rhizome 3–8 mm in diameter, soft, fleshy, tuberculate, with nodes 2–15 mm apart, usually branching, whitish, subterranean. Inflorescence 7–32 cm long, erect, with 3–6 flowers, usually produced terminally on the rhizome or on its side branches; peduncle covered with 4–8, mostly overlapping cataphylls, of which 1–4 are above ground; cataphylls 13–27 mm long, ovate, cymbiform, with a cylindrical sheathing base and a loosely sheathing, spreading, cymbiform apex; bracts 2–17 mm long. Flowers 3–4 cm across; sepals and petals cream to pale yellow or brownish pink with a diffuse, central, purple-red stripe to near the apex; labellum white with red spots on the mid-lobe and purple-red stripes on the side lobes, which become confluent at the margin; ridges white, sometimes stained pink. Dorsal sepal 19–26 by 4–6 mm, narrowly obovate to ligulate, acute, erect; lateral sepals similar, spreading. Petals 14–20 by 5–7 mm, narrowly elliptic, oblique, acute, usually porrect and covering the column. Labellum 12–17 by 9–11 mm when flattened, almost rhombic in outline, subentire to 3-lobed, papillose; side lobes erect, obtuse to subacute at the apex; mid-lobe 5–7 by 4–6 mm, triangular to ligulate, acute to obtuse, recurved, the margin usually undulating; ornaments of 2 ridges, convergent towards the apex, forming a short tube at the base of the mid-lobe. description: Epiphytic or lithophytic herb. description: Lithophytic herb. Pseudobulb up to 3 by 3 cm, lens-shaped, with 2–6 distichous leaves and 4–5 cataphylls; the lower leaves and cataphylls deciduous; mature pseudobulbs wrinkled,  usually with 2–4 apical leaves, not covered by the leaf bases, with nodes towards the base and the apex only. Leaves up to 17–22 by 3–3.5 cm, narrowly elliptic, twisted. Inflorescence 12–23 cm long; peduncle (sub)erect; rachis usually longer than the peduncle, with 2–5 large, distant  flowers; bracts 4–9 mm long. Flowers 4–5 cm across; honey-scented; sepals and petals olive-green to mustard, shaded red-brown and spotted towards the base with purple-brown; labellum white, turning pink on pollination, with almost entirely purple-brown side-lobes, and spots and transverse dashes of red-purple on the mid-lobe; ridges white, spotted purple. Dorsal sepal 37–42 by 8–13 mm, narrowly obovate with recurved margins, obtuse or subacute, mucronate, suberect, curved over the column; lateral sepals similar, narrowly elliptic, decurved, not fully spreading. description: Epiphytic or lithophytic herb, often with erect aerial roots near the base. Pseudobulbs 5–15 by 2–6 cm, elongate-ovate, bilaterally flattened. Leaves 5–11, sessile, up to 95 by 4 cm, linear elliptic, acute, mid-green. Inflorescence up to 130 cm long, suberect, arching; rachis bearing 10–20 flowers; bracts c. 3 mm long. Flowers up to 15 cm across; scent strong, sweet; sepals and petals yellowish-green to olive-green, strongly stained with irregular, dull, red-brown veins and spots; labellum pale yellow to cream, side lobes veined dark red-brown, mid-lobe marked with scattered spots and vertical dashes of red-brown, with a central reddish stripe almost to the front of the ridges; ridges cream, spotted with red along the crests. Dorsal sepal concave, porrect, 55–80 by 14–19 mm, narrowly obovate, acute; lateral sepals similar, asymmetric and twisted. Petals spreading or reflexed, 54–72 by 8–14 mm, ligulate, usually falcate. Labellum fused to the column for the basal 4–5.5 mm; side lobes 11–16 mm broad, triangular, acute and porrect, margins hairy (hairs over 2 mm long), indumentum otherwise shorter with the hairs mainly pigmented red brown and confined to the veins; mid-lobe 18–21 by 18–30 mm, elliptic, mucronate, recurved, with scattered hairs on the upper surface, except in the centre where there are 3 rows of long hairs from the ridges to the centre of the mid-lobe, margin finely erose, undulate and partially reflexed; ornaments of 2 ridges, tapering towards the base and dilated towards the apex, densely covered in long hairs, with a third line of hairs between them. Column 34–44 mm long; pollinia 2. Capsule up to 15 by 6 cm, fusiform-ellipsoid, stalked, with a 2 cm apical beak.

description: Terrestrial, achlorophyllous, mycoheterotrophic, erect herbs, often with thick and fleshy roots arising from short rhizomes; stems often several from each rhizome, simple or branched, fleshy, papillose, often yellowish-brown to reddish-brown in colour. Foliage leaves reduced to scale-like sheaths or bracts, one at each node, glabrous to pubescent. Inflorescence consisting of a terminal and often several lateral racemes, few-to many-flowered; rachis pubescent or mealy hairy; bracts persistent. Flowers usually not opening widely, greenish, yellowish or brownish. Sepuls free, 6- to 9-veined, often papillose outside, fleshy. Petals free, 7- to 9-veined, slightly shorter than the sepals, glabrous. Labellum concave, entire, with thickened disc, base adnate to base of column. Column stout, slightly curved, without foot, usually with lateral toothed wings; pollen assembled in 2 mealy pollinia without caudicles or viscidium. Ovary slender. Fruit a fleshy berry, pink, red or orange, often shiny. Seeds with stout testa, with or without a narrow surrounding wing.</br></br>A genus of about 5 species, distributed from Sri Lanka to NE India, S China, Japan, Indo China, Thailand, Peninsular Malaysia, Borneo, Sumatra, Java, the Philippines and New Guinea; 3 species in Thailand.

description: Flowering shoots 20–65 cm tall, erect, 4–6 mm in diameter at base, branched; nodes with sheaths; sheaths glabrous to pubescent, ovate, 4–10 mm long, acute, coriaceous. Sepals furfuraceous outside, 6- to 9-veined, apex acute; dorsal sepal lanceolate-oblong, 15–20 by 6–8 mm; lateral sepals obliquely ovate, 14–20 by 8–9 mm, larger than dorsal sepal, apex slightly hooded. description: Caespitose or solitary, monoecious palm trees. Stem often conspicuously ringed by leaf scars and with numerous adventitious roots at the base. Leaves reduplicate, pinnately divided; leaf sheath tubular forming a distinct crownshaft, falling neatly by abscission; petiole usually short, pinnae single-fold, regularly arranged. Inflorescence infrafoliar, branched to 2–4 orders, enclosed in prophyll until leaf fall, peduncle short, peduncular bract incompletely enclosing the inflorescence, rachis longer than peduncle, first order branches robust spreading, rachillae numerous, always with spirally arranged floral triads of one female flower and two male flowers, these sunken in shallow pits, partly covered by shallow triangular rachillae bracts. Male flowers with petals twice as long as sepals and united basally to c. ⅓ of their length, stamens 8–15, connate at the base; female flowers about the same size or slightly larger, petals slightly larger than sepals, staminodal ring membranous and reduced, gynoecium unilocular, ellipsoidal with three sessile, recurved stigmas. Fruit ellipsoidal to sickle-shaped, often black at maturity with persistent perianth basally and apical stigmatic remains, epicarp smooth, mesocarp thin, endocarp poorly differentiated. Seed with homogeneous endosperm.</br></br>Seven species in Peninsular Thailand to Papuasia. One species in Thailand.

description: Terrestrial herbs with a fleshy, branched rhizome rooting from its nodes or devoid of roots. Flowering shoots terminal, erect, leafless or with a few leaves in a basal rosette. Foliage leaves (if present) short-petiolate; petiole channelled, sheathing at base. Inflorescence spicate; bracts ciliate. Flowers resupinate. Sepals free, 1- to 2-veined. Petals connivent with the dorsal sepal. Labellum basally adnate to the column, straight (i.e., not twisted), differentiated into hypochile, mesochile, and epichile; hypochile forming two conspicuous lateral sacs, each containing a subsessile appendage; mesochile with margins incurved to meet in the middle, glabrous to rugose-papillose; epichile triangular to transversely rectangular with incurved margins (sometimes vestigial). Column straight (i.e., not twisted); stigma bilobed, flat: rostellum triangular, more or less bifid; viscidium 1, naked; anther versatile; pollinia 2, basitonous. Ovary glabrous or pubescent. Fruit not seen.</br></br>A genus of ca. 20 species distributed in nearly all of Malesia, across Peninsular Malaysia to southern Thailand, and on the Palau Islands; 1 species in Thailand.

description: Solitary or clustered, stemless to high-climbing hapaxanthic or pleonanthic dioecious rattans. Leaves usually cirrate, even in non-climbing species the apical leaves showing some vestige of a cirrus; sheaths usually heavily armed with spines, the spines frequently grouped; knee present or not; ocrea inconspicuous; flagellum absent; leaflets variously arranged, never discolorous. Inflorescences male and female superficially similar, the male branching to 3 orders, the female to 2, within the genus inflorescnces of two basic types, one with all bracts enclosed within the outermost bract (prophyll), splitting along their length to expose the flowers but with the bract tips still included within the outermost bract, the other with bracts borne on a more elongate inflorescence, the bracts tubular at first, then at flowering splitting along their entire length to leave no tubular portion, and usually quickly falling, the prophyll sometimes persisting; bracts variously armed; partial inflorescences usually shorter than the subtending bract; involucre and involucrophore inconspicuous, the latter often stalk-like. Male flower with small cup-like calyx with 3 short lobes; corolla split ± to the base into 3 petals; stamens 6, slightly epipetalous; pistillode minute. Sterile male flower borne with the female as a pair, like the fertile males but with empty anthers and soon falling. Female flower usually larger than the male, with calyx truncate or 3-lobed; corolla with 3 petals; staminodes 6, joined at the base to form a ring; ovary covered in reflexed scales, and tipped with 3 stigmas, and with 3 locules. Seed usually 1 only, covered in thin to thick, sweet or sour sarcotesta; endosperm deeply ruminate, embryo basal. Seedling leaf usually with 4 or more leafl ets.</br></br>A hundred and three species in Tropical and Subtropical Asia. Fifteen species in Thailand.

description: Moderate clustering rattan. Stems rarely more than 15 m tall, often fertile when only 3 m tall, without sheaths c. 1.2 cm diam., with sheaths to 3 cm diam., internodes to 15 cm long. Leaf cirrate; sheaths dark green, armed with scattered, somewhat reflexed, variable, grey to black triangular spines, 0.4–2.5 cm long with yellow bases; knee prominent; petiole to 40 cm long usually ± rounded in cross section, armed with sparse spines on the yellowish lower surface and rather dense groups of short spines on the dark green upper surface; rachis to 1.1 m long; cirrus to 1 m long; leaflets to c. 20 on each side of the rachis, usually arranged in divergent opposite or alternate pairs but sometimes arranged ± regularly in the proximal portion and paired in the distal portion only, or subregularly throughout, the leaflets usually rather broad, to 35 by 3.5 cm, rarely narrow lanceolate, 40 by 2 cm, bristly along the margins, otherwise unarmed. Inflorescences to 20 cm long, rarely to 50 cm long, male and female superficially similar, the male branching to 3 orders, the female to 2 orders, with all but the first bract quickly falling at anthesis; peduncle and first bract densely armed with partial whorls of short triangular spines to 0.5 cm long; partial inflorescences up to c. 5, often 1 or 2 only; rachillae and flowers covered in red-brown indumentum; male rachillae to 2 by 1.2 cm; female rachillae 3–4 by 0.3 cm. Ripe fruit ovoid to 2.5 by 2 cm, covered in 12–15 vertical rows of rather swollen reddish-brown scales densely covered with red resin. Seed ovoid, to 1.3 by 1.2 cm with slight flattening; endosperm deeply ruminate. Seedling leaf with 4–6 broad leaflets.

description: Moderate-sized, usually solitary rather short rattan. Stems usually less than 5 m long, but occasionally to 20 m, often flowering when merely 1–2 m long, without sheaths to 2 cm diam., with sheaths to 3.5 cm diam., internodes to 10 cm long, usually less. Leaves cirrate; sheaths dark shiny green with abundant greyish-brown indumentum, armed with oblique almost diagonal partial whorls of reflexed flattened black spines to 4 cm long mixed with fine spines to 0.5 cm long, the spine bases confluent in low collars persisting after spines disintegrate in old sheaths, spines around the leaf sheath mouth obliquely upward pointing, to 10 cm long, often paler than those on the body of the sheath; knee a low rounded swelling, usually unarmed and hence conspicuous; ocrea absent; petiole to 1 m long, usually armed with large patent pale straw-coloured spines to 7 cm long, these tending to trap leaf litter, distally armed with scattered groupsof reflexed spines; rachis 1–1.5 m; cirrus 0.4–1 m; leaflets up to 40 on each side of the rachis, usually irregularly arranged in groups of 3–10, sometimes ± regular, dark green, the largest to 35 by 2 cm. Inflorescences pendulous, to 60 cm long, the male and female superficially similar, the male branched to 3 orders, the female to 2 orders; peduncle conspicuous, to 40 cm long, armed with short lateral spines to 1.5 cm long; prophyll and peduncular bracts thin, almost papery, soon splitting and falling or disintegrating, armed with groups of very slender horse-hair like spines; male rachillae to 35 by 0.3 cm, with very densely crowded strictly distichous flowers; female rachillae to 80 by 0.4 cm. Mature fruit ± spherical, to c. 2.2 cm diam., with a short beak to 0.2 by 0.2 cm, and covered in 15–17 vertical rows of pale straw-coloured channelled scales with darker margins and usually with red flecks. Seed ± rounded, somewhat flattened on one side, c. 1.2 cm diam., endosperm deeply ruminate. Seedling leaf with 4–6 leaflets.

description: Clustering moderate-sized to robust rattan. Stems climbing to 20 m long, without sheaths c. 1.8–3 cm diam., with sheaths c. 3–5 cm diam., internodes 20–30 cm long. Leaves cirrate; sheath pale green to pale brown armed with scattered or partially whorled black spines to 5 cm long, interspersed with caducous black indumentum; knee conspicuous; ocrea insignificant; petiole to 40 cm armed with short, grouped spines along the margins; rachis to 1.5 m long, it and the rachis crimson in emerging leaves; leaflets c. 30 on each side of the rachis, rather distant, broad, when newly emerged dull bluish-green, not shining, becoming dark green with age, the largest to 50 by 4.5 cm, very sparsely bristly or unarmed. Inflorescences erect, ± sessile, the male and female superficially similar, but the male branched to 3 orders and the female to 2 orders, the whole inflorescence to c. 70 cm long, usually less, 15 cm wide, smaller in impoverished stems; prophyll boat shaped with a beak to 15 cm long, and densely armed with black spines and abundant dark indumentum, enclosing the entire inflorescence with all its bracts, the prophyll splitting at anthesis but bract tips usually remaining captured within the tip of the prophyll; rachillae very densely crowded. Mature fruit rounded, 2.5 cm diam., with a short beak to 0.15 by 0.15 cm, and covered in 14–16 vertical rows of yellowish-brown, channelled scales with darker margins. Seed rounded c. 2 cm diam.; endosperm deeply ruminate. Seedling leaf with c. 6 broad bluish-green leaflets.

description: Clustering moderate-sized to robust rattan tending to form dense thickets. Stems to 25 m or more long, but often flowering when much less, without sheaths 1.5–3 cm diam., with sheaths 3–6 cm diam., internodes 25–40 cm long. Leaves cirrate; sheaths dull green to pale brown, with abundant reddish to dark brown indumentum and armed with abundant scattered and grouped black spines, the largest flattened, 3–4 cm long, interspersed with smaller less obviously flattened spines 0.3–2 cm long, the spines sometimes arranged in partial whorls; knee conspicuous, armed as the rest of the sheath, although sometimes less densely so; ocrea minute, scarcely developed; petiole 10–50 cm long, much longer in juvenile stems and rosette leaves, armed abaxially and along margins with black spines 0.2–1 cm long; rachis to 2 m long, armed as the petiole; cirrus 50–90 cm long; leaflets to 70 or more on each side of the rachis, regularly arranged, linear, the largest 30–70 by 1.5–3.8 cm, bristly along 3 nerves adaxially, along margins, and along midrib abaxially. Inflorescences erect, ± sessile, or peduncle very short, not exceeding 6 cm long, the male and female superficially similar, but the male branched to 3 orders and the female to 2 orders, the whole infl orescence to c. 65 cm long, rarely more, 15 cm wide, smaller in impoverished stems; prophyll boat-shaped with a beak to 7–15 cm long, and densely armed with black spines and abundant dark indumentum, enclosing the entire inflorescence with all its bracts, the prophyll splitting at anthesis but bract tips usually remaining captured within the tip of the prophyll; rachillae very densely crowded, male to 3 by 0.2 cm, female to 8 by 0.3 cm. Mature fruit rounded, c. 1.9 cm diam., with a short beak to 0.15 by 0.15 cm, and covered in 17–18 vertical rows of yellowish-brown, channelled scales with darker margins. Seed rounded c. 1.3 cm diam.; endosperm deeply ruminate. Seedling leaf with c. 8 closely set linear leaflets.

description: Clustering, moderate-sized acaulescent to short-climbing rattan. Stems often very short, sometimes climbing to 5 m, without sheaths to 3.5 cm diam., with sheaths to 5.5 cm diam., internodes 5–10 cm long. Leaves cirrate or, very rarely in acaulescent forms, ecirrate; sheaths dull brownish-green, densely covered with reddish-brown or dull dark brown indumentum and armed with dark brown to blackish spines to 4 cm long, erect or reflexed, arranged in oblique or horizonal partial whorls, the larger spines often interspersed with smaller spines, spines around the leaf sheath mouth erect and much larger than other spines, to 6 cm long; knee absent in non-climbing forms; ocrea absent; petiole up to 1 m long, much less in climbing forms, armed with lateral spines 0.6–2 cm long; rachis to 2 m long, usually less; cirrus very short (rarely absent) or to 1 m long; leaflets to c. 65 on each side of the rachis, regularly arranged, rather close, the longest to 50 by 2.5 cm, armed adaxially with brown bristles on 3 nerves, abaxially only on midrib. Inflorescences male and female superficially similar, the male branched to 3 orders, the female to 2 orders, borne on a conspicuous peduncle to 50–80 cm or more long in short stemmed forms, much less in climbing forms, the peduncle armed with abundant short grouped spines to 0.4 cm long; prophyll and up to 7 peduncular bracts armed with grouped short spines, the bracts splitting longitudinally and all falling except for the prophyll that persists; male rachillae to 5.3 by 0.2 cm, the female to 1.2 by 0.4 cm. Mature fruit rounded, c. 1.8 cm diam., with a short beak to 0.15 cm long, and covered in 15–18 vertical rows of rich brown channelled scales with slightly darker margins. Seed rounded c. 1.2 cm diam.; endosperm deeply ruminate. Seedling leaf with 4–6 leaflets.

description: Clustering moderate-sized rattan. Stems climbing to 40 m long, without sheaths c. 1.5 cm diam., with sheaths to 3 cm diam., internodes to 15 cm long. Leaf cirrate; sheaths bright green, bearing complete and partial pale coloured collars to 1 cm, tipped with black and brown horsehair-like spines, 1–6 cm long, the longest tending to be paler in colour and all bearing abundant dark grey, caducous indumentum, at least some of the collars interlocking to produce ant galleries; knee conspicuous, usually less heavily armed than the sheath; ocrea absent; petiole to 40 cm, armed near the base with low collars bearing black spines, distally with scattered or grouped triangular spines; rachis 1.1 m long; cirrus to 1 m long; leaflets very variable in arrangement, to c. 20 on each side of the rachis, rarely subregular, usually grouped in threes to sixes, the basal 2 groups being congested and the leaflets pointing in several directions, the longest usually the most basal, to 40 by 2.5 cm, unarmed except for short marginal bristles. Inflorescences pendulous, to 60 cm long, the male branching to 3 orders, the female to 2 orders; primary bracts densely armed with fine black spines, all except the prophyll quickly falling at anthesis, other bracts inconspicuous; male rachillae to 1.5 by 0.1 cm, female rachillae to 5 by 0.2 cm. Mature fruit ovoid, very shortly beaked, c. 1.6 by 1.2 cm, rarely spherical, covered with 14–17 vertical rows of yellowish-brown scales. Seed c. 1.2 by 0.9 cm; endosperm deeply ruminate. Seedling leaf with divergent leaflets.

description: Clustering moderate-sized rattan, often forming thickets. description: Usually solitary, variable, moderate-sized rattan. Stems rarely exceeding 15 m long, often much less, without sheaths to 2 cm diam., with sheaths to 3 cm diam., internodes rather short, rarely exceeding 12 cm long. Leaves cirrate; sheaths bright green, densely armed with interlocking pairs of green collars bearing very fine black horse-hair like spines to 2 cm long, intermingled with numerous large flattened yellowish-green to blackish spines to 6 cm long, the interlocking galleries usually occupied by ants, dark brown indumentum abundant on young sheaths, particularly on spines and collars, the indumentum often utilized by ants to construct vertical galleries linking the horizontal galleries, spines around the leaf sheath mouth erect, to 8 cm long, tending to trap leaf litter; knee present but largely obscured by the spines and collars; ocrea not developed; petiole 35–40 cm long, armed with reflexed black spines to 5 cm long, interspersed with groups of minute black bristles; rachis to 2.6 m long; cirrus to 1 m, often less; leaflets 45–60 on each side of the rachis, regularly arranged, close, linear, the longest to c. 40 by 2.3 cm, abaxially sparsely bristly on mid nerve and lateral veins. Inflorescences borne on peduncles to 30–65 cm long, armed with lateral spines to 1 cm long, the male and female superficially similar, the male branched to 3 orders, the female to 2 orders; bracts on primary axis straw-coloured, thin, almost papery, armed with groups of slender black bristles to 1.5 cm long, all primary bracts splitting and soon falling apart from the first bract (prophyll) which may persist; male rachillae to 5 by 0.3 cm, the flowers strikingly distichous and very crowded, female rachillae to 12 by 0.4 cm. Mature fruit rounded to 1.5 cm diam., with a short beak to 0.1 by 0.1 cm, and covered with c. 15 vertical rows of straw-coloured to reddish-brown channelled scales with darker margins. Seed rounded, slightly angled, c. 0.9 cm diam., somewhat pitted; endosperm deeply ruminate. Seedling leaf pinnate with few close-set leaflets.

description: Deciduous, perennial herb, 30–150 cm tall, with erect, thick, rhizomes. Stems erect, branched, sparsely covered with white, spreading hairs in lower part, densely covered with curled or ascendant hairs in upper part. Basal and lower cauline leaves pentagonal reniform, 3–25 by 3–25 cm., cordate to deeply sinuate at base, 5–7-fid, segments obovately cuneate, 3-lobate, lobes often lobulate, coarsely dentate, teeth ovate, acute, upper surface sparsely pubescent, lower surface pilose with long, white hairs, petioles 10–45 cm, patent hairy, dilated near base. Middle cauline leaves smaller, shortly petiolate; upper ones cuneate, 3-partite to 3-sect, usually nearly sessile. Inflorescences racemose, 2–8-flowered, branched at lower part, pilose with curled, white, glandular hairs, bracts lanceolate to linear, pedicels 1.8–5 cm, pilose or subvillose, bracteoles 2, alternate, usually at middle of pedicels. Flowers half-open, 15–23 mm diam., 27–35 mm long. Sepals blue or blue violet, densely covered with yellowish hairs outside, glabrous inside; upper one 10–14 mm long, spurs 14–20 mm long; lateral ones broadly elliptic, 10–14 by 5–6 mm; lower ones elliptic, 12–15 by 2–6 mm. Petals concolorous with sepals; upper 2 glabrous, acute to acuminate, bilobate at apex, 11–13 by 5–6 mm, spurs 17–18 mm long; lower 2 obvate, 6–7 by 3–5 mm, barbate above, hispid beneath, bifid, lobes with claws 5–7 mm long. Anthers spherical or elliptic, lateral, ca 1 mm long, dark purple, filaments edentate, dilated downwards. Follicles 3, villose on inner part or throughout, hairs yellowish, ascending, 12–14 mm long, beaks straight, 2.5–4 mm long. Seeds obvate, 1.7–2 mm long, transversely lamellate.

description: Very small to medium-sized epiphytic or lithophytic (rarely terrestrial) herbs with short to elongated rhizomes and 1-leaved, clustered to well-spaced pseudobulbs. Foliage leaves long lived, duplicate or (sub)terete, much longer than pseudobulbs. Inflorescences synanthous (to hysteranthous) or heteranthous, racemose, several- to many-flowered, usually arcuate with nodding to pendent rachis; floral bracts persistent, glumaceous, more or less scarious. Flowers usually distichous, less than 2 cm across, often fragrant, most flowers in an inflorescence open at the same time. Sepals and petals free (except for connate lateral sepals in one Philippine endemic). Labellum versatile or firmly attached, entire to fiddle-shaped or 3-lobed, not sigmoidly curved at base, neither spurred nor saccate (except in one Philippine endemic). Column straight to moderately incurved, with or without a pair of stelids (and often prolonged into an apical wing or hood), with or without a solid column foot; anther subterminal, incumbent, versatile; pollinia 4, superposed, entire, solid, with obscure to distinct caudicles; rostellum more or less protruding, producing neither a stipe nor a viscidium; receptive part of stigma concave with more or less elevated margins. Fruit a short-pedicelled, ellipsoid to spherical capsule dehiscing by longitudinal slits.</br></br>A genus of c. 280 species distributed throughout Malesia and reaching Myanmar in the north-west and Taiwan in the north-east; 4 species in Thailand.

description: Small terrestrial, mycoheterotrophic achlorophyllus herbs; rhizome tuberous, oblong to fusiform, fleshy, gradually narrowed to apex; roots filiform. description: Terrestrial, achlorophyllous, mycoheterotrophic, rhizomatous, erect herbs; rhizome tuberous, fusiform or moniliform; roots arising from neck between rhizome and aerial stem; aerial stem slender, with a few scale-like sheaths near base, leafless, glabrous. description: Terrestrial, rarely lithophytic or epiphytic herbs; rhizome short. Stems tall, clustered, stout, cylindrical, glabrous, leafy above, covered by sheaths below. Foliage leaves many, duplicate, distichous, suberect, elliptic or elliptic-lanceolate, coriaceous, stiff, articulated to a sheathing base. Inflorescence terminal, racemous or sparingly to much branched, many-flowered; peduncle terete, with several sterile bracts; rachis cylindrical; bracts longer than ovaries, spathaceous, conspicuous, papery, caducous. Flowers resupinate, medium-sized, showy but not opening widely; pedicel and ovary cylindrical. Dorsal sepal free, hooded over column. Lateral sepals free, similar to dorsal sepal but oblique. Petals free, linear-lanceolate, smaller than sepals. Labellum 3-lobed, without spur; mid-lobe entire, apex reflexed; disk ornamented by 3–5 smooth to verruculose keels from base to apex of labellum; side lobes erect. Column clavate, somewhat incurved, narrowly winged; without column foot; anther 4-locular; pollinia 8 in 2 groups of 4, solid, bilaterally compressed, without caudicles; stigma semi-circular; rostellum a broad flap, not forming a stipe or viscidium. Fruit a capsule, subglobose to ellipsoid.</br></br>A genus of c. 8 species distributed from Indo-China, Borneo, Maluku, Java, Sumatra, Philippines, Sulawesi to New Guinea; 1 species in Thailand.

description: Flowering shoots 1–1.5 m tall, terrestrial or low-growing epiphyte; rhizome short. Stems stout, placed close together on rhizome, 6–7 mm in diameter; sheaths 3–6 cm long, apex acute. Flowers 10–15, usually facing the same way, not opening widely; pedicel and ovary slender, 10–20 mm long. Sepals lanceolate, 25–30 by 6–8 mm, apex acute, dull yellow inside, more or less purplish-pink outside. Petals similar to sepals but slightly narrower. Labellum yellow or yellowish-green marked with purplish-red, 3-lobed, suboblong, 15–20 by 7–12 mm, ornamented by 3 keels which extend almost the whole length; side lobes triangular, erect, incurved; mid-lobe red with yellow erose margins, ovate, apex recurved. description: Tree ca 10 m tall; branchlets stout, reddish brown sericeous. description: Terrestrial herbs with underground tubers, stem glabrous or sparsely pubescent. description: Small to very large terrestrial, autotrophic (east of Wallace’s line also leafless mycoheterotrophic) herbs with underground rhizomes. Stems scrambling or climbing. Leaves numerous, duplicate, distichous, brittle-fleshy. Inflorescences lateral from upper leaf axils, racemose, lax. Flowers resupinate, most or all open at the same time. description: Trees with drooping branches, buttressed. Leaves simple, opposite, entire. Inflorescences of terminal, many-flowered corymbs; flowers 4–8–merous. Calyx-tube obconical or cup-shaped. Seeds numerous, linear, tailed. </br></br>Three species from the south-eastern Himalayas to New Guinea; one in Thailand.

description: Aquatic herbs; stem slender, prostrate, rooting at nodes. Leaves small, opposite, margin usually entire, shortly petiolate. Flowers very small, axillary, usually with only 1 flower at each node; sepals 2–4, base united, membranous, obtuse-acute; petals 2–4, longer than sepals, obtuse; stamens as many as or twice as many as petals. Ovary globose, compressed, apex truncate, 2–4-locular; ovules numerous; styles 2–4; stigmas capitate. Capsule membranous, 2–4-septicidal. Seeds numerous, straight, curved or hippocrepiform, angular and reticulate-striate, the surface with hexagonal or elliptical pits.</br></br>About 25 species: tropical, subtropical, and temperate regions; one species known in Thailand and another one expected.

description: Annual herbs, small, 1.5–3 cm tall. Stem prostrate, richly branched, rooting at nodes. Flowers axillary, solitary; pedicels conspicuous, 1.5–2.5 mm long, curved downward at fruiting stage; calyx 3-fid; lobes oblong-ovate or widely lanceolate, 0.5 by 0.3 mm, apex obtuse, shorter than petals; petals 3, narrowly elliptic, elliptic or ovate, 1–1.5 by 0.5 mm, reddish, 2–3 times as long as sepals; stamens 3, shorter than petals. Ovary obovoid, 3-locular; styles 3. Capsule oblong-ovoid, 3-locular, 3-septicidal. Seeds numerous, ca 0.5 mm long, nearly straight or slightlycurved, reticulate-striate, with hexagonal pits.

description: Moderate-sized, clustering, hapaxanthic, dioecious palm. Stem subterranean with short internodes, obscured by the persistent leaf bases. Leaves pinnate; leaf sheath open, not forming a crownshaft, armed with neat partial whorls of robust spines, except at the extreme base; petiole elongate, armed as leaf sheath; leaflets single-fold, linear to lanceolate in outline, equally spaced and orientated in one plane. Inflorescences gathered at a terminal position, erect in the centre of the crown, individual inflorescences (lateral) subtended by a highly reduced leaf, compact, shortly pedunculate, slightly dimorphic; prophyll short, quickly tattering. Flowers borne in dyads, enclosed by a tight spiral of imbricate subtending bracts in bud, exserted at anthesis; male flowers pinkish at anthesis, calyx tubular, 3-lobed; corolla tubular at the base, bearing 3, triangular, valvate lobes; stamens 6, borne at the mouth of corolla tube, filament fleshy, elongate, anthers elongate. Female flowers coupled with a sterile male flower in dyads, superficially similar to male flowers but larger, staminodes 6, gynoecium tricarpellate, triovulate, covered with flattened scales, stigmas 3. Fruit mostly 1-seeded, with a narrow base, otherwise irregularly shaped, with apical stigmatic remains; epicarp covered in neat vertical rows of reflexed scales, the scale tips spinelike and upward pointing, mesocarp spongy, endocarp not differentiated. Seed with thick sarcotesta, endosperm homogeneous, the apex with a pit. Germination adjacent ligular; eophyll entire, bifid.</br></br>One species from Thailand and Peninsular Malaysia to Borneo and Sumatra.

description: Clustering understorey palm, up to 8 m tall. Stem short, subterranean. Leaves numerous; leaf sheath 60–80 cm long, deeply split, yellowish-green, covered by dense, brown indumentum, armed with whorls of black to brown, 4–8 cm long spines; petiole 2.5–4 m long and rachis up to 4 m long, both similar to sheath in armature; leaflets 25–35 per side, 40–65 by 5–7 cm, equally distributed in one plane, marginally armed with short spines. Inflorescence compact, rounded, 30–50 cm across, visible at anthesis among the leaf bases in the centre of the crown; rachillae numerous, c. 15 cm long, densely crowded. Fruits gathered in head-like infructescences, 2–4 by 2–3 cm, narrow basally but otherwise irregularly shaped, densely covered in reddish-brown to brown, spine-like scales.

description: Herbs, perennial or annual, sometimes suffrutescent, with basal leafy rosettes, stolons, soboles (shoots), or turions (subterranean globose buds with fleshy scales); stems glabrous or pubescent, often with raised lines of hairs decurrent from margins of petioles. Leaves opposite, becoming alternate and bract-like in inflorescence; petiolate or sessile; stipules absent; bracteoles absent. Inflorescences simple or branched racemes, panicles, spikes, or corymbs. Flowers 4-merous, often protandrous, with floral tube, producing nectar at base of style; sepals green or reddish green; petals obcordate or obtrullate, notched at apex, pink, rose-purple or white [rarely cream coloured or orange-red]; stamens 8, in two unequal whorls; pollen yellow, shed in tetrads; style erect, stigma entire or 4-lobed. Fruit an elongate, slender capsule, 4-locular, loculidical. Seeds many [rarely only 4], with terminal coma of silky hairs [coma rarely lacking]. 2n = 18, 20, 24, 26, 28, 30, 32, 36, 38, 60.</br></br>About 165 species: montane, boreal, and/or arctic regions of North and South America, Asia, Europe, Africa, and Australasia, from sea level to 5000 m, often in moist, disturbed places; 2 species in Thailand.</br></br>The genus is divided into seven sections; only Epilobium sect. Epilobium, in Thailand.</br></br>Careful gathering of ripe seeds and perennating structures, usually at or just below the ground surface, facilitate identification. The pattern of vestiture on stems, also extremely valuable for identification, is sometimes obscure on specimens collected very late in the growing season.

description: Herbs, perennial, erect or ascending, with fleshy soboles that leave loose brown basal scales; stems 15–90 cm tall, simple to well-branched, strigillose throughout, sometimes mixed with glandular hairs on inflorescence, lacking raised lines decurrent from petioles. Leaves subcoriaceous, lanceolate or elliptic to narrowly ovate, 1.5–5(–8) by 0.5–2.2(–3) cm, subglabrous with strigillose margin and midvein, base subcordate to cuneate, apex subobtuse to acute, margin sharply denticulate with 7–22 teeth on each side; lateral veins prominent beneath, 5–6 per side; petiole 0–4 mm. Inflorescence erect to slightly nodding. Flower sepals 4.5–6.5 mm, keeled; petals 7–11 mm, pink to rose-purple; stigma entire, clavate. Capsules 3.5–7 cm, strigillose and often glandular; pedicels 0.4–1.5 cm. Seeds 1–1.1 mm, dark brown, coarsely papillose, with short chalazal collar; coma white, detaching easily. Fl. Jul–Sep(–Oct), fr. Sep–Oct. 2n = 36.

description: Terrestrial (very rarely lithophytic), sympodial herbs producing erect leafy shoots from a wiry, rooting rhizome. Foliage leaves alternate, sessile, plicate. Inflorescences terminal on leafy shoots, racemose, lax, often secund; rachis pubescent; floral bracts herbaceous. Flowers resupinate, spreading to pendent, mainly greenish or yellowish (sometimes with purple to maroon suffusion or markings). Sepals and petals free; sepals more or less pubescent on the dorsal side. Labellum firmly attached, porrect, differentiated into hypochile and epichile. Column stout (less than 3 times as long as anther), without column foot; anther dorsal, elongated, versatile, yellow; pollinia 2, mealy, partly cleft, pyriform to clavate, devoid of caudicles; rostellum producing a diffuse viscidium, but no stipe; receptive part of stigma flat. Ovary and pedicel more or less pubescent, pedicel twisted through 180. Fruit a capsule dehiscing by 6 longitudinal slits.</br></br>A genus of c. 25 species with a natural distribution encompassing an area ranging from Europe and the Mediterranean through southern and eastern Asia to Japan and NE Russia, an area ranging from the southern corner of the Arabian peninsula to tropical Africa, and an area in western North America (besides, one species has colonized much of North America as a naturalized exotic); 1 species in Thailand.

description: Leafy shoots densely gregarious from a branched, creeping rhizome, 18–85 cm tall; stem bearing 2–3 cataphylls, 4–7 sheathing foliage leaves and 0–2 small, non-sheathing leaves. Foliage leaves ovate to elliptic or linear-lanceolate, acute to acuminate, 1.7–11.2 by (0.3–)0.5– 5.8 cm. Inflorescence 1- to 14-flowered; rachis flexuous, 3.5–21 cm long; floral bracts spreading to suberect, ovate to lanceolate or elliptic, acute to acuminate, 5–47 mm long. Flowers long pedicelled, wide-open, mainly greenish-yellow (sepals and petals often with maroon margins, labellum cream to pale yellow and often with orange to maroon markings/suffusion). Sepals shallowly boat-shaped; dorsal sepal lanceolate (to lanceolate-oblong), (sub)acute, 8–10.1 by 2.5–3.9 mm; lateral sepals obliquely ovate to falcately lanceolate, acute, 8.9–11 by 2.7–4.6 mm. Petals recurved (apices often meeting behind the dorsal sepal), lanceolate to oblong, obtuse to rounded, 7–9.4 by 2.3–3.8 mm. Labellum 8.3–9.8 mm long, 6.3–8.2 mm wide across side lobes when flattened; hypochile concave with 2 erect, obliquely oblong to subtriangular, rounded side lobes, in its proximal to middle part ornamented by 2 adjoining keels furnished with tiny orange warts and ending in 2 oblongoid calli; epichile elastically attached, broadly oblanceolate to oblong-subspathulate, obtuse to rounded, ornamented by 2 marginal ridges proximally and a small shiny drop-like callus just above the middle. Column 5.4–6.2 mm long; stigma with 2 low swellings at base. Ovary (including pedicel) slenderly fusiform, 11–17 mm long.

description: Terrestrial, mycohetrotrophic herbs with a horizontal corm; devoid of roots. Flowering shoots erect; stem hollow, fragile, glabrous, pale brownish-white. Leaves alternate, membranous, scale-like, sheathing (below) or non-sheathing (above). Inflorescence racemose, usually lax; floral bracts membranous, glabrous. Flowers resupinate or non-resupinate, pendent. Sepals and petals free, glabrous. Labellum with (at least partially) papillose ornaments, spurred at base. Column stout, glabrous, without stelids and column foot; anther subterminal, versatile; pollinia 2, granular, longitudinally furrowed, with filiform caudicles; receptive part of stigma flat. Ovary long-pedicelled, glabrous. Fruit a capsule dehiscing by 6 longitudinal slits; pedicel not elongating during fruit ripening.</br></br>A genus of 3–4 species distributed in tropical Africa and from Europe across Siberia to Kamchatka and Japan, further south through E and SE Asia to Malesia, NE Australia and the SW Pacific Islands (east to Fiji); 1 species in Thailand.

description: Corm ellipsoid (to oblongoid), 1.4–3.9 cm long, 0.6–1.9 cm in diameter. Flowering shoots 13–48 cm tall; stem 2–9 mm in diameter at base, 1–4 mm just below rachis; scale leaves 5–9. Inflorescence 3- to many-flowered; rachis 4–20 cm long; floral bracts lanceolate to ovate or broadly elliptic, obtuse to acuminate, 5–17.3 by 2–8.7 mm, entire. Flowers resupinate, not opening fully, translucently white, labellum sometimes with purplish markings. Sepals 3-veined from the base; dorsal sepal linear, rounded to subacute, 7.7–10.2 by 1.9–2.1 mm; lateral sepals narrowly linear-lanceolate, slightly oblique, obtuse to subacuminate, 8.4–10.6 by 1.7–1.8 mm. Petals linear-lanceolate, slightly oblique, rounded to subacute, 7.4–9.6 by 2.1–2.3 mm, 3-veined from the base. Labellum boat-shaped, ovate, at apex abruptly tapering into a broad, rounded to obtuse apiculum, 8.9–10.4 by 7.4–8.5 mm when flattened, more or less erose, ornamented by 2 longitudinal, papillose keels throughout its length and distally with a much shorter, papillose median keel; spur parallel to the ovary, cylindric to subclavate, rounded to slightly indented at apex, 3.1–3.6 mm long. Column incurved, 2.4–2.8 mm long; anther strongly vaulted, broadly elliptic-oblong in upper view, rounded to truncate in front, 1.8–2.2 mm long, releasing the pollinia directly onto the stigma. Ovary ellipsoid, 3.5–8.5 mm long; pedicel 1.5–9 mm long. Capsule ellipsoid, 5–8 mm long, 4–6 mm in diameter.

description: Moderate to very large, slender to very robust, secondary hemiepiphytic, evergreen lianes with abundant trichosclereids. Stem root-climbing or less often prostrate, usually producing long flagelliform shoots with reduced cataphylls and abundant clasping roots. Leaves several to many, distichous to spiro-distichous and often forming conspicuous tufts at the tips of active shoots; petiole long-channelled, pulvinate apically and basally; petiolar sheath long, marcescent to deciduous, sometimes decomposing to conspicuous net-fibrous mass; leaf blade lanceolate, elliptic, elliptic-oblong, entire, pinnatipartite or pinnatisect, rarely minutely perforate (E. pinnatum), often oblique; primary lateral veins pinnate, running into marginal vein, secondary and often tertiary venation parallel-pinnate, higher order venation and sometimes tertiary venation reticulate. Inflorescences 1(–5) in each floral sympodium; peduncle relatively short, sometimes obscured by a mass of netted fibrous degraded cataphylls; spathe boat-shaped, withering after anthesis, usually deciduous; spadix subcylindrical, conical, sessile or stipitate, shorter than spathe; flowers bisexual, the lowermost ones pistillate or sterile, perigone absent; gynoecium with ovary subtetragonal-prismatic- cylindrical, truncate, 1-loculate; ovules usually 2, more rarely 4 or 6–8, anatropous, funicle short, placenta parietal or near base of parietal partial septa; stylar region prismatic as broad or broader than ovary; stigma umbonate to oblong-linear and longitudinal. Infructescence comprised of a 1–8-seeded monsterocarp with stylar region deciduous at maturity, mostly ripening dull orange. Seed reniform, testa thickish, brittle, smooth, embryo curved, endosperm copious.</br></br>Approximately 15 species from Japan (Ryukyu Islands) to Australia (Queensland) and India (Manipur) to Oceania (Cook Islands: Rarotonga). Three species in Thailand, none endemic, one (E. auruem) adventive or seminaturalized as an escape from cultivation.

description: Very large root-climbing secondary hemiepiphyte to 16 m. Stem (adult) 5–40 mm diam., with prominent irregular whitish longitudinal crests, active portions of stem mid-green to pale yellow-green, sometimes with large obscure dull yellow to white variegations, depending on leaf variegation, older stems with distinctive matte to sub-lustrous orange-brown papery epidermis; flagellate foraging shoots common, arising high in the canopy and reaching the ground. Leaves scattered on lower stem, becoming clustered distally; petiole 19.5–50 cm by 3–15 mm, canaliculate, smooth, mid-green to rather bright yellow-green, apical and basal pulvini barely greater in diameter than petiole; petiolar sheath extending to mid-way along apical geniculum, at first submembranaceous, soon drying chartaceous and degrading to untidy, slightly netted weak fibres, then falling to leave a smooth, mid-brown scar; leaf blade 10–93 by 5–60 cm, entire (juvenile) to irregularly pinnatifid, ovate to elliptic in outline, sub-coriaceous, apex acute to acuminate, base moderately cordate, divisions pinnatifid to pinnatipartite; pinnae up to half the length of the lamina wide, apex truncate, dull to somewhat glossy mid-green, usually irregularly yellow or white variegated, rarely entirely mid-green; pinnae each with 1 (very rarely more except for the terminal pinna) compound primary lateral vein and several to rather many interprimary veins, individual elements of the compound vein diverging at ca 10° from various points along the pinna; interprimary and secondary venation mostly remaining sub-parallel to compound primary vein; higher order venation reticulate. Inflorescences almost never produced.

description: Large to gigantic root-climber, to 30 m. Stem 10–35 mm diam., glossy dark green, smooth, older stems mid-brown. Leaves evenly distributed but lower ones often falling and then leaves tending to become clustered towards stem apices; petiole 33–62.5 cm by 6–20 mm, canaliculate, dark green to slightly glaucous, smooth; apical pulvinus 20–25 by 5–12 mm, basal pulvinus 2–4 cm by 7–15 mm; petiolar sheath extending to half way along petiole, at first sub-membranaceous, soon drying scarious, later breaking into regular sections and falling to leave a somewhat roughened, mid-brown scar; leaf blade entire, oblong-elliptic, 5.5–100 by 8.5–48 cm, slightly falcate, coriaceous, glossy bright green, margins hyaline and becoming prominently reddish in exposed situations, apex acute to slightly acuminate, base unequal-rounded, one side often produced into a rounded to truncate posterior lobe; primary lateral veins parallel, barely or not differentiated from interprimary veins; interprimary veins very numerous, prominent, remaining parallel to primary vein. Inflorescence solitary, rarely two or more together; peduncle 5–8 cm by 4–10 mm. Spathe canoe-shaped, 16–33.5 by 5.5–14 cm when pressed flat, shortly but stoutly tapering, gaping at anthesis and then falling before anthesis is complete, exterior green, interior waxy-glaucous to dull yellow, smelling strongly of peanut butter; spadix 15.5–28.5 by 1.5–4.5 cm, sessile, cylindrical, bluntly tapering towards the apex, orange at anthesis; flowers 2.5–4 mm diam. across the style; ovary 3–10 by 2.5–4 mm, cylindrical-ellipsoid, basal part strongly compressed; stylar region 4–10 by 1.5–4 mm, acroscopic-trapezoid, robust, apex flattened; stigma 0.8–3 by 0.1–0.5 mm, linear. description: Large root-climbing robust secondary hemiepiphytes to 15 m. Stem 5–40 mm diam., lustrous green with prominent irregular greyish crests, older stems with distinctive matte to sub-lustrous pale brown papery epidermis. Leaves scattered on lower stem, becoming somewhat clustered towards stem apices; petiole 19.5–60 cm by 3–13 mm, canaliculate, dark green, smooth; apical pulvinus 16–70 by 0.3–0.5 cm, basal pulvinus 3–7 by 1–1.5 cm; petiolar sheath extending ⅓–¾ along petiole, rarely (poorly developed leaves) reaching apical pulvinus, at first membranaceous, soon drying chartaceous and disintegrating into untidy partially netted fibres, later falling to leave a smooth, mid-brown scar; leaf blade 10–93 by 5–60 cm, entire (juvenile plants) to regularly pinnate, ovate to elliptic in outline, sub-membranaceous, lustrous dark green, rarely slightly to intensely blue-green and glaucous above, apex acute to acuminate, base rounded to slightly cordate, divisions pinnatifid to pinnatisect, occasionally midrib ± naked at sinus; pinnae 1.2–6.5 cm wide, apex truncate to acute, terminal pinna shallowly sinuous, many individuals with minute to somewhat well developed pellucid dots especially adjacent to the midrib, pellucid dots often perforating and enlarging, sometimes extending to blade margin (then fenestrations often additional to fully developed pinnae); primary lateral veins 1 per pinna; higher order venation reticulate. Inflorescence solitary, rarely two or more together, at anthesis partially to almost completely obscured by netted fibres; peduncle 5.5–21.5 cm by 4–10 mm; spathe canoe-shaped, 7–23.5 by 3–15 cm when pressed flat, stoutly attenuate to 15 mm, gaping at anthesis and then falling before anthesis is complete, exterior green, later dull greenish yellow to mid-green, interior dull yellow (reported as white by some collectors) at anthesis; spadix 8.5–25 by 1.1–3.5 cm, sessile, cylindrical, bluntly tapering towards the apex, glaucous grey-green to greenish cream, dark yellow or greenish white at anthesis; flowers 3–7 mm diam., across the style; ovary 4–12 by 2–7 mm, cylindrical-ellipsoid, basal part slightly compressed; stylar region 3–7 by 1.5 4 mm, acroscopic-trapezoid, rather robust, apex flattened; stigma 2–6 by 0.1–0.5 mm, linear. Infructescence mid-green, rarely somewhat to prominently glaucous, stylar region greatly enlarged, transversely dehsicent, the abscission developing at the base of the massive stylar region and this falling to expose the ovary cavity full of orange pulp.

description: Epiphytic herbs with pseudobulbous stems, evergreen. Flowering shoots to 70 cm tall. Pseudobulbs adjacent, with several fibrous leaf sheaths. Foliage leaves normally 2 on the apex of the pseudobulb, plicate, perennial, lanceolate-elliptic, petiolate, present during flowering. Inflorescences erect, unbranched or branched, arising from the base of the leafy shoot, usually as long as or longer than the foliage leaves; floral bracts persistent. Flowers few, medium-sized or large, resupinate, strongly veined with red or brown. Dorsal sepal free, hood-like; lateral sepals spreading, basally connate to form a short mentum together with the column foot. Petals free, reflexed. Labellum simple, spurless, without ornaments, mobile. Column with a prominent column foot, glabrous; anther incumbent, versatile, with 8 pollinia in 2 groups of 4.</br></br>A monotypic genus distributed in the eastern Himalayas, Myanmar, Thailand, Vietnam and SW China.

description: Terrestrial, rhizomatous herbs; the creeping stem-like rhizome rooting from its nodes. Flowering shoots terminal, erect from a decumbent base, 15–46 cm tall. Foliage leaves 3–7, scattered to crowded on the lower part of the stem, petiolate; petiole channelled, sheathing at base. Inflorescence spicate; bracts glandular-pubescent on the dorsal side. Flowers 5 to many, resupinate, predominantly reddish-green to yellowish-green with white epichile. Sepals free, 1- to 3-veined; dorsal sepal porrect over the column, 4.2–8 mm long. Petals connivent with the dorsal sepal, 1-veined. Labellum basally adnate to the column, straight (i.e., not twisted), differentiated into hypochile and epichile; hypochile with erect sides, entire, spurred (protruding below the bases of the lateral sepals when the flower is viewed from the side), spur devoid of ornaments or containing 2 clavate appendages; epichile simple, entire, recurved to reflexed, slightly narrower than the hypochile when spread out. Column straight (i.e., not twisted); stigma bilobed, flat; rostellum triangular, bifid; viscidium 1, naked; anther versatile; pollinia 2, basitonous. Ovary glandular-pubescent. Fruit a capsule, dehiscing by 6 longitudinal slits.</br></br>A genus of ca. 20 species distributed from Bhutan and southwestern China across tropical Southeast Asia and Malesia to Tonga in the Pacific; 2 species in Thailand.

description: Flowering shoots erect from a decumbent base, 15–46 cm tall; lower part of stem 2–4 mm in diameter. description: Terrestrial, achlorophyllous, mycoheterotrophic, climbing or scrambling herbs; aerial roots produced one at each node, short, fleshy, unbranched, used for attaching to the substrate; stems much branched, thin, cylindric, flexible, glabrous, pale brown to reddish-brown or yellowish-brown. Foliage leaves reduced to scale-like sheaths or bracts, one at each node, glabrous. Inflorescences terminal or lateral opposite the roots, racemes or panicles, many flowered, glabrous. Flowers not opening widely. Sepals free, fleshy, 5. to 7-veined, dorsal sepal arching forward. Petals free, 5-veined, narrower than the sepals. Labellum entire or obscurely 3-lobed, lateral margins rolled upward to form a floral tube around the column, with a longitudinal pubescent median ridge, both sides with many transverse ridges, base of midlobe with a woolly callus. Column with a short descending foot, tapering into the median ridge of the lip; pollen assembled in 2 firm pollinia without caudicles or viscidium. Ovary slender. Fruit a slender capsule. Seeds with stout testa and broad wings.</br></br>A genus of 2–3 species, distributed from Japan to Indo-China, NE India, Myanmar, Thailand, Peninsular Malaysia, Borneo, Sumatra, Java, the Philippines and E Australia; 1 species in Thailand.

description: Trees or shrubs, usually glabrous. Leaves alternate, often distichous. Flowers axillary, solitary or many in axillary fascicles or cymes, often heterostylous, a pair of bracteoles at base of each pedicel. Calyx campanulate, lobes imbricate in bud. Petals imbricate in bud, clawed, caducous, with a ligulate appendage on the inner face. Staminal tube usually toothed at apex. Ovary with 1ovule in single fertile locule. Styles free or connate. Drupe 1-seeded. Seed with a thin testa; endosperm variable in quantity or absent; embryo straight.</br></br>About 220 species, occurring throughout the tropics and subtropics, mainly in S. America. Three species are native to Thailand, easily recognised as belonging to Erythroxylum because of the distinct stipular scars on the branchlets.

description: Moderate to robust, clustering, spiny, hapaxanthic, polygamous, acaulescent palm. Stem subterranean, branching sympodially by basal (?axillary) suckers, internodes very short, usually covered by rotting leaf sheaths. Leaves pinnate, spirally arranged; sheath usually splitting opposite the petiole, unarmed at the very base, bearing black, flattened spines distally, and scales and branched hairs, sheath margin ligule-like distally; petiole well developed, adaxially deeply channelled in proximal portion, distally ± rounded in section, the abaxial surface sparsely to densely armed with black, scattered flattened spines; rachis armed as the petiole but more sparsely; leaflets single-fold, numerous, linear to lanceolate, entire, regularly arranged, bearing bristles along the main veins or the margins, and irregular bands of caducous indumentum, midribs prominent, transverse veinlets moderately conspicuous. Inflorescence system terminal, erect, branched, lateral inflorescences branched to 3rd order, subtended by reduced or by tubular, apiculate, spiny or unarmed bracts; branches of all orders bearing a tubular, 2-keeled prophyll, and terminating in a cupule of tightly sheathing bracts enclosing a flower pair; cupule bracts 11–13, flower pair consisting of a male and a large hermaphrodite flower. Male flowers shortly pedicellate; calyx tubular, coriaceous, striate, dull brown, with pointed lobes; corolla tubular in the basal ¼ to ⅓, distally with 3 narrow, elongate, woody, valvate lobes terminating in hard, sharp, spine-like tips; stamens 22–27; pistillode minute. Hermaphrodite flowers very similar in size and shape to the male, flattened on one side by pressure of the male flower in bud; gynoecium triovulate. Fruit ovoid, beaked, cupule bracts, calyx, and usually the corolla persisting; epicarp covered in irregular vertical rows of very small reflexed, fringed scales. Seed single, basally attached, seed coat thin, dry, endosperm homogeneous, hard; embryo basal. Germination remote-ligular; eophyll pinnate.</br></br>Six species in Peninsular Thailand to Peninsular Malaysia, Borneo. One species in Thailand.

description: Fiercely spiny acaulescent palm forming dense thickets of up to 12 individual stems in the forest undergrowth. Leaves 7–10 per mature shoot, up to 8 m long; petiole up to 3 m long, up to 5 cm diam. at the tip of the ligule, densely covered with irregularly arranged shiny black spines to 5 cm long, decreasing in size towards the petiole tip; rachis armed as the petiole; leaflets to 100 or more on each side of the rachis, regularly arranged, with abundant black bristles along the midrib, the longest leaflets to 90 by 2–4 cm. Inflorescence system terminal, shorter than the leaves, to 5 m tall, subtending leaves of lateral inflorescences gradually decreasing to bracts; ultimate branches terminating in cupules of 12–13 tightly imbricate brown striate unarmed bracts, enclosing a pair of flowers comprising a male and a hermaphrodite flower, the males of the inflorescence emerging first, followed by the hermaphrodite flower. Male flowers borne on a short pedicel, to 1 cm long, to 6 cm long, shiny brown; calyx to 2 cm, striate; petals to 6 cm, tubular at the base, distally split into 3 spine-tipped woody petals; stamens 22–27, anthers elongate, dangling at anthesis. Hermaphrodite flower similar to the male flower, but with an asymmetrically flattened tip in bud; gynoecium ovoid, tipped with conspicuous pyramidal stigma. Fruit at maturity 7–9 by 3–5 cm, beaked; epicarp scales brown, somewhat irregularly arranged; endocarp with 3 + 3 flanges penetrating the homogeneous endosperm.

description: Terrestrial, sympodial herbs with corms, a fleshy rhizome or pseudobulbs that are naked or covered with thin sheaths; autotrophic or mycoheterotrophic. Foliage leaves permanently absent in mycoheterotrophic taxa; in autotrophic taxa 1 to few per corm or pseudobulb, plicate or duplicate, deciduous, present or absent at the time of flowering; leaf bases usually forming a pseudostem. Inflorescence lateral, erect, racemose or paniculate, lax to moderately dense. Flowers resupinate, all or nearly all open at the same time. Sepals and petals free, more or less spreading, devoid of markings (at least on the dorsal side). Labellum firmly attached, not fused with column, saccate or spurred at base. Column glabrous, straight to slightly incurved, devoid of stelids; column foot flat or spurred, sometimes absent; anther subterminal, incumbent, versatile, usually with 2 small horn-like processes on top; pollinia 2, hard and bony, partly cleft; rostellum producing a strap-shaped, rounded to acute (rarely emarginate) tegule and a usually obtriangular to crescent-shaped or transversely linear viscidium; fertile part of stigma concave. Fruit a capsule dehiscing by longitudinal slits.</br></br>A genus of c. 230 species distributed in tropical and southern Africa, Madagascar, the Mascarenes, the Arabian peninsula, Indo-Malesia (with extensions to adjoining temperate parts of Asia), northern and western Australia, the SW Pacific islands and tropical America; 14 species in Thailand.
