description: Plant with pseudobulbs above ground (or partly buried). Pseudobulbs obliquely terete conical to (conical-)fusiform, 2.5–8 cm long, 1.3–2.9 cm in diameter. Foliage leaves 3–7, present at anthesis, leaf bases forming a 1–6 cm long pseudostem; free part of each leaf linear to narrowly lanceolate, acute to acuminate, (3–)5.5–20(–44.5) by 0.5–1.4(–1.9) cm. Inflorescence racemose,  (15–)24–74 cm tall, lax, 5- to many-flowered; peduncle green, 7.5–24.5 cm long; floral bracts shorter than ovaries. Flowers suberect to spreading, opening widely, mainly green to brownish-green (labellum white with green margins and maroon veins). Sepals acute to acuminate, sometimes mucronate; dorsal sepal linear to narrowly lanceolate, 11–16.2 by 1.2–3.7 mm; lateral sepals obliquely linear to (ob)lanceolate-linear, 12.2–18.6 by 1.5–3.8 mm. Petals obliquely (linear-)lanceolate, acute to acuminate, sometimes mucronate, 9–13.8 by 1.8–3.7 mm, glabrous. Labellum 3-lobed, 8–12.2 by 5–11.6 mm when flattened, widest across mid-lobe, spurred at  base, glabrous on the ventral surface; mid-lobe obovate to elliptic or suborbicular, rounded, margins undulate; ornaments of 3 entire to somewhat warty keels starting from the labellum base and terminating on the mid-lobe (lateral keels shorter than the median); spur subclavate, straight to slightly incurved, 3–4 mm long. Column 3–4.8 mm long; column foot subequal to column proper, not forming a spur. Ovary (including pedicel) 10–24 mm long. Capsule pendent, (ellipsoid-)fusiform, 2.5–2.9 cm long (excluding pedicel and perianth remnants), 1–1.4 cm in diameter.

description: Plant with underground corms. Corms fusiform to conical, 3.5–7 cm long, 1.3–3.2 cm in diameter. Flowers spreading, opening half-way or less, mainly rose-coloured to dark reddish-green or purplish-red (petals and labellum often whitish, labellum often with purplish veins and tinged yellow at centre); apochromic forms occur occasionally. Sepals acuminate; dorsal sepal (linear-)lanceolate, 17.3–30 by 4.5–7 mm; lateral sepals obliquely to falcately (linear-)lanceolate, 19.2–34 by 4–5 mm. Petals obliquely ovate to oblanceolate, obtuse to acute, 17.8–23 by 7–8.5 mm, glabrous. Labellum (oblong-) ovate to somewhat fiddle-shaped or weakly 3-lobed, rounded to retuse, 17–27 by 14–15 mm when flattened, spurless, glabrous on the ventral side, margins straight in proximal part, undulate in distal part; ornaments of 5–9 (often low) keels extending from the labellum base to near the apex where they are verrucose. Column 8–10 mm long; column foot subequal to column proper, forming a prominent, obliquely conical spur. Ovary (including pedicel) 14–29 mm long. Capsule not seen.

description: Terrestrial, achlorophyllous, mycoheterotrophic, climbing or scrambling herbs, often with stout, tuberous rhizomes; aerial roots produced one at each node, tendril-like, unbranched, used for attaching to the substrate; stems short- or long-branched, thick, cylindric, slightly fleshy, flexible, glabrous, reddish-brown in colour. Foliage leaves reduced to scale-like sheaths, one at each node, glabrous to furfuraceous. Inflorescences terminal or lateral, racemes or panicles, few-to many-flowered; rachis and flowers pubescent, covered with yellowish-brown hairs; bracts caducous or persistent. Flowers not opening widely, fleshy, yellowish or brownish. Sepals free, 5- to 9-veined, hairy outside, lateral sepals larger than dorsal sepal. Petals free, 3- to 7-veined, slightly smaller than the sepals, glabrous. Labellum concave, fleshy, with papillae inside, base with or without a prominent callus. Column short and stout, straight or curved forward, without foot, dilated at apex; pollen assembled in two cleft mealy pollinia without caudicles or viscidium. Ovary slender. Fruit a slender capsule. Seeds large, winged, with stout testa.</br></br>A genus of about 10 species, distributed from Madagasgar to NE India, Myanmar, S China, Japan, Indo-China, Thailand, Peninsular Malaysia, Borneo, Sumatra, Java, the Philippines and New Guinea; 2 species in Thailand.

description: Terrestrial, achlorophyllus, mycoheterotrophic herbs; rhizome horizontal, tuberous, fusiform to oblong; roots arising from neck between rhizome and aerial stem, filiform; aerial stem erect, with a few scale-like sheaths near base, leafless. Inflorescence terminal, racemose; floral bracts small. Flowers resupinate or non-resupinate. Sepals forming a tubular synsepal, often verrucose outside; distal part shallowly 3-lobed; the 2 anterior lobes separated by a deep sinus. Petals apparently attached on the sinus between dorsal and lateral sepals, usually smaller than sepals (and therefore, in reality, fused with sepals for almost their entire length). Labellum attached to apex of column foot and free from sepals and petals or attached on the sinus between lateral sepals, without spur, usually ornamented by 2 calli near base, often with thickened median  band-like keels or calli distally. Column elongate, winged distally, with a pair of tooth-like stelids at apex, with a distinct column foot; anther born on a filament, incumbent, subquadrate, more or less retuse; pollinia 2, granular, without caudicles; stigma shield-like, born on a raised projection at base of column; rostellum porrect, transverse, producing a suborbicular viscidium. Fruit an erect capsule; pedicel elongating rapidly during fruit ripening.</br></br>A genus of c. 65 species distributed from NE India through E Himalaya, S China, Taiwan, Japan, E Siberia and SE Asia to E Australia and the SW Pacific islands; also in tropical Africa, Madagascar and the Mascarenes; 6 species in Thailand.

description: Corms triangular-ovoid, 4–4.5 cm long, 3–3.5 cm in diameter. description: Epiphytic or terrestrial, autotrophic herbs. Stems elongate, often branching. Foliage leaves many per shoot, distichous, sheathing at base; sheath glabrous or hairy, smooth or verrucose; lamina duplicate, sometimes nearly terete. Inflorescence a subsessile, strongly condensed, 1- to many-flowered raceme, when young enveloped by a transparent, sometimes hairy or verrucose spathe. Flowers resupinate or not. Sepals and petals free, except for the lateral sepals that are often connate at base (rarely also connate with the dorsal sepal). Labellum adnate to proximal part of column, spurred or saccate at base, devoid of ornaments or with a transverse callus at base of the flat part. Column stout, straight to slightly incurved; column foot solid or absent; anther subterminal, incumbent, versatile; pollinia 4, solid, with connate caudicles; rostellum not producing a stipe, but sometimes a diffuse viscidium; receptive part of stigma concave. Ovary glabrous or hairy. Fruit a capsule, circular to triangular in transverse section, dehiscing by longitudinal slits.</br></br>A genus of c. 100 species distributed in Sumatra, Java, Sulawesi, Philippines, Maluku, New Guinea and the SW Pacific islands (east to Samoa), and with isolated records from Thailand and Laos; 1 species in Thailand.

description: Terrestrial, rhizomatous herbs; the creeping stem-like rhizome rooting from its nodes. Flowering shoots terminal, erect from a decumbent base, 5–103 cm tall. Foliage leaves 2–11, scattered along the stem or crowded on its basal to middle part, petiolate; petiole channelled, sheathing at base. Inflorescence spicate or racemose; bracts glabrous, ciliate, fimbriate or glandular-pubescent on the dorsal side. Flowers 2 to many, resupinate. Sepals free, 1- to 3-veined; dorsal sepal 2–16.2 mm long. Petals adherent or adnate to the dorsal sepal, occasionally connate at apex, 1-veined, glabrous. Labellum basally adnate to the column, straight (i.e. not twisted), 1.5–12.8 mm long, simple or 3-lobed with porrect to recurved apex; the concave to saccate basal part with tufted or scattered fleshy hairs inside. Column straight (i.e. not twisted), subclavate to subterete); stigma bilobed, flat or with raised margins; rostellum triangular, bifid; viscidium 1, naked; anther versatile; pollinia 2, basitonous. Ovary (glandular-)pubescent to glabrous. Fruit a capsule, dehiscing by 6 longitudinal slits.</br></br>A genus of ca. 100 species, distributed throughout most of North and Central America and Eurasia to northern Queensland and the western Pacific islands, and across the Indian Ocean to Madagascar and Mozambique: 8 species in Thailand.

description: Medium-sized to very large, robust epiphytic, rarely lithophytic or terrestrial herbs. Roots stiff, acuminate, branching, of two types: erect catch-roots that trap detritus, and normal spreading roots. Stems clustered, pseudobulbous, either (1) very elongate, very fleshy and many-leaved, covered in leaf-sheaths or (2) rather short and thick, sometimes of a single node, ovoid, conical or shortly fusiform, not covered in leaf-sheaths, distally few-leaved. Leaves distichous, plicate, long and narrow, flexible, tough and coriaceous, acutely articulated to short sheathing base. Inflorescences lateral, simple, erect, horizontal or pendulous, a laxly many-flowered raceme, flowers mostly open simultaneously; floral bracts triangular, acute, often fleshy and concave, persistent. Flowers resupinate, medium-sized to large, often showy, long-lasting, yellow, variously marked with brown or maroon. Sepals and petals spreading, similar, oblong, sometimes concave, usually obtuse; lateral sepals sometimes falcate. Labellum much smaller, 3-lobed, fused at the base to the base of the column, usually hairy; disk ornamented by 2 or 3 ridges. description: A large epiphytic or rarely terrestrial herb, often forming a large clump. Pseudobulbs clustered, erect at first then pendent, stem-like, cylindrical, many-noded, leafy in the apical part, dull yellow, 3–7 m long, c. 5 cm in diameter. Leaves several, arranged in 2 rows, linear, acute, 50–100 by 3 cm, drooping from the base when older. Inflorescences up to 2 m or more long, densely many-flowered, bearing a few well-spaced, distorted, sterile flowers near the base; peduncle stout, cylindrical, up to 1.6 cm in diameter; bracts somewhat reflexed, linear-lanceolate, acute. Flowers almost flat, large, up to 10 cm across; sepals and petals pale or greenish yellow, heavily spotted with maroon-brown, the labellum yellow with red-brown veins on the side lobes and red-brown marks on the mid-lobe; sterile flowers fragrant, with 2 sepals and petals but lacking a labellum and column. Sepals spreading, elliptic-spathulate, obtuse or rounded, 40–55 by 16–20 mm. Petals spreading, elliptic, obtuse, 40–55 by 22–26 mm, with somewhat undulate lateral margins. Labellum 3-lobed, lacking a spur, 25–30 mm long; side lobes erect, curved over the column, obliquely semi-circular-rounded, pubescent on veins; mid-lobe slightly deflexed, ovate, obtuse, 10 mm wide, pubescent on veins; disk ornamented by 3 short ridges. Column 14–20 mm long, with an outgrowth on each side at the base, joined to the base of the labellum to form a saccate hollow. Pedicel and ovary 4–10 cm long, off-white.

description: Almost always terrestrial, deciduous, tuberous herbs, mostly glabrous. Flowering shoots (5–)10–80(–150) cm tall, unbranched. Foliage leaves one to several, basal or cauline, lanceolate, elliptic or ovate. Usually with one to several sterile bracts above the foliage leaves, their margins often short-hairy. Inflorescence terminal, racemose. Flowers few to many, small, medium-sized or rarely large, resupinate in the Thai species, predominantly white to green, rarely yellow, pink or red; often fragrant. Sepals free; dorsal sepal concave and almost always erect in the Flora area, often forming a hood with the petals; lateral sepals spreading or reflexed. Petals entire or bilobed. Labellum 3-lobed or rarely entire, sometimes basally clawed; spur long or short, clavate, slender or saccate, very rarely absent. Column short; anther erect or somewhat reflexed, thecae mostly adjacent and only rarely separated by a wide connective, mostly with narrow basal extensions termed anther canals, pollinia 2, sectile; stigmas as freely projecting short or elongate stigmaphores; rostellum 3-lobed, central rostellum lobe insignificant or rarely prominent. Ovary glabrous or papillose, mostly indistinguishable from the pedicel. Fruit a capsule, dehiscing by six longitudinal slits.</br></br>A genus of ca. 600 species, distributed throughout the tropics and subtropics of the world, predominantly found in grassland or savanna, less commonly in densely forested habitats; 45 species in Thailand.</br></br>Notes: A more comprehensive version of this account was published in Thai Forest Bull., Bot., special issue: 7–105. 2009.

description: Flowering shoots  57–65 cm tall, glabrous below, with elongate papillae and stout branched or grouped hairs above. Sterile bracts 4–6, lanceolate, acuminate, 2.5–5.7 cm long, suberect or spreading, margins sometimes shortly hairy. Sepals subacute or obtuse; dorsal sepal erect, suborbicular, 2.5–3 by ca. 3 mm; lateral sepals recurved, with a false apex pointing downwards, 11–14 by 4–6 mm, united with the dorsal sepal and the labellum base.  Petals triangular, obtuse, forming a hood with the dorsal sepal, ca. 3 by 1.7 mm.  Labellum 28–32 mm long, 3-lobed above the united 4–4.5 mm long base; midlobe terete, to 28 mm long, irregularly spiralling; side lobes 6.7–9.3 mm long; spur with a wide mouth followed by a narrower part and a globular distal portion, 6–7 mm long.  Column ca. 2 mm tall; anther canals 10–12 mm long.  Ovary (including pedicel) 20–25 mm long, beaked, with very elongate papillae and stout grouped hairs.  Capsule not seen.

description: Flowering shoots glabrous, 10–25(–42) cm tall. description: Small, slender, seasonally dormant, rarely evergreen, weakly laticiferous herbs to 35 cm tall. Stems tuberous and/or stoloniferous, tubers small, depressed-globose to somewhat irregular, stolons comparatively robust. Leaves 1-few together; petiole terete, slender; petiolar sheath very short, its protective role taken over by the subtending prophyll or cataphyll; leaf blade cordate-sagittate, sagittate or hastate, mid-green, sometimes paler green or silver-grey variegated; primary lateral veins pinnate or mostly arising at petiole insertion, forming an arching submarginal collective vein, 1–2 marginal veins also present; higher order venation reticulate. Inflorescence 1–2 in each floral sympodium, with sympodia often enriching and thus several inflorescences together, appearing with leaf in seasonally dormant species or with new shoot activity in evergreen species; peduncle subequal or longer than petiole, slender; spathe slender, not distinctly constricted; lower spathe very slender, persistent, tightly convolute around pistillate flowers; spathe limb oblong-lanceolate, erect to reflexed and ± revolute at anthesis, briefly marcescent; spadix subequal or longer than spathe, slender; flowers unisexual, perigone absent; pistillate flower zone adnate to spathe, 2–7-flowered, ± biseriate, separated from staminate flower zone by short sterile zone; pistillate flowers with gynoecium oblong to lageniform, 1-locular, ovule 1, placenta parietal to subbasal (morphologically basal); stylar region very short; stigma subcapitate; staminate flower zone subulate to cylindrical, fertile to apex (not in Thailand) or with free or fused synandria at the apex, or with a long, terminal appendix (the last not in Thailand); staminate flower a 3-androus peltate synandrium, truncate, hexagonal, elongated in sense of spadix axis, shallow, stipitate, connective strongly dilated; thecae short, subglobose, remote, almost pendent from margin, dehiscing by pores. Synandria lower ones very few, ± remote, apiculiform, upper ones few, consisting of tiny, peltate synandrodes. Fruit an ellipsoid to globose berry, style persistent, pericarp thin, 1-seeded, white. Seed ellipsoid, testa smooth, very thin, embryo large, ellipsoid, light green, endosperm absent</br></br>Eight species distributed from Myanmar to SW China (Yunnan), south to N Borneo (Sarawak, Brunei). Four species in Thailand, one (H. kerrii) endemic. All Thai species are frequently (but not obligately) associated with limestone.</br></br>The cordate leaves are superficially similar to those of several Typhonium species, with which Hapaline shares reticulate venation, but differs by being laticiferous and by the synandriate staminate flowers, and an appendix (where present) clothed with synandrodia. The pistillate flower zone in Typhonium is hemispherical to conical-cylindrical while that of Hapaline comprises a single longitudinal row of pistillate flowers on a spadix axis adnate to the lower spathe.

description: Slender, tuberous, deciduous herb to 30 cm high. description: Glabrous shrub with clustered stems, up to 2 m tall; stems greenish brown, 0.5–1 cm diam., woody part 2–3 mm thick; pith spongy, white. description: Terrestrial herbs with underground tubers; stem glabrous. Foliage leaves 1(–2), basal. Inflorescence spicate; bracts much smaller than the foliage leaves, much shorter than the flowers. description: Minute to very large, solitary to clustering, erect to decumbent, less often creeping, usually strongly aromatic, evergreen mesophytes, rarely rheophytes, very rarely helophytes. Leaves mostly spirally arranged, sometimes with conspicuous reddish extrafloral nectaries; petioles terete to D-shaped in cross-section, lower part sheathing, almost always with a pulvinus mid-way along, rarely terminal at the leaf blade insertion; petiolar sheath persistent to marcescent; leaf blade simple, cordate to oblanceolate, glabrous; venation striate. Inflorescences several together; spathe persistent until maturation of fruit, boat-shaped or constricted into a lower convolute portion and distally a variously opening spathe limb, exterior smooth or externally ribbed and keeled along the dorsal midline, apex apiculate to strongly mucronate; spadix with pistillate and staminate flower zones occasionally separated by a naked to staminode-bearing interstice, and staminate part often secreting reddish to brown resin prior to or during anthesis; pistillate flowers each associated with a single staminode, rarely not (not in Thailand); ovary with style extremely short; stigma button-like to discoid, sometimes weakly lobed; staminate flowers 2–4androus; filaments very short; anthers opening by short apical longitudinal slits concealed, or not, by an expanded connective forming a flat cap. Infructescences pendent during development and at maturity, fruits contained within the persistent and often enlarged lower spathe; fruiting spathe dehiscent from the base upwards, usually the spathe circumscissile at the insertion of the peduncle then splitting into a few irregular strips and these curling upwards to reveal the ripe fruit; fruit a many-seeded, small, translucent, greenish berry, smelling of overripe fruit or butyric acid.</br></br>Homalomena is one of the most abundant, speciose and least well understood mesophytic aroid genera in tropical Asia. Furthermore, it is now becoming the focus of interest for pharmaceutical research into the terpenoids and flavonoids occurring in all tissues; such studies require a sound basis of taxonomic understanding.</br></br>The lack of a reliable taxonomy is owing to many factors, not least the poor state of preservation of many of the historical types coupled with the cryptic nature of most of the systematically significant characters, notably the presence, absence and disposition of sterile flowers and the generally large and complex vegetative structures that do not lend themselves readily to traditional herbarium vouchering methods. Another factor is the brief anthesis period which means that even well-prepared herbarium specimens are frequently useless to taxonomists because many significant structures on the inflorescences deliquesce soon after flowering or are damaged by the most frequent inflorescence visitors, chrysomelid beetles, before preservation.</br></br>At least 250 species, well over half yet to be described, occurring from Indo-Malaya to SW China eastwards through tropical Australasia as far as western Oceania (Solomon Islands) with major centres of diversity in Sumatra, Borneo and New Guinea.</br></br>Seven species in Thailand with an eighth, new species known (and included in the key) from material not suitable for formal description. This total is decidedly provisional as the genus is very poorly collected. It is conceivable that the true number of indigenous species is a dozen or more. Several exotic species are cultivated as ornamentals in the Kingdom, including neotropical H. wallisii and H. crinipes.

Inflorescences 1–5 together; peduncle 1–2.5 cm; spathe oblong-lanceolate, ca 2.5 by 0.5 cm, apex long-acuminate to rostrate, ca 4 mm long, spathe barely opening at anthesis and then soon closing, medium to pinkish green; spadix cylindrical, ca 1.7 by 0.3 cm, shorter than spathe, stipitate; stipe ca 2 mm long, obliquely inserted onto spathe base; pistillate flower zone ca 5 by 2 mm; ovary depressed ovoid-globose, ca 1 mm diam., without associated staminodes; staminate flower zone ca 1 cm by 2 mm; staminate flowers each with two stamens, ca 2 mm diam., white. Fruits depressed globose, ca 1.5 by 1 mm, ripening greenish white.

description: Moderate to large, robust, strongly aromatic (mango resin), stemless to erect to decumbent-stemmed herb to 1 m. Stem erect, later decumbent, 1–3 cm diam., usually covered with leaf bases for the terminal half, older portions naked or with semifibrous petiole and cataphyll remains. Leaves several together; petioles up to 45 cm long, pale to mid-green to deep red, with darker longitudinal streaks to ca 1.5 cm long; petiolar sheath 7–11cm, margins membranous, persistent, often darker coloured or red when petiole green; leaf blade ovate-sagittate, 15–45 by 10–22 cm, base sagittate, the sinus very wide (up to ca 7 cm) but shallow, apex acute, with a ca 2 mm tubular mucro, coriaceous, mid-green above, paler green to deep red below, drying distinctively dark brown; venation of posterior costae with ca 4 primary lateral veins arising more or less together, anterior costa with 5–9 primary lateral veins and a similar number of finer, interprimary veins diverging from the midrib at 30°–45°; secondary venation striate. Inflorescences 1–7 together; peduncle 10–18 cm, erect (developing and floral) to declinate (after anthesis and fruiting), coloured as for petioles; spathe oblong, 8–14 cm long; spathe limb gaping at anthesis, then closing again and persistent into fruit, greenish white internally, yellowish to medium red-white externally, usually with darker spotting on the base and dorsal surfaces associated with extrafloral nectaries; spadix tapering-cylindrical, 8–13 cm, barely exceeding spathe, short stipitate; stipe ca 2–4 mm, pale green; pistillate flower zone ca.3 by 1 cm, weakly fusiform; ovary depressed ovoid-globose, ca 1 mm diam., with an associated, very slender-stalked, globose-clavate topped staminode equalling the height of the ovary; ovary very pale green; stigma capitate, sessile, equalling the ovary diam., pale yellow-white, staminode ivory; staminate flower zone 5.5–6 cm by 1 mm, tapering fusiform; staminate flowers 4–5-androus, rhombohexagonal in plan view, ca 3 by 2 mm, overtopped by a large connective, ivory white, lowermost flowers sterile. Fruits ovoid, pale green, ca 3 mm diam.

description: Terrestrial, rhizomatous herbs; the creeping stem-like rhizome rooting from its nodes. Flowering shoots terminal, erect from a decumbent base. Foliage leaves scattered along the stem, petiolate; petiole channelled, sheathing at base. Inflorescence spicate; bracts ciliate, sparsely pubescent on the dorsal side. Flowers resupinate. Sepals free, 3- to 4-veined. Petals connivent with the dorsal sepal. Labellum basally adnate to the column, straight (i.e., not twisted), differentiated into hypochile and epichile; hypochile forming a subspherical sac that is hidden by the lateral sepals when the flower is viewed from the side; epichile linear-lanceolate, sulcate. Column straight (i.e., not twisted); stigma bilobed, flat, sometimes subtended by two small digitate appendages; rostellum linear-triangular, bifid; viscidium 1, naked; anther versatile; pollinia 2, basitonous. Ovary glandular-pubescent. Fruit not seen.</br></br>A genus of ca. 10 species. The distribution is mainly Malesian, reaching peninsular Thailand in the west, the Philippines in the north and the Solomon Islands in the east; 1 species in Thailand.

description: Small, solitary or caespitose, acaulescent or stemmed, understorey palms. Stems to 4 m tall, conspicuously ringed, with or without stilt roots at base, variously tomentose. Leaves regularly to irregularly pinnate or undivided and conspicuously pinnately ribbed, apically entire or bifid, variously tomentose; sheaths marcescent and not forming a crownshaft or rarely abscising neatly and forming a crownshaft; petiole present or lacking; pinnae single- or several nerved, margins parallel or diverging, tips praemorse, undivided blades with toothed margins. Inflorescences interfoliar or infrafoliar if crownshaft present, solitary, spicate or branched to 1 or 2 orders, erect initially, spreading or pendulous in flower and fruit; peduncle nearly lacking to very long; prophyll tubular, short, first peduncular bract attached just above prophyll and usually greatly exceeding it; rachis usually much shorter than peduncle; rachillae few, rarely exceeding 20, slender to moderately robust, glabrous or tomentose.</br></br>Iguanura includes 33 species from southern Peninsular Myanmar and middle Peninsular Thailand to Peninsular Malaysia, Borneo and Sumatra. description: Normally terrestrial pseudobulbous herbs. Pseudobulbs ovoid and irregularly swollen, adjacent, usually underground. Foliage leaves 1 or 2 on top of the pseudobulb, plicate, erect, linear-lanceolate, puberulous, petiolate, absent during flowering (at least in the only species known from Thailand). Inflorescences erect, arising from the base of the pseudobulb, puberulous; sterile bracts present, sheathing; flower-bearing part racemose, few-flowered; floral bracts  persistent. Flowers large, mostly golden-yellow in extra-Thai species, greenish-brown with  purple markings in the Thai species. Sepals free; dorsal sepal hooded over the column; lateral sepals spreading. Column slender, more than 10 mm long, straight or apically forward-curved, puberulous, with a prominent column foot; anther incumbent, versatile, with 8 clavate pollinia. description: Flowering shoots 12–18.5 cm tall. Pseudobulbs conical, 3‒4.5 by 2‒3.4 cm. description: Acaulescent to shortly trunked palms, solitary. Stem procumbent, usually subterranean. Leaf entire, diamond-shaped, large and often trapping litter; sheath tubular, disintegrating into fibrous mesh; petiole armed along the edges with small spines; hastula barely visible as a dead strip of tissue at petiole-blade transition; blade with prominent subpinnately ribbed costa, proximal margins armed like petiole, distal margins with alternating long and short indentations. Inflorescence interfoliar, short, often partly covered by litter, branched to 1–5 orders; prophyll densely tomentose, peduncular bracts up to seven; rachis shorter than peduncle; rachillae 3–6. description: Small to moderate-sized tree palm, solitary, dioecious, pleonanthic. Stem usually covered by the persistent remains of leaf bases. Leaves palmately divided, induplicate; sheath splitting cleanly to the base opposite the petiole, with caducous woolly indumentum; petiole long, channelled adaxially, unarmed; hastula conspicuous adaxially, abaxially absent; blade thin, divided along adaxial ribs into short single-fold segments, transverse veinlets conspicuous. Inflorescence solitary, interfoliar, emerging from a cleft in the subtending leaf, cream-coloured, rachis longer than peduncle, first order branches subtended by conspicuous, shortly tubular bracts, distally with triangular limb; male inflorescence eventually arching, branched to 4 orders, with numerous condensed rachillae; female inflorescence erect, branched to 2 orders, more robust and with fewer rachillae than the male. Male flowers with stalk-like corolla base, six free stamens and no pistillode; female flowers as the male, but larger, with empty anthers and a large 3-lobed gynoecium. Fruit 1(–2) seeded, globose; epicarp minutely and irregularly warty, mesocarp thick and spongy; endocarp thin; endosperm shallowly ruminate. description: Trees or shrubs, resting buds with cataphylls. Leaves usually pubescent at first, often becoming glabrous, entire or dentate. Plants monoecious. Inflorescence lateral or terminal, usually cymose, paniculate or fasciculate, pedicels usually thickening distally into the receptacle. Male flowers smaller than the females, with a minute apical opening surrounded by 2–4 decussate pairs of tepals; androecium usually with 4 large outer stamens and up to 4 smaller inner stamens or staminodes that may be rudimentary and ± connate; anthers opening by a single slit, with a filament or subsessile. Female flowers with a minute apical opening surrounded by about 5 decussate pairs of tepals; the inner pairs thickened and glandular; the upper half of the receptacle falling off as a calyptra after anthesis; carpels numerous, stigma almost sessile on the apex of the ovary. Drupes sessile or stipitate. </br></br>According to Philipson’s synopsis of Kibara, the genus comprises 43 species in the Malesian region, most of them in New Guinea. One species is known from Thailand.

description: Understorey tree to 20 m tall, 24 cm diam., rarely a scandent shrub. Leaves opposite (rarely subopposite or whorled), broadly ovate to elliptic oblong, 9–35 by 5–24 cm, coriaceous or chartaceous, base cuneate, rounded or subcordate, apex shortly to long acuminate, margin entire or minutely to coarsely dentate, glabrous or sparingly to rather densely pubescent beneath, midrib and principal lateral veins prominent beneath, lateral veins arched-ascending and meeting within the margin; petiole 5–25 mm, channelled above, glabrous or pubescent. Plants monoecious. Inflorescences axillary, terminal, or cauliflorous, pubescent, cymes solitary or several arising at the same node, varying from simple 3-flowered cymes to complex pleiochasia. Flowers on the lower branches; rachis and lateral branches of female part of the inflorescence stout and becoming woody after anthesis, those of the male parts finer and caducous, up to 20 cm long but often much shorter, pedicels 15–30 mm, gradually thickening below the flowers, those of the male more delicate than those of the female. Male flowers globose, 1.5–2 mm broad, only slightly wider than the pedicel, pubescent; tepals 6–8, apex rounded, usually with 4 outer stamens and up to 4 smaller inner stamens, filaments strap-shaped. Female flowers globose, ca 3–5 mm across; tepals ca 6, with swollen pendulous glands within the ostiole; carpels usually ca 20, stigma short, obtuse. Infructescence enlarged, woody, receptacle ca 20 mm diam., turning yellow-orange at maturity. Drupes ovoid, 15 mm long, shortly stipitate or sessile, blue-black at maturity.

description: Slender to robust, clustering, high-climbing, hapaxanthic, hermaphrodite rattans, frequently with stems branching in the forest canopy. Leaf sheaths without knee, variously armed; ocrea very conspicuous, variously armed, tubular and sheathing, expanded, net-like, inflated and forming an ant chamber; petiole absent to well developed; cirrus present; leaflets rather few ± regularly arranged, usually diamond-shaped, sometimes lanceolate, but always with the upper margins jaggedm praemorse, the leaflets often joined to the rachis on a short stalk, the lower surface of the leaflet frequently covered in indumentum. Inflorescences produced in the axils of the uppermost reduced leaves, branching to produce usually pendulous catkin-like flower-bearing branches, each covered with a tight or loose spiral of bracts; rachilla bracts each subtending a single hermaphrodite flower usually embedded in a mass of hairs; sepals 3, joined at the base; petals 3, much longer than the sepals, joined at the base to form a short tube; stamens 6, rarely 7, borne on the petals; ovary with sharp pyramidal stigma and rows of scales. Fruits tipped with the remains of the stigmas and often bearing the remains of the corolla surrounding the stigma; scales brownish, arranged in neat vertical rows; inner fruit wall fleshy, sweet. Seed with thin, non-fleshy testa; endosperm ruminate or homogeneous. Seedling leaf simple or forked with jagged upper margins.</br></br>Twenty seven species in Indo-China to New Guinea. Leaves (sub)opposite, decussate, or alternate (distichous), subsessile or petiolate; stipules absent or rudimentary. Inflorescences terminal or axillary, paniculate (or raceme-like), lateral branches cymose; bracts small, caducous. Flowers often showy, glabrous or hairy, 5–7(–9)-merous, actinomorphic (see note); calyx tube campanulate or turbinate, leathery, smooth or with broad or narrow ribs or ridges, at base gradually or ± abruptly narrowed into a shorter or longer stipe (pseudopedicel); calyx lobes (sepals) 6–9, (long-)triangular, sometimes subtended within by a line-shaped annulus; epicalyx appendages (auricles) alternating with calyx lobes, small or prominent, or absent; petals 6–9, pink, purple or white, narrowly clawed; stamens 15–100 or more, inserted inside at halfway or near base of calyx tube, exserted, dimorphic in most species: 6(–11) solitary in front of calyx lobes with thick filaments and larger anthers, the rest in clusters in front of petals with thin filaments and small anthers, rarely monomorphic, then all filaments thin, subequal; ovary sessile, (largely) free from calyx tube, globose or ellipsoid, 3–6 locular; style long-exserted; stigma small, capitate. Fruit a dry, hard capsule, at base more or less adnate to the base of the calyx tube, calyx tube including calyx lobes persistent, globose or ellipsoid, glabrous or (partially) hairy, loculicidally dehiscent, 4–6-valved, apex rounded or pointed. Seeds numerous, flattish, obpyramidal, with wing from raphe; cotyledons convolute.</br></br>About 55 species: tropical and subtropical Asia to Australia, north to Japan; 18 species in Thailand of which 2 endemic: L. huamotensis, L. subangulata, and 1 introduced: L. indica.

description: Trees (4–)10–30 m tall; bark smooth or with pustules, pale grey (tabaek) when young but roughly blackish fissured (salao) when older. Flowers: bud extremely short-hairy, obovoid, shortly nippled at apex, 10–15 mm long, pseudopedicel ca 1 mm long; calyx tube distinctly 6–9-ridged, ridges 0.5–1.5 mm wide, at apex confluent into auricles, calyx lobes (6–)7–9, minutely hairy in upper part within, 6–8 mm long; petals purple, blade broadly elliptic, 10–15 mm long, margin entire, somewhat undulate, claw 6–10 mm long; stamens radially dimorphic (6 or 7 outer stamens longer than numerous inner ones); ovary glabrous. description: Clump- and colony-forming, stoloniferous, evergreen, prickly helophytes. Stem thick, aculeate or unarmed, decumbent, green, epigeal or submersed, internodes relatively long or short. Leaves several together; petiole long, aculeate, weakly pulvinate apically, petiolar sheath relatively short; leaf blade sagittate to hastate-sagittate when juvenile, adult leaf blade deeply pinnatifid in anterior division, posterior divisions pedatifid, sometimes simple, adult blade rarely entire, or bipinnatifid (the last not in Thailand) with major veins aculeate on lower surface; primary lateral veins pinnate in anterior division, pedate in posterior divisions, primary lateral veins of each pinna forming submarginal collective vein in pinnatifid leaves, or running into marginal vein in simple leaves; higher order venation reticulate. Inflorescence solitary; peduncle subequal to petiole, aculeate; spathe linear, very long and narrow and opening only basally (L. spinosa) or broader and opening terminally (not in Thailand), very thick and spongy, spirally twisted or not, marcescent or deciduous, basal part enclosing spadix, gaping at anthesis, or remaining closed and the spathe gaping terminally; spadix shortly cylindrical, obtuse, sessile; flowers bisexual, perigoniate; tepals usually 4, more rarely 6, hooded; stamens 4(–6), free; filaments broad, connective slender; thecae ellipsoid, dehiscing by longitudinal slits; gynoecium ovoid to ellipsoid; ovary 1-locular; ovule 1, anatropous, funicle very short, placenta apical; stylar region well developed, shortly attenuate to cylindrical; stigma discoid-hemispherical. Fruit a quadrangular, apically densely muricate to spinose or smooth (the latter not in Thailand) 1-seeded berry, green or dull purple when ripe. Seed large, compressed-obovoid, testa thin, brown, hard, somewhat rugose, embryo large, somewhat curved.</br></br>Two species of medium to moderately large, prickly helophytes with mostly compound leaves and long-persistent inflorescences. One species in Thailand, frequently persisting in disturbed areas as a result of local use as a green vegetable.</br></br>Immediately distinctive by almost all vegetative parts prickly, it is the only Thai indigenous aroid so armoured, although related genera (Cyrtosperma and Podolasia) occur in Peninsular Malaysia. The prickly green fruits are also diagnostic.

description: Terrestrial, achlorophyllous, mycoheterotrophic, rhizomatous herbs; rhizome J-shaped; aerial stem simple or branched, thin, brittle, with sheaths, black, dark purple or brown. Foliage leaves reduced to triangular, scale-like sheaths or bracts. Inflorescences erect, terminal on the new shoot or lateral on the old stem, few- to many-flowered, opening in succession with one or two opening at a time. Flowers not opening widely. Sepals  free, 5- to 7-veined, glabrous. Petals free, 3- to 5-veined, glabrous. Labellum entire or 3-lobed, typically adnate along its margin to the base of the column forming a short tube, rarely free; disc covered with multicellular hairs, giving the distal part of the labellum a bearded appearance. Column elongate, with a pair of small wings on each side of the anther; pollen forming two friable masses. Ovary slender, with a cup-like denticulate calyculus at apex. Fruit a capsule, with persistent calyculus at apex. Seeds slender, with lateral micropyle and small testa cells.</br></br>A genus of ca. 20 species, distributed from Japan to Indo-China, NE India, Bhutan, Myanmar, Thailand, Peninsular Malaysia, Borneo, Sumatra, Java, the Philippines and New Guinea; 5 species in Thailand.

description: Flowering shoots 20–65 cm tall, erect, dark purple to black, 3–4 mm in diameter at base, branched; nodes with sheaths; sheaths glabrous, ovate, 3–5 mm long, acute, coriaceous, base amplexicaul. Inflorescence glabrous; rachis 1.5–4 cm long, 3- to 15-flowered; bracts ovate, glabrous, 0.5–1.5 by 1–1.5 mm, margin membranous. Flowers long-pedicelled, green to light brown. Sepals glabrous; dorsal sepal oblong-oblanceolate, 6–11 by 1.8–3 mm, 7-veined, apex hooded: lateral sepals oblong, 5.5–11 by 1.5–2.5 mm, 5-veined, apex hooded and apiculate. Petals glabrous, oblong, 5.5–10 by 2–3 mm, 3-veined. Labellum entire, rarely obscurely 3-lobed, 6–10 mm long along the mid-line, free from the column, 5-veined, major veins branched above; side lobes (if present) indistinct, not exceeding the column; midlobe oblong-oblanceolate, 2.5–3 mm wide, hooded, margin irregularly erose, with a small median hairy band. description: Small rosette plants to moderate sized shrubs, solitary or caespitose. Leaf palmate; petiole usually elongate, armed along the margins, spines gradually decreasing in size towards the blade; blade rarely undivided or divided to the base into a number of wedge-shaped segments, all sessile or middle segment rarely with a petiolule. Apices of individual segments dissected by a mixture of long indentations, leading to the adaxial (upper) ribs and short indentations leading to the abaxial (lower) ribs. Inflorescence interfoliar; peduncular bracts and rachis bracts tubular; number of partial inflorescences (first order branches) 1–7, spicate or branched, decreasing in size towards the distal nodes. Flowers hermaphrodite and protandrous, inserted in groups or solitary; stamens 6, fused to the corolla basally, the filaments distally free or connate and forming a cuplike structure. Fruit one-seeded ripening from green to red, globose and less than 1 cm diam.; endocarp thin and bony; endosperm homogeneous. Germination remote-tubular.</br></br>About one hundred and thirty five species from India to Vanuatu. Thirteen species and one variety in Thailand.

description: Caespitose palm, with up to 7 m tall stems. Stem 5–7 cm diam. Leaf sheath to 40 cm long, with ligule up to 10 cm long in young leaves; petiole up to 2.5 m long, ranging in colour from greenish-brown to orange brown, basally armed with 0.2–0.3(–0.5) cm long rounded spines, straight or curved, evenly sized, inserted more or less regularly; lamina divided into 8–12 more or less equal, 47–88 cm long segments, the middle one with 6–8 adaxial ribs, split to 8–15 cm above the base in two truncate lobes, the remaining ones with 2–7 adaxial ribs, indentations leading to the adaxial folds 2–3 cm long, those leading to the abaxial folds c. 0.5 cm long. Inflorescence 1.5–2 m long, with 6–7 partial inflorescences; peduncle 25–50 cm long, prophyll 25–30 cm long covered with a mixture of ferruginous ramenta and stellate hairs; peduncular bracts 1–2; rachis bracts splitting cleanly at the apex in a few irregular sized teeth 0.5–1 cm long; partial inflorescences with 4–8 rachillae; longest rachillae 12–20 cm long. Flowers up to 150 on one rachilla, mostly solitary but also in cincinni of 2–3, sessile; floral subtending bract to 0.5 mm long, deltoid; buds 0.25–0.3 cm long; calyx c. 0.2 cm long, glabrous, almost truncate apically, with three short, pointed teeth; corolla 0.25–0.3 cm long, drying striate, glabrous, erect, greenish; androecium 0.15–0.18 cm long, staminal ring 0.3–0.5 mm high, filaments filiform 0.1–0.2 mm long; anthers 0.4–0.5 mm long; ovary c. 0.1 cm long, glabrous, turbinate, truncate apically, filling about half the lumen inside flower, locules three times longer than wide, central in each carpel, style slender, filiform, c. 0.1 cm long, not overtopping the anthers. Fruit globose, 0.6–0.8 cm diam.

description: Solitary palm. Stem usually less than 2 m tall, c. 10 cm diam., often covered by old, black spine-like leaf bases. Inflorescences up to 3.5 m long, with about seven, spicate, pendent, partial inflorescences; peduncle to 1.2 m long; prophyll 35–40 cm long; peduncular bract one, 33–36 cm long, covered with scattered minute ramenta, green to dry and woody distally, splitting irregularly, often with narrow rim of fibrous mesh; basal 2nd order rachis on up to 15 cm long bare basal portion and a 35–55 cm long flower-bearing portion. Fruit ellipsoid, 1.2–1.9 by 0.9–1 cm.

description: Caespitose palm, 4–8 stemmed, individual stems up to 2.5 m tall, 2.8–3 cm diam. below the crown and with 0.5–1 cm long internodes. description: Licuala pitta is similar to the widespread L. spinosa in its caespitose habit and its overall leaf morphology. It differs from that species, however, by the inflorescences being presented among the leaves, the leaf segments converging basally in a funnel-like manner, the fewer and shorter flowering rachillae and the flowers being almost twice as long. Licuala pitta is reminiscent of L. taynguyensis Barfod & Borchs. (Barfod & Borchsenius 2000) from Vietnam but that species is solitary, and has much larger inflorescences, with zig-zag rachillae that bear fewer, rather large and densely long-haired flowers.

description: Solitary or caespitose palm, usually with one, up to 5 m tall stem, suckering at the base, 3–5 cm diam., covered by leaf sheath remnants distally. Leaf sheath 30–40 cm long, with ligule up to 15 cm long in young leaves; petiole 80–150 cm long, basal ¼ with up to 0.4 cm long spines; lamina divided into 9–11 segments; middle segment with 9–11 adaxial ribs, 40–55 cm long, the remaining segments decreasing gradually in width towards the base, here with 3–4 adaxial ribs, 30–45 cm long; indentations of middle and lateral segments leading to the adaxial ribs c. 1 cm long, those leading to the abaxial ribs c. 0.5 cm long, indentations of basal segments more irregular. Inflorescence 1–1.5 m long, with 5–7 unbranched partial inflorescences; peduncle 20–30 cm long; prophyll 20–30 cm long, loosely fitting, splitting irregularly to tattering apically; peduncular bract lacking; rachis 80–120 cm long; proximal rachis bracts 25–29 cm long, tubular, loosely fitting, inserted up to 40 cm below the divergence point of the partial inflorescences subtended; basal partial inflorescence 8–15 cm long, displaced above or hidden inside subtending bract, strongly zig-zagged to straight, narrowly diverging from rachis, densely covered with felt-like indumentum of stellate hairs. Flowers up to 40–60 on longest rachillae, solitary, rarely in pairs, sessile, subtended by c. 0.6 mm long, sparsely hairy, deltoid bracts; buds 0.7–0.9 cm long, bullet-shaped, often with a more or less oblique base; calyx to 0.7 cm long on longest(abaxial) side, basally covered with patches of ferruginous ramenta, to striate distally when dried, with 3 obtuse to rounded lobes up to 0.5 mm long; corolla c. 0.6 cm long, with minute ferruginous ramenta on exposed parts, erect at anthesis, yellow-greenish on lower ¾ and brown distally; androecium 0.25–0.3 cm long, fused to corolla for 0.1–0.15 cm, filaments to 0.1 cm long, narrowly deltoid; anthers elongate, 0.22–0.24 cm long, pointed apically; ovary c. 0.15 cm long, obovoid, tapering distally, locules in lower ½ to ¾; style slender, c. 0.15 cm long, stigma amidst the anthers. Fruit 0.9–1.2 cm diam., globose.

description: Solitary, acaulescent palm. Stem short subterranean. Leaf: petioleto 90 cm long, scarcely armed in basal 10 cm, spines c. 0.2 cm long, recurved and set more or less regularly 1 cm apart; lamina divided into 3–4 gently curved segments, converging basally in a funnel-like fashion, middle segment c. 32 cm long, with 19 adaxial ribs, slightly curved lateral margins, rounded apically and c. 12 cm wide, the remaining segments 15–20 cm long, with 2–5 adaxial ribs, narrowly wedge-shaped to linear, obliquely truncate apically; indentations leading to the adaxial folds c. 0.5 cm long in middle segment, to 2 cm long in remaining segments, those leading to the abaxial folds less than 0.5 cm long. Infl orescence patent, shorter than leaves, c. 30 cm long, with 2–3 partial inflorescences; peduncle c. 18 cm long; prophyll loosely sheathing; peduncular bracts absent; rachis c. 12 cm long; basal rachis bract c. 8 cm long, inflated in distal half; partial inflorescences spicate, inserted up to 8 cm above the mouth of their subtending bracts; rachillae up to 8 cm long, 0.1–0.2 cm diam., rigid, straight to slightly zig-zagged, narrowly diverging from rachis, densely covered with deciduous ferruginous felt-like hairs. Flowers in groups of up to 5(–7) on slightly swollen tubercles (prominent in fruiting specimens), solitary towards the apex; calyx cylindrical, 0.26–0.32 cm long, chartaceous, covered with scattered 0.4–0.7 mm long simple hairs, splitting neatly into three pointed lobes; corolla c. 0.25–0.32 cm long, rather thick, covered with patent white hairs in upper two thirds, glabrescent towards the base, lobes c. 0.2 cm long with acuminate apex; androecium with c. 0.5–0.7 mm long, truncate staminal ring; filaments filiform, c. 0.3 mm long; anthers reniform, c. 0.5 mm long; ovary 1–1.5 mm long turbinate to club-shaped, densely covered with coarse silky white hairs mostly on upper parts, style filiform, 0.1 cm long. description: Solitary palm, rarely suckering. Stem to 1 m tall, 1.7–2 cm diam., smooth, inconspicuously ringed. Leaf sheath 5–8 cm long on older leaves, with ligule up to 10 cm long; petiole 15–30 cm long, basally with few, scattered spines to 0.1–0.2 cm long; lamina thin chartaceous, often with a crumpled appearance, unevenly divided into 4–5 segments, with convexly curved lateral margins and converging basally in a funnel-like fashion; middle segment entire, with 13–14 adaxial ribs, 15–20 cm long, the remaining segments with 3–5 adaxial ribs, 15–77 cm long; indentations leading to the adaxial folds to c. 1.2 cm long, those leading to the abaxial folds c. 0.4 cm long. Inflorescences 15–34 cm long, patent to pendulous, spicate to furcate; peduncle c. 25–30 cm long; prophyll 17–22 cm long, inflated, with 6 cm long split along one side; peduncular bract lacking; rachis sinuous, almost glabrous; single rachis bract 2–5 cm long, loosely sheathing at the apex, inserted c. 3 cm above prophyll, sparsely covered with stellate hairs, splitting cleanly along one side; partial inflorescence spicate or branching near the apex of the subtending bract into two, 3–5 cm long rachillae, covered with simple, whitish to golden hairs. description: Caespitose palm, with up to 4 m tall stems forming large clumps. Individual stems 4–5 cm diam., ringed by leaf scars. Leaf sheath to 40 cm long, with ligule up to 10 cm long, in younger leaves with dense cover of ferruginous to hyaline ramenta; petiole variable in length up to 2.5 m in fully developed leaves, armed almost to the distal end, armature variable but usually quite noticeable; lamina divided into 15–19 segments, 44–72 cm long; the middle segment sessile or with a petiolule to 6 cm long, with 5–9 adaxial ribs, the remaining ones with 1–3 adaxial ribs, indentations leading to the adaxial folds 1–4 cm long, those leading to the abaxial folds 0.5–1 cm long. Inflorescence 0.9–2.5 m long, extended above the crown, with 5–9 partial inflorescences; peduncle 20–50 cm long, for a large part hidden in prophyll; prophyll 20–30 cm long, covered with patches of ferruginous ramenta; peduncular bracts absent or present; rachis bracts dark green to brown distally, tubular, similar to the prophyll in texture and hair-covering, splitting irregularly into up to 2.5 cm long teeth or disintegrated apically; partial inflorescence inserted 2–6 cm above mouth of subtending bract, covered with dense, puberulent tomentum of simple, ferruginous to hyaline hairs; rachillae 2–7; longest rachilla 20–40 cm long. description: Tall palm trees, solitary, hermaphrodite or occasionally functionally dioecious (Australian-New Guinean species). Stem erect, ringed, basally with persistent leaf bases. Crown more or less globose, with skirt of dead leaves. Leaf palmate to costapalmate, induplicate; petiole elongate, armed along margins, usually with robust spines; adaxial hastula conspicuous, abaxial hastula poorly developed to absent; blade splitting along adaxial ribs, usually into single-fold segments. Inflorescence interfoliar; branched to 4 orders; peduncle elongate, peduncular bracts lacking or one; rachis longer than peduncle; rachis bracts loosely tubular like the peduncular bract; partial inflorescences (first order branches) 3–9, decreasing in size towards the distal nodes. Flowers inserted in groups of 3–6; stamens 6, fused to the corolla basally forming a cuplike structure; gynoecium united apically in slender style. Fruit one-seeded, greenish-blue, leaden blue to purple at maturity, globose to elliptical, more than 1 cm long; epicarp smooth, mesocarp fleshy; endocarp bony. Seed with homogeneous endosperm penetrated by an intrusion of the seed coat. Germination remote-tubular.</br></br>Twenty five species in NE tropical Africa, S Yemen, Bangladesh to Japan and Australia. Three species in Thailand.

description: Lithophytic, rhizomatous herbs; the creeping stem-like rhizome rooting from its nodes. Flowering shoots terminal, erect from a decumbent base. Foliage leaves petiolate; petiole channelled, sheathing at base. Inflorescence spicate; bracts ciliate, otherwise glabrous. Flowers resupinate. Sepals free, 1-veined; dorsal sepal 7.7–10.4 mm long. Petals connivent with the dorsal sepal, 1-veined, glabrous. Labellum basally adnate to the column, twisted, 8.5–11.5 mm long, differentiated into hypochile, mesochile, and epichile; hypochile saccate (but not protruding below the bases of the lateral sepals when the flower is viewed from the side), sac inside with 1 slightly bilobed appendage on either side; mesochile devoid of lateral flanges; epichile simple, entire. Column twisted in opposite direction to the labellum, clavate; stigma bilobed, flat; rostellum triangular, bifid; viscidium 1, naked; anther versatile, bright yellow; pollinia 2, basitonous. Ovary white, pubescent. Fruit a capsule, dehiscing by 6 longitudinal slits.</br></br>Monotypic, distribution as for the species (see below).

description: Flowering shoots (6–)9–28 cm tall. Inflorescence broadly cylindric to secund, lax, pubescent; rachis (0.8–)1.7–9 cm long; bracts suberect to spreading, boat-shaped, (triangular-)ovate, acuminate, shorter than or subequal to the ovaries, 1-veined, 7–15 by 4.3–9.5 mm. Petals falcately (linear-) lanceolate, obtuse to rounded, 8–10.8 by 1.6–2.5 mm. Labellum sometimes indented along the mid-line of the hypochile; mesochile channelled, entire; epichile transversely rectangular, 3.2–3.3 times wider than long. Column porrect (more or less continuing the line of the ovary), 4–7 mm long; anther caudate in front, 4–4.5 mm long. Ovary 8–16.5 mm long. Capsule suberect, short-pedicelled, fusiform, pubescent, 1.2–1.6 cm long, 0.3–0.6 cm in diameter.

description: Herbs, shrubs, or rarely small trees; stems glabrous or pubescent, erect to prostrate and then often rooting at nodes, sometimes floating, underwater parts often swollen and spongy or with inflated white spongy pneumatophores. Leaves alternate (or opposite, not in Thailand), usually entire; stipules present, often deciduous. Inflorescences terminal spikes or racemes, pedicellate or sessile; bracteoles 2, at or near base of ovary, or absent. Flowers perfect, actinomorphic, in upper leaf axils or in spikes, racemes, or clusters; floral tube not prolonged beyond ovary; sepals (3 or)4 or 5(–7), green, persistent after anthesis; petals as many as sepals or absent (not in Thailand), yellow or white, caducous; stamens as many or twice as many as sepals; anthers versatile or sometimes basifixed; pollen shed in monads, tetrads or polyads; ovary with as many locules as sepals, rarely more, apex flat or conical, often with a depressed nectary surrounding base of each epipetalous stamen; stigma capitate or hemispherical, entire or lobed, distal ½–⅔ receptive. Fruit a capsule, obconic, obovoid, cylindrical or globose, dehiscent irregularly or by a terminal pore or by flaps separating from valve-like apex. Seeds numerous, in one to several rows per locule, free or embedded in powdery or woody endocarp, raphe small or conspicuous, sometimes equal in size to body of seed. 2n = 16, 32, 48, 64, 80, 96, 128.</br></br>Eighty-two species; cosmopolitan, except Antarctica; 6 species in Thailand.

description: Herbs, perennial with creeping or floating stems, rooting at nodes, with white, erect, short (1–3 cm), spindle-shaped pneumatophores in clusters at nodes of glabrous floating stems to 400 cm; terrestrial stems 20–60 cm, much branched, tips ascending, densely villous on branches. description: Terrestrial (rarely epiphytic), rhizomatous herbs; the creeping stem-like rhizome rooting from its nodes. Flowering shoots terminal, erect from a decumbent base. Foliage leaves petiolate; petiole channelled, sheathing at base. Inflorescence racemose. Flowers non-resupinate. Sepals free, more or less boat-shaped, obtuse to rounded; dorsal sepal 5–5.5 mm long. Petals connivent with and adherent to the dorsal sepal, 1-veined, glabrous. Labellum basally adnate to the column, twisted, ca. 5 mm long along the mid-line, differentiated into hypochile, mesochile and epichile; hypochile saccate (not protruding below the bases of the lateral sepals when the flower is viewed from the side), sac inside with 1 cylindric-clavate appendage on either side; mesochile flat; epichile simple, entire. Column twisted, irregularly subterete; stigma bilobed, flat; rostellum linear-triangular, bifid; viscidium 1, naked; anther versatile; pollinia 2, basitonous. Ovary glandular-pubescent. Fruit not seen.</br></br>A genus of ca. 10 species. The distribution is mainly Malesian, reaching peninsular Thailand, Vietnam and the Philippines in the northwest and Vanuatu in the east; 1 species in Thailand.

description: Flowering shoots 20–39 cm tall. description: Tree ca 20 m tall; branchlets reddish brown or greyish tomentose or glabrescent. Leaves mostly spirally tufted at the ends of branchlets or scattered; lamina coriaceous, obovate or elliptic, 4–9 by 2–4.5 cm; apex obtusely acuminate; base cuneate, decurrent; upper surface sparsely short appressed hairy or glabrous; lower surface sparsely short appressed hairy; midrib grooved above, minutely crested, rounded below; secondary veins 10–13 on each side, looped; tertiary veins reticulate; petioles 1–1.5 cm long, grooved at apex, rounded and thickened at base, with appressed hairs, glabrescent; stipules triangular, 3 by 1–2 mm, reddish brown tomentose outside, glabrous inside, caducous. Flowers 1–2 in axils of leaves or fallen leaves; pedicels angular, 2–2.3 cm long, tomentose. Sepals 4, reddish brown tomentose except for a glabrous basal part inside; outer sepals ovate to broadly ovate, 7.5 by 5–7.5 mm; inner sepals broadly ovate or orbicular, 7.2–8 by 5.8–6.5 mm, with membranous, glabrous, fimbriate margin. description: Trees or shrubs; branchlets glabrous or pubescent. description: Shrubby, acaulescent to short-stemmed, clustering palms. Leaf palmate, induplicate; sheath disintegrating into long persistent, coarse fibres; petiole elongate, unarmed; adaxial hastula distinct, triangular, shallow, with erose margin, abaxial hastula obscure; blade splitting for half to two thirds their radius along the adaxial ribs into numerous, single-fold segments, these shallowly indented at the tip. Inflorescence interfoliar; branched to 1–3 orders; peduncular bracts 1–3; rachis bracts tubular with triangular limbs. Flowers small, hermaphrodite or unisexual, inserted in groups of 2–3 or solitary; stamens 6, fused to form a shortly epipetalous, staminal tube; gynoecium of three free carpels, shortly united basally, hairy distally, with triangular styles. Fruit one-seeded, globose to ellipsoid, less than 1 cm diam.; epicarp silky hairy in young stages; mesocarp thin, fleshy; endocarp poorly developed. Seed with homogeneous endosperm, intrusion of the seed coat lateral and shallow. Germination remote; eophyll very narrow, strap-shaped.</br></br>Three species in Peninsular Thailand to Peninsular Malaysia. Two species in Thailand.

description: Small, terrestrial, rhizomatous herbs: the creeping stem-like rhizome rooting from its nodes. Flowering shoots terminal, erect from a decumbent base. description: Small to moderate sized, solitary or clustering, monoecious palms. Stem slender with green internodes and distinct leaf scars at least distally, basally often with cone of adventitious roots. description: Epiphytic or lithophytic herbs; rhizome stout, creeping; roots fibrous. Pseudobulbs close together, ovoid-cylindric to conical, sheathed. description: Terrestrial, rhizomatous herbs; the creeping and ascending stem-like rhizome rooting from its nodes, internodes green, dark green or purple with brown spots or bands. description: Flowering shoots 15−25 cm tall, internodes 2−4 by 0.3−0.5 cm, green with brown spots or bands. Foliage leaves 1−3, crowded on upper part of stem, pink or purplish, sometimes with pale red spots or bands on upper surface, pink, dark purple or green on lower surface; petiole  2−3 cm long; lamina ovate with more or less cordate and often oblique base, acute or acuminate, 4−10 by 2−6 cm. Inflorescence spicate, oblongoid, laxly 8- to 15-flowered; peduncle 5−6 cm long; rachis 3−5 cm long, floral bracts ovate-lanceolate. Flowers short-pedicelled to subsessile, drooping, green to greenish-yellow. Sepals glabrous, similar in shape and size, oblanceolate, 7−8 by 2−3 mm, green at base and yellowish or yellowish-green at margin with 3 dark green streaks, margin straight, apex curled down or slightly reflexed. Petals more or less similar to sepals, oblanceolate, 8−9 by 2−3 mm, glabrous, green at base and yellowish or yellowish-green at apex with 3 dark green streaks, margin straight, apex slightly reflexed. Labellum 9−10 by 4−5 mm, differentiated into a channelled hypochile and a more or less flat epichile, yellowish or yellowish-green; hypochile finely pubescent in 2 more or less confluent rows and with hairy margins; epichile ornamented by a tuft of high fat papillae; spur globular, dark green. Column 3−5 by 2−3 mm; anther c. 2 by 2 mm. Ovary c. 5 by 1 mm. Capsule 1.5−2 by 0.5−1 cm.

description: Small to medium-sized terrestrial herbs. Tuber globose, corm-like, few-noded. Stem giving rise to an inflorescence and a leaf in succession, the subterranean portion producing lateral runners during the leafing period. Runners slender, producing daughter tubers at apex. Leaf solitary; leaf lamina horizontal, held flush with or well above ground level, cordate, orbicular, reniform or elliptic, palmately veined, membranous or fleshy, glabrous or pubescent, base cordate, apex acute, obtuse, or rounded, borne on a short or elongate petiole-like stalk. Inflorescence erect, terminal, slender or stout, usually slightly fleshy, glabrous; peduncle with 1 to several tubular sheaths, elongating during fructification in 1-flowered species; rachis 1-, 2- or several-flowered. Flowers resupinate or not, erect or nodding. Sepals and petals free, similar, linear-lanceolate, oblanceolate or elliptic. Labellum distinctly or obscurely 3-lobed or occasionally simple, glabrous or pubescent, sometimes with a central ridge, base sometimes shallowly saccate (or spurred in some African species), apex entire or fimbriate. Column parallel to labellum, elongate, clavate, not winged; anther terminal, incumbent, helmet-shaped, 2-locular; pollinia 2, cleft, sectile, mealy; caudicles absent; viscidium reduced; rostellum broad, sometimes reduced or absent; stigma shield-shaped to orbicular. Fruit dehiscing by 6 longitudinal slits.</br></br>A genus of c. 70 species occurring in tropical and southern Africa, the Cape Verde Islands, Madagascar and the Mascarenes, the Arabian Peninsula (Yemen), S Asia, the Himalayas and southern China, Taiwan and western Japan, continental SE Asia, the Philippines, Malaysia, Indonesia, Papua New Guinea, tropical Australia and the SW Pacific islands; 10 species in Thailand.

description: Tuber white-cream to beige, 12.5–32.6 mm in diameter, 3- to 5-noded. Flowers resupinate, nodding, opening widely; pedicel 1.2–4.9 mm long; ovary 2.3–7.8 mm long, distinctly ridged. Sepals and petals yellowish-green, often with purple venation, narrowly elliptic to linear-oblanceolate, 3-veined, apex acute; sepals (11.2–)14–22.2 by 2–4 mm; petals (10–)12.6–21.5 by 2–3.8 mm. Labellum pale yellowish-green flushed white above the middle, with purple-mauve, brown or green venation, oblong, obovate or rhombic, (10.3–)12–17.5 by 4.1–11 mm, 3-lobed above the middle; lateral lobes loosely embracing the column, ovate to triangular, 1.8–2 by 2–2.8 mm, apices acute; mid-lobe triangular, ovate or sub-quadrate, 2.6–5.5 by 3–7.4 mm, entire, apex acute; labellum ornamented by sparse to dense villous hairs along the main veins or in a central band. Column pale yellowish, sometimes flushed mauve, arching, 6.5–9.2 mm long; anther 1–2 mm in diameter; pollinia c. 1.5 mm long; rostellum protruding; stigma shield-shaped. Inflorescence 8.1–14.5 cm long, 1-flowered; peduncle 1.8–2 mm in diameter, bearing 3 or 4 tubular sheaths; floral bract oblong-ovate, 4.6–5.9 by 1.7–2.2 mm, apex acute. Sepals and petals brown or red-purple with maroon flecks outside, ochre inside, oblong-elliptic or elliptic-obovate, apex acute; sepals 18–24.5 by 4.6–5.2 mm; petals 18.7–25 by 4.1–4.7 mm. Labellum lilac-purple sometimes with sparse white mottling, white along the central ridge, spathulate, 20.7–25 by 8.8–12.3 mm, 3-lobed below the middle, saccate at the base; lateral lobes rolled upwards and embracing the column, triangular-ovate, 1.6–2.1 mm long, apices acute; mid-lobe orbicular, 11.6–12.5 by 11–12.3 mm, margin entire but slightly undulate, apex truncate-rounded or slightly emarginate; labellum ornamented by a central ridge that extends almost to the apex of the mid-lobe, the ridge pubescent below the lateral lobes, glabrous elsewhere. Column white flushed purple, clavate, straight, 9.5–11.5 mm long; anther c. 2 mm in diameter; pollinia c. 2 mm long; rostellum protruding; stigma shield-shaped, raised. Capsule not seen.

description: Creeping, moderate sized palm, monoecious. Stem prostrate to subterranean, branching dichotomously, distinctively stepped by curved leaf scars; crown of few large, erect leaves. Leaf sheath splitting cleanly to the base, glabrous; petiole elongate, wide and channelled above proximally to rounded in cross section distally, unarmed; blade pinnately divided into numerous, regularly distributed, single-fold, reduplicate pinnae; individual pinnae coriaceous, apically acute, with prominent midrib bearing large, brown bifurcating ramenta, transverse veinlets inconspicuous. Inflorescence protogynous, interfoliar, erect, branching to 4-6 orders; peduncle elongate; prophyll, peduncular bract and rachis bracts tubular, splitting longitudinally, leathery brown; rachis shorter than peduncle; female flowers gathered in a single terminal head (rarely more), male rachillae borne on third to fifth order branches below, at male anthesis often overtopping the terminal head of female flowers; female flowers densely inserted on club-shaped apex on the inflorescence; perianthparts free; staminodes lacking; carpels three, free, much longer than perianth; asymmetrically urn-shaped with more or less lateral, funnel-shaped stigmatic opening; male flowers densely inserted on catkin-like rachillae, perianth similar to female flowers; stamens three, filaments and connective connate into a common stalk; pistillode lacking. Fruits aggregated in head-like structure, compressed and irregularly angled; epicarp smoooth; mesocarp fibrous; endocarp thick; endsosperm homogeneous. Germination adjacent, viviparous seedling eventually detached from mother plant by elongating plumule.</br></br>One species in Sri Lanka to Ryukyu Islands and Caroline Islands. Introduced and naturalized (invasive?) in West Africa, South America, Central America and the Caribbean.

description: Terrestrial, rhizomatous, sometimes mycoheterotrophic herbs; the creeping stem-like rhizome rooting from its nodes. Flowering shoots terminal, erect from a decumbent base, 4–40 cm tall. Foliage leaves (if present) 3–11, scattered along the stem or somewhat crowded, petiolate, sheathing at base. Inflorescence spicate; bracts glabrous, (erose-)ciliate or papillose to (glandular-)pubescent on the dorsal side. Flowers 1 to many, resupinate or non-resupinate. Sepals free or lateral sepals connate at base, 1- to 3-veined; dorsal sepal 4.5–16 mm long. Petals adherent to the dorsal sepal. Labellum basally adnate to the column, straight or twisted, 7.7–19 mm long along the mid-line, differentiated into hypochile, mesochile, and epichile; hypochile saccate (but not protruding below the bases of the lateral sepals when the flower is viewed from the side), often containing a low median keel and 1 stalked appendage on either side; mesochile with one or two pairs of entire to pectinate lateral flanges; epichile bilobed or simple and rounded-truncate. Column straight or twisted; stigma bilobed to bipartite, flat; rostellum triangular, bifid; viscidium 1, naked; anther versatile; pollinia 2, basitonous. Ovary glabrous to (glandular-)pubescent. Fruit a capsule, dehiscing by 6 longitudinal slits.</br></br>A genus of ca. 40 species distributed from the Himalayas and Japan across tropical Southeast Asia, Malesia and the Pacific islands (northeast to Hawaii); 8 species in Thailand.

description: Tall, clustering, monoecious palms. Individual stems slender, naked and ringed by scars, armed with robust spines below the crown, these usually eroded towards the base on old stems. Leaf sheath tubular forming a well defi ned crownshaft, densely covered by hairs and spines of varying lengths; petiole robust, armed similarly to the sheath in hair covering and armature; blade pinnately divided into numerous, single-fold, regularly arranged, reduplicate, apically acuminate pinnae, lacking spines. Inflorescence protandrous, infrafoliar, erect in bud to pendulous at anthesis, branching to 2 orders; peduncle short; prophyll coriaceous, with dense hair covering, more or less spiny; single peduncular bract similar to prophyll but more sparsely armed; rachis longer than peduncle; first order branches numerous to few, pendulous; rachillae basally with protandrous triads of one central female flower and two lateral male flowers, distally with solitary or paired male flowers. Flowers sessile, cream white; male flower slightly longer than female flower, with 6–9(–12) free stamens, elongate anthers and strongly reduced pistillode; female flower with highly reduced staminodes. Fruit globose, dark blue to black; epicarp smooth; mesocarp thin, fleshy, without fi bres; endocarp thin, crustaceous, with basal operculum. Seed with deeply ruminate endosperm. Germination adjacent ligular.</br></br>Five species in Sri Lanka to the Philippines. Two species in Thailand.

description: Tall solitary, monoecious palm. Stem naked, conspicuously ringed by leaf scars distally, unarmed. Leaf sheath deeply split, fibrous along margins, not forming a crownshaft; petiole variable in length, densely tomentose; blade pinnately divided into numerous pinnae, these unarmed, regularly arranged in one plane, linear-lanceolate, reduplicate, single-fold, apically praemorse, discolorous. Inflorescence protandrous, interfoliar, branching to 1–3 orders; peduncle variable in length, terete, often tomentose; prophyll included within the subtending leaf; peduncular bract 1(–2), large, conspicuous, enclosing inflorescence in bud, splitting longitudinally, eventually deciduous, apically with a flattened beak; rachillae spreading, flexuous, glabrous to tomentose, basally with protandrous triads of one central female flower and two lateral male flowers, distally with solitary or paired male flowers. Flowers sessile, creamy white, calyx much shorter than petals; male flower with 3–32, free or variously connate stamens, anthers elongate; female flower wider than the male, otherwise quite similar, with 3–11 staminodes, gynoecium trilocular, triovulate, with three short stigmas. Fruit developing from 1, 2 or 3 carpels, globose to lobed, greenish-yellow, orange or yellowish-brown at maturity, epicarp smooth, mesocarp thin or thick, fleshy, endocarp thin; endosperm homogeneous. Germination remote-tubular; eophyll usually bifid with praemorse tips.</br></br>Eighteen species from Madagascar, Peninsular Thailand to New Guinea. One species in Thailand.

description: Epiphytic herbs; rhizome erect or pendulous. Pseudobulbs arising from near the apex of the previous pseudobulb, cylindric to subcylindric. Foliage leaves 2 per pseudobulb, arising from pseudobulb apex, plicate, chartaceous or coriaceous, petiolate. Inflorescence racemose, proteranthous or synanthous, many-flowered, pendulous; peduncle sheathed; rachis straight or weakly zig-zag; floral bracts scarious, caducous or persistent. Flowers resupinate, small to medium in size, often white, with or without yellowish-brown markings. Sepals free, spreading, abaxially carinate. Petals subequal to sepals. Labellum 3-lobed, saccate at base, with or without  keels or ridges, side lobes usually clasping base of column. Column conspicuously elongated, slender, incurved, dilated at apex, without stelids; anther subterminal; pollinia 4, solid, with caudicles; stigma cup-shaped; rostellum large. Fruit a capsule.</br></br>A genus of c. 5 species distributed from NE India, Nepal, Bhutan, Myanmar and S China to Indo-China; 3 species in Thailand.

description: Plant epiphytic. Pseudobulbs subcylindric, 1.5–9.5 by 0.8–1.4 cm, with longitudinal ridges when dry, enclosed by tubular sheaths when young, rooting at nodes. Foliage leaves 2 per pseudobulb, arising from pseudobulb apex, narrowly oblong to oblong-lanceolate, 5–18 by 0.8–2.5 cm, apex acuminate, base attenuate, lamina glossy green, coriaceous; petiole 1–2 cm long. Inflorescence proteranthous or synanthous, glabrous, to 15 cm long; peduncle 2.7–6.5 cm long; rachis slender, weakly zig-zag, laxly 5- to many-flowered; floral bracts ovate-lanceolate, 5–12 by 2–5 mm, acute, obtuse or subtruncate, caducous. Flowers white, sometimes with yellowish-brown spots at base of labellum epichile; pedicel and ovary 5–10 mm long. Sepals similar, oblong-lanceolate; dorsal sepal 7–8(–10) by 2–3 mm, acute, 5- to 7-nerved; lateral sepals slightly oblique, acute to acuminate, 5- to 7-nerved. Petals narrowly oblong-lanceolate, 6–8 by 1–2 mm, acute or acuminate, 3-nerved. Labellum 3-lobed, 5.5–8 mm long, saccate at base; mid lobe oblong, apiculate, deflexed from base, more or less papillate adaxially; side lobes broad, not much longer than broad, acute, finely papillose outside, clasping base of column; sac ornamented by a median thickened longitudinal ridge inside. Column slender, 4–7 mm long, winged and dilated at apex; rostellum broadly ligulate. Fruit ellipsoid to obovoid-ellipsoid, 1–1.2 by 0.4–0.8 cm, ridged.

description: Plant epiphytic. Pseudobulbs pendulous, subfusiform to cylindric, 3–6 by 0.8–1.5 cm, rugose, enclosed by fibrous sheaths, longitudinally wrinkled when dry, rooting at nodes. description: Terrestrial herbs, deciduous, with fleshy underground rhizome with tuber-like swellings at the stem bases, giving rise to separate flowering and leafy shoots. Foliage leaves erect, narrow, usually shorter than the inflorescence, plicate, petiolate, often withered at flowering. Inflorescences erect, racemose, to just under 1 m tall, with several sterile bracts; rachis few- to many-flowered; floral bracts persistent. Flowers medium-sized, resupinate, somewhat nodding, pubescent, not opening widely. Sepals  free, subequal; lateral sepal bases forming a small mentum. Petals similar but narrower. Labellum fleshy, 3-lobed, attached to the apex of the column foot, saccate at the base, disk and mid-lobe ornamented by papillae and tuberculate keels. Column stout, less than 10 mm long, pubescent, with versatile anther, with 8 clavate waxy pollinia. Pedicel distinctly set-off from ovary.</br></br>A small genus distributed through the whole of tropical and extratropical SE Asia to New Caledonia. Although 28 species have been described, only 3−5 are currently recognised by most botanists; 1 species in Thailand.

Labellum 3-lobed in the upper half, 7–11 by 5–6.5 mm; mid-lobe oblong, 2–5 by 1.8–4 mm; side lobes oblong-ovate, acute, suberect, 1.5–2.5(–3) by 1.5–2.2(–2.8) mm, inserted above the labellum middle; basal sac to 1 mm long; labellum ornaments of 3 or 5 tuberculate keels. description: Small to large trees; branchlets pubescent or glabrescent. Leaves spiral, scattered or tufted at the ends of branchlets; lamina chartaceous to coriaceous, obovate, oblanceolate, elliptic or oblong; apex acute, acuminate or rounded, base narrowly to broadly cuneate, rarely rounded, glabrous or pubescent; venation arched, rarely looped; midrib grooved, flat or raised above, rounded or keeled below; secondary veins variable in number; tertiary veins transverse, reticulate or parallel-reticulate to the secondary veins; stipules tiny, caducous. Flowers bisexual, in 1–many-flowered fascicles, axillary or in axils of fallen leaves. Calyx of 2 whorls of 3 free or slightly united sepals. Corolla: lobes (4–) 6 (–7), usually contorted; corolla tube usually glabrous, rarely pubescent inside. Stamens 12 (–21), usually in a single whorl, inserted near the top of the corolla tube or at the base of the corolla lobes; filaments free, unequal, those alternating with the corolla lobes very short; anthers sagittate, oblong or ovoid, dorsifixed, nearly always extrorse, apex bifid or acuminate, glabrous or pubescent. Ovary pubescent or glabrous, discoid or conoid, (3–) 6-locular; style simple, filiform, usually long-exserted, glabrous or pubescent at base. Fruits globose, ellipsoid or oblong-ellipsoid, crowned by persistent calyx, 1–2 (–many)-seeded. Seed usually broadly oblong or ellipsoid with a broad adaxial scar.</br></br>About 110 species from the Indo-Sri Lankan region, through SE Asia to the Pacific islands. Ten indigenous species, including two endemic, in Thailand.

description: Tree ca 28 m tall; branchlets terete or subangular, reddish brown puberulous or glabrescent. Leaves mostly spirally tufted at the ends of branchlets; lamina chartaceous or subcoriacoous, elliptic, oblong or oblong-lanceolate, 11–21 by 3.7–8 cm; apex rounded, obtuse or obtusely acuminate; base narrowly cuneate or cuneate, decurrent; both surfaces glabrous; midrib grooved above, somewhat crested, slightly keeled or rounded below; secondary veins 12–21 on each side, vanishing near the margin, looped in apical part of leaf; teriary veins transverse but subparallel to the secondary veins; petioles 1.5–2.5 cm long, grooved, distinctly crested above, angular below, glabrous; stipules lanceolate, 1–1.5 by 0.5 mm, reddish brown puberulous outside, glabrous inside, caducous. Flowers 1–6 in axils of fallen leaves; pedicels angular, 5–20 mm long, reddish brown tomentose. Sepals (4–)6, reddish brown tomentose outside, glabrous inside, with plumulose apex; outer sepals ovate or triangular, 3–3.8 by 2.5–4 mm; inner sepals broadly elliptic or broadly ovate, 3–4 by 2.8–4 mm, crested with membranous, glabrous, fimbriate margin. Corolla 7–12 mm long, entirely glabrous; tube 1.8–3.1 mm long; lobes (4–) 6 (–7), oblong, lanceolate, ovate or elliptic, 5.5–7.5 by 2.7–3.7 mm, with ciliate apex. Stamens (12–) 14–20, 4.5–8.5 mm long, entirely glabrous; filaments filiform, 2.5–4 mm long; anthers narrowly oblong-ovoid or sagittate, extrorse, 2.5–4 mm long, sparsely hairy; connective truncate, acute or aristate, 0.1–0.4 mm long. Ovary conoid, 5–6-locular, 6-lobed, reddish brown tomentose; style exserted, 6-ribbed, 8.5–16 mm long, glabrous except for a thinly tomentose basal part (according to Royen entirely glabrous); stigma 6-lobed.
