description: Tree to 22 m tall; branchlets terete, pale or brown yellowish woolly or glabrescent. Leaves mostly spirally tufted at the ends of branchlets; lamina coriaceous, ovate or ovate-oblong, 10–20 by 6–11.5 cm; apex obtuse or short obtusely acuminate, with acumen to 1.5 cm long; base broadly cuneate to rounded, somewhat asymmetrical; upper surface glabrous or woolly near the base; lower surface reddish brown woolly, dense on midrib and veins; midrib grooved above, often with a narrow groove in the middle of larger groove, somewhat woolly, rounded below; secondary veins 20–26 on each side, looped; tertiary veins transverse; petioles 2.5–3 cm long, narrowly grooved above, densely yellowish or brownish woolly; stipules lanceolate, 7–12 by 3–5 mm, pale or yellowish brown woolly outside, sparsely reddish brown woolly inside. Flowers 7–25 in axils of fallen leaves; pedicels 1.5–3 cm long, densely woolly. Sepals 6, not folded, reddish brown tomentose outside, glabrous inside; outer sepals broadly ovate or triangular, 5–5.6 by 4–5 mm; inner sepals ovate, oblong-ovoid or triangular, 4–4.5 by 3–4 mm, with membranous, glabrous, fimbriate margin. Corolla 9–12 mm long, glabrous except for reddish brown sericeous on the tube and the lobe base outside; tube 2–3 mm long; lobes 6, broadly elliptic, ovate or obovate, 7.5–8.2 by 3.5–3.8 mm. Stamens 12, 4.3–5 mm long, entirely glabrous; filaments filiform, 2.5–2.8 mm long; anthers oblong-ovoid, extrorse, 3.5–3.8 mm long; connective bifid, 0.5 mm long. Ovary conoid, 6-locular, yellowish or brownish hirsute; style angular, 1.5–1.7 cm long, exserted, glabrous. Fruits globose or ellipsoid, brownish, 1.5–2 by 1.5 cm, with short style remnant.

description: Tree to 30 m tall; branchlets terete, reddish brown puberulous, glabrescent. Leaves scattered or mostly spirally tufted at the ends of branchlets; lamina chartaceous or coriaceous, elliptic or obovate, 5.5–11 by 2.5–5 cm; apex obtusely acuminate; base cuneate, decurrent; young leaves reddish brown tomentose, both surfaces of mature leaves glabrous; midrib grooved above and minutely crested, rounded or ribbed below, sparsely hairy; secondary veins 11–18 on each side, vanishing near the margin, looped in apical part of leaf; tertiary veins parallel-reticulate; petioles 1.2–2 cm long, flat but grooved above, reddish brown puberulous or glabrescent; stipules lanceolate or ovate, (1.8–) 3–5 by 0.5–2 mm, puberulous outside, glabrous inside, caducous. Flowers 4–10 in axils of leaves; pedicels angular, 6–8 mm long, reddish brown tomentose. Sepals 6, reddish brown tomemtose outside, glabrous inside; outer sepals ovate to broadly ovate or triangular, 2.8–4.5 by 2.3–3 mm, slightly crested; inner sepals triangular or ovate, 2.8–3.7 by 1.8–2.5 mm, with membranous, glabrous, fimbriate margin. Corolla 3.2–3.5 mm long, entirely glabrous; tube 0.5 mm long; lobes 6, lanceolate, oblong-ovoid or oblong, 2.7–3 by 1.3–1.8 mm. Stamens 12, 2–2.5 mm long; filaments filiform, 0.3–0.7 mm long; anthers ovate or lanceolate, extrorse, 1.7–2 mm long, glabrous; connective bifid. Ovary conoid, triangular, 6-locular, tomentose; style filiform, 2–8 mm long, included, glabrous except for a tomentose base. Fruits oblong, 3.5–4 by 1.5–2 cm.

description: Tree to 35 m tall; branchlets terete or angular, puberulous, glabrescent. Leaves scattered or mostly at apex of branchlets; lamina coriaceous, obovate, obovate-oblong or oblong, 13–29 by 5.5–14.7 cm; apex acute, obtusely acuminate or obtuse, rarely retuse; base narrowly to broadly cuneate, decurrent; upper surface glabrous or with sparse short appressed hairs, lower surface with sparse short appressed hairs; midrib grooved, minutely crested above, rounded below; secondary veins 7–14 on each side, vanishing near margin, looped in apical part of leaf; tertiary veins, transverse; petioles 1.5–3.5 cm long, grooved or flat in the apical half, rounded in the basal part, puberulous, glabrescent; stipules lanceolate or linear, 4–10 by 1.5 mm, puberulous outside, glabrous inside, caducous. Flowers 4–12 in axils of fallen leaves; pedicels angular, 1.6–2 cm long, reddish brown tomentose. Sepals 6, reddish brown tomemtose outside, glabrous inside; outer sepals triangular or broadly ovate, 2.7–4.5 by 2.8–4 mm; inner sepals orbicular or ovate, 3.5–4.1 by 3.5–4 mm, crested, with membranous, glabrous, fimbriate margin. Corolla 1.2–1.4 cm long, entirely glabrous; tube 5 mm long; lobes 6, lanceolate-oblong, 7.5–8.2 by 2.7–3.2 mm. Stamens 12, 6.5–7.5 mm long; filaments filiform, 5 mm long, glabrous; anthers sagittate, ovate or oblong-ovoid, extrorse, 3.5–4 mm long, reddish brown sericeous; connective acuminate, 0.2–0.3 mm long. Ovary conoid, 6-locular, 12-lobed, glabrous; style 2–2.8 cm long, exserted, glabrous. Fruits pruniform to globose or obpyriform, to 2.8 by 2.2 cm, 1–2-seeded. Seeds ellipsoid, ca 2.5 by 1.2 by 1 cm, laterally compressed.

description: Tree to 30 m tall; branchlets terete, yellowish woolly or glabrescent. Leaves mostly at apex of branchlets; lamina coriaceous, elliptic, obovate or oblong, 15.5–21.5 by 6.4–11 cm; apex rounded or retuse; base broadly cuneate or rounded; upper surface glabrous or yellowish woolly along midrib only; lower surface woolly, denser on midrib and veins; midrib grooved and minutely crested above; secondary veins 19–22 on each side, vanishing near the margin; tertiary veins transverse; petioles 1.5–2.5 cm long, flat above with shallow groove, yellowish woolly, rounded below; stipules lanceolate, ca 13 by 4 mm, woolly outside, glabrous inside, caducous. Ovary subglobose-ovoid, 6-locular, 6-lobed, yellowish hirsute; style angular, 5–8 mm long, glabrous. Fruits oblong-ovoid, slightly curved, 8–10 by 3–4 cm, 1-seeded, glabrous.

description: Epiphytic or lithophytic herbs; rhizome creeping, short. Pseudobulbs close together, 1 internode, cylindric to ovoid-globose. Foliage leaves 1–2 per pseudobulb, arising from pseudobulb apex, conduplicate, narrowly elliptic to linear-lanceolate, thinly coriaceous,  petiolate to subsessile. Inflorescence racemose, proteranthous, synanthous or heteranthous, 1- or 2-flowered in all species known from Thailand, erect to decurved; floral bracts shorter than ovaries, membranous, persistent. Flowers resupinate, small to medium in size, variously colored. Sepals similar, free, lateral sepals often oblique or slightly narrower and longer. Petals similar to sepals, often shorter and narrower. Labellum entire or 3-lobed, side lobes small, not embracing column, more or less sigmoidly curved at base, often ornamented by short, low to lamella like keels. Column slender, slightly incurved, as long as or much shorter than labellum, with or without stelids; column foot short or almost absent; anther overhanging; pollinia 4, waxy, obliquely obovoid, with caudicles; stigma cup-shaped; rostellum large, not producing a stipe. Fruit a capsule, ellipsoid to obovoid.</br></br>A genus of c. 12 species distributed in the Indian subcontinent, Bhutan, Myanmar, S China and Indo-China; 4 species in Thailand.

description: Plant epiphytic, 10–15 cm tall. Pseudobulbs ovoid, 1–2 by 0.5–1 cm, erect or suberect. Petals lanceolate, 8–10 by 2 mm, apex acute to acuminate, 3-nerved. Labellum 3-lobed, broadly oblong to obovate, 8–9 by 5–6 mm, with a saccate sigmoid claw; mid-lobe apiculate; side lobes broad triangular; disk ornamented by 2 brown spots and 2–3 longitudinal obscure keels. Column winged, 5–6 mm long.

description: Small to large terrestrial, lithophytic or epiphytic herbs with elongate, fibrous roots arising from a short to elongate rhizome; erect shoots leafy, clustered or less frequently well spaced. Leaves one to several, coriaceous, conduplicate, spreading or suberect, ligulate, elliptic, or oblong, obtuse to acute, often tridenticulate at apex, green or tessellated with dark and lighter green on upper surface, lighter green below, more or less ciliate. Inflorescence terminal, one-to many-flowered; rachis terete, hairy, glandular or glabrous; bracts conduplicate, green, sometimes spotted or flushed or striped with purple. Flowers deciduous, usually showy; pedicel short. Dorsal sepal erect to hooded over lip, entire, glabrous or pubescent. Lateral sepals fused to form a concave, entire synsepal. Petals free, spreading or pendent, flat, reflexed or spiralling, often pubescent in basal half within, usually ciliate. Labellum deeply slipper-shaped or urn shaped, with more or less pronounced incurved side lobes, hairy within especially towards the base, glabrous or hairy on outer surface. Column short, porrect; anthers two, bilocular, borne on short filaments; pollen powdery or viscid: staminode terminal on column, sessile or shortly stalked, transversely reniform, oblong, ovate, obcordate or linear, flat, convex or longitudinally conduplicate, glabrous to papillose or finely pubescent; stigma stalked, dependent, tripartite, more or less papillose. Fruit an erect to pendent capsule, three-ribbed, cylindrical to almost ellipsoidal.</br></br>A genus of ca. 75 species ranging from southern India, Nepal, NE India and Myanmar across to southern China to Hong Kong, SE Asia, the Malay archipelago, the Philippines, New Guinea and the Solomon Islands; 14 species in Thailand.

description: A terrestrial herb. Leaves 5–8, narrowly elliptic to oblong-elliptic, subacute to obtuse at tridenticulate apex, 7–25 cm long, 2–4 cm wide, sparsely ciliate at base, obscurely tessellated pale and darker green, more or less purple-marked at base on lower side. Inflorescence erect, 1-flowered (rarely 2-flowered): peduncle 17–48 cm long, purple, shortly pubescent; bract lanceolate, acute, 1.5–2.1 cm long, green, ciliate. Flower 6–10 cm across; sepals whitish-green or pale green, longitudinally veined with green; dorsal sepal faintly purple-tinged towards base; petals green below with darker green and brown stripes and maroon-black spots in basal half, purple above; labellum ochre to pale purple with darker veins and a yellowish or greenish margin; pedicel and ovary 3–6 cm long, pubescent. Dorsal sepal ovate, cordate at base, apiculate above, 2.7–4.5 cm long, 2–3.2 cm wide, with recurved basal margins. Synsepal elliptic-lanceolate, acuminate, 2–3 cm long, 1.1–1.5 cm wide. Petals spathulate, acute or tridenticulate at apex, 4.4–5.8 cm long, 1.2–1.8 cm wide, half-twisted in apical half, with marginal warts in basal part of upper margin. Labellum 3.6–4.6 cm long; front margin obliquely bluntly dentate. Staminode transversely elliptic, tridentate at apex, 7–9 mm long, 8–9 mm wide; lateral teeth falcate, divergent, longer than middle tooth.

description: A terrestrial herb, usually of clustered growth. Leaves 4–5, oblong-elliptic, rounded and minutely emarginate at apex, usually up to 14 cm long, 5 cm wide, very dark green, mottled with pale green above, heavily purple-spotted below. Inflorescence 1-flowered (rarely 2-flowered), very short, usually arcuate; peduncle 2–4.5 cm long, arcuate, white-pubescent, purple or green, mottled maroon; bract conduplicate, elliptic-ovate, acute to obtuse, 23–27 mm long, 15–25 mm wide, pubescent, pale green, spotted purple. Flower subcampanulate, large for size of plant, about 5.5–8 cm in diameter, white or creamy yellow, usually heavily spotted on all segments with large maroon spots, shortly pubescent on outside; ovary about 3 cm long, green, spotted dull maroon. Dorsal sepal concave, broadly transversely elliptic to broadly ovate, obtuse to retuse, 2.7–4 cm long. 3.3–5.6 cm wide. Synsepal deeply concave, cordate, obtuse to rounded at apex, 2–3.1 cm long, 2.2–3.3 cm broad. Petals somewhat concave, broadly elliptic, rounded at apex, 4.5–6.3 cm long, 2.7–5.3 cm wide. Labellum narrowly ovoid to ellipsoidal, 2.5–4.2 cm long, 1.5–2 cm wide, all margins strongly incurved. Staminode subquadrate-obcordate, with a short apical tooth, 8–11 mm long, 8–9 mm wide.

description: A terrestrial herb. Leaves 3–5, narrowly elliptic, oblong-elliptic or obovate, tridenticulate at acute apex, 10–20 cm long, 3.2–4.8 cm wide, ciliate at base, tessellated pale and dark above, sometimes purple at base on lower surface. Flower large, 8–11 cm across; sepals white flushed with purple in lower half, veined with purple and green; petals white to yellow-green with a purple apical third, spotted with maroon on upper margin and sometimes in basal half; labellum green, heavily flushed deep maroon; staminode pale green with darker veins, flushed purple; pedicel and ovary 3–6.5 cm long, green, flushed with purple, purple-pubescent. Dorsal sepal broadly ovate to subcircular, apiculate, 4–5.5 cm long, 4.2–6 cm wide, with recurved ciliate margins. Synsepal concave, elliptic or lanceolate, acute, 2.7–3.2 cm long, 1.6–2.5 cm wide. Petals sometimes reflexed, subsigmoid, ligulate, obtuse or rounded at apex, 4.6–6.8 cm long, 1.2–1.8 cm wide, maroon-ciliate. Labellum 2.5–4.4 cm long, 2–2.5 cm wide, warty on incurved side lobes. Staminode lunate, 11 mm long, 7 mm wide, apical lateral teeth falcate, acute to obtuse.

description: A terrestrial herb. Leaves oblong-elliptic or linear-oblong, acute and tridenticulate at apex, up to 15 cm long, 2.8 cm wide, green above, spotted purple near base below. description: A terrestrial herb, often of clustered growth. Leaves 3–5, narrowly elliptic to oblong rounded and minutely tridentate at apex, 3.5–9.5 cm long, 1–2.4 cm wide, mottled very dark and pale green above, heavily mottled purple below, ciliate at the base. Inflorescence 1-flowered (rarely 2-flowered), 6–17(–23) cm long; peduncle 4–15 cm long, purple, shortly but densely white-pubescent; bracts conduplicate, broadly ovate, obtuse, 7–8 mm long, 3.5–3.9 mm wide, pale green, spotted purple. Flowers 3.3–4.2 cm in diameter, white, often highly dotted purple towards base of segments and on front of labellum, with a yellow or yellow-green centre to the staminode, pubescent on outside and at base of petals within; ovary 3.5–5.6 cm long, green flushed with dark purple, densely shortly pubescent. Dorsal sepal very broadly ovate, obtuse, 1.7–2.1 cm long, 1.8–2.2 cm wide. Synsepal concave, ovate, obtuse, 1.3–1.8 cm long, 0.8–1.6 cm wide. Petals elliptic, rounded, 2.2–2.6 cm long, 1.4–1.5 cm wide, shortly ciliate on margins. Labellum rather small, ovoid to ellipsoidal, with incurved margins, 2–2.1 cm long, 1–1.4 cm wide. Staminode shortly trullate to transversely subelliptic, one-to three-toothed at apex, 5.5–7.7 mm long, 7.2–8.3 mm wide.

description: A terrestrial herb. Inflorescence 1-flowered; peduncle 16–20 cm long, slender, green, purple-spotted; bract narrowly elliptic to elliptic, obtuse, 4–4.4 cm long, 2–2.4 cm wide, green to yellow-green, heavily spotted with dark purple. Dorsal sepal ovate-elliptic, obtuse, 3.8–4.2 cm long, 2.8–3.2 cm wide, pubescent on outer surface. Synsepal oblong-elliptic, obtuse, 1.8–2.3 cm long, 1–1.5 cm wide. Labellum 2.8–3.2 cm long, 1.4–1.6 cm wide. Staminode obovate, obtuse to rarely retuse, 10 mm long, 6 mm wide, with a glossy boss two thirds of the way.

description: An epiphytic or rarely lithophytic herb, often forming clumps. Leaves 4–5, linear-ligulate, acuminate to acute at unequally bilobulate apex, 14–42 cm long, 2.5–4 cm wide, mid-green on undersurface, purple-spotted at the base, basal margins ciliate. Inflorescence suberect to arcuate, 1-flowered; peduncle 7–24 cm long, green, often spotted purple, with long villose purple hairs; bract elliptic, obtuse, 3.7–6.5 cm long, 3–3.8 cm wide, green, spotted with maroon, glabrous. description:
Trees; branchlets pubescent or glabrescent. Leaves alternate and distichous, scattered; lamina chartaceous to coriaceous, elliptic, ovate, obovate or lanceolate; apex acute or acuminate; base cuneate, glabuous or pubescent; venation looped; midrib grooved or raised above and crested, rounded below; secondary veins variable in number; tertiary venation 
parallel-reticulate to the secondary veins; stipules present, caducous. Flower bisexual, in axillary fascicles. Calyx of 2 whorls of 2 more or less free sepals. Corolla lobes 8, imbricate, equal to or longer than the corolla tube; tube usually glabrous inside. Stamens 16, inserted in 1 (–2) whorls at the top of the corolla tube; anthers extrorse or latrorse. Ovary pubescent (6–) 8-locular, style exserted, tapering gradually to the apex. Fruits 1–2-seeded. Seed laterally compressed, with a long narrow adaxial scar.</br></br>About 15 species in mainland SE Asia and Malesia. Four species native in Thailand.

description: Tree to 35 m tall; branchlets terete or angular, reddish brown tomentose or glabrescent. description: Terrestrial herbs with underground tubers. Flowering shoots 10–120 cm tall; stem glabrous. Foliage leaves (1–)2–14, sessile, sheathing at base, scattered along the stem or crowded at its base; upper part of stem sometimes carrying 1–5 small non-sheathing leaves. Inflorescence racemose; bracts much smaller than the foliage leaves, boat-shaped, acuminate, glabrous, at least those in the distal part of the inflorescence shorter than the flowers. Flowers 1–17, resupinate, predominantly white to pale yellowish-green, more or less fragrant. Sepals plain (i.e. not saccate), glabrous, dorsal sepal 7–30 mm long. Petals recurved or suberect. Labellum narrowly attached to the column, ovate to deeply 3-lobed to irregularly flabellate, smooth on the ventral side, spurred at base; spur longer than the labellum lamina, not constricted at base. Column complanate, with a flat to slightly concave stigma consisting of two hardly coherent lobes; distal part of rostellum broad; viscidia 2, naked; anther firmly attached, thecae basally extending from the column together with the lateral parts of the rostellum; pollinia 2, basitonous. Ovary glabrous. Fruit not seen.</br></br>A genus of ca. 7 species distributed in mainland Southeast Asia south of a line from the southern Himalayas to Japan, and in Indonesia (except Kalimantan and Papua); 3 species in Thailand.

description: Shrubs or densely branched trees (0.5–)1–5 m tall, base of trunk to 10 cm diam. Leaves decussate; petiole to 2 mm long; lamina narrowly elliptic to lanceolate, 10–30 by 3–15 mm, thick, succulent, base attenuate, apex acute or obtuse, often terminating in a minute hydathode. Flowers axillary; bracteoles 2, minute, at base of pedicel 5–15 mm long; calyx tube 4–6 mm long, finely 12-ridged, thick-walled; calyx lobes short, about one-quarter as long as calyx tube; epicalyx appendages ca half as long; petals elliptic, or (ob)ovate or suborbicular, 5–8 by 3–5 mm, crumpled in bud; stamens 12, scarcely biseriate, 6 exserted in short-styled flowers, or all included in long-styled flowers; style long-exserted or included, stigma broad capitate. Capsule 1-locular (incompletely 3-locular), subglobose or obovoid, 6–9 mm long, somewhat exserted at maturity. Seeds ca 20, with one thickish margin, not winged, 2–3 mm long.

description: Delicate, perennial, unbranched or few-branched decumbent herb. Leaves alternate, petiolate; blades ovate, margin sinuate-dentate, apex subacute. Flowers small, white or pale pinkish, solitary, axillary or terminal; pedicel long, slender, erect; calyx lobes long-triangular; corolla regular, campanulate, deeply 5-lobed, lobes sublinear, apex subobtuse; stamens 5, filaments linear, free; anthers linear; style slender, stigma with 3 recurved lobes; ovary (2–)3-locular. Fruit a thin-walled, membranous capsule, slightly contracted at apex, few-seeded, rupturing irregularly. Seeds comparatively large, oblong.</br></br>The genus comprises one species, endemic to eastern Asia.

description: Herb 5–25 cm long, often rooting at lower nodes; stem glabrous or pubescent. Leaves: petiole 0.2–1.5 cm long; blade somewhat fleshy, glabrous or hairy, ovate, 0.5–3.5 by 0.5–2.5 cm, base (sub)truncate(cordate), margin serrulate or crenulate with 2–10 teeth per side, apex acute or rounded. Flowers solitary, axillary, rarely few-fascicled; pedicel slender, to 50 mm long; braceoles absent; calyx lobes 1–2 by 0.5–1 mm, margin entire; corolla white, rarely with purple shading at the tips, campanulate, 5–10 mm long, deeply 5-lobed, tube 1(–4) mm long, lobes sublinear, 1–6 mm long, apex subobtuse; ovary glabrous, 5-ribbed, 2–3.5 by 0.5–2.5 mm, (2–)3-locular, style inserted on a thin, hemispherical, nectariferous disc on top of the ovary, included, 3–6.5 mm long, hairy in upper third, stigma consisting of (2– or) 3 filiform lobes; filaments subglabrous, 1.5–3 mm long, widest and hairy towards the base, anthers 1–1.5 mm long. Capsule nodding, distended by the mature seeds. Seeds 10–16 per capsule, 1–2 mm long, finely striate.

description: Terrestrial, deciduous, tuberous herbs, glabrous in the Flora area. Flowering shoots 12–60(–108) cm tall, unbranched. Foliage leaves one to several, basal or cauline and scattered along the stem or clustered in its middle, lanceolate, ovate or oblong, sessile. Usually with one to several erect, suberect or spreading sterile bracts above the foliage leaves, their margins sometimes glandular-papillose or shortly hairy. Inflorescence terminal, racemose; floral bracts lanceolate, margins sometimes shortly hairy. Flowers few to many, resupinate, small to medium sized, mostly with greenish, yellowish or whitish colours. Sepals free; dorsal sepal erect, usually forming a hood with the petals. Petals unlobed. Labellum 3-lobed or rarely entire, spur short or rarely long, cylindric, clavate, fusiform or globular, usually with a constriction at the base. Column short, anther canals absent or very short, pollinia 2, sectile: stigmas short or long, connate with or adpressed to the labellum base; central rostellum lobe insignificant. Ovary glabrous or papillose, normally not distinct from the pedicel.</br></br>A genus of ca. 105 species widely distributed from the Mascarenes through tropical and subtropical Asia to the Pacific; 17 species in Thailand.</br></br>Notes: A more comprehensive version of this account was published in Nord. J. Bot. 28: 21–46. 2010.

description: Flowering shoots glabrous, 14–38 cm tall. Sterile bracts 1–3, spreading or suberect, lanceolate, acuminate, 0.9–2.3 cm long. Inflorescence dense or semi-dense, many-flowered; rachis 5–13 cm long; floral bracts lanceolate to ovate, acuminate, 4–9 by 1.5–2.5 mm. Flowers green or white. Sepals elliptic, obtuse or subacute; dorsal sepal erect, 2.5–3 by 1.5–1.7 mm; lateral sepals reflexed or spreading, mucronate, ca. 2.8 by 1.1–1.3 mm, usually partly rolled-in, basally connate with the labellum. Petals erect, obliquely ovate-elliptic, acute, 2.5–2.8 by 1.3–1.7 mim. Labellum 2.7–3.2 mm long, 3-lobed above a basal portion 1.7–2.7 mm long, in front of the spur mouth a concavity with a papillose area; midlobe orbicular to ovate, 1–1.3 by 0.8–1.5 mm; side lobes obtusely triangular, 1–1.2 by 0.6–1.2 mm; spur globular with wide mouth, to 1.6 mm long. Column 0.8–1 mm long; stigmas clavate and connate with the labellum, ca. 1.3 mm long. Ovary (including pedicel) 4.6–5.3 mm long. Capsule not seen.

description:
Terrestrial or rarely lithophytic herbs, evergreen, in Thailand mostly glabrous except for the floral parts; stems either short and pseudobulbous or elongate-fusiform and cane-like. Flowering shoots 40–200 cm tall. Pseudobulbs (if present) insignificant and largely hidden by the bases of the foliage leaves, adjacent. Foliage leaves few, plicate, perennial, lanceolate-oblong, acute or acuminate, petiolate, sometimes forming a pseudostem; laminas rounded to cuneate at base. Inflorescences racemose, basal or lateral on the stem; peduncles with sterile bracts; rachis few-flowered; floral bracts persistent or caducous. Flowers usually large, resupinate, in the Thai species mostly with yellow, pink or white colours; damaged or old flowers turn dark blue. Sepals and petals similar, free, campanulate or spreading. Labellum more or less 3-lobed with a glabrous spur, free from the column or fused with it only at the base; side lobes often erect and enclosing the column; labellum sometimes ornamented, mostly by keels. Column long, without a column foot, mostly hairy on the front side; anther incumbent, versatile, pollinia 8, clavate, waxy; rostellum entire, not producing a viscidium. Ovary not distinct from the pedicel.

About 40 species, mainly in Asia, with a few found in Africa, N Australia and the Pacific Ocean Islands; 6 species in Thailand.

description: Flowering shoots pseudobulbous, vegetative parts glabrous. Pseudobulbs insignificant, hidden by the bases of the foliage leaves, ovoid or fusiform, 10–14.5 by 4.5–5.7 cm. Flowers spreading, with both sides of sepals and petals greenish-yellow, labellum white with yellow and red markings. Sepals ovate-lanceolate, acuminate, to 68 by 12–18 mm. Petals lanceolate-elliptic, acuminate, to 63 by 12–17 mm. Labellum weakly 3-lobed, obovate, acute, fused with the column only at the base, 45–65 by 27–53 mm; mid-lobe ovate, cuspidate, distinctly protruding, 25–30 mm wide; side lobes erect and enveloping the column; disk ornamented by 3 obscure keels; spur usually apically bifid, 11–15 mm long. description: Shrubby, creeping to large palms, solitary or clustered, dioecious. Stem with spirally arranged, closely inserted leaf bases. Leaf sheath dissolving in fibrous mesh; petiole short to elongate; blade pinnately divided into single-folded, induplicate leaflets, regularly arranged in one plane or grouped in various ways and pointing in different directions, the proximal ones modified as spines. Inflorescence interfoliar, branching to 1 order, male and female inflorescences more or less similar until anthesis; peduncle flattened, elongating in female inflorescence after anthesis, peduncular and rachis bracts strongly reduced and inconspicuous; rachillae numerous, often inserted in groups along the rachis, with spirally arranged solitary flowers. Male flower ovoid in bud, with sepals connate forming a low cupule; petals free, much longer than the calyx; stamens (3–)6(–9), free or shortly adnate to corolla, with short filament and elongate anther, pistillode lacking; female flower globose, about ½ the length of the male flower, petals about twice as long as the calyx cupule, staminodes reduced and inconspicuous; carpels three, free, with short, narrow recurved stigma. Infructescence long pedunculate. Fruit usually developing from one carpel, ovoid to oblong; epicarp smooth, mesocarp fleshy; endocarp membranous. Seed with homogeneous endosperm in Thai species. Germination remote tubular.</br></br>Fourteen species in Africa, Crete to W & C Malesia. Three species and one variety in Thailand.

description: Tall, solitary palm, hermaphrodite. Stem erect, ringed with inconspicuous leaf scars. Leaf costapalmate, induplicate; sheath dissolving in mesh of reddish-brown fibres; petiole elongate, often with two conspicuous, yellowish stripes, armed along the margins with very long, robust, horizontal, basally swollen spines; adaxial hastula conspicuous, triangular, abaxial hastula inconspicuous or lacking; blade splitting deeply into 3–4 folded segment groups along adaxial ribs almost to the hastula, individual segments futher divided to ½–⅔ the radius into single-folded, apically indented segments. Inflorescence interfoliar; branched to 4 orders; peduncular bracts 1–6, conspicuous, tubular; rachis longer than peduncle; rachis bracts tubular; rachillae with spirally arranged flowers, solitary or in groups of 2–3. Flower sessile on low tubercles, calyx shallowly cup-shaped; petals free; stamens 6, connate to form a conspicuous tube, free from the corolla; gynoecium hairy, united apically in a slender style. Fruit one-seeded, large, orange to brown, globose; epicarp smooth or cracked in the Thai species into numerous corky warts; mesocarp thick, more or less fleshy, orange; endocarp crustaceous. Seed with thick, homogeneous endosperm, penetrated laterally by a convoluted intrusion of the seed coat. Germination remote-tubular.</br></br>Six species in Peninsular Thailand to Malesia. One species in Thailand.

description: Lithophytic or epiphytic herbs, erect or pendulous; rhizome short, creeping. Pseudobulbs crowded or distant on rhizome, slender or swollen, sometimes connected to each other at both ends or connected by a short rhizome to middle part of another pseudobulb. Foliage leaves 1–2 per pseudobulb, duplicate, usually coriaceous, shortly petiolate. Inflorescence racemose, terminal from pseudobulb apex, erect, arching or pendulous, distichously many-flowered, glabrous in Thai species; rachis usually slightly zig-zag; floral bracts, caducous or persistent, concave. Flowers small, resupinate, not opening widely. Sepals free or lateral sepals connate at base, usually concave, lateral sepals often keeled on the back. Petals similar to sepals or narrower. Labellum firmly attached, sessile, subentire or 3- or 4-lobed, saccate, not sigmoidly curved at base, often ornamented by keels; epichile deflexed. Column short, winged or hooded at apex; column foot short or absent; anther terminal, incumbent; pollinia 4 in 2 pairs, solid, connected by inconspicuous caudicles, each pollinium with a tiny pore; stigma cup-shaped; rostellum large, not producing a stipe. Fruit a capsule.</br></br>A genus of c. 40 species distributed from India, Sri Lanka, Nepal, Bhutan, Myanmar, S China, Taiwan, Indo-China and Malesia to the SW Pacific islands; 8 species in Thailand. The occurrence of Pholidota chinensis Lindl. in Thailand is uncertain. There are specimens from markets but there is no record from the natural habitat.

Inflorescence synanthous, to 8 cm long; peduncle 1–2 cm long; rachis curved, subdensely 20- to 35-flowered; floral bracts distichous, on the side opposite to the flowers, semi-circular, 6–8 by 6.5–9 mm, rounded to subtruncate, partly overlapping each other, persistent until after fruiting. Sepals dissimilar; dorsal sepal oblong-obovate, 3–5 by 1.5–3 mm, obtuse to rounded, 3-nerved; lateral sepals ovate-oblong, 3.5–4 by 1.5–2 mm, acute, 3-nerved. description: Terrestrial herbs with a short stout creeping rhizome rooting from the nodes; leaves, peduncle, rachis and floral bracts covered with yellowish-brown hairs. Pseudobulbs ascending, each bearing either a single leaf or an inflorescence, articulated at junction with petiole or peduncle, initially covered by scale-like cataphylls that soon disintegrate into fibres. Foliage leaves long-lived, convolute, plicate, short-petiolate; petiole channelled. Inflorescence erect, racemose, lax, both peduncle and rachis elongating during flowering; floral bracts persistent, entire. Flowers non-resupinate, wide-open. Sepals and petals free; sepals densely pubescent on the dorsal side, (sub)glabrous on the ventral side; petals glabrous. Labellum versatile, sessile, 3-lobed, glabrous, spurless, ornamented by 2 conspicuous double-crested ridges. Column suberect, incurved, semiterete-clavate with 2 lateral subspathulate stelids and a solid, spurless column foot; anther partly hidden in an apical column hood, incumbent, versatile; pollinia 2, solid, devoid of caudicles; rostellum short, truncate, neither producing stipe nor viscidia; receptive part of stigma concave. Ovary (including pedicel) terete, densely covered with yellowish-green hairs. Fruit a capsule dehiscing by longitudinal slits.</br></br>A monotypic genus; distribution as for the species (see below).

description: Small, understorey palms, seldom moderately tall. Stems clustered or less often solitary, usually ringed with prominent leaf scars. Leaves pinnate or occasionally undivided; leaf sheaths closed and forming a prominent crownshaft, rarely crownshaft not developing; pinnae regularly arranged along the rachis and spreading in the same plane, linear to sigmoid, 1- to several-veined; pinnae at leaf apex joined with only a short split at the tip, giving praemorse appearance. Inflorescences branched to one order, sometimes spicate, borne below the crownshaft, rarely among the leaves; rachillae covered initially with prophyll only, peduncular bract absent; rachillae few, usually pendulous, glabrous or seldom variously hairy. Flowers borne in triads, the triads spirally arranged or more often distichously arranged along the rachillae. Fruits small to moderate, spindle-shaped, commonly beaked, red, orange, or black, 1-seeded. Seed with ruminate endosperm, germination adjacent, eophyll bifid.</br></br>About 130 species from India through Indo-China and into southeast Asia to New Guinea. Fifteen species in Thailand.

description: Small to medium-sized, evergreen, obligate rheophytes. Stem erect or decumbent, usually more or less condensed. Leaves several; petiole semiterete to canaliculate on upper side; petiolar sheath short with long, marcescent ligule; leaf blade elongate-lanceolate to elliptic or oblanceolate, coriaceous, basally cuneate, apex with tubular mucro; primary lateral veins pinnate, running into distinct marginal vein; secondary laterals and higher order venation either parallel-pinnate or tessellate. Inflorescence one per module, emerging orthotropic, maturing (prior to the onset of anthesis) anatropic; peduncle subequal to or longer than petiole; spathe stoutly ellipsoid, not constricted, usually pink, rarely white, lower part persistent and cup-like, upper part inflating and then gaping at anthesis, soon-caducous, cuspidate to acuminate, often with a pronounced terminal rostrum becoming reflexed at anthesis, interior frequently with one to several pronounced crests, especially in the distal part; spadix sessile with oblique insertion, often with staminodes basally; pistillate flower zone cylindrical; pistils connate into a synandrium, or free but cohering to neighbouring ones; ovary 1-locular; ovules many, placenta 2–4, parietal; stigma ± sessile, usually as broad as ovary and more or less contiguous with adjacent ones; staminate flower zone contiguous with pistillate, cylindrical to ellipsoid, equal in thickness to pistillate, obtuse; stamens arranged in pairs or irregular, free, compressed, anthers truncate, connective ± flat or expanded apically or with conical beak (the last not in Thailand), overtopping thecae; thecae oblong-ellipsoid, dehiscing by apical pore; appendix absent. Infructescence a cluster of berries subtended by the obconical spathe base carried on an erect peduncle, spadix above fruiting portion degrading and shed entirely soon after fertilization; berry obovoid to subcylindrical, small, green, either fused into a syncarpium (most species), or free but cohering to adjacent berries (not in Thailand). Seed numerous, elongate-ellipsoid to cylindrical, with long, curved micropylar appendage, testa slightly costate, embryo elongate, endosperm copious.</br></br>Eleven species in Malesia, the majority (nine) endemic in Borneo. One species in Thailand.</br></br>Piptospatha is defined by the combination of shedding spathe limb, thecae lacking a horn, parietal placentation, an erect splash cup, fruits either fused into a syncarpium (most) or free but cohering (P. insignis N.E.Br.), and the presence of a micropylar appendage on the seed.

description: Rheophytic herb 10–40 cm tall. Stem short, condensed, 2–4 by 0.7–1 cm; roots thick, extensive and tough, 1.5–2 mm diam., with many thinner roots of second order. Leaves few to several together; petiole 6–15 cm long, 1.5–2 mm diam., canaliculate on upper side, sheathing only at the extreme base, the wings extended into a narrow ligular portion 3–7 cm long; leaf blade coriaceous, adaxially dark mid-green, paler abaxially, elliptic (to oblong elliptic) 10–26 by 1.5–7 cm, base cuneate, apex acute and shortly apiculate for 1–1.5 mm, margins weakly to strongly crispate especially distally; midrib and primary venation very prominent abaxially, drying pale orange to straw-coloured; primary lateral veins 5–8(–10) on each side, running to a thick marginal vein; secondary venation distinctly finer than primaries; tertiary venation forming a obscure tessellate pattern. Inflorescence solitary (sometimes 2–3 in series but alternating with foliage leaves); peduncle erect, 3–16 cm long; spathe nodding at anthesis, narrowly ovoid, ca 3 cm long, apically beaked for ca 4 mm, lower part dull pale green, limb creamy white to white, caducous; spadix ca 2 cm long, shortly stipitate; stipe adnate to the spathe; pistillate flower zone thickly discoid, about as broad as the ovary (dry), papillate, not contiguous with neighbouring stigmas (dry); interpistillar staminodes confined to a small group or irregular whorl at the base of the pistillate zone, individually stipitate, flat-topped, about as long as the pistils, ca 0.5 mm diam.; sterile interstice absent; staminate flower zone fertile to apex, bluntly ellipsoidsubcylindrical, ca 1 by 0.5 cm; stamens truncate, more or less flat-topped to somewhat rounded, narrowly rectangular-elliptic, anthers ﬁnely and densely pubescent, ca 0.8 mm across. Fruiting spathe obconical, green; berries yellowish when ripe, in a more or less hemispherical group ca 1.5 cm diam., obovoid, 2.2–2.4 by 1.5 mm, with persistent, apical stigma remnant. Seeds several, subcylindrical, ca 1–1.2 mm long; testa slightly ribbed, brown, with a prominently curved micropylar appendage.

description: Small, free-floating, stoloniferous, evergreen herb with pendent feathery roots. Stem very short, acaulescent, stoloniferous. Leaves several in a rosette up to 30 cm across but often much less, densely pubescent; petiole very short, almost absent, sheath very short, ligulate, very thin, scarious at base; leaf blade somewhat spongy, obovate-cuneate to obovate-oblong, up to 10 by 7 cm, apex rounded, truncate or retuse; midrib absent; primary veins subparallel, all arising from base, diverging slightly and running into margin near apex, strongly prominent on lower surface, higher order venation reticulate. Inflorescence solitary, very small, much shorter than leaves and partially hidden among leaf bases; peduncle 3–5 mm, pubescent; spathe pubescent externally, glabrous within, somewhat constricted centrally, ca 10–12 by 5–7 mm, lower margins connate and adnate to ovary wall together forming tube, free margins between tube and spathe limb folded between stigma and staminate organs forming a partition between an upper staminate partial chamber and a lower pistillate one, limb erect, ovate, expanded, acute-acuminate; spadix shorter than spathe, mostly adnate to spathe, ca 5–7 mm, only the apical staminate zone free; pistillate flower zone bearing a single gynoecium at base and a thin, green, pouch-shaped flap just below spathe partition; ovary obliquely adnate to spadix axis, ovary ovoid, ca 1 mm diam., 1-locular; stylar region attenuate, bending inwards towards staminate flowers; stigma small, discoid-subcapitate; staminate flower zone subtended by a thin, marginally lobed, green, annular flap, composed of a basally naked spadix axis supporting a single whorl of 2–8 flowers with the naked axis sometimes extending a little beyond; flowers unisexual, perigone absent; synandrium composed of 2 connate stamens, ca 2 mm diam., subtended by a thin, marginally lobed, green, annular flap; thecae dehiscing by a single apical slit. Fruit a thin-walled, utricular, many-seeded, ellipsoid berry, irregularly breaking up and decaying to release seeds. Seed barrel-shaped, ± subtruncate and excavated at apex and base, testa thick, reticulate-alveolate, thicker and with operculum at micropylar end.</br></br>A single species of free-floating aquatic stoloniferous evergreen herbs. Pistia stratiotes, the only accepted species, has a very considerable synonymy, with the formerly recognized ‘species’ separated on trivial characters.

description: Terrestrial (rarely epiphytic) herbs with tubers or fasciculate fleshy roots. Flowering shoots 7–120 cm tall; stem glabrous. Foliage leaves 1–7, sheathing at base, scattered along the stem or crowded on its lower part; upper part of the stem bearing 1–3 small non-sheathing leaves. Inflorescence spicate; bracts much smaller than the foliage leaves, at least those in the distal part of the inflorescence shorter than the flowers. Flowers 2 to many, resupinate, white to (yellowish-)green. Sepals plain (i.e., not saccate), glabrous; dorsal sepal 2–9 mm long. Petals connivent with the dorsal sepal. Labellum narrowly attached to the column, linear, entire. smooth on the ventral side, spurred at base; spur longer than the labellum lamina, subacute, not constricted at base. Column semiterete, with a slightly bilobed, concave stigma; distal part of rostellum broad; viscidia 2, naked; anther firmly attached, thecae not extending from the column; pollinia 2, basitonous. Ovary glabrous. Fruit a capsule, dehiscing by 6 longitudinal slits.</br></br>A genus of ca. 200 species. The very wide distribution mainly encompasses subarctic, temperate and subtropical areas of the northern hemisphere, but it also extends southward through tropical regions to Central America and to major parts of Malesia, including New Guinea; 2 species in Thailand.

description: Moderate to robust, solitary or clustering, high-climbing, dioecious hapaxanthic rattans. Leaf sheath without knee, usually armed with partial whorls of spines and indumentum; ocrea inconspicuous. Leaf frequently very robust, terminating in a long cirrus; petiole present or absent; leaflets numerous, usually irregularly arranged, grouped and fanned within the groups, often discolorous. Male and female inflorescences superficially similar, produced simultaneously from the topmost nodes; primary axes held ± horizontally, stiff; secondary axes limply pendulous, bearing close imbricate distichous bracts, each one subtending and ± hiding a short branch bearing the flowers. Male flowers with calyx short, terminating in 3 teeth; corolla with 3 petals free almost to the base; stamens 6, shortly epipetalous; pistillode minute; female flower with calyx terminating in 3 lobes; corolla with 3 petals free almost to the base; pistil with fimbriate scaly ovary and 3 stigmas. Fruit 1-seeded, covered in fimbriate or smooth margined scales, the scale tips often reflexed; mesocarp quite thick. Seed with thin sarcotesta; endosperm homogeneous; embryo basal. Seedling leaf lanceolate, undivided; second seedling leaf bifid.</br></br>Sixteen species in E. Himalaya to Hainan and Malesia. Three species in Thailand.

description: Robust, solitary rattan. Leaves cirrate; sheaths dull green, armed with horizontal or oblique combs of golden brown or deep reddish-brown spines to 4 cm long, and abundant white or buff-coloured indumentum; knee absent; petiole to c. 30 cm long; rachis to 4 m long; cirrus to 3 m long; leaflets to c. 60 on each side of the rachis, arranged irregularly in groups of two to seven and fanned within the groups, bluish-green on the upper surface, whitish beneath. Inflorescences produced from the top 7–10 nodes, to c. 80 cm long and bearing c. 12 crowded pendulous branches to c. 1 m; bracts chestnut brown, c. 7 by 5 cm, with triangular tips but scarcely truncate. Male flowers up to c. 20 within each bract; female flowers 3–9 within each bract, ± completely concealed. Mature fruit c. 8 within each bract (if fewer, then fruit larger), very crowded, c. 1.5 cm diam., with reflexed stigmas and covered in c. 50 vertical rows of fimbriate-margined reddish-brown scales. Seed c. 1 cm diam. Seedling leaf lanceolate, undivided.

Inflorescences produced simultaneously in the axils of many uppermost leaves, the male and female superficially similar, to 2 m long and bearing pendulous first order branches to 80 cm long, bearing conspicuous pale brown bracts, tubular at first, soon splitting along their length, each subtending a short rachilla, bracts in male inflorescences 4–5.5 cm long, male rachillae 2–2.8 cm long, bracts in female inflorescence 4–5.5 cm long, female rachillae 1.2–2.5 cm long, all bracts becoming chestnut brown with age and persisting to fruiting. description: Moderately robust, clustering rattan. description: Clustering high-climbing dioecious hapaxanthic rattans with moderate to robust stems. Leaf cirrate, sheaths without knees, ocrea sometimes conspicuous; rachis bearing entire ± regularly arranged concolorous leaflets. Inflorescences produced simultaneously in the axils of the uppermost leaves, male and female superficially similar; primary axis branching to 1 or 2 orders, the branches bearing tubular triangular-tipped bracts subtending clusters of 2–7 flowers. Male flower with tubular calyx with 3 triangular lobes and 3 petals joined at the base; stamens 6, borne on the petals; pistillode minute; female flower with tubular calyx with 3 very short obtuse lobes, and corolla with 3 lobes; staminodes 6 epipetalous; ovary tipped with 3 small divergent stigmas; calyx enlarging considerably and splitting irregularly, persisting to mature fruiting; corolla also persistent. Mature fruit tipped with minute stigmatic remains, covered in many somewhat irregular vertical rows of scales. Seed with thin sarcotesta; endosperm homogeneous. Seedling leaf bifid.</br></br>Six or seven species known from Myanmar and Thailand south to Peninsular Malaysia, Sumatra, Billiton and Borneo. Two species in Thailand. A genus of rather coarse clustering rattans normally found in secondary forest or seral facies of primary forest (such as old landslips or the clearings formed by the death or fall of large trees). Generally not used as the cane has a soft pith and poor external appearance. However, the apex of at least one species is eaten in some parts of Borneo.

description: Clustering, moderate to robust rattan, forming rather dense thickets. description: Clustering, moderate-sized rattan forming rather dense thickets. Stems climbing to 30 m long, without sheaths distinctly triangular in cross section, to 1.3 cm diam., with sheaths to 2 cm diam., internodes to 40 cm near the ground, usually much less (c. 20 cm) in stems in the forest canopy. Leaves cirrate; sheaths dull green, armed with evenly scattered, slightly upward pointing golden spines to 0.3 cm long and covered with sparse reddish-brown indumentum; ocrea very short, to 0.5 cm long, truncate, golden brown; flagellum absent; petiole to c. 15 cm long, densely covered in caducous red brown scales and abaxially very sparsely armed with reflexed spines; rachis to 90 cm long; cirrus to c. 1 m long; leaflets 15–20 on each side of the rachis, regularly arranged, rather distant (c. 5 cm apart), the longest to c. 30 by 3 cm, acuminate in long drip tips, armed along the adaxial surface of the main vein with short golden spinules to 0.2 cm long. Inflorescences to 30 cm long, produced simultaneously from the axils of the uppermost reduced leaves, the male branched to 2 orders, the female to 1 order; first order branches to c. 20 cm long. Male flowers borne on very short c. 0.8 cm, strongly curved branches from bracts on the first order branches; female flowers borne in groups of 2 or 3 flowers only. Mature fruit borne on persistent enlarged and split calyx and corolla, slightly oblate and obscurely three-angled, c. 2.5 by 3 cm, with a short beak to 1 by 1 mm, and covered in c. 22 vertical rows of yellow brown scales with dark margins. Seed c. 2 by 1.5 cm; endosperm homogeneous. Seedling leaf unknown.

description: Epiphytic, lithophytic or (less frequently) terrestrial dwarf herbs, usually growing in dense patches on rocks or trees. Pseudobulbs annual, clustered on the rhizome, ovoid, conical, pyriform or turbinate, covered by sheaths when young. Foliage leaves 1–2 per pseudobulb, arising from pseudobulb apex, deciduous, erect to arcuate-spreading, plicate, elliptic-oblong, elliptic-lanceolate, oblong-lanceolate or oblanceolate, chartaceous, mostly shortly petiolate. Inflorescence basal, 1- to 2-flowered, arising from an old pseudobulb, erect, appearing either before or after leaves; floral bracts persistent. Flowers resupinate, large, showy, sometimes fragrant, white or pink to rose-purple or magenta, more rarely yellow, marked with yellow, red or brown on the labellum. Sepals free, spreading, linear-oblong to oblong-lanceolate. Petals similar to sepals but slightly narrower. Labellum obscurely 3-lobed or entire, apical margins erose to lacerate; ornamented by 2 to several ridges or lines of hairs along the veins of the upper surface of the labellum. Column slender, slightly arcuate, winged above, entire, erose or denticulate at apex; column foot absent; anther subterminal, incumbent; pollinia 4 in 2 pairs, waxy, often bilaterally flattened; rostellum producing neither stipe nor viscidium. Fruit a capsule, fusiform, with 3 longitudinal ribs.</br></br>A genus of c. 21 species distributed from NE India, Nepal, Bhutan, Bangladesh, Myanmar, S China and Taiwan to Laos and Vietnam; 2 species in Thailand.

description: Plant epiphytic or lithophytic, 15–25 cm tall when producing leaves. Pseudobulbs turbinate to pyriform, 1–3 by 1–1.5 cm, usually with a distinct neck, often covered by remains of old smooth sheaths. Foliage leaves 2 per pseudobulb, elliptic-oblong to oblanceolate, 8–25  by 1.7–3.5 cm, apex acute, base attenuate, chartaceous. Inflorescence appearing before the leaves, glabrous, to 6 cm long; peduncle covered by membranous, inflated, smooth sheaths; floral bract broadly obovate or suborbicular when flattened, 1.5–3 cm long, obtuse, cucullate. Flower 1, suberect to spreading, fragrant; pedicel and ovary 4–5 mm long. Sepals creamy white, occasionally lightly streaked with pink; dorsal sepal oblong-lanceolate, 30–40 by 7–8 mm, obtuse, 5-nerved; lateral sepals lanceolate-falcate, more or less the same size as dorsal sepal, acute, 5-nerved. Petals creamy white, oblanceolate, slightly falcate, 30–40 by 7–8 mm, acute, obscurely 1-nerved. Labellum white with a yellow centre, large purple and yellow blotches on the apical margin, 3-lobed, ovate-oblong, 25–35 by 20–25 mm, slightly saccate at base; mid-lobe oblong, emarginate; side lobes obscure; margin undulate, erose; ornaments of 5–7 papillate lines, extending to the apex of the labellum. Column arcuate, 17–20 mm long, apex irregularly erose dentate. Fruit fusiform, 1.8–2.5 by 0.5–1 cm.

description: Terrestrial herbs, evergreen, either with fusiform pseudobulbs bearing one apical foliage leaf (rarely 2 or 3 leaves) or reed-like with several foliage leaves. Flowering shoots mostly 50–100 cm tall. Foliage leaves suberect or spreading, plicate, lanceolate-oblong, prominently petiolate or not. Inflorescences unbranched or rarely branched, few- to many-flowered, erect, mostly as tall as or taller than the foliage leaves, arising from the base of the leafy shoot; with sterile bracts; floral bracts persistent. Flowers medium-sized, resupinate, a few open at a time; in Thai species mostly yellow, often with red markings or red flush. Sepals free, ovate to elliptic, spreading, pubescent on the outside. Petals similar but narrower, glabrous. Labellum fleshy, spurless, with 2 basal flanges joining it to the column at the base or up to one third, usually with explosive mechanism through which the labellum snaps upwards when touched, normally glabrous, sometimes ornamented by small calli. Column rather short; anther incumbent, versatile, with 4 solid pollinia with amorphous viscidium (stipe absent); rostellum flap-like.</br></br>A genus of 40–45 species in tropical Asia, ranging from the Andaman Islands, Thailand and Indochina southwards to Peninsular Malaysia, Java and Sumatra, and eastwards as far as New Guinea and nearby islands; 5 species in Thailand.</br></br>Notes: a more comprehensive version of this account was published in Gard. description: Flowering shoots as reed-like stems, without prominent pseudobulbs. Foliage leaves 5–7, lanceolate-elliptic, acuminate, glabrous, laminas 11.5–21 by (1.6–)2–3.5 cm; petioles to 1.5 cm long. Inflorescences lax, pubescent, 67–92 cm tall; peduncles to 58 cm long; sterile bracts 7–8, lanceolate-oblong, acute, glabrous or hairy, 1.6–5 cm long; rachis 14–37 cm long, 10- to 25-flowered; floral bracts ovate-lanceolate, acuminate, green or purple, 8–10 by 2–4 mm. Flowers to 29 mm in diameter; yellow and tinged red, lateral sepals shiny red at the base, labellum yellow with dark markings, column white or yellow. Sepals ovate-lanceolate, subacute, outside hairy; dorsal sepal 18–25 by 5.2–8 mm; lateral sepals 13–22 by 5–10 mm. Petals narrowly linear-lanceolate, subacute, glabrous, 18–25 by 3–5 mm. Labellum quadrangular, 3-lobed, glabrous, side margins erose or fimbriate-hairy, 8–12 by 8–12 mm; mid-lobe tooth-like, sometimes reflexed, 1–2 by 1.2–2 mm; side lobes square or triangular, obtuse, with calli near the tip, 2–5 by 3.5–5 mm. Column 9–11 mm long; rostellum beaked, obtuse. Ovary (including pedicel) pubescent, 7–18 mm long. Capsule not seen.

description: Small to very large, slender to rather robust primary hemiepiphytes. Stems rather ‘woody’, lower branches rooting, upper ones free and pendent in most species, buds of lateral shoots sometimes perforating the leaf sheath or ± infra-axillary. Leaves distichous, juvenile plants of some species with a shingle form; petiole pulvinate apically, either broad, completely flattened and usually auriculate apically, or morphology normal with a long sheath, sometimes sheath reduced to a pair of hyaline ridges; leaf blade linear-lanceolate to ovate or elliptic, sometimes oblique; primary lateral veins either mostly arising near base of blade, long arcuate, and running into marginal vein near apex, or pinnate, weakly differentiated, forming submarginal collective vein, 1–2 marginal veins also present and these crossing the primary lateral veins to produce a distinctive ‘pothoid’ venation; higher order venation reticulate. Inflorescence morphologically axillary or infra-axillary, solitary or forming short free, very rarely elongating and rooting, synflorescences of several inflorescences, bearing 4–6 or more rigid, coriaceous cataphylls at the base; peduncle very short to very long, sometimes reflexed; spathe ovate to linear, rarely very long, persistent into fruiting; spadix globose, ovoid, cylindrical, ellipsoid or obovoid, sessile to long-stipitate, densely or laxly flowered; flowers bisexual, perigoniate; tepals 4–6, usually arched, free or partially to completely connate; stamens 4–6, free; filaments oblong, flattened, connective slender; thecae ellipsoid, dehiscing by slits; gynoecium with ovary ovoid-oblong or depressed, (2?–)3-locular; ovules 1 per locule, anatropous, funicle short, placenta axile at base of septum; stylar region sometimes as broad as ovary; stigma discoid-hemispherical to umbonate. Fruit an ellipsoid to ovoid 1(–3)-seeded berry, usually red or rarely whitish or dull purple when ripe. Seed ellipsoid, testa smooth, embryo large, endosperm absent.</br></br>Approximately 75 species ranging from Madagascar to India, the subtropical eastern Himalayas, throughout subtropical and tropical Asia into western Oceania and tropical eastern Australia.</br></br>Eight species in Thailand, none endemic.

description: Small to very large, slender to robust, homeophyllous root-climbing hemiepiphyte to 10 m. Flowering shoot much abbreviated, arising from most of the midto distal leaf axils of fertile shoots, bearing a minute prophyll and a few 3–15 mm sequentially longer cataphylls. Inflorescence 1–2 together; peduncle rather stout, 3–25 by 1.5–2.5 mm, erect to variously curved, green to brown-tinged; spathe 4–12 by 4–10 mm, ovate, concave, margins in-rolled, base cordate, clasping and slightly decurrent on the peduncle, apex hooded to recurved, acute to subacute with a rather stout mucro, greenish white to green, occasionally faintly purpletinged, somewhat waxy; spadix stipitate; stipe terete in cross-section, 5–10 by 1–1.25 mm, erect, straight, green; fertile portion globose to ovoid, 3.5–13 by 3–10 mm, pale green to white; flowers ca 1–2 mm diam. Infructescence with 1–5 berries; fruit obclavate to ovoid or ellipsoid, 1–1.8 by 1–1.4 mm, mid-green ripening to scarlet, often with basal chartaceous tepal remains.

description: Trees or shrubs; branchlets pubescent or glabrescent. Leaves spiral, scattered; lamina chartaceous to coriaceous, obovate or elliptic; apex acute, obtuse or obtusely acuminate; base narrowly to broadly cuneate, glabrous or pubescent; venation arched, rarely looped; midrib grooved, flat or slightly raised above, rounded below; secondary veins variable in number; tertiary venation transverse or parallel-reticulate to the secondary veins; stipules absent. Inflorescence axillary, fasciculate, either in axils of leaves or of fallen leaves. Flowers bisexual or both bisexual and pistillate. Calyx a single whorl of 5 free united quincuncial sepals. Corolla tubular, glabrous; tube shorter than or rarely exceeding the lobes; lobes 5, ± erect. Stamens 5, fixed in the upper half of the corolla tube, included, glabrous; filaments short; anthers ovoid, extrorse, basifixed or dorsifixed. Staminodes 5, glabrous. Ovary conoid or globose, 5-locular, pubescent; style exserted short; stigma inconspicuous or lobed. Fruits globose, ovoid or subovoid.</br></br>About 325 pantropical species. Five native species and one introduced in Thailand. Triono et al. (A phylogeny of Pouteria (Sapotaceae) from Malesia and Australasia. Australian Systematic Botany 20: 107-118. 2007) concluded that it might be possible to classify some species of Pouteria in Planchonella Pierre but the evidence was not strong so, in this account, Pouteria is used in the sense of Pennington (Gen. Sapot. 1991).

description: Tree ca 20 m tall; branchlets terete, reddish brown sericeous or glabrescent. Leaves coriaceous, oblanceolate or elliptic, 20–40 by 2.8–5.8 cm; apex narrowly attenuate to broadly acute or obtuse, base narrowly attenuate, margin entire; upper surface glabrous, shining; lower surface minutely appressed puberulous to glabrescent; midrib raised above; secondary veins 12–18 on each side, vanishing near the margin; tertiary veins transverse; marginal vein present; petioles 2.5–3 cm long, raised above, subglabrous. Flowers bisexual, solitary or many-flowered in clusters; pedicels angular, 1.5–2.2 cm long, appressed puberulous. Sepals ovate, rounded, 2.5–5 mm long, both sides puberulous, sometimes ciliate. Corolla 4–6 mm long; tube 1.5–2 mm long; lobes broadly elliptic to suborbicular, 2.5–4 mm long, apex rounded, glabrous. Stamens 1.7–2 mm long; filaments 0.1–0.2 mm long, glabrous; anthers lanceolate, 1.5–2 mm long, glabrous; staminodes lanceolate with a narrowly attenuate apex, ca 2 mm long. Ovary broadly conical, strongly and irregularly longitudinally ribbed, puberulous; style 0–1 mm long, after anthesis glabrous; stigma discoid to capitate. Fruits ellipsoid, slightly asymmetrical, apex acute, base obtuse or rounded, smooth or finely lenticellate, glabrous, 1.5–1.8 cm long, yellowish. Seed ellipsoid, obtuse at base and apex, ca 1.3 cm long.

description: Tree ca 15 m tall; branchlets terete or angular, reddish brown sericeous or glabrescent. Leaves coriaceous, elliptic-oblong or obovate-oblong, 9–14.5 by 3–4.5 cm; apex acute, rarely obtuse or retuse; base cuneate, asymmetrical, decurrent; upper surface glabrous; lower surface reddish brown sericeous, glabrescent except for a few scattered hairs along midrib and veins; midrib grooved above and minutely crested; secondary veins 10–14 on each side, vanishing near the margin; tertiary veins transverse; petioles 2–3.5 cm long, grooved above, thickened in the basal part, reddish brown puberulous or glabrescent. Flowers bisexual and pistillate, 3–5 in clusters; pistillate flowers smaller than bisexual flowers; pedicels angular, 6–8 mm long, reddish brown tomentose. Sepals triangular or broadly ovate, 2.5–3.2 by 1.4–2.5 mm, both sides reddish brown tomentose, margin of the inner ones membranous. Corolla 4.3–5 mm long; tube 2–3 mm long; lobes subquadrangular, 2.3–2.5 by 1.7–2 mm. Stamens 1.7–2 mm long; filaments subulate, 0.8–1 mm long; anthers ovoid, ca 1 mm long, dorsifixed; staminodes lanceolate, spathulate or oblong, 1.2–1.5 by 0.3–0.4 mm. Ovary conoid or globose, reddish brown hirsute; style angular, 2.5–2.8 mm long, glabrous; stigma 5-lobed. Fruits ovoid or subovoid, 0.8–20 by 12–15 by 7–8 mm, glabrous except at base, black, pericarp thin, chartaceous. Seed light brown, ca 15 by 10 by 7 mm.

description: Tree to 30 m tall; branchlets angular, sparsely puberulous or glabrescent. description: Tree ca 25 m tall; branchlets terete, reddish brown tomentose or glabrescent. Leaves chartaceous to thinly coriaceous, narrowly obovate or broadly obovate, 13.5–17.5 by 4.5–8 cm; apex acute; base cuneate, decurrent; upper surface glabrous; lower surface reddish brown tomentose, glabrescent, glaucous, easily rubbed off; midrib flat or grooved above, minutely crested; secondary veins 7–13 on each side, vanishing near the margin, looped in apical part of leaf; tertiary veins transverse and reticulately connected; petioles 2–3 cm long, flat above, thickened at base, reddish brown tomentose or glabrescent. Flowers bisexual, 6–10 in clusters; pedicels angular, 2–4 mm long, reddish brown tomentose. Sepals broadly ovate, 2.2–3 by 2–2.5 mm, reddish brown tomentose outside, glabrous inside, with fimbriate apex; margin of the inner ones membranous. Corolla 2.5–2.8 mm long; tube 1.8–2 mm long, longer than lobes; lobes lanceolate or ovate, 0.8–1 by 0.5–0.8 mm. Stamens 1–1.2 mm long; filaments 0.5–0.7 mm long; anthers ovate, ca 0.5 mm long, dorsifixed; staminodes spathulate or oblanceolate, 0.5–0.8 by 0.1–0.3 mm. Ovary globose, reddish brown tomentose; style 1.7–2 mm long, glabrous; stigma minute. Fruits more or less globose, 2–3.5 by 1.5–2.5 by 1.5–2.5 cm when dry, 2–3-seeded, densely reddish brown puberulous or glabrescent.

description: Tree to 20 m tall; branchlets terete, reddish brown puberulous or glabrescent. Leaves coriaceous, elliptic, ovate, obovate or lanceolate, 6.5–16.5 by 2–7 cm; apex acute to obtuse; base cuneate, decurrent; upper surface glossy, sparsely hairy, glabrescent; lower surface reddish brown or greyish puberulous or glabrescent; midrib flat above somewhat minutely crested; secondary veins 7–13 on each side, vanishing near the margin, looped in apical part of leaf; tertiary veins reticulate but with one vein more distinct and parallel to the secondary veins; petioles 1–2.5 cm long, flat above, reddish brown or blackish puberulous or glabrescent. Flowers bisexual and pistillate, 4–10 in clusters; the bisexual flowers larger than the pistillate flowers; pedicels terete, 2–4 mm long, reddish brown puberulous. Sepals semiorbicular or orbicular, 1.8–2.5 by 2.2–2.5 mm, the outer ones blackish or yellowish puberulous outside, glabrous inside; the inner ones yellowish puberulous outside, glabrous inside, with membranous fimbriate margin. Corolla 3–3.2 mm long, exserted from the calyx in the bisexual flowers, not exserted in the pistillate flowers; tube 0.8–1.2 mm long; lobes broadly ovate or oblanceolate, 1.5–2 by 1.5–2 mm. description: Tree to 35 m tall; branchlets terete, densely brown tomentose or glabrescent. Leaves subcoriaceous, obovate, (12–) 18–19 (–24) by 6–11 cm; apex acute; base cuneate, entire; upper surface sparsely hairy, glabrescent; lower surface pale green, glabrescent; midrib sunken above; secondary veins 7–9 on each side, vanishing near the margin; tertiary veins reticulate, distinct; petioles 1.5–3.5 cm long, puberulous or glabrescent. Flowers 10–14 in clusters; bracts at base of the pedicels brown hirsute, ca 1 mm long; pedicels 2.5–3 mm long, light brown, puberulous. Sepals suborbicular, obtuse, 2.5–3 mm diam., outside pale green and finely brown pilose, glabrous inside. Corolla 3–4 mm long; glabrous, pale green or white; tube ca 3 mm long; lobes ligulate, apex truncate, minutely erose, ca 1.5 mm long. Stamens ca 1.5 mm long; filaments filiform, 1–1.5 mm long; anthers ovate, ca 1 mm long; staminodes subulate, glabrous, 1.5–2 mm long. Ovary depressed globose, densely brown velutinous, shallowly 5-lobed and 5-locular; style ca 2 mm long; stigma minute, glabrous. Fruits light green, ripening dark red, depressed globose, 24–28 by 28–30 mm when fresh, 19–21 by 19–22 mm when dry, deeply 5-lobed, 5-seeded, pericarp 4 mm thick when fresh, sour (fide Maxwell).

description: Tuber depressed globose to elongate, napiform or with several vertical branches, 5–20 by 3–30 cm, rarely with a few annual, globose offsets. Leaves one or several together; petiole 5–70 by 0.5–3 cm, wholly green or background green to pale brownish, variously spotted with whitish, blackish or dark green spots, these elliptic or elongate, isolated or confluent, with or without a greyish wax layer; leaf blade trifoliolate to highly decompound, central main segment often smaller than lateral main segments, 20–120 cm in diam.; leaflets lanceolate to broadly elliptic, 2–45 by 1–35 cm, margin sometimes sinuous or crisped, apex acute or acuminate, upper surface mid green, sometimes with a white, regularly interrupted line along each side of the main vein, sometimes with a dull bluish waxy layer, usually glossy, lower surface pale green or with a pale grey wax layer. Inflorescence developing alongside the developing leaves or later, 1–3 per season; peduncle coloured as petiole or paler, shorter, as long as or longer than petiole; spathe cymbiform, triangular-ovate, apex slightly hooded or not, 5–20 by 2.5–15 cm, pale green on both sides, turning whitish at staminate anthesis, top acute, base within bearing scattered or numerous tiny verrucae; spadix shorter than or as long as spathe, 4–15 cm long; pistillate flower zone cylindrical, 10–35 by 8–10 mm, flowers congested; ovaries obovoid, slightly depressed, 1.8–2 mm in diam, off white; style very short and thick, 0.1–0.4 by 1 mm, off-white; stigma depressed to subhemispherical, 1–1.5 by 0.4–1 mm, entire, or with a central depression, off-white; staminate flower zone cylindrical, 3.5–8 by 1–1.8 cm, flowers more or less distant, lower ones sometimes more congested; staminate flowers 3–5(–6)-androus; stamens 2–2.5 mm long; filaments free, basally or entirely fused into a column 1–1.5 by 0.5–0.8 mm; anthers free or variously fused within one flower, sometimes all fused forming a disc; appendix stipitate (stipe to 10 mm long) conical, 2–5 cm by 10–15 mm, subacute to obtuse, surface deeply corrugated, separating into rod-like papillae and short sinuous muri, off-white. description: Shrubs or small trees; branchlets often terminating in spines. Leaves (sub)opposite, sometimes crowded, entire; stipules absent. Flowers (sub)sessile, solitary (or 2), (sub)terminal or axillary, sometimes a few clustered, actinomorphic, bisexual; bracteoles 2, minute; calyx tube glabrous, long cup-shaped, thick-leathery, adnate to ovary and produced above it; calyx lobes (sepals) 5–9, thick, valvate, persistent; petals red, large, crumpled in bud; stamens numerous, caducous, inserted in several rows within thickened calyx tube above ovary, anthers small; ovary (largely) inferior, 6–13-loculed, in 2 or 3 superposed layers, placentation various with numerous ovules, style exserted, stigma capitate. Fruit berry-like, with leathery rind, crowned by persistent calyx lobes, irregularly dehiscent. Seeds not winged, many, angular, with translucent juicy sarcotesta; cotelydons convolute.</br></br>Two species, one endemic to Socotra (Indian Ocean), one native probably in C and SW Asia, at present widely cultivated.

description: Small to large, slender to robust, seasonally dormant herbs. Stem a subglobose tuber. Leaves 1–2 together; petiole smooth, rough or aculeate, mottled, sheath very short; leaf blade tri-partite to ‘dracontioid’, anterior division simple to trifid, segments simple to pinnatifid, posterior divisions simple to bifid to pedatifid, segments then simple to pinnatifid, ultimate lobes decurrent, ovate-elliptic to triangular, acute to acuminate; primary lateral veins pinnate, running into distinct marginal vein; higher order venation reticulate. Inflorescence solitary, appearing before or with leaf; peduncle much shorter than petiole, although predominantly epigeal, similar in appearance and texture to petiole; spathe margins not overlapping, upper spathe strongly hooded, thick, marcescent; spadix much shorter than spathe, conical to ovoid-conoid, stipitate, fertile to apex; flowers bisexual, perigone absent; stamens ca 6 or more per flower, free, crowded densely together with those of neighbouring flowers; filaments oblong, flattened, connective slender; thecae oblong-ellipsoid, dehiscing by apical, pore-like slits; gynoecium elongate-flaskshaped, ovary 1-locular, ovule 1, anatropous to hemianatropous, funicle short, placenta basal to subparietal, stylar region greatly elongated, straight or somewhat curved, projecting well beyond stamens; stigma small, scarcely or no broader than style. Fruit a globose berry, pericarp densely covered with conical prickles or smooth, with conspicuous, persistent style remnant, dark green. Seeds reniform, black or very dark brown, testa hard, thick, verrucose.</br></br>Two species of seasonally dormant tuberous-stemmed geophytic herbs with complex umbrella-like leaves superficially similar to (although ontogenetically quite distinct from) those of Amorphophallus. Despite the overall similarity of Pycnospatha(especially P. arietina) to various Amorphophallus species, they are not at all closely related. Two species in Thailand.

description: Robust, medium to large, tuberous seasonally dormant herb, to 2.5 m tall. Stem an irregular globose tuber 4.5–15 by 2.5–7.5 cm. Leaves solitary to two together, produced after, rarely with, the inflorescence; petiole (adult) 50–130 cm by 6–10 mm, smooth, rough or aculeate, if aculeate then with scattered to rather dense prickles 0.8–1 mm long, greyish green to pale grey, mottled blackish green to reddish brown; petiolar sheath very short, inconspicuous; leaf blade (adult) ‘dracontioid’, up to 60 by 100 cm, anterior division trifid with the central partition bipinnate, posterior segments with secondary and tertiary segments irregularly pinnatifid, all ultimate lobes decurrent, ovate-elliptic to triangular, acute to acuminate, glossy dark green with a slight bluish green sheen. Inflorescence solitary, appearing before or with leaf; peduncle much shorter than petiole, 8.5–18 cm by 8–10 mm, similar in appearance and texture to petiole; spathe strongly hooded, 9–20 by 3–5 cm, margins not overlapping, thick, exterior pale grey with very dense purple speckling, interior deep purple, marcescent following anthesis; spadix conical to ovoid-conical, shortly stipitate, much shorter than spathe, 4–6 by 1–1.5 cm, pale greyish, stained purple; gynoecium with prominent straight style to 5 mm. Infructescence naked or partially enclosed in decaying spathe remains; fruits globose, ca 2 cm diam., pericarp densely covered with conical prickles, with conspicuous, persistent, style remnant, dark green when ripe.

description: Annual or perennial herbs. Roots fasciculate. Leaves alternate, pedately, or subpinnately lobate to sect, or compound, rarely simple; petioles dilated downwards into the sheath. Inflorescences definite, loosely corymbiform or modified from this, or single-flowered. Flowers bisexual, actinomorphic, heterochlamydeous, usually opening flat. Sepals 3 or 5, usually sepaloid. Petals 3, 5, or more, petaloid, usually larger than sepals, with 1, rarely to 3 nectaries. Stamens numerous, anthers lateral or extrorse. Carpels uniovular, ovule basal, ascending. Achenes many, aggregated; pericarps thick, usually without veins on lateral sides.</br></br>About 650 species in all continents. Three species in Thailand.

description: Small to medium-sized, seasonally dormant, lithophytic or epiphytic herbs. Stem a subglobose tuber, producing erect to spreading, unbranched or branching stolons which then produce small, ovoid bulbils at nodes, each with numerous, apically revolute or flexuose barbs (the tips of minute cataphylls). Leaves 1–2 together; petioles robust or slender; petiolar sheath relatively short; leaf blade cordate-lanceolate to cordate-ovate, peltate, acuminate, usually thinly membranaceous; basal ribs well-developed; primary lateral veins pinnate, forming submarginal collective vein very close to margin, marginal vein also present; secondary and tertiary laterals arising from the primaries at a wide angle, then arching towards leaf margin and forming inconspicuous interprimary collective veins (‘colocasioid’ venation); higher order venation reticulate. Inflorescence solitary, appearing before or after leaves; peduncle shorter than petiole; spathe strongly constricted between tube and limb, sometimes with secondary constriction above the spadix, lower spathe with convolute margins, persistent, enclosing pistillate zone and sterile zone of spadix; spathe limb yellow or red (the latter not yet seen in Thailand), longer than tube, fully expanded or remaining convolute and opening only at base, sometimes becoming reflexed, later caducous; spadix sessile or subsessile, much shorter than spathe; flowers unisexual, perigone absent; pistillate flower zone subcylindrical, about half as long as spathe tube, separated from staminate zone by much narrower zone of sterile staminate flowers; pistillate flowers lacking staminodes; ovary subcylindrical to subglobose, 1-locular or partially 2–4– locular at apex, ovules many, placentae 2–4 and parietal or 1 and basal; stylar region very shortly attenuate; stigma discoid-subcapitate or slightly 3–4-lobed; staminate flower zone ellipsoid or subclavate, fertile to apex, obtuse; staminate flowers 2–3-androus, stamens connate into cuneate-clavate, 4–6-sulcate synandrium, fused filaments distinct, synconnectives somewhat excavated at apex; thecae 4–6, oblong to ellipsoid, dehiscing by apical pore-like slits; synandrodia elongated. Fruit an obovoid to globose many-seeded berry. Seed ellipsoid to subglobose, covered by thick, succulent sarcotesta, or testa verruculose to irregularly costate.</br></br>Four species, two in Thailand, neither endemic, R. vivipara throughout the Old World tropics. Remusatia is immediately recognizable by producing elongate, erect to spreading, aerial stolons bearing clusters of barbed bulbils along their length.</br></br>Gonatanthus is currently included in the circumscription of Remusatia. Formerly, it was differentiated on the presence of a lower spathe with constrictions corresponding to the interstice between the pistillate and staminate flower zones and another above the pistillate flower zone, and basal (vs. parietal placentation). Molecular evidence is beginning to indicate that merging the two genera may have been too hasty.

description: Small to medium, slender, epiphytic or lithophytic, seasonally dormant herb to 25 cm. Stem a globose tuber 1–2.55 cm diam., epigeal, covered with the fibrous remains of petioles and cataphylls, often a few tubers together; stolons numerous, spreading, much branched, 10–20 cm by 1–3 mm; bulbils ellipsoid, 0.5 by 2 mm, barbs recurved, ca 1 mm. Leaves 3–4 together; petiole slender, 15–40 cm; petiolar sheath occupying lower ¼–⅓; leaf blade ovate to oblongovate peltate, 8–23.5 by 7–14.5 cm, acute or slightly acuminate, base shallowly cordate, sinus 5–45 mm wide; basal ribs well-developed; primary lateral veins 4–5 each side, radiating from petiole and pinnately from midrib of main lobe; secondary venation pinnate from primary veins; dull green on both surfaces, areas between primary veins often purple below and/or above. Inflorescences appearing when plants in leaf, usually one per tuber; peduncle 6–10 cm; spathe 14–22.5 cm long, with two constrictions, one between tube and spathe limb and another above the spadix; lower spathe globose, 1–1.5 by ca 1 cm, green; spathe limb 13–21 cm; the lower part of limb separated in two parts by a constriction; lower subglobose, 1.5–2.5 cm, opening to reveal staminate part of spadix, upper narrowly lanceolate apex long-acuminate, 11.5–21 cm by 6–15 mm, membranous, yellow or yellow-green on both surfaces, erect, elongate, fully opening only for a short time (less than 4 hours), then withering; spadix 2–2.5 cm, much shorter than the spathe; pistillate zone 5.5–7.5 by 3.5–4.5 mm, with 3–4 whorls of staminodes at top and 1–2 whorls at base, ovary globose-ellipsoid, green; stigma capitate, paler; sterile interstice slender, 4–5 mm, tapering upwards, covered with elongated synandrodes, yellow; staminate flower zone clavate, ca 10 by 4 mm, violet to purplish white; synandria 0.6 by 1 mm, violet to purplish white. Fruiting spathe ellipsoid, splitting to reveal globose berries ripening red.

description: Medium to large, generally rather robust, epiphytic, lithophytic, rarely (in Thailand) terrestrial, seasonally dormant herb to 75 cm. Stem a depressed globose tuber 3.5–5 cm diam., partially epigeal to hypogeal, generally covered with the fibrous remains of petioles and cataphylls, often several tubers together; stolons stout, erect, simple or little-branched, 20–40 cm by 5 mm; bulbils ellipsoid, 0.5 by 2.5 mm, barbs recurved, ca 1.5 mm.
