description: Moderate to very large or gigantic, slender to very robust secondary hemiepiphytic, rarely rheophytic, evergreen herbs with abundant trichosclereids. Stem root-climbing, less often prostrate, compressed terete to rectangular in cross-section, often producing long flagelliform shoots with reduced cataphylls and abundant dimorphic clasping and feeding roots. Leaves several to many, distichous to spiro-distichous and often forming tufts at the tips of active shoots, juvenile shingle plants occurring in some species; petiole pulvinate apically and basally, channelled to carinate, rarely sub-terete; petiolar sheath reaching to the pulvinus in many species, somewhat less often reaching only to half-way along petiole, marcescent to deciduous, sometimes decomposing to conspicuous net-fibrous mass; leaf blade lanceolate or oblong, ± oblique, entire, perforate or pinnatifid to pinnatisect, sometimes very large, lobes often subfalcately narrowed; primary lateral veins pinnate, running into marginal vein, often not differentiated from secondaries; secondary laterals ± parallel-pinnate; higher order venation reticulate, but in some species so deeply embedded in leaf tissue as to be almost invisible. Inflorescence usually solitary, occasionally several produced in a synflorescence, arising either on the main clinging axis or, more commonly, from free lateral shoots; peduncle relatively short; spathe boat-shaped, deciduous to marcescent, rarely persistent (not in Thailand); spadix subcylindrical, conical, clavate, sessile to stipitate, mostly shorter than spathe; flowers bisexual, perigone absent; stamens 4, free; filaments oblong-linear; anthers much shorter than filaments, connective slender; thecae ellipsoid, dehiscing by longitudinal slits; gynoecium obconic-prismatic to oblong, truncate, ovary 1-to partially 2-locular; ovules few to many, anatropous, funicle long, placentae parietal to basal, sometimes axile, partial septa variably intrusive; stylar region well developed, equal to broader than ovary, usually truncate apically, sometimes elongate-conical; stigma broadly elliptic or oblong and then transverse, or longitudinal, or punctate-prominent. Infructescence a many-seeded monsterocarp with stylar region deciduous at maturity, revealing a cavity with red, yellow or white pulp. Seed oblong, testa thin, smooth.</br></br>About 100 species of secondary hemiepiphytic, very rarely rheophytic, evergreen climbing herbs. Rhaphidophora is one of the least well understood aroid genera in Thailand and suffers from inadequate field observations and collections. These often massive plants are difficult to represent on herbarium sheets which often show only the most easily sampled portions. Crucially, many historical types are poorly collected, often ill-preserved and at times mixed. Furthermore, our knowledge of the lianescent aroid flora of most countries neighbouring Thailand is still inadequate.</br></br>For these reasons, and in an attempt to make this account useful in the field, we include all possible Rhaphidophora taxa which may occur in Thailand in the key below, un-numbered, non-bold, italic, while providing descriptions only of those that are definitely known.

description: Small to medium-sized, heterophyllous rheophyte, very rarely short liane, to 75 cm; juvenile plants shingling. Stem smooth, mid- to dark green, with very sparse petiolar sheath fibre; feeding roots densely scaly. Leaves distichous, (juvenile) appressed and shingling; (adult) erect or spreading and scattered on pre-adult shoots, tending to become distally clustered on adult shoots; petiole narrowly canaliculate to carinate, 8–31 by 0.3–1.5 cm, smooth, apical and basal pulvini prominent; petiolar sheath prominent, extending to the apical pulvinus, variably persistent and mostly degrading into semipersistent weak fibres; leaf blade entire in seedling and pre-adult individuals, entire, pinnatipartite or pinnatisect in adult plants, narrowly lanceolate to oblong-elliptic, slightly oblique, 21–51 by 2–23 cm, subcoriaceous to slightly fleshy, base decurrent, apex acuminate with a moderately prominent tubule; midrib prominently raised abaxially, sunken adaxially; primary venation pinnate, raised abaxially, slightly impressed adaxially; interprimaries sub-parallel to primaries, slightly raised abaxially, ± flush adaxially, often forming a weak reticulum; secondary venation prominently reticulate, slightly raised; tertiary venation a network of broadly spaced tessellate veins arising at ca 90° from the midrib and crossing the primaries and interprimaries. Inflorescence one to three together, subtended by a prominent cataphyll degrading to fibres before anthesis; peduncle terete, 8–12 by 0.2–0.4 cm; spathe narrowly canoe-shaped, stoutly beaked, 6.5–7 by 1–1.5 cm, stiffly fleshy, dirty white at anthesis, soon falling; spadix cylindrical, sessile, inserted perpendicular to peduncle, 4.5–7 by 0.6–1 cm, dull whitish; stylar region rather well developed, mostly rhombohexagonal, ca 1–1.5 by 1–1.5 mm, truncate; stigma elliptic, longitudinally orientated, occasionally almost circular, ca 0.5 by 0.3 mm, often very prominent especially in dried material; anthers exserted at anthesis. Infructescence 7–9 by 1–2 cm, often markedly irregular in outline, mid-green when ripe.

description: Very large, often enormous, very robust, pachycaul, heterophyllous secondary hemiepiphyte to 20 m or more. Stem robust, 3–5 cm diam., terete. description: Large, slender to rather robust, pachycaul, heterophyllous secondary hemiepiphyte to 10 m. Stem 0.7–2.5 cm diam., terete in cross-section. Infructescence 12–15 by 3–3.5 cm when ripe, subtended by persistent withered spathe remains early in development, stylar tissue falling to expose ovary cavities with the seeds embedded in copious, pale orange pulp.

description: Medium to large, moderately robust, pachycaul, homeophyllous secondary hemiepiphyte to 15 m. Stems terete, ca 2 cm diam., mid-green, densely grey-ramentose when young, later glabrous. description: Very large, occasionally enormous, slender to rather robust, pachycaul, heterophyllous secondary hemiepiphyte to 20 m; juvenile plants shingling. Stems smooth, light green, with sparse to copious prophyll, cataphyll and petiolar sheath fibre, especially at the stem apices; feeding roots densely ramentose-scaly. Leaves distichous; petiole shallowly grooved, upper part ± terete, 9–65 by 0.2–1.5 cm, smooth, apical and basal pulvinus prominent; petiolar sheath prominent, membranaceous, slightly unequal, extending almost to or reaching the apical pulvinus, short-lived, soon degrading into persistent netted fibres, these eventually falling to leave a prominent, slightly corky scar; leaf blade (juvenile) overlapping in the manner of roof shingles, entire, lanceolate, 5–11 by 3.5–6 cm, base slightly cordate; leaf blade (adult) free, entire, pinnatipartite, pinnatisect or pinnatifid, 14–94 by 10–44 cm, broadly oblong-elliptic to oblong lanceolate, slightly oblique, membranaceous to chartaceous & sub-coriaceous, base truncate and very briefly decurrent, apex acute to acuminate, individual pinnae 1–10 cm wide, frequently perforated basally adjacent to the midrib, thus appearing stilted; midrib very prominently raised abaxially, slightly sunken adaxially; primary venation pinnate, raised abaxially, somewhat impressed adaxially, 2–4 primary veins per pinna; interprimaries sub-parallel to primaries, slightly raised abaxially, slightly impressed adaxially; secondary venation strongly reticulate, slightly raised; tertiary venation invisible. Inflorescence solitary to several together, first inflorescence subtended by a membranaceous prophyll and one or more cataphylls, these soon degrading to netted fibres, subsequent inflorescences subtended by one or more soon degrading cataphylls, the whole forming a mass of developing and open inflorescences and developing infructescences partially concealed by persistent netted cataphyll and prophyll remains; peduncle slightly laterally compressed to terete, 6–26 by 1–1.5 cm; spathe narrowly canoe-shaped, stoutly beaked, 10–30 by 3–5 cm, stiffly fleshy, dull yellow at anthesis, gaping wide at female receptivity and then soon falling to leave a large straight scar at the base of the spadix; spadix cylindrical, sessile, inserted ± level on peduncle, 9–26 by 1.5–2 cm, dull green to dirty white; stylar region rather well developed, mostly rhombohexagonal, 1.5–2 by ca 2 mm, slightly conical; stigma punctiform to slightly elliptic, if the latter then mostly longitudinally orientated, ca 0.3–0.5 by 0.2–0.4 mm; anthers barely exserted at anthesis. Infructescence 14–27 by 3-3.5 cm, dark green ripening to dull orange, stylar tissue abscising to reveal orange ovary cavity pulp.

description: Small to moderate, somewhat slender, leptocaul, homeophyllous secondary hemiepiphyte to 5 m. Stems puberulent-scabrid to asperous, especially on older growth, climbing stems weakly rectangular to ± terete in cross-section, free stems ± terete in cross-section, often branching extensively and growing to moderate lengths, hanging under their own weight, dull brown, without prophyll, cataphyll and petiolar sheath fibre. Leaves weakly spiralled and often sparsely arranged on adherent and proximal portions of free shoots, densely spirally-distichous distally on flowering shoots; petiole grooved adaxially, 4–9.5 by 0.2–0.3 cm, smooth, with moderate apical and prominent basal pulvini; petiolar sheath slightly prominent, extending beyond the apical pulvinus by two ligules, very soon drying and falling in strips to leave a continuous scar from the petiole base, around the top of the apical pulvinus and back to the base; leaf blade entire, narrowly elliptic to elliptic-lanceolate to oblong or oblanceolate, 6–24 by 2–10 cm, very softly coriaceous, upper surfaces slightly glossy, lower surfaces pale satin-matte, drying markedly discolorous, dark brown above, pale brown below, base cuneate to acute or sub-ovate, briefly decurrent, apex acute to ovate-acuminate, with a prominent apiculate tubule; midrib slightly raised abaxially, slightly sunken adaxially; primary venation pinnate, slightly raised abaxially, prominent (dark veins against pale lamina) in dried material; interprimaries parallel to, but much less distinctive than primaries, very slightly raised abaxially; secondary and tertiary venation ± invisible in fresh material, barely visible in dried specimens, reticulate. Inflorescence solitary, subtended by a fully developed foliage leaf and a very quickly falling cataphyll; peduncle compressed-cylindrical, 1.5–5 by 0.15–0.4 cm; spathe ovate-elliptic, stoutly long-beaked, 3–5 by 0.4–1 cm, thickly fleshy, exterior minutely puberulent, dull yellowish at anthesis, soon falling to leave a substantial, slightly oblique scar; spadix slender cylindrical, sessile, inserted level on peduncle, 3–3.5 by 0.4–0.5 cm, dull yellow-white; stylar region rather well developed, mostly rhombohexagonal, 1.9–2.4 by ca 2 mm, truncate; stigma punctiform, ca 0.3 mm diam., prominent in dried material; anthers barely exserted at anthesis. Infructescence oblong-cylindrical, 2.5–4 by 1–1.2 cm, ripening dirty white, stylar plates sloughing away to reveal amber coloured pulp and pale grey seeds.

description: Large, occasionally very large, robust, pachycaul homeophyllous secondary hemiepiphyte to 20 m. Stems smooth, climbing stems markedly rectangular in cross-section, the angles often winged, the surfaces between slightly convex, free stems spreading, irregularly four-angled in cross-section, sometime irregularly terete, branching little, growing moderate lengths, green, later mid-brown, with very sparse to very copious untidy prophyll, cataphyll and petiolar sheath fibre at the apices of active shoots. description: Very large to gigantic, very robust, pachycaul, homeophyllous secondary hemiepiphyte climbing 40 m or more. Inflorescences in fascicles of up to four per synflorescence on the tips of primary clinging shoots, as synflorescence develops primary axis reiterating, overtopping the synflorescence such that the inflorescence cluster is displaced and appears to be produced laterally; peduncle green, 15–18 by ca 2 cm; spathe oblong-cymbiform, 20–27 by ca 16 cm, very thick, initially gaping, then spreading, greenish white, then light yellow, opening deep yellow internally; spadix cylindrical, 18–25 by ca 2.5 cm, sessile, yellow-green at anthesis, apex obtuse, base oblique; stigma pronounced-punctiform. description: Medium to large, occasionally very large, moderately robust, leptocaul to semipachycaul, homeophyllous secondary hemiepiphyte to 20 m. Stems smooth, climbing stems rectangular in cross-section, the angles often slightly winged and surfaces between slightly concave, free stems rectangular to sub-terete in cross-section, green, later mid-brown, without prophyll, cataphyll and petiolar sheath fibre. Leaves distichous on adherent and free shoots, those distal on flowering shoots densely so; petiole deeply grooved adaxially, 1–8.5 by 0.15–0.3 cm, smooth, apical and basal pulvini weakly defined; petiolar sheath very prominent, extending to and encircling the apical pulvinus, briefly ligulate, very soon drying and falling to leave a continuous conspicuous scar from the petiole base, around the top of the apical pulvinus and back to the base; leaf blade entire, lanceolate-elliptic to falcate-lanceolate, slightly to markedly oblique, 4.5–32 by 1.75–8.5 cm, thinly coriaceous, upper surfaces slightly glossy, lower surfaces semimatte, base sub-acute to briefly truncate, apex acute to slightly attenuate, with a prominent apiculate tubule; midrib slightly raised abaxially, slightly sunken adaxially; primary venation pinnate, slightly raised abaxially and adaxially; interprimaries parallel to primaries and only slightly less prominent, very slightly raised abaxially and adaxially; secondary and tertiary venation ± obscure in fresh material, visible as a faint reticulum in dried specimens. Inflorescence solitary, subtended by a fully developed foliage leaf; peduncle compressed-cylindrical, 2–8.5 by 0.15–0.5 cm; spathe narrowly elliptic, very shortly, stoutly beaked, 4.5–7.5 by 1–3 cm, thinly but stiffly fleshy, dull yellow at anthesis, paler internally, soon falling; spadix weakly clavate-cylindrical, sessile, inserted ± level on peduncle, 3–6 by 1–2.5 cm; stylar region mostly rhombohexagonal, 1–2 by 1.5–2 mm, truncate; stigma punctiform, raised, ca 0.25–0.3 mm diam.; anthers exserted at anthesis. description: Small, clustering palm, dioecious or polygamous. Stem slender, bamboo-like, erect, covered by persistent leaf bases, eventually naked and conspicuously ringed by leaf scars. Leaf palmate, induplicate; sheath dissolving into loose mesh of interlocking fibres; petiole elongate, slender, unarmed; adaxial hastula small, abaxial one absent; blade circular in outline, entire to deeply bifid, splitting in single- to several-folded, apically toothed segments, tranverse veinlets conspicuous. Inflorescence interfoliar, branching to 1–3 orders; peduncle short, often contained in leaf sheath; prophyll splitting longitudinally on abaxial face; peduncular bract lacking; rachis longer than peduncle, with tubular rachis bracts, the proximal 1–2 conspicuously enlarged; rachillae spreading to crowded in male inflorescences, with spirally arranged, solitary, rarely paired flowers. Male and female flowers similar in overall shape, size and in the perianth parts; sepals fused in shallow cup-shaped calyx; petals much longer than calyx, connate into fleshy corolla tube, further elongated especially in the male flowers by stalk-like extension of the receptacle above the calyx; stamens six, adnate basally to corolla tube, with short anthers, staminodes when present reduced in size; gynoecium of three free carpels, glabrous, apically with minute tube-shaped stigma. Fruit usually developing from one carpel only, globose, purplish brown to white at maturity; epicarp smooth; mesocarp fleshy; endocarp thin. Seed with homogeneous endosperm and lateral intrusion of seed coat. Germination remote-tubular.</br></br>Eight species in S China to Indo-China. Two species in Thailand.

description: Terrestrial, rhizomatous herbs; the creeping stem-like rhizome rooting from its nodes. Flowering shoots terminal, erect from a decumbent base, 20–51.8 cm tall. Foliage leaves 3–7, scattered to crowded on the stem, petiolate, sheathing at base. Inflorescence spicate; bracts glabrous to pubescent on the dorsal side. Flowers 7 to many, more or less resupinate. Sepals free, 1- to 2-veined, glabrous; dorsal sepal 2.5–7.8 mm long. Petals adherent to the dorsal sepal. Labellum basally adnate to the column, straight (i.e., not twisted), 4.2–9 mm long along the mid line, differentiated into hypochile, mesochile, and epichile; hypochile saccate (but not protruding below the bases of the lateral sepals when the flower is viewed from the side), inside with 1 stout appendage on either side and divided longitudinally by a low keel that raises abruptly in the apical two-thirds to three-fourths into an erect bicarinate semi-discoid callus; mesochile usually with one pair of (sub)entire lateral flanges; epichile bilobed or simple and rounded-truncate. Column straight (i.e., not twisted); stigma bipartite, flat; rostellum triangular, bifid; viscidium 1, naked; anther versatile: pollinia 2, basitonous. Ovary glabrous. Fruit a capsule dehiscing by 6 longitudinal slits.</br></br>A genus of ca. 22 species. The largely Indomalesian distribution reaches Sri Lanka and the Himalayas in the west, Japan in the north and Vanuatu and New Caledonia in the southeast; 3 species in Thailand.

description: Herbs amphibious or terrestrial, annual or perennial, glabrous. Stem erect or ascending, or floating. Leaves decussate, whorled or rarely alternate, sessile or short-petiolate. Bracts leaf-like or scale-like; bracteoles 2 or absent. Flowers sometimes heterostylous (not in Thailand), sessile, solitary in the axils of bracts along the main axis or in lateral or terminal racemes; calyx tube campanulate, enclosing the ovary, calyx lobes 3–6, valvate, persistent, tooth-like calyx appendages or small folds sometimes present between the calyx lobes; nectaries often present at the base of the calyx tube; petals 0–6, minute or large and showy, usually crumpled in bud; stamens 1–6, episepalous, inserted in the calyx tube in the lower half, anthers dorsifixed, introrse; ovary superior, 2–4-locular, placentation axile becoming free-central at maturity, stigma capitate (or 2-lobed, India). Fruit a septicidally dehiscent capsule opening by 2–4 valves, the valves with microscopic horizontal striations; one valve crowned by the persistent style. Seeds numerous or few, semi-ovoid or ellipsoid, with mucilaginous hairs.</br></br>Worldwide ca 45 species, mainly (sub)tropical. One species in Australia, 24 species in Asia; in Thailand 6 species, and two more species to be expected (see key); none endemic.

description: Herbs, amphibious or terrestrial, annual. Stems erect, branched or simple, to 50 cm tall, with 4 distinct white wings running into the leaf or bract margins. Leaves decussate, sessile; lamina lanceolate to ovate or oblong, to 25 mm long, cordate at base, subobtuse at apex. Bracts on main stem like foliage leaves, bracts on lateral inflorescences lanceolate or oblong, spreading or recurved, cordate at base, 2–3 times as long as subtended flower; bracteoles 2, minute, ca 0.2 mm long. Flowers subsessile, usually borne on contracted lateral branches or occasionally on the main stem; calyx tube campanulate, becoming subglobose in fruit, 1–1.5 mm long; calyx lobes 4, triangular, 0.5 mm long, acuminate, usually minutely toothed at margin; calyx appendages absent; petals pink or purple, obovate, equalling or to twice as long as calyx lobes, persistent in fruit; stamens 4, inserted at about one-third up the calyx tube; anthers as long as or or slightly exceeding the tips of the calyx teeth; ovary globose; style 1–1.5 mm long, persistent; stigma exserted. Capsules globose, 1–1.5 mm diam., included within the calyx tube, opening by 3 valves. Seeds subovoid, ca 0.5 mm long.

description: Moderate-sized clustering, pleonanthic or hapaxanthic dioecious palms. Stem subterranean, decumbent or shortly erect, internodes short, usually obscured by the persistent leaf bases. Leaves pinnate; leaf sheath and petiole elongate, open, not forming a crownshaft, armed with flattened spines, arranged in rows or whorls; leaflet single-fold, except for the terminal pair which is usually joined, linear or sigmoid in outline, equally spaced and orientated in one plane or grouped and pointing in different directions, acuminate. Inflorescence axillary and emerging though a groove along the abaxial surface of the leaf base or inflorescences terminal and subtended by reduced leaves, sometimes spicate, male inflorescences usually branched to 1 more order than female; peduncle short; prophyll rather inconspicuous, partly enclosed within the leaf sheath slit. Male flowers borne in dyads, sunken in pits, exserted at anthesis; calyx tubular, 3-lobed; corolla often with a short stalk-like base, and a long proximal tube, bearing 3 triangular, valvate lobes; stamens 6, borne at the mouth of corolla tube, filament short, anthers rounded to elongate. Female flowers either solitary or coupled with a sterile male flower in dyads, gynoecium tricarpellate, triovulate, covered with flattened scales, stigmas 3. Fruit (1–)3-seeded, globose to pear-shaped or ellipsoidal, with apical stigmatic remains; epicarp covered in somewhat irregular vertical rows of reflexed scales, the scale tips spinelike and upward pointing, mesocarp thin at maturity, endocarp not differentiated. Seed with thick sarcotesta, endosperm homogeneous, the apex with a pit. Germination adjacent ligular; eophyll entire, bifid.</br></br>Twenty species in India (Assam) to S China and W Malesia. Four species in Thailand.

description: Terrestrial, deciduous, tuberous herbs, usually glabrous. Flowering shoots unbranched. Foliage leaves one to few, in the Asian species cauline and scattered in the lower portion of the stem, ovate-lanceolate or elliptic. Usually with one to few erect or deflexed sterile bracts above the foliage leaves. Inflorescence terminal, racemose; floral bracts deflexed, much longer than the ovary. Flowers many, not resupinate, in the Asian species ranging from pink to white or yellow. Sepals and petals unlobed, spreading, basally fused to each other and to the labellum for about one fifth to one quarter of their length, margins often denticulate or erose. Labellum unlobed, deeply galeate, size of the entrance ranging from one half to two thirds of the galea width, with an apical flap; spurs two, pendent, on both sides of the ovary and shorter to somewhat longer than it. Column with elongate undifferentiated column-part; anther pendent, pollinia 2, sectile; stigma as a flap; rostellum shield-like, in the Asian species with 2 lateral viscidia. Ovary (including pedicel) with pronounced ridges.</br></br>A genus of ca. 90 species distributed mainly in Africa with two widespread species in India, Sri Lanka, Nepal, Bhutan, Myanmar, Thailand and China; predominantly found in grassland or savanna, less commonly in forested habitats: a single species recently recorded in Thailand.

description: Seasonally dormant, tuberous, geophytic herbs. Stem a depressed-globose tuber. Leaves entire, sagittate-hastate or pedatisect (only the last in Thailand). Infructescence with lower part of spathe caducous or remaining; fruits ovoid, 1 (or 2)-seeded. Seeds with endosperm.</br></br>Eight species occurring from Bhutan, Cambodia, China, India, Indonesia, Laos, Myanmar, Nepal, Vietnam; three species in Thailand, one endemic.

description: Stem a subglobose to depressed globose tuber, producing annual offsets. Leaves one or a few together; petiole 3–60 cm long, variable in colour, uniform, striped or spotted, ranging from green to purple; leaf blade pedatisect, with 7–13 lobes; lobes elliptic to lanceolate, acute, margin flat or sinuous, entire or occasionally crenate, upper surface mid to dark rich velvety green, with or without reddish main vein or splashed with golden spots along the main vein, lower surface pale to grey green, sometimes with scattered reddish purple spots. Inflorescence solitary; peduncle 2–20 cm long; spathe base convolute, ovoid, occasionally with one or a few shallow keels, top more or less constricted, outside pale or mid green, dull mid to dark brown, with or without a few reddish or blackish brown spots or stripes, inside white or whitish green; spathe limb 6–17 by 4–6 cm, ovate to oblong-ovate, cymbiform, slightly hooded, acuminate to caudate, often keeled at the midrib, outside pale or mid green, dirty greenish, dirty pale brownish, with or without a few indistinct darker spots, inside whitish, pale green, with or without a few scattered blackish purple spots; spadix shorter than spathe; pistillate flower zone cylindrical or slightly conical, 2.5–10 by 4–8 mm; ovary ovoid to oblong-ovoid, unilocular, uni- or bi-ovulate; stigma very small, in a depression of the top of the ovary or ring-like surrounding the depression; sterile zone elongate, narrowly fusiform-conical, 2–6 cm long, 3–7 mm diam. at the base, entirely covered by staminodes; lower staminodes with rhombic, flat base and aristate to clavate process, the latter strongly bent upwards, white, the clavate part yellowish white or occasionally dark red, subbasal staminodes exclusively aristate, strongly pointing upwards parallel to the spadix axis, creamish; upper staminodes fused into vertical ridges with numerous, irregular, short processes, often arranged in ridges, white; staminate flower zone cylindrical, 6–10 by 2–7 mm, upper flowers often sterile and differently shaped; staminate flowers white, the upper ones often sterile and subclavate to spathulate or occasionally aristate; appendix subsessile or more distinctly stipitate, cylindrical or rarely fusiform, 1.5–4.5 cm long, 2–6 mm diam., slightly tapering to the obtuse top, base attenuate to the stipe, surface smooth or strongly corrugate, cream or more rarely greyish brown with purple spots, stipe sometimes ridged-verrucate. Fruits with persistent spathe base; obovoid to ellipsoid, pale green when mature, corrugate and shallowly grooved.

description: Medium-sized, seasonally dormant herb. Stem a depressed globose tuber to ca 4 by 2.5 cm, producing annual, short, fusiform offsets, these covered by woody scales. Leaves few together; petiole very pale dirty greyish green, with a very faint reddish purplish flush at the base, 23 cm by 7 mm, smooth; leaf blade pedatisect, ca 21 cm diam., 5-foliolate, the basal-most leaflet with a small extra lobe, anterior leaflet elliptic, 13 by 6 cm, acuminate, adaxially dark velvety green, main vein flushed with reddish purple, abaxially paler dirty green, veins (especially in unfolding stage) flushed with reddish purple, slightly glossy, margin with numerous, small undulations and flushed with violet, smallest (basal) leaflets strongly asymmetrical, 8 by 3 cm. Inflorescence appearing with the leaf; peduncle 4 cm by 4–5 mm, smooth, largely subterranean, pale greenish with violet striations; spathe 8.5–13 cm long, coriaceous; lower part 3.5–4 by 1 cm, convolute with a faint, mainly dorsal constriction at the middle, coinciding with a more or less distinct thickened annulus on the interior opposite the middle part of the upper staminodial zone; spathe limb triangular, horizontally flexed, 5–9 by 3–5 cm, acute, exterior lower part dirty greenish with reddish purple flushes, constriction reddish purple and green striate, above constriction whitish greenish with pale reddish purple, tiny spots, base interior with a slippery, shiny, waxy layer, lower half glossy pale green, above constriction dull dirty whitish, limb exterior semiglossy whitish greenish with faint pale purplish spots, interior uniformly dull whitish green; spadix shorter than spathe, 5–8.5 cm; pistillate flower zone broadly conical, 5–12 by 7–11 mm, flowers congested; ovaries angular-globose, 1–1.5 mm, white, with 3 to 4 prominent, narrowly or broadly conical projections (ca 0.5 mm long) around the stigma; stigma in depression between projections, very small, nearly invisible; sterile interstice 15–18 mm, covered with two types of staminodes; staminodes of lower staminodial whorl consisting of clavate/spathulate staminodes, lowermost ones to ca 7 mm long, stalked, top part bent downwards and anvil shaped, others near-sessile, horizontal, clavate part dorso-ventrally flattened and often two-topped, all parts dark purple; upper staminodes contiguous with the lower ones but consisting of only the basal part without any extension, narrowly spindle shaped, to ca 5 by 1 mm, raised, flattened, whitish; staminate flower zone cylindrical, top and base oblique, 10–21 by 4.5–8 mm; stamens ca 1 mm long, narrowly rectangular in cross-section, orangeish yellow, connective very broad, pores rounded or vertically oval, subapical, with a pale violet flush; appendix stipitate, stipe thin, laterally compressed, 4–5 by 2–3 mm, whitish yellow, appendix conical, laterally compressed, directed backwards, base truncate, top obtuse, 15–34 by 8–11 mm, with several small, shallow depressions, otherwise smooth, orangeish yellow.

description: Small to moderate, rarely gigantic, evergreen, terrestrial or lithophytic or rheophytic (the last not in Thailand), odourless or, very occasionally, aromatic herbs. Stem pleionanthic or hapaxanthic, hypogeal or epigeal, sometimes erect or decumbent, rarely root-climbing or scandent. Leaves several to many together, spiro-distichous, rarely distichous; petiolar sheath very short or, more often, less than half the petiole length, sometimes variously auriculate or attached only basally but then with a long apical ligule; leaf blade narrow-elliptic, elliptic, lanceolate, oblanceolate, ovate, obovate, cordate, or cordate-sagittate, mostly glabrous, sometimes pubescent or furnished with coarse trichomes on one or both surfaces, sometimes variegated with paler or silvery green, white or yellow; primary lateral veins pinnate, running into a distinct marginal vein; secondary and tertiary laterals parallel-pinnate; higher order venation transverse-reticulate to tessellate. Inflorescences 1–3 (or more) in each floral sympodium; peduncle shorter than petiole; spathe usually constricted between tube and limb, sometimes only slightly so, rarely not at all, lower spathe convolute, persistent, spathe limb thinner, mostly erect, broadly boat-shaped, gaping and then usually caducous during anthesis, less often persistent, rarely marcescent, usually white to cream, sometimes greenish yellow, very rarely pink, cuspidate to acuminate; spadix shorter than or equalling spathe, lower part consisting of cylindrical to conoid pistillate zone, free or partially adnate to spathe, sometimes bearing sterile organs at the very base, upper part of spadix usually subcylindrical to clavate, either fertile staminate below and sterile terminally, or sterile below and fertile staminate terminally, or sterile below, centrally fertile staminate and sterile terminally, lowermost sterile zone sometimes very laxly flowered, often constricted; flowers unisexual, perigone absent; staminate flower 2–3-androus, stamens very short to long, mostly free; filaments usually well developed, sometimes connate basally, always with distinctive tannin cells (dark in dried specimens), connective mostly rather slender, sometimes thicker apically, anthers truncate, often concave apically; thecae opposite, cylindrical or obconical to ovoid, dehiscing by apical, broadly elliptic, or bilobed (8-shaped) or simple pores; sterile staminate flowers comprising staminodes less compressed than stamens, obpyramidal to clavate, usually truncate, short to long; pistillate flowers a gynoecium sometimes accompanied by 1–4 clavate, rarely peltate staminodes with generally distinctly swollen apices, or with sterile flowers scattered among gynoecia; ovary 1-locular; ovules (1–)few to many, anatropous to hemianatropous, funicle rather long, placentae 1–4, parietal, usually extending from base to apex of locule; stylar region inconspicuous or shortly conoid; stigma discoid to capitate, small to as wide as ovary. Fruit an oblong to globose berry, ripening green or dull yellow or rarely deep red, few- to many-seeded. Seed ellipsoid, testa costate, embryo straight, elongate, endosperm copious.</br></br>A large genus of terrestrial mesophytes, less often rheophytic, evergreen herbs. Superficially similar to Homalomena, but tissues odourless. Schismatoglottis in flower are unmistakeable by the spathe limb shedding at the onset of staminate anthesis. Inflorescences are invariably powerfully fragrant (esterases). Three species in Thailand.

description: Decumbent herb, tissues stongly aromatic (terpenoids) when crushed. Stems epigeal, pleionanthic, rooting in the internodes, dull dark green, ca 2 cm diam. Leaves 3–6 together; petiole 5–25 cm long, to 6 mm diam., with the margins sharp to minutely winged, minutely hairy and faintly rough, deep dull green; petiolar sheath occupying the lower ½–¾ of petiole, wings membranous, persistent, eventually marcescent; leaf blade broadly ovate to oblong ovate, to ca 20 cm long, base obtuse to auriculate, tip rather abruptly acuminate for ca 1–2 cm, margin irregularly wavy, pale green when young, later slightly glossy dark green adaxially, paler abaxially, somewhat chartaceous; primary lateral veins numerous, slightly prominent adaxially near the midrib, the rest flush, prominent abaxially, ca 1 cm apart, diverging at 60–80°, regularly alternating with lesser interprimaries; secondary venation flush abaxially and adaxially, emerging from the midrib and the basal parts of the primary veins; tertiary venation forming a distinct tessellate pattern abaxially. Inflorescences 1–3 together; peduncle ca 4 cm long, 3 mm diam., erect at and after anthesis; spathe 5–12 cm long, conspicuously mucronate for up to 2 cm, shiny mid-green throughout; lower spathe narrowly ovoid to ovoid, 2–4 by 1–2 cm; spathe limb narrowly lanceolate, separated from the lower spathe by a rather weak constriction, gaping slightly in the upper part, the lower part, like the lower spathe, convolute, rather leathery, persistent shortly after anthesis but eventually yellowing and deliquescent; spadix 4.5–9 cm long; pistillate flower zone 1.5–3 cm long, slightly tapering distally, ca 8 mm thick, obliquely inserted to adnate for ca half its length; ovaries 0.5 mm diam., subglobose with 3–4 conspicuous longitudinal bulges, green; stigma sessile, faintly 3–4-lobed, minutely papillate; interpistillar staminodes absent or very few except for a single ring around the spadix immediately below the pistillate zone, stalked, more or less flat-topped and irregularly polygonal, about twice the height of the pistils, white; sterile interstice 0.5–1 cm long, more or less cylindrical, 4–8 mm thick; staminodes mushroom-shaped, ca twice height of pistils, ca 1 mm diam., white, resembling the interpistillar staminodes; staminate flower zone 1.2–2 cm long, slightly thickening distally (the base corresponding with spathe constriction), 4–8 mm thick, pale yellow; stamens ca 1 mm across, filament slab-like; anther flat-topped; appendix 1.4–3 cm long, tapering to a point, deeper yellow than the staminate zone; appendical staminodes columnar, flat-topped, circular to reniform in outline, ca 1 mm diam., slightly taller than stamens so that appendix slightly but abruptly thicker than male zone. Fruiting spathe erect, rather narrowly urceolate, dehiscing from the base; fruits grey-green.

description: Stoloniferous herb forming colonies, or clump-forming, 15–60 cm tall. Stems hypogeal, hapaxanthic, 1–2 cm diam. Leaves several together; petiole smooth, ca 5–50 cm long (often less); petiolar sheath for ca ⅓ its length; wings of sheath fully attached, persistent, tapering or, especially in diminutive forms, shortly and bluntly ligular at the apex; leaf blade mostly cordate to sagittate, sometimes oblong-lanceolate, 7–35 by 4–18 cm, usually dull mid green, sometimes variegated with 1–2 bands or irregularly spotted grey-green to yellowish green; midrib somewhat abaxially prominent; primary lateral veins 6–15 per side, irregularly alternating with lesser interprimaries, nearly always raised adaxially towards the midrib, marginally impressed, entirely raised abaxially; secondary venation arising mostly from the midrib, sometimes from the bases of the primary veins; tertiary venation inconspicuous. Inflorescences 1–8 together, with a strong esteric odour at pistillate anthesis; peduncle 2–14 cm, erect at anthesis, then deflected; spathe 3.5– ca 12 cm long; lower spathe narrowly ovoid, ca half the length of the whole spathe, green, often minutely longitudinally ridged and rough; spathe limb differentiated from lower spathe by an abrupt constriction corresponding to the base of the staminate zone of the spadix, at pistillate anthesis much inflated, narrowing and turbinate, the apex conspicuously mucronate, completely surrounding the spadix and gaping ventrally or with the margins loosely overlapping, creamy to pale greenish yellow, caducous immediately after pistillate anthesis; spadix ca ¾ the length of the spathe, narrowly hourglass-shaped; pistillate flower zone about half the length of the whole spadix, sessile, somewhat to markedly obliquely inserted to partially adnate to spathe, ca 5–8 mm diam. below, distally tapering to ca 3–4 mm diam.; ovaries flask-shaped, ca 1 mm by 0.5 mm diam.; stigmas button-like, papillate, raised on a short style; interpistillar staminodes white, mostly conspicuously taller than pistils, few in number, scattered, stalked, clavate, rarely absent in very small forms; sterile interstice between staminate and pistillate zones absent save sometimes for a relative concentration of interpistillar staminodes amongst the distal pistils; staminate flower zone narrowly obconical, approximately half the length of the pistillate zone, distally ca 0.5–1 cm diam., ivory; anthers dumbbell-shaped from above, ca 0.5 by 1 mm, with thecae apically impressed, the connective shorter than to very slightly elevated above the thecae; appendix bullet-shaped to hemispherical, basally nearly always somewhat wider than apex of staminate zone, creamy yellow; appendix staminodes columnar, irregularly polygonal, flat- to slightly round-topped, ca 0.5 mm diam. Fruiting spathe declinate, urceolate.

description: Clump- to colony-forming, usually stoloniferous herb, sometimes with individual crowns markedly distant. Stems hapaxanthic, hypogeal. Leaves to 5 together; petiole 15–45 cm long, smooth, adaxially flattened to somewhat channelled, the angles blunt to somewhat acute, but not winged; petiolar sheath in lower ca ¼, wings persistent, membranous, straight to slightly inrolled, to ca 1 cm wide, tapering, fully attached except for ca 1 mm ligular apex; leaf blade 8–30 by 2–17 cm, very variable in shape, mostly more or less oblong-ovate, occasionally broadly ovate to oblong-lanceolate, base cuneate to obtuse, more rarely truncate to cordate with posterior lobes 0–6 cm long, mid- to very dark green and dull to somewhat glossy adaxially, paler and dull green abaxially, often variegated with a dark green central strip, or bivittate grey-green; midrib somewhat prominent abaxially; primary lateral veins impressed adaxially, prominent abaxially,(6–)10–14 on each side of the midrib, 1.5–3 cm apart; interprimary veins irregular but conspicuous, especially in larger-leaved forms; secondary venation often very inconspicuous; tertiary venation barely visible. Inflorescences (1–)2–several together, with a powerful esteric odour; peduncle mostly hidden within the subtending leaf sheath, to ca 12 cm long; spathe (4.5–)8–18 cm long; lower spathe more or less cylindrical at anthesis, green, (0.4–)1–2.5 cm diam.;spathe limb (incl. terminal mucro) about equalling the lower spathe in length, ivory to pale yellow, inflated to ca 4 cm diam. and turbinate at anthesis, slightly gaping or with the margins loosely overlapping, then abruptly caducous, the interface between the limb and the lower spathe only weakly constricted; spadix (2.5–)6–12 cm long, sessile, cylindrical to distally subclavate; pistillate flower zone about half the length of the spadix, obliquely inserted to adnate for ca ½ its length to the spathe; ovaries more or less flask-shaped, ca 1 mm tall; stigma sessile, button-like; interpistillar staminodes scattered, narrowly stalked and clavate-headed, about twice the height of the pistils, sometimes also crowded at the interface between the female and sterile zones; sterile zone between pistillate and staminate flower zones abruptly but slightly thicker than distal part of pistillate zone, cylindrical, somewhat shorter than (then hidden within lower spathe) to somewhat exceeding (then distally exposed from mouth of lower spathe, rarely completely exserted) the staminate zone, composed of columnar, flat-topped staminodes markedly dissimilar to interpistillar ones; staminate flower zone cylindrical with the apex rounded, to somewhat clavate, ca (0.3–)0.7–1 cm diam.; stamens more or less rectangular to dumbbell-shaped from above (connective reaching anther apex in the former, not in the latter), ca 0.7 mm across, the thecae impressed apically, the rims interrupted laterally by a narrow slit; appendix absent or reduced to a small cluster of columnar staminodes at the summit of the male zone apex. Fruiting spathe very narrowly urceolate to subcylindrical, to ca 5 cm long.

description: Small to very large, slender to very robust, evergreen, scandent, climbing secondary hemiepiphytes, or perching epiphytes with abundant trichosclereids. Stem root-climbing or less often prostrate, often producing long flagelliform shoots with reduced cataphylls and abundant, dimorphic, clasping and feeding roots. Leaves several to many, distichous to spiro-distichous and often forming tufts at the tips of active shoots, juvenile sometimes in a shingl form; petiole mostly channelled, pulvinate apically; petiolar sheath usually broad, persistent or marcescent, occasionally decomposing into a persistent net-like fibrous mass with abundant, stinging sclereids; leaf blade entire, lanceolate, elliptic or ovate to obovate, acuminate, often variegated when juvenile; primary lateral veins either hardly or well differentiated, pinnate, running into marginal vein, secondaries and also sometimes tertiaries parallel-pinnate, higher order venation inconspicuous, transverse-reticulate. Inflorescence very often solitary; peduncle shorter than petiole; spathe boat-shaped, only slightly gaping at anthesis, or opening almost flat, sometimes grossly thickened, caducous to deciduous or persistent or marcescent; spadix sessile to shortly stipitate, cylindrical, narrowly ellipsoid or clavate, shorter than spathe; flowers bisexual, perigone absent; stamens 4, free; filaments oblong, flattened, broad, connective slender; thecae oblong-ellipsoid, dehiscing by apical slits; gynoecium compressed ± rhombo-cylindrical, 1-locular; ovules 1(–2), anatropous, funicle short, placenta basal; stylar region well-developed, prismatic, truncate or with shortly conical central projection supporting stigma; stigma globose, elongate-globose, elliptic, linear, or punctiform. Infructescence a monsterocarp with stylar region deciduous at maturity, ripening dull orange to dull red or white; ovary 1-seeded. Seed rounded, subreniform, compressed, testa thickish, sparsely verruculose or smooth, embryo curved, endosperm present.</br></br>A small genus of secondary hemiepiphytes, or perching epiphytes, rarely scandent shrubs. Leaf blades of juvenile forms, especially the larger-growing species, are often strikingly different in appearance to the adults, not least in the presence of leaf variegation.</br></br>Approximately 30 species distributed from the tropical eastern Himalaya throughout tropical Asia to Australia (Queensland); four species in Thailand (but see note below), none endemic. The common and widespread Sundaic Scindapsus pictus Hassk. and S. treubii Engl. have yet to be recorded from Thailand despite being common species to the south across the Malaysian border with Peninsular Thailand. They are included in the key for the sake of utility but omitted from the species descriptions.

description: Large to gigantic root-climber to 30 m. Stem 10–35 mm diam. Leaves evenly distributed but lower leaves often falling and then leaves tending to become clustered towards stem apices; petiole canaliculate, 33–62.5 cm by 6–20 mm, dark green, smooth, apical pulvinus 20–25 by 5–12 mm, basal pulvinus 2–4 cm by 7–15 mm; petiolar sheath extending to half way along apical pulvinus, at first sub-membranaceous, soon drying scarious, later breaking into regular sections and falling to leave a somewhat roughened, mid-brown scar; leaf blade oblong-elliptic, 45–100 by 25–48 cm, very stiffly coriaceous, matte green adaxially, slightly glaucous abaxially, apex acute to slightly acuminate, base shallowly and narrowly cordate; primary lateral veins parallel, barely or not differentiated from interprimary veins; interprimary veins very numerous, prominent, remaining parallel to primary vein. Inflorescence solitary on the tips of clinging shoots; peduncle 5–8 cm by 4–10 mm; spathe canoe-shaped, 28–33.5 by 11–14 cm when pressed flat, shortly but stoutly tapering, gaping at anthesis and then caducous before anthesis is complete, exterior green, interior yellow at anthesis; spadix cylindrical, 26–28.5 by 3–4.5 cm, sessile, bluntly tapering towards the apex, dull yellow; stylar region 4–10 by 1.5–4 mm, acroscopic-trapezoid, robust, apex flattened; stigma 0.8–3 by 0.1–0.5 mm, transverse-linear. Infructescence light-green, stylar region greatly enlarged and recurved along the margins, waxy-looking, ripening yellow.

description: Medium to large, moderate to rather robust, semipachycaul, homeophyllous secondary hemiepiphyte to 10 m. Stems terete, ca 1.5–2 cm diam., smooth with pale green epidermis when fresh, drying with epidermis orange-brown and flaking easily. Leaves tending to cluster at tips of shoots; petiole prominently winged, 10–17 by 1–3 cm, apical and basal pulvini weakly defined; petiolar sheath very prominent, spreading and wing-like, persistent, briefly ligulate apically; leaf blade ovate-lanceolate to ovate-elliptic, 14–25 by 8–18 cm, slightly oblique, base rounded and very briefly cuneate, usually oblique, apex acute to attenuate, with a prominent apiculate tubule, dull pale to medium green, juvenile leaves occasionally with irregular, jagged, silvery streaks; midrib raised abaxially, slightly sunken adaxially; primary lateral veins pinnate, slightly raised abaxially and adaxially; interprimaries parallel to primaries and only slightly less prominent, very slightly raised abaxially and adaxially; secondary and tertiary venation ± obscure in fresh material, visible as a faint reticulum in dried specimens. Inflorescence solitary, subtended by a fully developed foliage leaf, arising on free lateral and less often adherent shoots; peduncle compressed-cylindrical, 9–14 by 1–1.5 cm; spathe broadly cigar-shaped, 11–16 by 3–5 cm, stoutly long-beaked, thinly stiff-fleshy, dull yellow, paler internally, caducous at pistillate anthesis; spadix cylindrical, 6–11 by 1–2.5 cm, sessile, inserted ± level on peduncle; stylar region mostly longitudinally rhombohexagonal, 4–6 by 2–3 mm, truncate; stigma longitudinally elongated, ca 3 mm. Infructescence stoutly fusiform cylindrical, 12–15 by 2–3 cm, stylar plates each with their edges recurving, somewhat waxy in appearance; stigma longitudinally annulate; fruits yellow when ripe with stylar plates sloughing away to reveal red pulp cavities.

description: Medium-sized, moderately robust, leptocaulous, homeophyllous, scandent secondary hemiepiphyte to 2 m. Stems terete, 1–1.5 cm diam., smooth, bright green when fresh, drying dark brown; stilt-roots stout, arising at each node. Leaves scattered; petiole 10–17 by 0.3–1 cm, apical and basal pulvini defined; petiolar sheath prominent, reaching to the base of the apical pulvinus, persistent; leaf blade ovate-lanceolate to ovate-elliptic, 10–16 by 4–12 cm, very stiffly coriaceous, base rounded, apex acute, with a prominent apiculate tubule, glossy green when fresh, drying dull orange-brown; midrib raised sharply abaxially, slightly sunken adaxially; primary venation pinnate, slightly raised abaxially; interprimaries parallel to primaries and only slightly less prominent, slightly raised abaxially; secondary and tertiary venation ± obscure in fresh material and dried specimens. Inflorescence solitary, subtended by a fully developed foliage leaf, arising on a free lateral shoot; peduncle cylindrical, 6–12 by 0.3–0.4 cm; spathe ellipsoid-cigar-shaped, 6–11 by 3–3.5 cm, stoutly long-beaked, thinly stiff-fleshy, deep yellow, late-caducous; spadix fusiform-cylindrical, 5–8 by ca 1 cm, sessile, tapering markedly basally, inserted ± level on peduncle, white. Fruits not seen.

description: Terrestrial herbs with underground tubers. Flowering shoots 10–40 cm tall; stem papillose-pubescent. Foliage leaves 1(–2), basal, green with purple (to dark green) spots above, mottled purple/green underneath; petiole not perceptible for most of the flowering period, but later elongating to 3–5.5 cm; lamina acute to acuminate. Inflorescence spicate, lax; rachis 2–15 cm long; bracts much smaller than the foliage leaves, shorter than the flowers. Flowers 2 to many, resupinate, predominantly pink to rose-coloured. Sepals plain (i.e. not saccate), rounded to subacute; dorsal sepal (narrowly) elliptic-oblong, 2.8–9 mm long; lateral sepals obliquely (ovate-) elliptic. Labellum narrowly attached to the column, 3-lobed, smooth or with numerous tufts of papillae on the ventral side, spurred at base; spur approximately as long as the labellum lamina, not constricted at base. Column with a bilobed, concave stigma; distal part of rostellum narrow, straight, squeezed in between the thecae; viscidia 1–2, contained in one versatile bursicle; anther firmly attached, thecae not extending from the column; pollinia 2, basitonous. Ovary papillose-pubescent. Fruit a capsule, dehiscing by 6 longitudinal slits.</br></br>A genus of 3 species distributed in the Shan State of Myanmar, northwestern Thailand and Yunnan; 3 species in Thailand.

description: Flowering shoots 27–34 cm tall. Foliage leaf narrowly (ovate- elliptic, 9.7–12 by 4–6 cm. description: Glabrous mangrove trees, not buttressed, branches drooping (S. caseolaris) or not. Roots radiating, horizontal. Pneumatophores vertical above the surface, stout, elongate, cone-shaped, sometimes forked, with soft spongy light wood. Leaves simple, opposite, entire, smooth, coriaceous. Flowers solitary or in groups of 2 to 5, terminal, 4–8–merous, nocturnal. Calyx thick, coriaceous; tube obconical or cup-shaped, persistent; lobes ovate-lanceolate or ovate-triangular, sometimes coloured inside. Petals as many as calyx lobes, very narrow, caducous, or absent. Stamens massive, up to about 300, inflexed in bud, straight in open flower, caducous; filaments coloured or not; anthers reniform. Ovary 10- or more-celled; stigma capitate. Disc saucer-shaped. Fruit a depressed-globose berry, crowned by the stylar base, resting on the persistent cup- or plate-shaped calyx. Seeds numerous, angular.</br></br>Five species, from tropical east Africa to Asia, Malesia, Ryukyu Islands, N. Australia, Micronesia, and New Caledonia; four in Thailand.

description: Terrestrial herbs with adjacent pseudobulbous stems. Flowering shoots (16–)30–130(–150) cm tall. Pseudobulbs mostly underground and borne just below the soil surface. Foliage leaves few (very rarely one), plicate, lanceolate-oblong or grass-like, often deciduous, acuminate, glabrous, petiolate. Inflorescences racemose, few-flowered, basal, mostly pubescent; sterile bracts one to few, apically grading into the persistent floral bracts. Flowers medium-sized or large and often showy, resupinate, in Thailand yellow, white or pink. Sepals  free, spreading, outside usually pubescent. Petals similar but normally glabrous. Labellum 3-lobed, spurless, ornamented by basal twin-calli; mid-lobe spathulate or rarely linear-oblong, usually with 2 lateral teeth at the base of the claw; side lobes most commonly large, oblong, erect and enclosing the column. Column long, glabrous, without a column foot; anther versatile, incumbent, pollinia 8, waxy, clavate. Ovary pubescent, not distinct from the pedicel. Capsule variously ellipsoid.</br></br>A genus of c. 40 species distributed from India in the west throughout tropical and extra-tropical SE Asia to northern Australia (Queensland) and the islands of the Pacific Ocean, with Spathoglottis plicata also naturalised in other parts of the world; 7 species in Thailand.</br></br>Notes: a more comprehensive version of this account was published in Rheedea 18: 63–74. 2008.

description: Terrestrial herbs producing fasciculate fleshy roots from the base of an erect, more or less glandular-pubescent stem. Foliage leaves crowded on the basal part of the stem, petiolate (below) to sessile (above). Inflorescence racemose, spirally twisted. Flowers many, resupinate, translucent, white to predominantly pink. Sepals free. Petals connivent with the dorsal sepal. Labellum straight (i.e., not twisted), 3.5–6 mm long, oblong-pandurate with rounded apex, concave at base, inside provided with 1 lateral appendage on either side. Column straight (i.e. not twisted); rostellum triangular, bifid; viscidium 1, naked, anther versatile; pollinia 2, deeply cleft, acrotonous. Ovary more or less glandular-pubescent. Fruit a capsule, dehiscing by 6 longitudinal slits.</br></br>A genus of ca. 40 species distributed throughout most of North America and Eurasia (except the arctic and some of the northernmost temperate regions); in the south reaching northernmost South America, Mediterranean North Africa, eastern Australia and New Zealand; 1 species in Thailand.

description: Erect, twining, or trailing herbs, glabrous or hairy, with short perennial rootstock; roots many, tuberous, fusiform; stem in lower part with sheathing cataphylls; prophyll inconspicuous (fig. 1). Leaves alternate, opposite, or in whorls; petiole at base somewhat pulvinate, not sheathing; blade simple, ovate or (narrowly) elliptic, margin entire, apex acute-acuminate, 6–13-veined from the base, and curved to the apex, secondary venation fine, transverse and scalariform between the primary veins. Inflorescences axillary, sessile or pedunculate; flowers few, subumbellate, raceme-like, bracts narrow; buds elongate, 5–55 mm long, acute. Flowers with articulate pedicels, the part below articulation persistent; bracts narrow, acute, margin entire, (sub)persistent; perianth of 4 tepals; tepals imbricate, free, narrow (the outer ones narrower), out curved or reflexed at anthesis, apex mostly acute (-acuminate); longitudinally striped and veined; persistent in fruit; stamens 4, anthers with the thecae dorsally attached to a long connective with a petaloid outgrowth, the two thecae either apically with 1 common additional appendage and the apices of all 4 stamens connivent, or additional appendage lacking, filaments short, bases shortly connate and adnate to tepals; ovary superior, ovoid, small, 1.5–3(–4) mm long, 1(–3) mm wide, glabrous, one-celled, ovules few or many, basally attached, stigma minute, sessile. Fruit ripening green, glabrous, capsular, opening with 2 valves from the apex, elongate, apex acute or shortly beaked; pericarp thin; perianth persistent. Seeds 3–20, red or brown, mostly elongate, (5–)7–12(–15) mm long, (2–)3–4 mm wide, often shortly beaked (globose in S. kerrii, ca 5 mm across), longitudinally ridged; aril consisting of finger-like or vesicular lobes, covering the base of the seed; funicle long, pseudo-funicle lacking.</br></br>A genus of about 20 species distributed in China and Japan, through Malesia east to Australia; 11 species in Thailand.

description: Terrestrial, mycohetrotrophic herbs with a vertical corm; devoid of roots. Flowering shoots erect; stem hollow, fragile, glabrous, pale brownish-white. description: Corm oblongoid (to ellipsoid or ovoid), 1.6–4.4 cm long, 0.6–2.1 cm in diameter. Inflorescence 3- to many-flowered; rachis 3–19 cm long; floral bracts lanceolate, acuminate, 3.5–11.6 by 1.2–4.3 mm, entire. Flowers not opening fully, white with purple-tipped sepals, petals and labellum. Sepals 3-veined from the base; dorsal sepal linear-triangular, acute to acuminate, 8.2–9.2 by 1.7–2.2 mm; lateral sepals obliquely to falcately linear-triangular, acuminate, 8–10.1 by 1.6–2.2 mm. Petals linear-lanceolate, acute to acuminate, 8.1–9.2 by 2.2–2.3 mm, 3-veined from the base, entire. Labellum continuing the line of the ovary, concave at base, (ovate-)lanceolate with strongly incurved sides that enfold the column, obtuse to subacuminate, entire to irregularly undulate-crenate, glabrous, smooth, ornamented by a pair of ellipsoid calli at base, 9.3–11.2 by 3.4–3.7 mm when flattened. Column incurved, 3–3.5 mm long; anther more or less saddle-shaped, (linear-)oblong in upper view, rounded in front, bilobed at base, 2.5–3 mm long, releasing the pollinia directly onto the fertile stigma. Ovary ellipsoid, 3–8.2 mm long; pedicel 1.5–5 mm long. Capsule ellipsoid to subspherical, 5–11 mm long, 3–7 mm in diameter.

description: Small to robust, usually evergreen, sometimes seasonally dormant, monoecious herbs. Stem epigeal, stout, erect or creeping, covered with fibrous remains of leaves and cataphylls. Leaves solitary or few to several together; petiole terete, sheath very short; leaf blade peltate, ovate or ovate-oblong, acuminate, emarginate basally, sinus very shallow, posterior lobes almost absent, membranaceous; basal ribs short, well-developed; primary lateral veins pinnate, forming submarginal collective vein very near margin, marginal vein also present; secondary and tertiary laterals arising from the primaries at a wide angle, then arching towards leaf margin and forming ± conspicuous interprimary collecting vein (‘colocasioid’ venation); higher order venation reticulate. Inflorescence solitary; peduncle shorter than petiole; spathe ovate or ovate-lanceolate, acuminate, not constricted, barely convolute at base, ± fully expanded at anthesis, lower part persistent to fruiting stage, upper part becoming reflexed and revolute, marcescent, yellow or ± dark purple within; spadix much shorter than spathe; flowers unisexual, perigone absent; pistillate flower zone cylindrical, often longer than staminate flower zone, mostly adnate to spathe; pistillate flowers with gynoecium surrounded by whorl of 2–5, short, staminodes claviform, more rarely staminodes absent; ovary subglobose to ovoid, 1-locular; ovules numerous, hemiorthotropous, funicle distinct, placentae 2–5, parietal, in basal part only or extending from base to apex; stylar region ± lacking; stigma strongly 2–5-lobed; staminate flower zone contiguous with pistillate, cylindrical, ellipsoid or subglobose, fertile to apex, obtuse; synandria 3–6-androus, strongly lobed, apically truncate, synconnective relatively small, impressed at apex; thecae oblong, contiguous, dehiscing by apical pore. Fruit an ovoid berry, many-seeded. Seed ovoid to ellipsoid, testa costate, embryo axile, short, conoid, endosperm copious.</br></br>A genus of about 10 species of small to moderately large, rhizomatous or creeping, mesophytic herbs with creeping to semi-erect rhizomes with conspicuous netted fibres, peltate leaves and large, brightly coloured inflorescences, the spathe reflexing early during anthesis.</br></br>Remarkably, given that the genus is one of the most horticulturally desirable in Asia, the taxonomic status of Steudnera is far from fully resolved and the names applied here must be regarded as provisional. Three distinct species are definitely present in Thailand, although each known from a single collection, with one (here called S. colocasiifolia) known only from a single living plant. The Flora of China account lists an additional two species (S. griffithii (Schott) Schott and S. henryana Engl.) which have not yet been recorded in Thailand, although a sterile collection [K.Larsen & B.Hansen 1730 (BKF)] may be referable to S. henryana.</br></br>All known Thai Steudnera collections are from relatively well-botanized areas in the north. Furthermore Steudnera species are striking and not easily overlooked even when sterile; it thus seems probable that Steudnera species are genuinely rare in Thailand.

description: Erect or decumbent branched herbs with short crowded rootstock, leafy shoots several years of age; roots lacking tubers; lower part of stem with sheathing cataphylls often with fimbriate margins; prophyllum present at point of ramification; in erect plants the upper branches often leaning over. Leaves alternate, subdistichous; petiole slightly sheathing at base or not; blade simple, ovate-oblong or elliptic, margin entire, apex acute-acuminate, lateral veins 2–4 pairs, curved, one pair basal, venation finely trabeculate. Inflorescences axillary, pedunculate, with a few to ca 40 flowers arranged in clusters or raceme-like, only 1 or 2 flowers at apex at anthesis; buds (depressed) globose. Flowers small, perfect or functionally unisexual with some reduction of one sex and some dimorphism; pedicel filiform, stiff, articulate, persistent below articulation; bracts narrow, margins fringed, acute, persistent; perianth of 4 tepals, imbricate, almost free, often recurved; stamens 4, free, filaments at base shortly adnate to tepals; anther comprising 2 dorsifixed thecae, horizontal or curved over the apex of the filament, connective broad or narrow, without appendages; ovary superior or semi-inferior, green, ovoid, minute, ca 0.5 mm diam., one-celled, ovules 2–4, placentation apical, style lacking, stigma minute, sessile, 1 (but see the note under Stichoneuron membranaceum). Fruit elongate, apex acute or beaked, green, capsular with 1–4 seeds; pericarp thin; perianth persistent. Seeds large, brown or reddish brown, broadly ellipsoid, (irregularly) longitudinally ridged, aril (elaiosome) of 5–8 finger-like hyaline appendages or irregularly shaped, surrounding seed to about halfway; funicle shorter than the seed, pseudo-funicle (always present?) as long as the fruit.</br></br>A genus of 5 species distributed in NE India, northern Burma south to Peninsular Malaysia. description: Terrestrial, sympodial, autotrophic herbs with (often more or less buried) pseudobulbs that are clustered or (more often) distinctly separated along a rhizome. description: Pseudobulbs consisting of several internodes, erect (to somewhat prostrate), obliquely (conical-)ellipsoid, 1.3–2.5 cm long, 1.8–3.1 cm in diameter. Inflorescence arising from a node, 24–79 cm long; rachis (3.4–)11.5–30.8 cm long, (3–)6- to 16-flowered; floral bracts 4–15 mm long. Flowers mainly green to yellowish brown (labellum white with purple markings). Sepals acuminate; dorsal sepal oblanceolate-linear to lanceolate-oblong, 13.5–17.3 by 3–3.9 mm; lateral sepals obliquely oblanceolate-linear to lanceolate-oblong, 13.5–18 by 3–4.3 mm. Petals obliquely oblanceolate, acute, sometimes mucronate, 13.5–17.4 by 3.9–4 mm. Labellum 3-lobed, 12–15.3 by 5.5–6.4 mm when flattened, 2.2–2.4 times as long as wide, with a 2–4 mm long spur at base; mid-lobe suborbicular to transversely elliptic, rounded, 2.5–3.7 by 4.8–5 mm, margin entire and straight; side lobes obtuse to acute, 1.5–1.7 mm long (measured along front edge); labellum ornamented by 5 keels starting from (near) its base and terminating on the mid-lobe; all keels straight, abruptly increasing in height just below the mid-lobe and usually distinctly erose dentate distally. Column 7.5–8.7 mm long, without a column foot. Ovary (including pedicel) 8–17 mm long.

description: Terrestrial, sympodial herbs with vertical subspherical corms producing inflorescences devoid of foliage leaves and erect leafy shoots with pseudostems formed by convolute leaf bases. Foliage leaves plicate, sometimes starting to wither before the end of anthesis. Inflorescences racemose or paniculate with up to 3 suberect lateral branches, many-flowered; floral bracts persistent. Flowers opening in succession (up to 10 at a time) from the inflorescence base upwards, resupinate. Sepals and petals free, glabrous, dull yellowish-green (sometimes weakly suffused with purple). Labellum versatile, erect from base but soon recurved by a knee-like bend, oblong, slightly widened in its distal part, bright green with 2 darker green keels and a transparent median band. Column stout (less than 3 times as long as anther), with a short column foot; anther subterminal, elongated, versatile, light brown; pollinia 2, sectile, partly cleft, devoid of caudicles; rostellum producing a viscidium, but no stipe; receptive part of stigma concave with slightly elevated margins. Ovary and pedicel twisted through 180, glabrous. Fruit a capsule dehiscing by longitudinal slits.</br></br>A monotypic genus; distribution as for the species (see below).

description: Corm 2.6–3.7 cm long, c. 3 cm in diameter, with a dense tangle of unbranched roots. Foliage leaves 3–4, distichous; pseudostem 20–32 cm long; free part of each leaf linear lanceolate to obovate, 10–30 by 2.3–9.7 cm, acuminate. Inflorescence 35–91 cm tall; peduncle purplish-brown, glaucescent, bearing 3–6 scale-like leaves; rachis of primary stem 14–37.6 cm long, lateral branches (if present) 8.9–24 cm long; floral bracts oblong-lanceolate, long-acute to acuminate, 5–12.5 mm long. Flowers not opening widely. Sepals acute, minutely mucronate; dorsal sepal strongly boat-shaped, linear-lanceolate, 3-veined from the base, 12.4–13.1 by 3.1–3.8 mm; lateral sepals more or less boat-shaped, falcately oblong-lanceolate, 3- to 5-veined from the base, 9.9–12 by 3.7–4.3 mm; petals connivent with the dorsal sepal, falcately linear-(ob)lanceolate, obtuse to acute, 1-veined from the base, 9.5–10.8 by c. 2.3 mm, subentire. Labellum shortly clawed, obtuse to acute, sometimes minutely mucronate, 9–10.2 by 4.8–5.3 mm, glabrous and smooth, subentire, ornamented by 2 entire longitudinal keels in its proximal  half. Column erect, incurved, subterete, 5.5–6.4 mm long; anther (narrowly) ovate in upper view, obtuse to subacute, 2.7–2.9 mm long; rostellum porrect, broadly trapezoid, truncate; receptive part of stigma (linear-)oblong. Ovary (including pedicel) terete-fusiform with 3 distinct entire keels, 10–12.3 mm long. Capsule fusiform-terete, tapering at base, 1.5–2.8 cm long (excluding perianth remnants and pedicel), 0.4–0.6 cm in diameter.

description: Pernnial herbs, often with rhizomes; roots fibrous, sometimes tuberous. Stems often striate. Leaves alternate, ternately or pinnately compound, rarely simple, leaflets lobate, crenate upwards, petioles sheathing at base. Inflorescences terminal, usually paniculiform, corymbiform, or modified from these, several to many-flowered. Flowers generally small, bisexual or unisexual, actinomorphic. Sepals 4, or more, often caducous. Petals none. Stamens numerous, glabrous, anthers lateral, filaments filiform or clavate. Carpels uniovular, ovule pendulous. Achenes few to many, with longitudinal ribs on lateral sides, beaks usually persistent.</br></br>About 370 species distributed in the north hemisphere, and also in Africa, South America and Malesia. Four species and 1 variety in Thailand.

description: Perennial, evergreen, rhizomatous herbs 43–100 cm tall. Stems erect, a little branched upwards, leafy, glabrous, striate. Basal and lower cauline leaves 1–3, 7–10 cm long, glabrous, bi- or triternate, leaflets broadly ovate to obovate, 1–3 by 0.9–3.5 cm, slightly cordate to round at base, 3-lobed, lobes entire, 3-lobulate-crenate or 5–7-crenate-dentate, teeth round or obtuse, mucronate, coriaceous, upper surface glabrous, slightly reticulate, lower surface glaucous, prominently reticulate, glabrous, petioles 6–13 cm long , sheaths auriculate, slightly fissured or entire. Upper cauline leaves smaller, simpler, nearly sessile. Inflorescences corymbose or subpaniculate, glabrous, dichotomous by unequal elongation of branches, 5–20-flowered, pedicels 2–13 mm long, bracts minute, linear, sometimes 3-partite. Flowers bisexual, flat, with caducous sepals and spreading stamens, 4–7 mm diam. Sepals 4, ovate-elliptic, obtuse or slightly acute at apex, 2.5–3 by 1.5–2 mm, white, drying blackish, glabrous on both sides. Stamens as long as, or longer than sepals, anthers elliptic, 0.8–1.2 mm long, sometimes tortuose, connectives hardly projected, filaments drying blackish, clavate, glabrous, 2–3.5 mm long, as broad as, or slightly broader than anther, more or less rugulose. Achenes 3–9 in a head, drying black, ovoid to obovoid, slightly compressed, sessile, 2–3.5 by ca 1.2 mm, glabrous, 2–4 longitudinally costate on each side, abruptly contracted to a narrow, hamate beak upwards, 0.5–0.8 mm long.

description: Evergreen perennial, rhizomatous herb, 0.9–2 m tall, often robust. Stems erect, branched upwards, leafy, glabrous, slightly striate. Basal and lower cauline leaves several, 14–55 cm, 3–6-times pinnately ternate; leaflets ovate-orbicular, ovate-elliptic or obovate-orbicular, 1.5–3.5 by 1–3.5 cm, round to cordate at base, 3–7-crenate-lobate, lobes entire, apiculate, herbaceous, upper surface glabrous, lower surface slightly reticulate, glabrous; petiolules 6–20 mm long; petioles 6–17 cm long, glabrous, sheaths membranaceous, shallowly fissured. Upper cauline leaves smaller, simpler, shortly petiolate. Inflorescences paniculate, with numerous flowers, glabrous, lower bracts leafy, upper ones linear, small; pedicels 3–20 mm long. Flowers bisexual, sometimes male, flat, 8–10 mm diam. Sepals 4, caducous, oblong, obtuse to acute at apex, 3.5– 5 by 1.5–2.5 mm, white or slight bluish, drying blackish, glabrous on both sides. Stamens as long as, or longer than sepals, anthers linear, 2.5–3 mm long, sometimes twisted, connectives projected, filaments drying blackish, filiform, 1.5–5 mm long. Achenes 1–7 in a head, drying blackish, obovoid-ellipsoid or ellipsoid, swollen, slightly compressed, sessile, 2.2–4 by 1.2–1.5 mm, thick, glabrous, 1–3 longitudinally costate on each side, abruptly constricted to a beak, beaks up to 1.2 mm long, narrowly arrowhead-shaped, nearly straight or slightly curved, sometimes folded at base.

description: Perennial herbs 18–60 cm. Stems erect, striate, glabrous. description: Epiphytic, sympodial herbs with short rhizomes. Pseudobulbs flattened, ridged, closely aggregated, each consisting of one internode and bearing 1 leaf. Foliage leaves duplicate, much longer than the pseudobulbs, glabrous, present during flowering, deciduous, not sheathing at base but with a grooved petiole. Inflorescences long-lived, pendulous, racemose, arising from the base of pseudobulbs, lax, 3- to many-flowered. Flowers medium-sized. Sepals and petals free. Labellum 3-lobed, versatile, ornamented by 2 calli at base. Column strongly incurved (forming a C together with the column foot), at apex hooded and provided with 2 stelids; column foot conspicuous, hollow with an entrance at base of labellum; anther conical; pollinarium composed of 4 solid pollinia arranged in 2 unequal pairs and attached to a long narrow stipe (tegule); viscidium not clearly differentiated; Ovary glabrous. Fruit a pedicelled capsule dehiscing by longitudinal slits.</br></br>A genus of 2 species recorded from Vietnam, Thailand, Peninsular Malaysia and Borneo; 1 species in Thailand.

description: Pseudobulbs subovoid to oblongoid, 2–3.6 by 0.9–1.7 cm. Foliage leaves rather thick, glabrous; lamina elliptic to oblong-lanceolate, acute, 5.5–21.5 by 2.4–4.2 cm, leaves of first and second year much smaller than leaves of third year. Inflorescences glabrous; peduncle 1.5–3  cm long; rachis 3.8–5.5 cm long; floral bracts minute, triangular, 1.5–2 by 2–3 mm, glabrous. Flowers 3–11, opening widely; pedicel (including ovary) 10.5–13 mm long. Sepals glabrous,  acute; dorsal sepal narrowly oblong-elliptic, concave, 16–18 by 5.3–6 mm, incurved in its distal two-thirds; lateral sepals broadly and falcately ovate to triangular-ovate, spreading, abruptly recurved about one-third below apex, 13–13.5 by 8–8.2 mm. Petals porrect, incurved towards column, glabrous, falcately linear-lanceolate, acute, 15–16 by 3–3.1 mm. Labellum 7.7–8 mm long, distinctly clawed; side lobes very broadly and obliquely spathulate, erect from just above  the claw, 2–2.5 by 4–4.5 mm; mid-lobe broadly ovate, recurved, obtuse to broadly acute, shortly pubescent on ventral surface, 4.5–5 by 3.8–4 mm; disk ornamented by 2 basal bilaterally flattened calli that are bent in a right angle so as to almost block the entrance of the hollow column foot. Column glabrous, 12.5–13 mm long; column foot c. 5 mm long; stelids obliquely (triangular-) oblong, 2–3 by 2–2.2 mm. Capsule ellipsoid, 2.2–3.3 cm long, 1–1.7 cm in diameter.

description: Pseudobulbs conical to ovoid, 2.5–5.5 by 1–2.8 cm. Foliage leaves linear-oblong to oblong-elliptic, acute, thin-textured, glabrous, 15–32 by 2–5 cm. description: Terrestrial, lithophytic or epiphytic herbs, usually large and tall, without pseudobulbs; rhizome thick and short; roots fasciculate. Stems fascicled, erect or spreading, simple, cylindrical, fleshy, biennial, sheathed below and with normal leaves above. Foliage leaves many, distichous, chartaceous, glaucous beneath, sessile and sheathing below, deciduous. Inflorescence racemose, terminal on young leafy shoots, few- to many-flowered, arching or pendulous; floral bracts spathaceous, large, persistent. Flowers large, showy, not opening widely, short-lived. Sepals free, usually oblong-lanceolate, with several veins. Petals subsimilar to sepals, free, often slightly narrower and shorter than sepals. Labellum simple or obscurely 3-lobed, enclosing column, spurred at base, fringed on front margin, ornamented by several papillose keels in upper half of labellum. Column slender, winged at apex, straight to slightly incurved; column foot absent; anther terminal, incumbent, 2-celled, each cell subdivided into 2; pollinia 4, often deeply 2-lobed, solid, without disctinct caudicles; stigma concave; rostellum more or less 3-lobed. Fruit a capsule.</br></br>A genus of c. 4 species distributed from NE India, Nepal, Bhutan, Myanmar and S China to Peninsular Malaysia; 3 species in Thailand.

description: Shrubby to moderate-sized, solitary or clustering palms, dioecious or polygamous. Stem decumbent or erect, distally covered by skirt of dead leaves and persistant leaf bases. Leaf palmate, induplicate; sheath dissolving into mesh of fine and course fibres; petiole elongate, unarmed or rarely with very fine teeth; adaxial hastula well developed, abaxial one absent; blade almost circular, glaucous green abaxially in several species, splitting equally to unequally along adaxial ribs into numerous, single-fold segments, these shallowly indented at the tip. Inflorescence interfoliar; branching to 4 orders; peduncle short; prophyll conspicuous, with caducous tomentum; peduncular bracts 1–3; rachis shorter or longer than peduncle; rachis bracts tubular basally. Male and female flowers similar in overall size, shape and in the perianth parts; sepals united at the base; petals free, much longer than the calyx; stamens 6, filaments free, with short anthers, staminodes when present similar but with empty anthers; gynoecium of three, free carpels, hairy, apically with partially open, stigmatic slits. Fruit usually developing from one carpel only, kidney-shaped to oblong, purplish-black at maturity; epicarp hairy in young fruits to glabrous at maturity; mesocarp thin; endocarp crustaceous. Seed with homogeneous endosperm, with lateral intrusion of the seed coat. Germination remote-tubular.</br></br>Eight species in Himalaya to S China. One species in Thailand.

description: Solitary polygamo-dioecious palm. Stem up to 9 m tall at maturity, 10–16 cm diam., erect, naked, conspicuously ringed. Leaves 20–25 in crown; sheath c. 25–30 cm long dissolving in spreading fine fibres; petiole 40–50 cm long, margins minutely toothed and somewhat tomentose; adaxial hastula prominent to 3 cm long; blade rounded in outline, moderately undulate to flat, 0.9–1.1 m diam., evenly splitting to c. ½ radius into 60–90, single-folded segments, individual segments shortly indented, green adaxially, glaucous green abaxially. Inflorescences 3–5 on one palm, arching, prophyll 15–25 cm long, peduncular bracts and rachis bracts similar, 15–35 cm long, decreasing in length towards the distal parts, tubular proximally, inflated distally; male inflorescences 30–50 cm long, with 15–20 cm long peduncle; female (sometimes hermaphrodite?) inflorescences 0.8–1 m long, with 30–50 cm long peduncle; rachillae 3–10 cm long, stiff. Flowers minute in bud. Fruit kidney-shaped, 0.6–0.8 cm long and 10–12 cm wide, yellow to yellowish-brown at maturity.

description: Aquatic, (sub)annual herbs, rarely branched, the upper leaves forming a floating rosette. Adventitious roots 2 emerging from either side of submersed leaf-scars, thread-like with numerous rectangular outgrowths, containing chlorophyll. Leaves alternate; petiole swollen about or above the middle; stipules small, divided to the base; lamina of floating leaves glabrous above, sparingly or densely hairy beneath, rhombic or deltoid, toothed in upper part. Flowers solitary from upper leaf axils, pedicellate, hermaphrodite, 4-merous; sepals, free, not imbricate; petals pale purplish or white; stamens episepalous, perigynous; ovary half inferior, bilocular, ovules 1 per locule, pendulous from apex; style about as long as calyx and stamens; disc lobed. Fruits drupaceous, 1-seeded; pericarp thin, decaying; endocarp (seeds) hard, variably 2–4-horned, horns usually barbellate at apex; cotyledons strongly unequal in size. Seed as the fruit.</br></br>Two species in Europe, Asia, and Africa; naturalised in America and in Australia.
