description: Autotrophic (rarely mycoheterotrophic) terrestrial herbs with a short rhizome producing fibrous fasciculate, richly branched roots. Stem erect, rigid, branched or unbranched, bearing tubular cataphylls in its basal part. Foliage leaves sessile, sheathing at base, plicate (foliage leaves absent in the few mycoheterotrophic species). Inflorescences 1 to several, lateral (leaf-opposed) and/or terminal, racemose, short and dense. Flowers non-resupinate, not opening fully, mainly (greenish-)white to cream (labellum often with a yellow to orange blotch). Sepals and petals subsimilar; dorsal sepal free, more or less boat-shaped; lateral sepals connate, at least at base; petals free, entire. Labellum sessile, adnate to base of column, (linear-)lanceolate to somewhat fiddle-shaped, saccate to spurred at base, ornamented by a pair of keels or calli. Column less than 3 times as long as anther, dominated by the prominent rostellum; anther dorsal, versatile, elongated, acuminate, often dorsally keeled; pollinia 2, sectile, with slender caudicles; rostellum erect, producing a hamule and a viscidium; receptive part of stigma flat. Ovary and pedicel  (sub)terete, often scurfy-pubescent. Fruit an erect to spreading, short-pedicelled to subsessile, 6-ribbed capsule dehiscing by longitudinal slits.</br></br>A genus of 15–30 species distributed from Mexico and Florida to Venezuela, Colombia and Ecuador (including Galapagos), and throughout Indo-Malesia to northern Queensland and the SW Pacific islands (east to Tonga); 3 species in Thailand.

description: Flowering shoots (15–)20–48 cm tall; cataphylls widely spaced. Foliage leaves 2 (very rarely 1 or 3), subopposite on distal part of stem, elliptic to broadly elliptic-ovate (rarely lanceolate), acuminate to caudate; longest leaf (5.6–)7–18.5 by (1.7–)2.6–12.2 cm. Inflorescence 1, terminal, cylindric, 12- to many-flowered, 5–10.7 cm long; peduncle (1.5–)2–5.2 cm long, sometimes bearing 1–4 more or less spreading bract-like leaves; floral bracts shorter than, equal to or longer than ovaries, narrowly linear-triangular, acuminate to caudate, 4–15 mm long. Sepals sparsely pubescent to subglabrous; dorsal sepal linear to narrowly linear-lanceolate, acute to acuminate, mucronate, 11.2–11.4 by 2.2–2.3 mm; lateral sepals connate for almost their entire length, the resulting synsepal tightly embracing the labellum’s spur at base, the non-tubular part boat-shaped, linear-triangular to linear-lanceolate, bifid with acuminate, often mucronate lobules, 11.9–12.5 by 4.6–5.2 mm. Petals boat-shaped, obliquely lanceolate, obtuse to acute, 9.9–10.7 by 3.2–3.5 mm. Labellum boat-shaped, spurred at base, lanceolate, obtuse to acute, sometimes minutely mucronate, 9–10.6 by 4–4.7 mm, subentire to somewhat erose, ornamented by a pair of longitudinal keels in its proximal half; spur subparallel to ovary, cylindric, rounded to obtuse, 6.5–7 mm long. Column 7.1–8.2 mm long (to apex of rostellum); anther lanceolate to narrowly linear-lanceolate in upper view, 3.4–5.3 mm long. Ovary (including pedicel) 4–12 mm long. Capsule oblongoid to ellipsoid, (0.7–)1.1–1.8 cm long (excluding perianth remnants), 0.4–0.7 cm in diameter.

description: (Shrubs to) usually small trees. Stipules very early caducous, triangular. Leaves imparipinnate, but simple when young, unifoliolate to 4-jugate; petiole basally sometimes slightly constricted when dry, round to apically flattened or slightly channelled, rachis slightly reniform throughout, with usually 2 papillate teeth at every node, sometimes worn down to bumps; leaflets opposite; petiolules reniform, subapically with or without 2 papillate teeth, blade slightly asymmetric (except terminal leaflet), acroscopic side larger than basiscopic side, margin flat, serrate, teeth glandular, pointing upwards, tip of apex very blunt to rounded, both surfaces glabrous, upper surface dark green, lower surface (light) green; venation slightly raised on both sides, tertiary (secondary in non-compound leaves) veins looped and closed near margin, higher order veinlets reticulate. Inflorescences terminal and axillary panicles (Thailand), cymose, branches angular to somewhat grooved, somewhat flattened at nodes, glabrous or with papillae-like hairs, glabrescent; bracts gradually becoming smaller towards smaller branches and flowers, ovate to triangular, ciliate along margins. Flowers scented; pedicel round, with a subbasal abscission zone; sepals 5, imbricate, margin usually papillate, apex rounded to truncate, 2 outer smaller; petals 5, glabrous, apex rounded to truncate, rather translucent and membranous; stamens 5, filaments strap-like, basally broadened, touching each other, bent inwards, apically narrow, anthers dorsifixed, 2-thecate, introrse, opening by lengthwise slits, connective with or without convex apical knob; disc an upright annular ring, upper margin erose, 5-lobed; ovaries 3 (or 4), basally connate, each locule subovoid, glabrous, with 2 or 4‒6 ovules each, styles slender, stigmas connate, together knob-like, shortly papillate. Fruits drupaceous, with a variable number of ovules developed into seeds, short remnants of styles often sticking out from sides, smooth to warty; wall woody when dry, thin to very thick. Seeds ± triangular in transverse section, convex on outside, smooth, shiny; hilum apical, small, triangular.</br></br>Turpinia has 30‒40 species and in Asia it ranges from India and Sri Lanka to S China and Japan, throughout SE Asia and Malesia to New Guinea. It is also present in the tropical regions of S. America and the West Indies (type). Four species are present in Thailand.

description: (Shrubs to) trees, to 20 m tall, to 20 cm dbh; flowering branches 1.5‒4.5 mm diam. Outer bark rough to cracked and flaking, brownish to grey to blackish grey; inner bark brown. Stipules very early caducous, triangular, 1.5‒3 by 1.5‒3 mm, outside with very few and short hairs, glabrescent? Leaves (1- or) 2- or 3-jugate; petiole 2.5‒10.2 cm long; rachis 1‒17 cm long; petiolules 2‒21 mm long; subapically with 2 papillate teeth; blade (ovate to) elliptic to oblong (to slightly obovate), 3.5‒18.7 by 1.4‒6.6 cm, 2‒3.6 times as long as wide, papery to (sub)coriaceous, base cuneate to rounded, marginal teeth pointing upwards, 1.5‒9 mm apart (measured in middle of leaflet), apex acuminate to cuspidate; tertiary veins 8‒14 per side. Inflorescences to 29 cm long, rachis 0.7‒3.5 mm diam. At 2 cm from base, green; longest side branches to 12 cm long, branches with papillae-like hairs in grooves, especially near nodes, glabrescent. Flowers 2‒2.5 by 2.5‒4 mm; pedicel 1‒3.7 mm long, glabrous; sepals ovate to obovate, 1.3‒2 by 0.9‒1.6 mm, light green to light yellow; petals elliptic to obovate, 1.5‒2 by 0.8‒1.3 mm, white to light yellow; stamens: filaments 0.9‒1.5 mm long, white to light yellow, anthers 0.3‒0.5 by 0.3‒0.5 mm, light yellow, connective with convex apical knob; disc light yellow; ovaries 3, subovoid, 0.5‒0.8 by 0.5‒0.8 mm, green, carpels with 4 ovules per locule in 2 pairs, styles 0.5‒1 mm long, green, stigmas white. Fruits irregularly subglobular to flattened globular, 5‒11(‒20) mm diam., short remnants of styles sticking out from sides, otherwise smooth (central Thailand) to somewhat warty (northern Thailand), becoming yellow or blackish red; wall thin, < 2 mm thick. Seeds 3.2‒3.5 mm high by 4.4‒5 mm wide to 2.3‒3.5 mm thick.

Leaves (unifoliolate to) 1‒3-jugate; petioles 5.6‒13.6 cm long, rachis 5.2‒19.5 cm long; petiolules 1.5‒10 mm long, subapically without (to sometimes with vestiges of 2) papillae-like teeth; blade ovate to oblong, 6‒30.5 by 2.6‒14.8 cm, 1.7‒2.9 times as long as wide, coriaceous, base cuneate to generally attenuate, marginal teeth pointing upwards to somewhat inwards, 4.5‒9 mm apart (measured in middle of leaflet), apex acuminate to caudate; tertiary veins 7‒13 per side. Flowers 4‒7.5 by 5‒9 mm; pedicel 2.2‒6.5 mm long, glabrous; sepals: 2 outer 1.8‒3.4 by 2.2‒3.2 mm, these and a third ovate, others obovate, 3.8‒5.5 by 2‒4 mm, pale green with a dark red-purple streak in bud, turning tan-greenish to uniform dark red-purple with age, very stiff, drying dark brown; petals oblong, 2.2‒5 by 1.5‒3 mm, cream to pale orange tinged red-purple to tan-orange; stamens: filaments 3‒3.3 mm long, translucent to tan-orange, anthers 1.2‒1.5 by 0.8‒1 mm, bright yellow to tan-orange, connective without convex apical knob; disc pale yellow to tan-orange; ovaries 3 (or 4), subovoid, 1‒1.2 mm by c. 1 mm, red, carpels with 4 ovules each, in 2 pairs, styles 1.4‒1.8 mm long, red. Fruits irregularly subglobular to obpyramidal, when young horned with remnants of styles, still visible when older, 15‒28 by 15‒34 mm, yellow to yellow-orange, wall very woody, 2‒6 mm thick, smooth, usually with three dehiscence lines visible, these not present in wall itself (indehiscent). Seeds c. 8.5 mm high by 7.3 mm wide to 4.5 mm thick.

description: Very small to medium-sized, seasonally dormant or evergreen, glabrous, rarely pubescent or glandular-pubescent, monoecious herbs. Stem a globose, subglobose or irregular tuber, sometimes rhizomatous or stoloniferous, rarely an epigeal stem. Leaves few to several together; petiole D-shaped to terete, apex and middle portion sometimes tuberculate, sheath rather short; leaf blade usually cordate-sagittate, sagittate to hastate, trifid, pedatifid or pedatisect, rarely linear, narrowly lanceolate, elliptico-oblong or cordate, apex rarely tuberculate; primary lateral veins pinnate, forming submarginal collective vein, 1–2 marginal veins also present; higher order venation reticulate. Inflorescence solitary, appearing with or without or after the leaves; peduncle shorter than petiole, often partially to wholly hypogeal; spathe variably constricted between lower part and limb; lower part with convolute margins, persistent or rarely evanescent; spathe limb eventually bending backwards to become strongly revolute or even strongly, circinnately recoiled, broadly ovate to lanceolate, ± acuminate; spadix sessile, shorter, subequal or much longer than spathe; flowers unisexual, perigone absent; pistillate flower zone cylindrical, subconical to subglobose, separated from staminate flower zone by a rather long axis covered either entirely or only in basal part with staminodes of various shapes, rarely with staminodes above staminate flowers; pistillate flowers with gynoecia orientated horizontally or vertically; ovary ovoid, ellipsoid or obovoid, free, rarely syncarpic, unilocular, ovules 1–3, orthotropous, funicle short, placenta basal; stigma sessile, discoid-hemispherical; staminodes either all similar or diverse in the same spadix, capitate, clavate to spathulate, cylindrical, filiform, subulate or globose, rarely stout and flattened at the tip, or branched, or reduced to verrucae, straight to flexuose, suberect, spreading or decurved; staminate flower zone cylindrical to ellipsoid, usually densely but rarely sparsely flowered; staminate flowers 1–3-androus but usually 1-androus, free, stamens free or sometimes ± connate, anthers subsessile, connective slender, sometimes prominulent; thecae ovoid to ellipsoid, dehiscing by pores or lateral slits extending to the middle or nearly to the base and confluent apically; appendix usually shortly stipitate, rarely with disc-like extension at the base or sessile, smooth, conoid to extremely slender and filiform-subulate, usually long-exserted. Fruit an ovoid berry, 1- or rarely 2-seeded, orange-red, green or white when ripe. Seed globose to obnapiform, testa thin, rugulose to smooth, strophiolate; embryo axile, elongate, straight, endosperm copious.</br></br>About 100 species distributed from E Himalaya and throughout tropical and subtropical Asia as far east as New Guinea & Australia.</br></br>Thirty-two species are recognized in Thailand, 24 of them (75%) endemic. Five undescribed species are included in the key below, bringing the total to 37 but the true number is without doubt far greater.</br></br>Typhonium sensu lato (see, e.g. Hetterscheid & Boyce, 2000) has recently been investigated at the molecular level and a new taxonomy of it has been published by Cusimano et al., (Taxon 59(2): 439–447. 2010). Whereas Hetterscheid & Boyce (2000) based their decision to sink Sauromatum in Typhonium exclusively on morphological analysis, the molecular data and analysis by Cusimano et al., show a well-separated Sauromatum clade which cannot be maintained in Typhonium. The Sauromatum clade contains six species, of which three occur in Thailand. The Australian members of Typhonium s.l. will also be separated from Typhonium as Lazarum A.Hay.

description: Carnivorous, annual or perennial herbs. Usually hairless. Thai material always small and delicate. Aquatic to terrestrial, always growing in wet places. Leaves diverse in form, often absent at flowering. In terrestrial and semi-aquatic species, the blade, when present, is delicate and few nerved. In aquatic and some semi-aquatic species, the leaves are finely divided into numerous, very thin, linear, hair-like or blood-capillary like segments, which are often microscopically setose and which have no distinct blade. Traps minute, ovoid or globular, present on leaves and / or stolons, capturing and digesting small, often microscopic organisms. Bracts and bracteoles either attached at the base or in the middle. Inflorescence a spike or raceme or, rarely, flowers solitary, occasionally twining (Thai species always twining in a sinistrose or clockwise manner). Flowers hermaphrodite, 5-merous, strongly zygomorphic, sometimes cleistogamous, borne above the surface of the water. Sepals fused, deeply 2-lobed, the lobes more or less free from each other and usually widely divergent. Corolla fused, two-lipped, spurred, with a very short tube: the lower lip often with a conspicuous bump which, in the descriptions which follow, I include as part of the palate. The palate itself lies behind the bump and is often of different colour to the rest of the corolla, may be fringed with hairs and may almost close the mouth of the flower. Stamens 2, inserted on the corolla, filaments short and bent; anthers often connate. Ovary superior, of 2 carpels with a single locule; ovules numerous, on a free-central placenta. Style 1, long, stigma unequally bifid (in some species it has been reported that the lobes of the stigma are either sensitive, closing when touched or after pollination: this, however, has, as far as I know, not yet been observed in Thai material). Fruit usually a vertically circumscissile globose or ovoid capsule. Seeds numerous, minute, almost dust-like in some species, with distinct and varied microscopic surface sculpturing.</br></br>Twenty-seven native species in Thailand. Two additional species which are potentially present, but which are either unrecorded or doubtfully recorded, are also included.</br></br>As is well known, Utricularia catches small prey through its active trapping mechanism. Traps are thin-walled, globose or ovoid and vary in size from ≤ 0.2 mm to usually ≤ 8 mm in Thai species. Untripped traps are flat. When prey passes the entrance to the trap it is sprung, the trap inflates and the prey, together with surrounding water, is sucked into the trap through a hinged trap-door. The door then closes itself in ca 1/500th of a second. The trapped organism dies of anoxia, is digested and the trap eventually resets itself. As well as minute animals it has recently been found that traps may contain algae, and that algae may be present in the absence of trapped animal prey; though whether the algae are actively trapped or merely accidentally sucked in remains to be determined. The trap’s size, morphology and internal structure offer numerous, minute, taxonomic characteristics. Of particular importance are the shape and size of the hairs contained within the trap. These are most easily visualised by cutting open the trap before staining it with Toluidine Blue: the hairs appear as brightly and deeply stained entities which stand out well against the more poorly stained cells of the walls of the trap. Two types of hair are often present in the traps: these bear either two or four arms. The four-armed hairs, sometimes called quadrifids, and in particular the angle, disposition, shape and size of their arms, are of taxonomic value. In some Thai species four-armed hairs are absent altogether and, occasionally, I have found their absence a useful confirmatory characteristic of species identity. The traps are borne in a variety of positions on the plant and what these positions are is also a useful taxonomic characteristic. Finally, the traps are ornamented by appendages which usually occur around the entrance to the trap. The detailed structure of these appendages is taxonomically important. However, because they are extremely fragile, they are often broken or damaged in herbarium material; indeed, in many herbarium specimens they may appear to be entirely absent, but this is an artifact caused by damage. The flowers vary in colour, size and shape and are spurred. The spur also varies, in size, shape and orientation and in the disposition of its internal nectarial glands. Whilst the latter characteristic has been extensively used in the delimitation of certain species in Europe it appears not to have been so far recorded for Thai material.</br></br>The seed-coat is of taxonomic value but its surface features are very difficult to see and, therefore, they have not been extensively used in this account. Unfortunately, the type of hair on the seed’s surface is the only simple morphological means of distinguishing between some of the species of spathulate-leaved Utricularia in Thailand. As the seeds of these species are only 0.2–0.3 mm long and their surface hairs are correspondingly tiny (at an order of magnitude smaller) I have found a pocket microscope of 50 x magnification extremely useful.</br></br>Liquid (50–55% alcohol, 40% water and 5–10% glycerine) preserved material is easier to use than dried herbarium material but unfortunately, collections of liquid preserved material from Thailand are sparse, some of those that exist are not well-maintained and Utricularia’s minute seeds are not easily found again in large volumes of preservative. In general, therefore, it is best to supplement dried with liquid collections rather than relying solely on the latter. The impression that it is almost impossible to correctly identify dried herbarium material is inaccurate - nearly all of it can be identified. Rehydration of dried material is particularly effective in this genus, and I have found that traps from even the most decrepit and elderly specimens can be successfully rehydrated by 36 hours immersion in water at room temperature; the addition of detergent to the water is unnecessary.</br></br>Following Taylor's pragmatic approach I use the term ‘leaves’ rather than 'foliar organs'as used by Maxwell.

description: Suspended aquatic. Stolons filiform, up to 1 m long, occasionally inflated. Rhizoides usually present at the base of the peduncle, branched. Floats rarely present at the base of the peduncle, borne in whorls, ca 2–6 cm long by 3–5 mm wide, the surface with occasional scattered, branched, short filiform rhizoides. Leaves filiform, hair-like, much branched, 2–8 cm long. Auricles (at the base of the leaves) 2–4 mm long, divided into filiform segments, not easily distinguishable from the leaves. Traps usually numerous, ovoid, (1–)4 mm long; mouth lateral, with 2 very fragile appendages (often absent due to damage in dried specimens), often blackish. Internal hairs both 2-armed and 4-armed, the latter or , rarely in shape. Inflorescence erect, emergent, generally solitary, (5–)20(–30) cm long; peduncle hairless, sometimes reddish at base; 5–7-flowered; flowers widely spaced. Scales absent. Bracts ovate, attached at the base, 1–2 mm long, blunt or apiculate at tip, much shorter than pedicels. Bracteoles absent. Pedicels ca 10 mm long and erect in flower; longer, thickened and strongly deflexed in fruit. Calyx lobes ± equal, 2–3 mm long on flowering; up to 9 mm long, enlarging markedly (3 x–5 x) and widely spreading in fruit so that the lobes lie opposite, at 180°, to each other. The maturing fruit lies between the two calyx lobes and almost always is topped by its style; the lobes and fruit form a three pointed star shape when seen in side view. Corolla bright yellow, 1–1.5 cm long; upper lip erect, smaller than lower lip, lower lip downwards facing, with purple guidelines near throat, palate prominent, often deeper yellow and with reddish lines or dots, spur 1–1.5 cm long, subparallel to lower lip, straight or slightly curved, shortly-pointed. Seeds flattened, disc-shaped, usually with 5 sides each with distinct ridged or winged edges, and with a distinct rounded dot like scar in the middle of one of the flat faces, 1–2 mm long.

description: Terrestrial. Stolons numerous, often mat forming, filiform. Rhizoides numerous, filiform, branched. Floats absent. Leaves linear, 0.4–1.5 cm long, 1-nerved (but with 2 very, very faint lateral nerves visible in material with cleared leaves), usually present at flowering. Auricles absent. description: Terrestrial. Stolons infrequent, filiform. Rhizoides infrequent filiform, branched. Floats absent. description: Terrestrial, epiphytic or lithophytic. Stolons numerous, capillary, unbranched. Rhizoides few, capillary, unbranched. Floats absent. description: Terrestrial, sometimes in shallow water. Stolons numerous, capillary, branched. Rhizoides few, capillary, branched. Floats absent. Inflorescence erect, solitary, peduncle sometimes fluted especially when dry, usually ca (4–)10– 18(–25) cm long; peduncle hairless; usually few (1–)2–6(–10)-flowered; flowers widely spaced, usually held such that mouth of the flower is subvertical and the lower lip spreading horizontally. Scales similar to bracts. Bracts attached at their base, ovate, acute, 2–3 mm long. Bracteoles similar to, but smaller than, the bracts, sometimes subulate. Pedicels ca 2–3 mm long in flower, only slightly longer than the subtending bract. Calyx lobes subequal, ovate to almost circular, ca 3–5 mm in diameter, markedly expanded in fruit, minutely (microscopically) denticulate. Corolla blue; ca 6–8 mm long; upper lip much smaller than lower lip, which is spreading, palate sometimes whitish, prominent; spur ca 3–4 mm long, pointing downwards, very much longer than the calyx, strongly curved. Seeds ovoid; ca 0.3 mm, with the coarse reticulations clearly visible.

description: Terrestrial or hemiepiphytic, chlorophyllous, climbing herbs; aerial roots produced one at each node; stems branched, cylindric or quadrangular, sometimes longitudinally grooved, thin to thick, succulent, smooth, glabrous, green. Foliage leaves large and fleshy or reduced to small scales and caducous, base not sheathing, one at each node, distichous or spirally arranged, glabrous; petiole usually twisted at intersection to stem. Inflorescences axillary, racemose, few to many-flowered; rachis with scale-like bracts. Flowers large, showy, short-lived, opening in succession. Sepals free, spreading, smooth, 5- to 7-veined. Petals free, spreading, 5-veined, often with strong midvein. Labellum adnate to the sides of column with its basal margins, forming a chamber, the free part entire or 3-lobed, usually with hairy appendages inside, often longitudinally grooved outside. Column long, slender, curved near the top; anther pointing downwards on the front of the column; pollen forming up to 4 sticky pollen smears without caudicles or viscidium, rostellum broad below anther. Ovary slender, articulate to sepals and petals. Fruit fleshy, cylindric, indehiscent. Seeds large, with stout testa.</br></br>A genus of ca. 107 species, distributed throughout tropical America, Africa, Madagascar to tropical Asia and the Pacific Islands (absent from Australia); 5 species in Thailand.

description: Terrestrial, rhizomatous herbs; the creeping stem-like rhizome rooting from its nodes. Flowering shoots terminal, erect from a decumbent base, 8–32 cm tall. Foliage leaves 3–9, scattered along the stem to crowded on its lower or upper part, petiolate, sheathing at base. Inflorescence racemose, short and dense; bracts longer than the ovary, glabrous to glandular pubescent on the dorsal side. Flowers 7 to many, resupinate, scarcely opening. Sepals free, boat-shaped, 1-veined; dorsal sepal 2.1–5.8 mm long. Petals connivent with the dorsal sepal, 1-veined, entire. Labellum basally adnate to the column, straight (i.e., not twisted), 0.9–4.3 mm long, shorter than the sepals, simple with incurved margins, hooded at apex, proximally with a spur that protrudes below the bases of the lateral sepals when the flower is viewed from the side; spur inside with 1 stalked appendage on either side. Column straight (i.e., not twisted); stigma bipartite, flat; rostellum triangular to subquadrate, retuse to bifid, producing an infundibular tegula that encloses the attenuated bases of the pollinia; viscidium 1, naked; anther versatile; pollinia 2, basitonous. Ovary glabrous. Fruit a capsule, dehiscing by 6 longitudinal slits.</br></br>A genus of ca. 35 species distributed from scattered areas in mainland Southeast Asia (west to northeastern India) throughout Malesia to northern Queensland and Fiji; 3 species in Thailand.

description: Shrubs or small trees, irregularly branching. Leaves opposite (decussate), (sub)sessile, whitish short hairy, lower surface glandular punctate; stipules absent (some hairs present only). description: Trees; branchlets terete, angular or compressed, pubescent or glabrescent. Leaves spirally arranged or tufted on short shoots; lamina chartaceous or coriaceous, elliptic-obovate or rhomboid; apex obtuse or acute; base cuneate; venation looped or arched; midrib grooved, raised or flat above; secondary veins variable in number; tertiary venation reticulate; stipules absent. description: Tree to 13 m tall; branchlets terete or compressed, sparsely pubescent, glabrescent, somewhat spiny; lenticels elliptic, conspicuous. Leaves scattered; lamina chartaceous or coriaceous, narrowly to broadly elliptic or obovate, 6–14.5 by 2.5–6.5 cm; apex acute to obtusely acute or obtuse; base cuneate, glabrous; young leaves sparsely pubescent, glabrescent; midrib flat or raised, crested above, densely or sparsely pubescent on both surfaces; secondary veins 11–16 on each side; petioles (0.5–) 1.2–2 cm long, whitish tomentose, glabrescent. Flowers axillary, in 2–5-flowered fascicles; pedicels 6.8–10 mm long, tomentose. Sepals , two exterior ovate, 5–5.8 by 2.7–3 mm, whitish tomentose outside, reddish brown sericeous inside except for a glabrous base; two interior sepals narrowly ovate or lanceolate, 5.3–6.9 by 2.3–3.5 mm, with membranous margin, reddish brown sericeous on both surfaces except for a glabrous base inside; the fifth sepal narrowly to broadly ovate 5.6–6.5 by 2.3–3.3 mm, the margin, which is covered by one exterior sepal, membranous, reddish brown sericeous on both surfaces except for a glabrous base inside. description: Terrestrial, rhizomatous herbs; the elongate (to very strongly condensed) rhizome rooting from its nodes. Flowering shoots (2–)3.5–48 cm tall. Foliage leaves 3–9(–17), scattered (to crowded) on the stem. Inflorescence spicate or racemose: bracts glabrous or (glandular-) pubescent on the dorsal side. Flowers (2–)7 to many, more or less resupinate. Sepals free, 1 to 5-veined; dorsal sepal 3–9 mm long. Petals free or adherent to adnate to the dorsal sepal. Labellum basally adnate to the column, straight (i.e., not twisted), 2.7–7.5 mm long along the mid-line, differentiated into hypochile, mesochile, and epichile; hypochile concave to saccate (but not protruding below the bases of the lateral sepals when the flower is viewed from the side), inside with 1–3 appendages on either side; mesochile devoid of lateral flanges (but sometimes with low keels); epichile bilobed or simple. Column straight (i.e., not twisted), sometimes provided with two prominent wings or low vertical keels or lamellae on the front; stigma bipartite, flat; rostellum triangular, bifid, sometimes producing a tiny tegule; viscidium 1, naked; anther versatile; pollinia 2, basitonous. Ovary glabrous to (glandular-)pubescent. Fruit a capsule, dehiscing by 6 longitudinal slits.</br></br>A genus of ca. 70 species, distributed from tropical and southern Africa across the Indian Ocean to (sub)tropical mainland Asia, Malesia, Queensland and Fiji; additionally, a few probably anthropochorous occurrences elsewhere (see Z. strateumatica); 10 species in Thailand.

description: Flowering shoots (6–)10–35 cm tall. Sepals 3-to 5-veined, pubescent on the dorsal side (rarely subglabrous); dorsal sepal lanceolate-oblong to ovate, rounded to obtuse, 4.5–9 by 2.7–4.7 mm; lateral sepals obliquely (elliptic-)oblong to (ovate-lanceolate, rounded to subacute, 3.8–7.1 by 1.7–3.4 mm. Labellum 3.7–7.5 mm long along the mid-line; hypochile inside with 1 papilla-like appendage on either side; mesochile smooth on the outside: epichile bilobed, with a distinct V-shaped sinus at apex when spread out distinctly wider than the hypochile, lobules (obtriangular-)obovate to subcircular, 2.1–7.1 by 1.6–4.8 mm (length measured along the hind edge), 1.1–2.4 times as long as wide. Column devoid of ornaments on the front or with 2 vertical keels that are sometimes abruptly protruding just below the rostellum. Ovary pubescent. description: Flowering shoots 18–33 cm tall, sometimes branched at base. Foliage leaves petiolate (below) to subsessile (above), blackish-green to reddish-green above, dark green to reddish grey underneath; lamina lanceolate to narrowly ovate, slightly oblique, acute to obtuse, minutely mucronate, (1.3–)2–6.7 by (0.7–)1–3 cm. Inflorescence pubescent; rachis 3.7–8 cm long; bracts ovate-lanceolate, acuminate, ciliate, otherwise glabrous, 5.4–10 by 2.4–4.4 mm. Flowers sessile, mainly dull reddish with white petals, cream to yellow labellum and olive-brown ovary. Sepals 3-veined, glabrous; dorsal sepal ovate, rounded, 5–6 by 2.8–4.2 mm; lateral sepals linear lanceolate, slightly oblique, obtuse, 4.5–6 by 1.3–1.6 mm. Petals adnate to the dorsal sepal, obliquely to falcately oblanceolate, not abruptly narrowed below the apex, 4.6–5.4 by 1.4–1.5 mm. Labellum 3.9–4.2 mm long along the mid-line; hypochile inside with 1 scale-like appendage on either side; mesochile minutely papillose-pubescent on the outside; epichile subquadrate to transversely subrectangular, truncate when spread out, half as wide to approximately as wide as the hypochile. Column with two low, slightly incurved, obliquely triangular lamellae on the front. Ovary glabrous. Capsule suberect, sessile, obliquely oblongoid-fusiform, glabrous, 12–14 mm long, 3.5–4 mm in diameter.

description: Flowering shoots 12–32 cm tall. Foliage leaves petiolate; lamina lanceolate, acute, mucronate, 2.7–9.4 by 0.8–3 cm. description: Flowering shoots 5–17 cm tall. Foliage leaves petiolate, dark purplish with a pale mid-line; lamina obliquely (oblong-lanceolate (to ovate), acute, mucronate 1.5–2.3 by 0.5–0.8 cm.
